# Source-grounded requirements and open-rule register

This note grounds the current prototype in the materials already supplied in this workspace. It does not treat the MO-IT107 design set as an automatic replacement for any MO-IT110 milestone requirement.

## Project decisions already made

- Start a fresh project; there is no personal MS1 implementation to extend.
- Use Java for the backend and payroll logic, with an HTML/CSS browser interface instead of Swing.
- Use Firebase as a development data service. Project `motorph-jd` and web app `motorphdev` exist; Email/Password Auth is enabled and the user reports publishing the narrowly scoped demo rules in `docs/firestore.rules`. Live synthetic API tests verified allowed own-user employee/attendance operations and denied cross-user/payroll/extra-salary operations. Exact Firestore location and Firebase authorization from the current Arena preview origin remain unconfirmed.
- Use the other teams' submissions selectively as pattern references, not as a full project to submit.
- Earlier MO-IT108 MotorPH Requirements Analysis and System Design documents are supplemental legacy context, not the current MO-IT110 MS2 rubric. They clarify attendance-view scope and proposed role/data fields, but not a complete hour or payroll algorithm. See `docs/legacy-mo-it108-traceability.md`.
- `The Code.pdf` is a C++ inventory-management exercise, not a payroll module; no code from it is reused.
- Keep synthetic data only; never use the uploaded inventory CSV as payroll data.
- Do not invent payroll formulas, current statutory rates, or expected payroll outputs.
- The UI should be professional, restrained, and non-game-like, using permitted/credited code selectively.

## Firebase development boundary

The browser uses Firebase Authentication only to establish a user identity. The Java backend forwards the resulting ID token to Firestore REST, so Firestore Security Rules authorize access; it does not use an Admin SDK or service-account credential. The published development rules scope `users/{uid}/demoEmployees` and `users/{uid}/demoAttendance` to synthetic data, separate from any eventual production employee/payroll schema. Live tests verified the required own-user paths and tested deny cases. The latest published-rules smoke used disposable Auth accounts and employee documents, all deleted after testing; one cancelled synthetic leave record (`LV-3502C01F0E60`) and one cancelled ticket (`TK-F05DD2B0D6CC`) remain under their deleted test UIDs because workflow deletes are denied. This sandbox is not a production role/HR access design.

## Supplied source set

- `uploads/MO-IT107 - 2nd Milestone_ Database Design for the MotorPH Payroll System H2101 TORRES, J.D..pdf`
- `uploads/MO-IT107 Homework_ Data Dictionary for MotorPH Payroll System Database H2101 Torres, J.D..pdf`
- `uploads/MO-IT107 Homework_ Data Flow Diagram of MotorPH Payroll System H2101 Torres, J.D..pdf`
- `uploads/MotorPH_Payroll_System_Full_Synthesis.md` — detailed text reconstruction of those three PDFs.
- The user's earlier MO-IT108 Requirements Analysis, System Design, and Terminal Assessment proposal PDFs are summarized in `docs/legacy-mo-it108-traceability.md`; treat them as older-course context, not a substitute for the active MO-IT110 rubric.
- `uploads/The Code.pdf` — inspected and classified as unrelated C++ inventory-management code; it was not used as a payroll source.
- MO-IT110 modules/requirements were reviewed earlier and summarized in `repo_review/submission-comprehensive-report.md`; the readable project-level conclusion is that the modules teach the Java/OOP design-to-implementation progression, but do not provide a complete payroll formula oracle.
- `repo_review/submission-comprehensive-report.md` — repository tests, module links, scope cautions, and limitations for the nine reference submissions.

## Facts used in the current slice

### Employee directory

The MO-IT107 Data Dictionary describes Employee identity/status and links to Address, Position, Department, Government, and Supervisor. The exact direct-vs-derived relationships differ between that dictionary, Database Design prose, and the ERD. Therefore the current UI uses only a small display projection (ID, name, department, role, location, status) with fully synthetic records. It does not claim to implement the full Employee table or decide the disputed relationships. Government identifiers and other PII are intentionally absent.

### Attendance read-only model

The supplied Data Dictionary lists these Attendance fields:

- `attendanceID` — integer primary key;
- `scheduleID` — foreign key;
- `date` — date, unique in combination with `scheduleID`;
- `timeIn` and `timeOut` — time values, with the source check `timeIn <= timeOut`;
- `dayType` — enum, with members not specified.

The prototype maps these to `AttendanceRecord` and validates positive synthetic identifiers, required values, `timeIn <= timeOut`, and unique `(scheduleID, date)` entries. A minimal employee-to-schedule mapping allows records to be viewed for an employee. The screen provides read-only inclusive date filtering and, following the older MO-IT108 Requirements Analysis, defaults to the selected employee's earliest/latest available record dates. This is a view convenience, not a claimed payroll-period calendar. `dayType` is shown as `DEMO`, not as an official enum value. No work hours, overtime, paid leave, undertime, or pay values are derived.

The database-design PDF also describes attendance as tied to Schedule and the DFD routes attendance through Schedule and Time Tracking, then Timesheet Validation. The exact source/import mechanism and MS2 workflow are not asserted by this read-only fixture.

### Payroll and payslip fields

The source set names payroll components and storage fields, including:

- `Payroll`: employee, wage/rebate/summary IDs, month, PTO maximum, hourly/daily/monthly rates, net pay;
- `Payslip`: payroll ID, period start/end, regular/overtime/holiday-overtime/PTO/undertime hours, worked days/holidays/rest days, gross income;
- `Earnings`: overtime/PTO/holiday/rest-day pay, subsidies/stipends, other incentives, total benefits;
- `Deductibles`, `Other Transactions`, `Government Deductibles`, `Contributions`, `Government Tally`, and `Summary` for deduction and contribution amounts/totals.

The DFD labels Timesheet Validation, Leave Monetisation, Wage and Adjustments, Government Deductibles, Basic Payroll Computation, Payslip Generation & Distribution, and Monthly Summary Compilation. These descriptions establish the concept names and broad flow, not their exact computation.

## Unresolved source conflicts kept open

The PDFs disagree on several schema details. The prototype has not chosen a definitive production schema for these:

- `Schedule.restDay SET` versus `Schedule.restDayID` plus a separate Rest Day table;
- direct Employee `departmentID` / `governmentID` versus deriving department via Position and linking Government via `Government.employeeID`;
- Address region stored directly versus derived through City;
- presence of `Supervisor.departmentID`;
- presence of `Leave.scheduleID`;
- key/version fields for Rates and Government Tally;
- some Holiday uniqueness and relationship-matrix cardinalities.

See Sections 16 and 17 of the full synthesis for the complete discrepancies.

## Payroll-rule status

The source documents do **not** supply the arithmetic formula or current effective values for gross pay, salary conversion, overtime, holiday/rest-day rates, undertime, paid leave, leave monetisation, SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, withholding tax, deductions, net pay, or rounding. They also do not provide an authoritative worked payslip example. The payroll screen therefore remains intentionally disabled. The nine GitHub submissions' formulas/tests are comparison evidence only, not a policy authority.

## Scope boundary

MO-IT107's DFD/database design is broad (five actors; employee management, payroll processing, and archival; PII approval intent; many database tables). The current project begins as a narrow web-based Java/OOP slice. Do not add every actor, all tables, two-person PII workflow, monthly reports, or archive deletion unless the active MO-IT110 milestone explicitly requires it. Keep such items traceable to the source and clearly labelled reference-only until scope is confirmed.
# Legacy MotorPH coursework → current MS2 traceability

**Purpose:** use the user's earlier MO-IT108 MotorPH documents to clarify the current prototype without silently expanding its approved scope. These are earlier-course sources (A.Y. 2024–2025), not the active MO-IT110 MS2 rubric. They can inform design and requirements mapping, but do not override the user's current instruction to keep payroll calculations disabled.

## Sources inspected

- `/home/user/uploads/MO-IT108 - 1st Milestone_ Requirements Analysis Document of MotorPH Payroll System H1103 Torres, A. (1).pdf` — a requirements document with ten functional-requirement groups and non-functional requirements.
- `/home/user/uploads/MO-IT108 - 2nd Milestone_ System Design Document of MotorPH Payroll System H1103 Torres, A. (1).pdf` — module descriptions, scenarios, data concepts, and an RBAC matrix.
- `/home/user/uploads/MO-IT108 - Terminal Assessment_ Business Technology Proposal for MotorPH Payroll System H1103 Torres, A..pdf` — a broad technology proposal. Several major sections still contain template prompts/placeholders, so treat it as vision/context rather than an approved detailed specification.
- `/home/user/uploads/The Code.pdf` — C++ inventory-management iterations using stock fields such as ID, brand, age, date, and status. Despite a MotorPH inventory CSV filename, it is not a payroll system or a reusable MotorPH payroll module. No code from it was integrated.

## What the legacy documents clarify

### Attendance view

The MO-IT108 Requirements Analysis says employees can view attendance metrics over a date range, defaulting from the earliest to latest available record. The System Design expands this into daily logs and counts for present, absent, tardy, overtime, undertime, and leave usage. It also names concepts such as `ClockInStatus`, `ShiftStartTime`, `ShiftEndTime`, `GracePeriod`, `AttendanceTag`, `TotalWorked`, `WorkHourTag`, `AbsentCount`, `PresentCount`, `TardyCount`, `OvertimeHours`, `UndertimeHours`, `LeaveTaken`, and `LeaveBalance`.

This clarifies the intended *shape* of the attendance screen, but not a complete calculation policy. The documents do not provide actual grace-period values, the absence threshold, break treatment, rounding, overnight-shift handling, missing-punch corrections, timezone policy, overtime triggers, or a worked expected example. One field is described as `TotalWorked` based on clock-in/out, but that alone does not settle those rules. Therefore the app now defaults the raw-record filter to the selected synthetic employee's earliest and latest available dates; the user may narrow the inclusive range. This is a data-range convenience, **not** a payroll period, and no hour/category totals are derived.

### Payroll snapshot and pay cycle

The legacy System Design lists proposed snapshot fields such as `PayrollCycleStart`, `PayrollCycleEnd`, `HourlyWage`, `RegHours`, `OTHours`, `PTOHours`, holiday hours/shifts, incentives, tax, other deductions, gross/net pay, and a snapshot timestamp. The Requirements Analysis also names wage components, incentives, statutory/other deductions, payroll reports, and payslip distribution.

These are useful field names and workflow hints, not formulas or current policy values. The documents do not give exact semi-monthly cut-off dates, salary-to-hourly conversion, rule tables/effective dates, rounding, statutory values, or a complete end-to-end expected payroll result. Salary snapshots, calculations, and payslips therefore remain disabled.

### Identity and roles

The legacy documents describe Employee, Supervisor/Lead, HR, Payroll Staff, and System Admin roles. Their RBAC matrix distinguishes self/team access, HR/Payroll actions, and approvals for government details; the requirements also call for 2FA and branch-aware access. The current prototype has Firebase Email/Password sign-in and an isolated per-user synthetic sandbox only. It does **not** implement 2FA, branch routing, team membership, HR/Payroll roles, production PII handling, or the legacy RBAC matrix. No real employee information is permitted.

## Ten legacy functional-requirement groups vs current prototype

| Legacy requirement | Current state | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Employee login | **Partial** | Firebase Email/Password sign-in is live; no employee-ID login, 2FA, branch routing, or production session/RBAC policy. |
| 2. Clock in/out | **Not implemented** | No live clocking, QR verification, or attendance-write workflow. |
| 3. Employee attendance | **Partial** | Raw synthetic entries, selected employee, inclusive date filters, and earliest–latest default. No absent/present/tardy/overtime/undertime/leave summaries. |
| 4. Salary tracker | **Intentionally disabled** | The source's snapshot fields do not define a full calculation or authoritative values. |
| 5. Tickets | **Partial, owner-scoped create/cancel** | Fictional ticket submission/cancel and queue labels for overtime, leave, timesheet, payroll, HR, and technical support; nothing is delivered or resolved. Firebase persistence requires the updated candidate rules to be published. |
| 6. Leave tracker/calendar | **Partial, owner-scoped create/cancel** | Validated fictional request submission/cancel only; no balance/accrual, approval, payroll treatment, or calendar. Firebase persistence requires updated rules. |
| 7. Team management | **Partial read-only roster** | Shows synthetic directory records; no team membership, schedules, supervisor scope, or approval workflow. |
| 8. HR handling | **Partial synthetic directory maintenance** | Signed-in Firebase users can create/update allowlisted fictional directory fields in their own sandbox; local mode is unauthenticated process memory. No HR role, schedule assignment, delete, onboarding/offboarding, or sensitive PII. |
| 9. Payroll supervision | **Intentionally disabled** | No adjustments, statutory calculations, payroll approval, or reports. |
| 10. Payroll distribution | **Not implemented** | No payslip generation, email delivery, retry handling, or distribution status. |

## Percent estimate: two different denominators

There is no single valid percentage “against the submitted folders”: those projects have different feature sets, tech stacks, and course scopes, and several are near-duplicates. The ranges below are **feature-completeness estimates, not a grade or quality score**.

- **Agreed current Tasks 1–3 scope: about 85–90%.** Task 1's live Firebase proof is complete. Task 2's browser sign-in and employee selection are verified on localhost, with the exact Arena preview-origin authorization still unverified. Task 3's employee/date inputs and raw-record path are complete; derived attendance-hour totals remain gated because their algorithm and test oracle are missing and payroll calculations must stay disabled.
- **Full legacy MO-IT108 functional breadth: roughly 25–35% represented, but less operationally complete.** The app has a real sign-in/data foundation, limited owner-scoped synthetic directory editing, read-only attendance, and owner-scoped leave/ticket create/cancel routes (published user-scoped Firestore rules live-smoke-tested for leave/ticket create/cancel). These limited workflows do not include reviewers or approvals. Clocking, leave balances/approvals/calendars, delivered and resolved tickets, actual team/supervisor management, HR lifecycle operations, payroll calculations, payslips, reports, RBAC/2FA, and production operations remain unimplemented.
- **Compared with the more complete numbered submissions (especially folders 6 and 9): roughly 25–35% of end-to-end feature breadth.** This prototype is stronger in live Firebase Auth/Firestore integration, browser accessibility/responsiveness, and current test evidence; those reference projects include payroll engines/results and broader workflows that this app deliberately does not yet have. Compared with the smallest procedural/demo submissions, the comparison can reverse because this project already has a live web/data foundation.

The largest gap to “parity” is not another Firebase feature: it is the **unbuilt payroll/business workflow** (validated attendance summaries, approved pay rules, payroll results/payslips, and applicable roles). Do not close that gap by importing unverified formulas from another submission.

## What works

- Overview, searchable employee directory/detail, raw attendance register, Requests & tickets, Team roster, HR desk, and the payroll rules gate. Employee details open from a native keyboard-operable button without overriding table semantics; result counts and form feedback use polite status regions.
- Java employee/attendance services plus a workflow service. Local preview workflow records are held in Java process memory; Firebase mode uses the signed-in user’s Firestore subcollections.
- Leave requests and tickets validate inputs, derive employee names from the caller’s own synthetic directory, show documented queue labels, and support owner-sandbox cancellation. A monthly leave-request calendar displays pending/cancelled request dates only; it does not imply approval or leave balances. No reviewer/approval/resolve/delete routes exist. The user has published the rules; live tests confirmed leave and ticket create/cancel persistence, plus cross-user denial.

package ph.motorph.web;

import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.NoSuchElementException;
import java.util.OptionalInt;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;

/** Reads raw attendance for one employee; deliberately does not calculate paid hours. */
public final class AttendanceService {
    private final EmployeeService employeeService;
    private final EmployeeScheduleStore scheduleStore;
    private final AttendanceStore attendanceStore;

    public AttendanceService(EmployeeService employeeService, EmployeeScheduleStore scheduleStore,
                             AttendanceStore attendanceStore) {
        if (employeeService == null || scheduleStore == null || attendanceStore == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("attendance service dependencies must not be null");
        }
        this.employeeService = employeeService;
        this.scheduleStore = scheduleStore;
        this.attendanceStore = attendanceStore;
    }

    /** Inclusive optional date filtering; no pay-period calendar is inferred. */
    public List<AttendanceRecord> findForEmployee(String employeeId, LocalDate from, LocalDate to) {
        if (!employeeService.findEmployee(employeeId).isPresent()) {
            throw new NoSuchElementException("employee not found");
        }
        if (from != null && to != null && from.isAfter(to)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("from date must be on or before to date");
        }
        OptionalInt scheduleId = scheduleStore.findScheduleIdForEmployee(employeeId.trim());
        if (!scheduleId.isPresent()) return java.util.Collections.emptyList();
        return attendanceStore.findByScheduleId(scheduleId.getAsInt()).stream()
            .filter(record -> from == null || !record.getDate().isBefore(from))
            .filter(record -> to == null || !record.getDate().isAfter(to))
            .collect(Collectors.toList());
    }
}
package ph.motorph.web;

import java.util.List;

/** Storage boundary for raw attendance entries. */
public interface AttendanceStore {
    List<AttendanceRecord> findByScheduleId(int scheduleId);
}
package ph.motorph.web;

import com.google.gson.JsonElement;
import com.google.gson.JsonObject;

import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.time.LocalTime;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;

/** User-scoped synthetic attendance records read through Firestore REST. */
public final class FirestoreAttendanceStore implements AttendanceStore {
    private final FirestoreRestClient client;

    public FirestoreAttendanceStore(FirestoreRestClient client) {
        if (client == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("client must not be null");
        this.client = client;
    }

    @Override
    public List<AttendanceRecord> findByScheduleId(int scheduleId) {
        List<AttendanceRecord> records = new ArrayList<>();
        for (JsonObject document : client.listDocuments(client.userCollection("demoAttendance"))) {
            records.add(fromDocument(document));
        }
        return records.stream().filter(record -> record.getScheduleId() == scheduleId).collect(Collectors.toList());
    }

    private static AttendanceRecord fromDocument(JsonObject document) {
        JsonObject fields = document.has("fields") ? document.getAsJsonObject("fields") : new JsonObject();
        return new AttendanceRecord(
            integerValue(fields, "attendanceId"), integerValue(fields, "scheduleId"),
            LocalDate.parse(stringValue(fields, "date")), LocalTime.parse(stringValue(fields, "timeIn")),
            LocalTime.parse(stringValue(fields, "timeOut")), stringValue(fields, "dayType"));
    }

    private static int integerValue(JsonObject fields, String name) {
        JsonElement element = fields.get(name);
        if (element == null || !element.isJsonObject()) return 0;
        JsonElement value = element.getAsJsonObject().get("integerValue");
        return value == null || value.isJsonNull() ? 0 : Integer.parseInt(value.getAsString());
    }

    private static String stringValue(JsonObject fields, String name) {
        return FirestoreEmployeeStore.stringValue(fields, name);
    }
}

# Roadmap to full peer-level MotorPH feature parity

**How to read “100%”:** the nine submitted folders do not share one feature set, so there is no single objective peer-completion percentage. This roadmap uses the richest relevant comparison: the payroll/attendance/leave workflows in the stronger MO-IT110-style submissions (especially folders 6 and 9), plus the user's earlier MO-IT108 Requirements Analysis and System Design. It is a feature-completion target, not a grade.

**Current user constraints remain in force:** synthetic data only; no payroll calculations until authoritative rules are provided; no guessed pay-period calendar; no Firebase Console changes by the assistant. The legacy Terminal Assessment proposal contains template placeholders and is not treated as a detailed specification. `The Code.pdf` is unrelated C++ inventory work and is excluded.

# MotorPH MS2 — browser payroll foundation

An original browser-based prototype with an HTML/CSS interface and Java 11 backend. Employee and attendance data are synthetic. Payroll remains gated until the supplied course materials define complete calculation rules and expected-value examples.

## Run locally

Requires JDK 11+, Node.js 20.19+ (or a current supported Node release), and npm.

```sh
npm install
./run.sh
```

Then open <http://localhost:8080>. `run.sh` builds the Vite frontend and serves it from the Java server. Set `PORT` to choose a different HTTP port.

For development with Vite hot reload, use two terminals:

```sh
# terminal 1: Java backend
./run-api.sh

# terminal 2: frontend
npm run dev
```

Open <http://localhost:5173>. Vite proxies `/api` calls to the Java service at `http://127.0.0.1:8080` by default; set `API_PROXY_TARGET` to use a different backend. Set `HOST=127.0.0.1` for the Java backend when Vite is proxying it locally.

Run Java domain checks:

```sh
./test.sh
```

Run browser end-to-end checks (the suite starts isolated local API/Vite processes, uses only synthetic in-memory records, and cleans them up on exit):

```sh
npx playwright-core install chromium
# Linux, if system libraries are missing:
sudo npx playwright-core install-deps chromium
npm run test:e2e
```

The app uses a small vendored Gson JAR for the Java Firestore REST adapter; its license is recorded in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and `third_party/licenses/`.

## Firebase development sandbox

- `.env.local` contains the Firebase **Web** app config used by the browser SDK; `.gitignore` lists this file. The user-supplied Web API key for `motorph-jd` is installed assistant-side. The user does not need to edit `.env.local`.
- The Web API key is a public client identifier, not a server credential. Do not add a service-account key or Admin SDK credentials.
- Authentication uses Email/Password and in-memory browser persistence. Live sign-up/password sign-in and the browser sign-in flow passed with disposable synthetic accounts, which were deleted. Do not use real staff accounts or data.
- Firestore requests are made by the Java backend through the REST API, forwarding the signed-in user's Firebase ID token. Firestore Security Rules authorize those requests; no privileged server identity bypasses the rules.
- The app uses `users/{uid}/demoEmployees`, `demoAttendance`, `demoLeaveRequests`, and `demoTickets`. Workflow documents are owner-scoped with no reviewer or delete permission in the candidate rules. The opt-in seed writes fictional employee/attendance records only.
- The user published the updated `docs/firestore.rules`. Live Firebase smoke testing with disposable accounts verified owner-scoped employee create/update, leave and ticket create/cancel/read-back, and a cross-user denial (`403`). Both disposable Auth accounts and employee documents were deleted; one cancelled synthetic leave and one cancelled synthetic ticket remain under their deleted test UIDs because workflow deletes are intentionally denied (`LV-3502C01F0E60`, `TK-F05DD2B0D6CC`). No real employee data or credentials were used. These are **development-only** rules, not production role/HR policy.
- If Firebase is not configured locally, the app uses the in-memory synthetic fixture. No Firebase writes are made in that mode.
- `measurementId` / Firebase Analytics is not used.
- Browser auth is verified on `localhost`. The current Arena preview host is `8080-is3s38ic4lxn7e4e77g8b.e2b.app`; its authorized-domain status could not be tested from the sandbox because Arena's traffic-access token is injected only in the user preview session. If the preview reports `auth/unauthorized-domain`, add that exact host under Firebase Console → Authentication → Settings → Authorized domains.

See `docs/firebase-setup-guide.md` for the console checkpoint and `docs/firestore.rules` for the development rules.

## What works

- Overview, searchable employee directory/detail, raw attendance register, Requests & tickets, Team roster, HR desk, and the payroll rules gate. Employee details open from a native keyboard-operable button without overriding table semantics; result counts and form feedback use polite status regions.
- Java employee/attendance services plus a workflow service. Local preview workflow records are held in Java process memory; Firebase mode uses the signed-in user’s Firestore subcollections.
- Leave requests and tickets validate inputs, derive employee names from the caller’s own synthetic directory, show documented queue labels, and support owner-sandbox cancellation. A monthly leave-request calendar displays pending/cancelled request dates only; it does not imply approval or leave balances. No reviewer/approval/resolve/delete routes exist. The user has published the rules; live tests confirmed leave and ticket create/cancel persistence, plus cross-user denial.
- Read-only Team roster plus a synthetic directory editor. In Firebase mode, signed-in users can create/edit only name, department, role label, location, and demo status in their own sandbox. Local preview has no user authentication and shares one process-memory store for that API process. IDs are server-generated; delete, termination, schedule, salary, and government-ID fields are not exposed. New records receive no schedule mapping, so their raw attendance view is empty. This is not an HR role or a production employee-admin workflow.
- CSV export for currently visible synthetic employee results, loaded raw attendance rows, and owner-sandbox workflow records. CSV cells are quoted and spreadsheet-formula prefixes are neutralized; exports contain no derived hours or payroll values.
- Server-side employee search/detail and inclusive raw-attendance date filtering for a selected employee. The date fields default to that employee's earliest/latest available records, following the earlier MO-IT108 Requirements Analysis; the user can narrow the range. This is not a payroll-period calendar. No paid hours, deductions, or pay are calculated.
- Firebase email/password sign-in, development-account creation, and password-reset email UI; reset responses do not disclose whether an email has an account. The app stays behind the sign-in gate when Firebase config is complete.
- `/api/health`, employee list/search/detail plus owner-sandbox create/update, raw attendance query, owner-scoped workflow list/create/cancel routes, and opt-in demo seed endpoint.
- Verification: `npm run test:web` passes 16 workflow/calendar/CSV tests; `./test.sh` passes 150 Java checks; `npm run test:e2e` passes the local browser flow for employee create/edit, empty unscheduled attendance, reversed-date rejection, leave/ticket submit/cancel, request-calendar navigation, reload persistence, CSV download, and mobile width; `npm run build` passes; `npm audit` reports 0 vulnerabilities. A disposable-account browser check also passed Firebase sign-in, user-scoped Firestore reads, and sign-out on localhost without Firestore writes. The exact Arena preview-origin sign-in remains unverified.

## Not implemented / important limits

- No production hosting, HR authorization roles, admin controls, audit trail, backup, or production security review. The built-in JDK HTTP server is a learning prototype, not a hardened public service.
- No live employee, attendance, or payroll information. Do not use this prototype for payroll processing.
- No work-hour derivation algorithm, payroll formulas, rates, pay-period calendar, payslips, or payroll calculations. The supplied material does not define a complete attendance algorithm or exact semi-monthly cut-offs, so the program will not infer them.
- Leave/ticket records are persistent only in the signed-in user’s sandbox after the updated rules are published; the current local preview uses process memory. There is no supervisor/reviewer role, real queue delivery, approval, notification, audit trail, team assignment, HR lifecycle editing, attendance import, or approved source-system integration.

function showWorkspace(user) {
  state.user = user;
  resetSessionData();
  authGate.hidden = true;
  appShell.hidden = false;
  document.getElementById('sign-out-button').hidden = !user;
  document.getElementById('operator-label').textContent = user ? 'USER SANDBOX' : 'LOCAL PREVIEW';
  document.getElementById('employee-storage-mode').textContent = user ? 'User-scoped Firestore' : 'Shared local process memory';
  document.getElementById('operator-avatar').textContent = user ? (user.email || 'D').slice(0, 1).toUpperCase() : 'D';
  loadEmployees();
  loadWorkflows();
}

function setWorkflowStorageMode(value) {
  document.getElementById('workflow-storage-mode').textContent = value;

async function loadWorkflows() {
  const status = document.getElementById('workflow-load-status');
  status.hidden = true;
  status.textContent = '';
  setWorkflowStorageMode(state.user ? 'User-scoped Firestore' : 'Local API memory');
  try {
    const response = await fetch('/api/workflows', { headers: await apiHeaders() });
    const payload = await response.json();
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(payload.error || `Request failed (${response.status})`);
    if (!payload || !Array.isArray(payload.leaveRequests) || !Array.isArray(payload.tickets)) {
      throw new Error('Unexpected workflow response.');
    }
    state.workflow = {
      ...createWorkflowState(),
      leaveRequests: payload.leaveRequests,
      tickets: payload.tickets
    };
    setWorkflowStorageMode(payload.storage === 'user-scoped-firestore' ? 'User-scoped Firestore' : 'Local API memory');
    renderWorkflow();
  } catch (error) {
    state.workflow = createWorkflowState();
    renderWorkflow();
    setWorkflowStorageMode(state.user ? 'Rules access required' : 'Local API unavailable');
    status.textContent = error.message || 'Could not load workflow records.';
    status.hidden = false;
  }
}

import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { spawn, execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { mkdtempSync, readdirSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs';
import net from 'node:net';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { chromium } from 'playwright-core';

const projectRoot = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '../..');
const sourceDir = path.join(projectRoot, 'src/main/java/ph/motorph/web');
const gsonJar = path.join(projectRoot, 'lib/gson-2.13.2.jar');
const timeoutMs = 15_000;
const javaClasses = mkdtempSync(path.join(tmpdir(), 'motorph-e2e-classes-'));
const serverChildren = [];
let browser;

function freePort() {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const server = net.createServer();
    server.once('error', reject);
    server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', () => {
      const { port } = server.address();
      server.close(error => error ? reject(error) : resolve(port));
    });
  });
}

function start(command, args, env, label) {
  const child = spawn(command, args, {
    cwd: projectRoot,
    env,
    detached: process.platform !== 'win32',
    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe']
  });
  child.log = '';
  child.on('error', error => { child.log += `${label}: ${error.message}\n`; });
  for (const stream of [child.stdout, child.stderr]) {
    stream.setEncoding('utf8');
    stream.on('data', chunk => { child.log = (child.log + chunk).slice(-8000); });
  }
  serverChildren.push(child);
  return child;
}

async function waitForServer(url, child, label) {
  const end = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  let lastError = 'no response';
  while (Date.now() < end) {
    if (child.exitCode !== null) throw new Error(`${label} exited early.\n${child.log}`);
    try {
      const response = await fetch(url);
      if (response.ok) return response;
      lastError = `HTTP ${response.status}`;
    } catch (error) {
      lastError = error.message;
    }
    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 150));
  }
  throw new Error(`${label} did not become ready (${lastError}).\n${child.log}`);
}

async function stop(child) {
  if (!child || child.exitCode !== null) return;
  try {
    if (process.platform === 'win32') child.kill('SIGTERM');
    else process.kill(-child.pid, 'SIGTERM');
  } catch { /* already stopped */ }
  await Promise.race([
    new Promise(resolve => child.once('exit', resolve)),
    new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 2500))
  ]);
  if (child.exitCode === null) {
    try {
      if (process.platform === 'win32') child.kill('SIGKILL');
      else process.kill(-child.pid, 'SIGKILL');
    } catch { /* already stopped */ }
  }
}

}

function populateWorkflowEmployees() {
  ['leave-employee', 'ticket-employee'].forEach(id => {
    const select = document.getElementById(id);
    const current = select.value;
    select.replaceChildren();
    const placeholder = document.createElement('option');
    placeholder.value = '';
    placeholder.textContent = state.allEmployees.length ? 'Choose synthetic employee' : 'Load directory first';
    select.append(placeholder);
    state.allEmployees.forEach(employee => {
      const option = document.createElement('option');
      option.value = employee.id;
      option.textContent = `${employee.id} — ${employee.name}`;
      select.append(option);
    });
    if (state.allEmployees.some(employee => employee.id === current)) select.value = current;
  });
}

function showWorkflowTableMessage(tbody, columnCount, message) {
  tbody.replaceChildren();
  const row = document.createElement('tr');
  const cell = document.createElement('td');
  cell.colSpan = columnCount;
  cell.className = 'table-message';
  cell.textContent = message;
  row.append(cell);
  tbody.append(row);
}

function makeWorkflowStatus(status) {
  const badge = document.createElement('span');
  badge.className = `status-pill${status === 'Cancelled' ? ' workflow-cancelled' : (status.toLowerCase() === 'active' ? '' : ' leave')}`;
  badge.textContent = status;
  return badge;
}

function makeCancelButton(action, item, employeeId, label) {
  const button = document.createElement('button');
  button.type = 'button';
  button.className = 'button button-quiet workflow-cancel';
  button.dataset.action = action;
  button.dataset.id = item.id;
  button.dataset.employeeId = employeeId;
  button.textContent = label;
  button.setAttribute('aria-label', `${label} ${item.id} for ${item.employeeName}`);
  return button;
}

function renderLeaveCalendar() {
  const tbody = document.getElementById('leave-calendar-grid');
  if (!tbody) return;
  const calendar = buildLeaveCalendar(leaveCalendarMonth, state.workflow.leaveRequests);
  document.getElementById('leave-calendar-month').textContent = calendar.title;
  tbody.replaceChildren();
  calendar.weeks.forEach(week => {
    const row = document.createElement('tr');
    week.forEach(day => {
      const cell = document.createElement('td');
      cell.className = `calendar-day${day.inMonth ? '' : ' outside-month'}${day.isToday ? ' today' : ''}`;
      if (!day.inMonth) {
        cell.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
        row.append(cell);
        return;
      }
      cell.setAttribute('aria-label', `${day.date}${day.requests.length ? `, ${day.requests.length} request date${day.requests.length === 1 ? '' : 's'}` : ''}`);
      const dateNumber = document.createElement('span');
      dateNumber.className = 'calendar-date-number';
      dateNumber.textContent = String(day.day);
      cell.append(dateNumber);
      if (day.requests.length) {
        const list = document.createElement('ul');
        list.className = 'calendar-events';
        day.requests.forEach(request => {
          const event = document.createElement('li');
          event.className = `calendar-event${request.status === 'Cancelled' ? ' cancelled' : ''}`;
          event.textContent = `${request.leaveType} · ${request.status}`;
          event.title = `${request.employeeName} · ${request.employeeId} · request date only`;
          list.append(event);
        });
        cell.append(list);
      }
      row.append(cell);
    });
    tbody.append(row);
  });
}

function renderWorkflow() {
  if (!document.getElementById('leave-request-rows')) return;
  const leaveRows = document.getElementById('leave-request-rows');
  leaveRows.replaceChildren();
  if (!state.workflow.leaveRequests.length) {
    showWorkflowTableMessage(leaveRows, 6, 'No session requests yet.');
  } else {
    state.workflow.leaveRequests.forEach(request => {
      const row = document.createElement('tr');
      [request.id, `${request.employeeName} · ${request.employeeId}`, request.leaveType,
        `${request.startDate} — ${request.endDate}`].forEach(value => row.append(makeCell(value)));
      row.append(makeCell(makeWorkflowStatus(request.status)));
      row.append(makeCell(request.status === 'Pending review'
        ? makeCancelButton('cancel-leave', request, request.employeeId, 'Cancel') : '—'));
      leaveRows.append(row);
    });
  }
  const leaveCount = state.workflow.leaveRequests.length;
  document.getElementById('leave-request-count').textContent = `${leaveCount} ${leaveCount === 1 ? 'request' : 'requests'} in this sandbox`;

  const ticketRows = document.getElementById('ticket-rows');
  ticketRows.replaceChildren();
  if (!state.workflow.tickets.length) {
    showWorkflowTableMessage(ticketRows, 6, 'No session tickets yet.');
  } else {
    state.workflow.tickets.forEach(ticket => {
      const row = document.createElement('tr');
      [ticket.id, `${ticket.employeeName} · ${ticket.employeeId}`, ticket.ticketType, ticket.queue]
        .forEach(value => row.append(makeCell(value)));
      row.append(makeCell(makeWorkflowStatus(ticket.status)));
      row.append(makeCell(ticket.status === 'Open'
        ? makeCancelButton('cancel-ticket', ticket, ticket.employeeId, 'Cancel') : '—'));
      ticketRows.append(row);
    });
  }
  const ticketCount = state.workflow.tickets.length;
  document.getElementById('ticket-count').textContent = `${ticketCount} ${ticketCount === 1 ? 'ticket' : 'tickets'} in this sandbox`;
  document.getElementById('leave-export-button').disabled = leaveCount === 0;
  document.getElementById('ticket-export-button').disabled = ticketCount === 0;
  renderLeaveCalendar();
}

function setWorkflowStorageMode(value) {
  document.getElementById('workflow-storage-mode').textContent = value;
}

async function sendWorkflowRequest(url, body) {
  const headers = await apiHeaders(body === undefined ? {} : { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
  const options = { method: 'POST', headers };
  if (body !== undefined) options.body = JSON.stringify(body);
  const response = await fetch(url, options);
  const payload = await response.json();
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(payload.error || `Request failed (${response.status})`);
  if (!payload || !payload.item) throw new Error('Unexpected workflow response.');
  return payload;
}

async function handleWorkflowCancel(event) {
  const button = event.target.closest('button[data-action]');
  if (!button) return;
  const isLeave = button.dataset.action === 'cancel-leave';
  const formStatus = isLeave ? 'leave-form-status' : 'ticket-form-status';
  const collection = isLeave ? 'leaveRequests' : 'tickets';
  button.disabled = true;
  try {
    const payload = await sendWorkflowRequest(`/api/workflows/${isLeave ? 'leave' : 'tickets'}/${encodeURIComponent(button.dataset.id)}/cancel`);
    applyWorkflowItem(collection, payload.item, payload.storage);
    setWorkflowStatus(formStatus, `${button.dataset.id} cancelled in this user sandbox. No reviewer was notified.`);
  } catch (error) {
    setWorkflowStatus(formStatus, error.message || 'Could not cancel this demo item.', true);
    button.disabled = false;
  }
}

# i-have-adhd

The reader has ADHD. Output is not just brief. It is shaped so an ADHD brain can act on it.

## Persistence

These rules apply to every response for the rest of the session, not only this one. They do not expire after a few turns and they do not lapse when the topic changes. If you are unsure whether they still apply, they do.

Turn them off only when the reader says "stop adhd mode" or "normal mode". Confirm in one line, then return to your default style.

## What ADHD changes about reading

Five facts drive every rule below:

1. Working memory is small. Anything not on screen is forgotten. Do not ask the reader to "keep in mind X."
2. Knowing the answer is not doing the answer. The friction between "got it" and "done it" is where work dies.
3. Starting is the hardest step. The first action must be obvious, small, and doable now.
4. Time estimates feel uniform. "A bit of work" and "a few hours" register the same. Vague estimates fail.
5. Dopamine is scarce. Visible progress matters. Buried wins do not register.

## Rules

### 1. Lead with the next action

The first line is something the reader can do. Not context. Not a plan. The action.

Bad: "Let's think about this. Your auth flow has a few moving pieces..."
Good: "Edit `src/auth.ts:42` to update the token validation."

If the answer is a command, path, or snippet, it goes first. Prose comes after, if at all.

### 2. Number multi-step tasks

If the work takes more than one step, write a numbered list. Each step is one bounded action. No step contains "and then" twice.

Use the fewest steps that still work. Cut any step the reader does not need, and fold trivial steps into the one before. A short path finished beats a complete path abandoned.

Bad: "First open the file, find the function, swap it out, then run the tests."

Good:
```
1. Open `src/auth.ts`
2. Replace `verifyToken` (lines 42 to 58) with the snippet below
3. Run `npm test -- auth.spec.ts`
```

### 3. End with one concrete next action

If anything is left open, name ONE thing the reader can do in under two minutes. Even "open the file" counts.

Bad: "Hope that helps. Let me know if you want to dig deeper."
Good: "Next: run `npm test` and paste the first failing line."

### 4. Suppress tangents

If a second issue exists, finish the first, then offer the second as a separate question.

Bad: "Here's the fix. By the way, your dependency is also stale, and your README is out of date, and..."
Good: "Here's the fix. Separately: there is also a stale dependency. Want me to handle that next?"

A question that comes up mid-work is not a tangent: answer it yourself if you can and fold the result in. If it still needs the reader, surface it once, at the end.

### 5. Restate state every turn

The reader cannot hold "we are on step 3 of 5" between messages. Restate it.

Bad: "Done. Ready for the next part?"
Good: "Step 3 of 5 done: schema updated. Next: backfill the new column. Run the script?"

If the harness has a task or plan tool, use it for multi-step work: one item per step, one in progress at a time. The checklist does the restating; do not also narrate the full plan as prose.

### 6. Give specific time estimates

Vague estimates fail. Ballpark in concrete units.

Bad: "This will take some work."
Good: "About 15 minutes if tests already cover this. An afternoon if not."

### 7. Make completed work visible

Show what now works, in concrete terms. Do not bury wins in a recap.

Bad: "I've made some changes to the auth flow. Among other things..."
Good: "Login now works with magic links. Try: `npm run dev`, open `/login`."

### 8. Matter-of-fact tone for errors

Never use "Uh oh," "Oh no," or "There seems to be a problem." State cause and fix.

Bad: "Uh oh, the test is failing. There seems to be an issue..."
Good: "Test fails at `auth.spec.ts:42`: expected 200, got 401. Cause: missing auth header. Fix: add `Authorization: Bearer ${token}` to the request."

### 9. Cap lists to 5 items

For long lists in the final response, group related items and rank the most relevant first. Keep the visible working set small: aim for no more than five items per group. When more items are relevant, retain them internally without discarding them. Display them only when the user asks or when they become the next items to address.

Never omit relevant items when completeness matters. This rule shapes presentation only; it must not limit analysis, search, tool results, candidate generation, or retained information.

### 10. No preamble, no recap, no closing pleasantries

Forbidden openers: "Great question," "Let me...", "I'll...", "Sure!", "Looking at your...", "To answer your question..."

Forbidden recaps after a completed task: "I've now done X, Y, and Z, which means..."

Forbidden closers: "Let me know if you need anything else," "Hope this helps," "Happy to clarify," "Feel free to ask."

Start with the answer. End when the answer is done.

## When to break the rules

Override the defaults when:

1. User asks to "explain" or "walk me through." Explain fully. Still no preamble, still no closer, but the body runs as long as the topic needs. Add headers so the reader can skim back.
2. Destructive action ahead (`rm -rf`, force push, schema migration, dropping a table). Confirm before acting. Safety wins over brevity.
3. Debug spiral. If the last three turns have been "still broken," stop iterating on code. Name the assumption that might be wrong. Ask one diagnostic question.
4. Real ambiguity in the request. One short clarifying question beats guessing and rewriting.
5. A rule fights the task. When a rule would delete the answer itself, the task wins; the shape stays. Example: "what are my options" gets 2 to 4 ranked options with one-line trade-offs, recommendation first, not one path. The options are the answer.
6. A rule fights the harness. Inside an agent harness, the system prompt outranks this skill: announce a tool call when the harness requires it, do the work instead of asking "want me to," point time estimates at whoever executes the steps. Same principle as 5: the constraint wins, the shape stays.

## Pre-send check

Before sending, delete:

1. The first sentence if it announces what you are about to do.
2. The last sentence if it asks "anything else?" or recaps what just happened.
3. Any "by the way" sidebar.
4. Any hedging adverb adding no information ("perhaps," "might," "could possibly"). Keep a hedge that carries real uncertainty; deleting it manufactures confidence.
5. Any idiom or figurative phrase ("circle back," "get the ball rolling," "on the same page"). Replace with the literal action.

Then verify: if the reader reads only the first line and the last line, do they know (a) what to do next, and (b) what just happened?

If yes, send.

**Structure and flow:** `Main.main()` starts the Swing login. On successful login, `initializeApplication()` constructs a `DataRepository`, loads employees and attendance, then wires `EmployeeService`, `PayrollService`, `ReportService` to their controllers and gives those controllers to `MainFrame`. The view is divided into dashboard, employee, payroll, reports and leave panels. The packages are `controller`, `service`, `model`, `repository`, `dao`, `security`, `leave`, `util` and `view` (including dialogs/renderers).

- `DataRepository` reads employee and attendance CSVs, parses dates/times and builds `Employee`/`AttendanceRecord` objects.
- `EmployeeService` searches and manages employee records and writes employee changes back to CSV; attendance lookup is exposed by date/range methods.
- `PayrollService` selects an employee and period, builds a `PaySlip`, and can generate payroll for all employees. `PayrollProcessor` supplies gross-pay, SSS-table, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG and withholding-tax calculations. `ReportService` builds payslip and weekly/monthly summaries.
- Controllers validate request parameters and delegate to services; Swing panels call controllers.
- The CSV files contain employee details, attendance records and user credentials. The bundled sample files have 35 employee data rows and 5,168 attendance rows (excluding headers); the runtime probe loaded 35 employee rows.

**Caveats:** the repo mixes a reasonably separated architecture with helper/demo code (`EmployeeDAO`, CSV tests and test utilities) that is not obviously part of the main wiring. The leave request classes/panel exist, but the startup wiring shown in `Main` does not construct a `LeaveRequestService` or pass it into the frame. Several test classes are standalone/manual `main` programs, and some use hard-coded Windows paths; the presence of JUnit in the Maven file does not mean the available checks are all JUnit tests. Payroll formulas still need validation against the current approved specification, not merely against code in another folder.

**Course connection:** useful as a CP2 example of Swing + CSV and of separating controllers/services/models/repositories. The course identity is inferred from the source path, not stated in an official README; there is no explicit MS1/MS2 linkage.

## Folder 6 — explicit MO-IT110 MS2 refactor example

**Location:** `6/-/`. Its README names MO-IT110 OOP Milestone 2 and says the project refactors a CP2 Java Swing app into an approved MS1 design. It has 22 production Java files under `src/motorph/`, 10 plain-Java tests under `test/motorph/`, CSV data, CP2 reference outputs, NetBeans metadata and an Ant build file. The declared main class is `motorph.MotorPH`.

**Structure and flow:** `MotorPH` opens `LoginFrame`. UI classes are under `ui/`; the payroll domain is separated into `model/`, `deduction/`, `service/` and `user/`.

1. `CSVDataHandler` loads employees and attendance from CSV and creates model objects.
2. `Employee` is an abstract class; `RegularEmployee` and `ProbationaryEmployee` supply subtype behavior such as allowances.
3. `AttendanceRecord` calculates hours/cutoff membership.
4. `PayrollProcessor` accepts a list of `Deduction` objects (SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG and tax), totals cutoff hours, calculates gross/deductions/net, and creates an immutable `Payslip`.
5. UI frames display employee/payroll results and save payroll CSV output.
6. `User`, `EmployeeUser` and `PayrollStaff` demonstrate authentication/role permissions for the employee-lookup vs staff screens.

The README says the implementation preserves CP2's cutoff behavior and describes how it rounds money, applies deductions and lists allowances. It also cautions that the salary tables/rules were carried from CP2 rather than independently verified against a current MotorPH/government specification. The README reports 167 checks and 0 failures, with CP2 comparison differences on 3 of 476 rows; those are project-reported results, not runs performed in this review.

**Course connection:** direct MS2 relevance by its own README; the code is a concrete example of implementing an approved design, using encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism and a view/backend split. The CP2 source commit and authorship/permission should be confirmed before adopting any code or presenting it as the user's work.

## Folder 7 — Swing/CSV payroll app with unclear submission identity

**Location:** `7/-/src/motorphpayrollsystem/`. There are 35 Java files, NetBeans forms/assets, and bundled OpenCSV, Commons Lang and AbsoluteLayout libraries. There is no README, no course/team label, and no CSV data file in the folder. The project main class is `MotorPHPayrollSystem`.

**Structure and flow:** the main class tries to create `attendance.csv`, loads employee data through `EmployeeData`, and opens `loginUI`. Login looks up an employee row in a CSV and compares a password against column 20. On success it opens `DashboardUI`. `EmployeeData` keeps the CSV rows in a static shared list and offers add/update/delete/profile methods that rewrite the CSV. The UI includes employee dashboard/profile, attendance clock-in/clock-out and history, employee records, admin employee add/update/delete, payroll screens and a bulk-payroll/export screen. `Attendance` and `CSVUtil` provide CSV persistence; `Payroll`, `ContributionCalculator`, `PayrollCalculator` and `PayrollProcessor` contain pay logic; `FullTimeEmployee`/`PartTimeEmployee` and `EmployeeMapper` provide model objects.

**What is only partial or unclear:** `MotorPH_Employee Data.csv`, required by `EmployeeData`, is not included. Attendance data is created as an empty CSV when absent. `LeaveRequest` and `OvertimeRequest` are domain classes, but a search shows no leave-request workflow in the screens; the overtime request model is stored on the processor but not used by its main processing method. The payroll processor's comments describe overtime as a temporary/unfinished path. So the classes indicate intended scope, not proof every listed capability is operational.

**Course connection:** its class hierarchy and UI/backend concepts could be compared to OOP course topics, but no source evidence ties it to a particular MO-IT110 module, MS1 design or user's own submission. It is not self-contained enough to treat as a runnable reference without its expected employee CSV.

## Folder 8 — MO-IT103 Group 18 console + Swing project

**Location:** `8/-/MO-IT103-Group18-master/MO-IT103-Group18-master/`. There are 36 Java files under `Backend/`, `Console/`, `GUI/` and one top-level labels file, plus NetBeans/Ant metadata, JARs and three local CSV datasets (employee details, attendance and credentials). No README is included.

**Two front ends use the data differently:**

- `Console.TACP2` is a terminal workflow: login with employee number/last name; view profile, daily attendance, weekly hours and payroll. It downloads published Google Sheets CSV over HTTP, so it depends on internet access and the sheet schema.
- The Swing UI starts from `GUI.LogIn` and proceeds to `GUI.MainMenu`. It uses the bundled local CSVs and has profile, attendance, payroll, employee table and employee add/update/delete screens.

The `Backend/` package contains employee/attendance records, CSV loading, payroll processors (regular, final-pay and 13th-month variants), statutory deduction calculators, regular/holiday overtime classes, plus leave and payslip-dispute domain classes. The regular payroll processor uses attendance totals and a `Payslip`; deduction types are separate classes. The GUI exposes employee dispute submission and a payroll-side review/resolve/reject frame.

**Caveats:** leave records shown by the GUI are explicitly hard-coded sample rows because there is no leave data file. Payslip disputes live in a singleton in-memory list, not persistent storage, so the records disappear on process exit. The payroll-side dispute frame itself notes role authorization is not implemented. The console path fetches external sheets; the GUI path reads local data—do not confuse them as one identical data flow. This is a CP2-labeled comparison project, not an MS1-approved design by evidence in this folder.

## Folder 9 — documented MO-IT110 Team 3 CP2-to-OOP project

**Location:** `9/-/`. This is the most documented folder: README, old `README.CP2.md`, `SETUP.md`, `oop/NOTES.md`, parity/matrix reports, console/test outputs, a QA workbook, and code. It has 15 Java files in the original GUI `src/`, 13 in `oop/src/` (12 backend classes plus `ConsoleBackendTest`), and 3 test/probe files. The README identifies the OOP work as MO-IT110 OOP Team 3, and identifies the CP2 baseline as MO-IT103 Group 4. Those are source-repository statements, not confirmation of the current user's authorship or reuse permission.

**Two connected source roots:**

- `src/motorphemployee/` is the earlier CP2 Swing app (login, landing screen, dashboard, employee forms, leave screens and related UI). Its data remains in CSV.
- `oop/src/motorphemployee/oop/` is the OOP payroll backend. `Person` → `Employee` → `RegularEmployee`/`ProbationaryEmployee` is the data hierarchy; `GovernmentContributionCalculator` has concrete contribution/tax calculators; `AttendanceLog` models attendance; `PayrollCalculator` coordinates employee + attendance + calculators and produces `PayrollRecord`.
- `ConsoleBackendTest` provides a console test harness before GUI integration. The GUI's `MainMenu`/`Dashboard` were rewired to call the OOP backend rather than compute payroll themselves.
- `AttendanceRepository` loads the real timecard CSV and supplies worked-day data to the payroll flow. `LeaveService` processes approval/rejection and writes the related CSV files; `LeaveForm` still has a separate direct append path noted as an open issue.

package ph.motorph.web;

/** Synthetic leave request stored only in a user's development sandbox. */
public final class DemoLeaveRequest {
    private final String id;
    private final String employeeId;
    private final String employeeName;
    private final String leaveType;
    private final String startDate;
    private final String endDate;
    private final String note;
    private final String status;
    private final String submittedAt;
    private final String cancelledAt;

    public DemoLeaveRequest(String id, String employeeId, String employeeName, String leaveType,
            String startDate, String endDate, String note, String status, String submittedAt, String cancelledAt) {
        this.id = id;
        this.employeeId = employeeId;
        this.employeeName = employeeName;
        this.leaveType = leaveType;
        this.startDate = startDate;
        this.endDate = endDate;
        this.note = note;
        this.status = status;
        this.submittedAt = submittedAt;
        this.cancelledAt = cancelledAt == null ? "" : cancelledAt;
    }

    public DemoLeaveRequest cancelled(String timestamp) {
        return new DemoLeaveRequest(id, employeeId, employeeName, leaveType, startDate, endDate,
            note, "Cancelled", submittedAt, timestamp);
    }

    public String getId() { return id; }
    public String getEmployeeId() { return employeeId; }
    public String getEmployeeName() { return employeeName; }
    public String getLeaveType() { return leaveType; }
    public String getStartDate() { return startDate; }
    public String getEndDate() { return endDate; }
    public String getNote() { return note; }
    public String getStatus() { return status; }
    public String getSubmittedAt() { return submittedAt; }
    public String getCancelledAt() { return cancelledAt; }
}
package ph.motorph.web;

/** Synthetic help-desk ticket stored only in a user's development sandbox. */
public final class DemoTicket {
    private final String id;
    private final String employeeId;
    private final String employeeName;
    private final String ticketType;
    private final String queue;
    private final String summary;
    private final String status;
    private final String submittedAt;
    private final String cancelledAt;

    public DemoTicket(String id, String employeeId, String employeeName, String ticketType, String queue,
            String summary, String status, String submittedAt, String cancelledAt) {
        this.id = id;
        this.employeeId = employeeId;
        this.employeeName = employeeName;
        this.ticketType = ticketType;
        this.queue = queue;
        this.summary = summary;
        this.status = status;
        this.submittedAt = submittedAt;
        this.cancelledAt = cancelledAt == null ? "" : cancelledAt;
    }

    public DemoTicket cancelled(String timestamp) {
        return new DemoTicket(id, employeeId, employeeName, ticketType, queue, summary,
            "Cancelled", submittedAt, timestamp);
    }

    public String getId() { return id; }
    public String getEmployeeId() { return employeeId; }
    public String getEmployeeName() { return employeeName; }
    public String getTicketType() { return ticketType; }
    public String getQueue() { return queue; }
    public String getSummary() { return summary; }
    public String getStatus() { return status; }
    public String getSubmittedAt() { return submittedAt; }
    public String getCancelledAt() { return cancelledAt; }
}
package ph.motorph.web;

import com.google.gson.JsonElement;
import com.google.gson.JsonObject;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Comparator;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.NoSuchElementException;

/** Firestore user-subcollection adapter. Firestore Rules enforce owner-only access. */
public final class FirestoreWorkflowStore implements WorkflowStore {
    private static final String LEAVE_COLLECTION = "demoLeaveRequests";
    private static final String TICKET_COLLECTION = "demoTickets";
    private final FirestoreRestClient client;

    public FirestoreWorkflowStore(FirestoreRestClient client) {
        if (client == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("client must not be null");
        this.client = client;
    }

    @Override
    public List<DemoLeaveRequest> listLeaveRequests() {
        List<DemoLeaveRequest> requests = new ArrayList<>();
        for (JsonObject document : client.listDocuments(client.userCollection(LEAVE_COLLECTION))) {
            requests.add(leaveFromDocument(document));
        }
        requests.sort(Comparator.comparing(DemoLeaveRequest::getSubmittedAt).reversed());
        return requests;
    }

    @Override
    public DemoLeaveRequest createLeaveRequest(DemoLeaveRequest request) {
        if (!client.createDocument(client.userCollection(LEAVE_COLLECTION), request.getId(), leaveFields(request))) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Request ID already exists; try submitting again.");
        }
        return request;
    }

    @Override
    public DemoLeaveRequest cancelLeaveRequest(String id, String cancelledAt) {
        DemoLeaveRequest current = listLeaveRequests().stream().filter(item -> item.getId().equals(id)).findFirst()
            .orElseThrow(() -> new NoSuchElementException("Leave request was not found in this user sandbox."));
        if (!"Pending review".equals(current.getStatus())) throw new IllegalStateException("Only a pending leave request can be cancelled.");
        JsonObject fields = new JsonObject();
        fields.add("status", stringField("Cancelled"));
        fields.add("cancelledAt", timestampField(cancelledAt));
        if (!client.updateDocument(client.userCollection(LEAVE_COLLECTION), id, fields,
            java.util.Arrays.asList("status", "cancelledAt"))) {
            throw new NoSuchElementException("Leave request was not found in this user sandbox.");
        }
        return current.cancelled(cancelledAt);
    }

    @Override
    public List<DemoTicket> listTickets() {
        List<DemoTicket> tickets = new ArrayList<>();
        for (JsonObject document : client.listDocuments(client.userCollection(TICKET_COLLECTION))) {
            tickets.add(ticketFromDocument(document));
        }
        tickets.sort(Comparator.comparing(DemoTicket::getSubmittedAt).reversed());
        return tickets;
    }

    @Override
    public DemoTicket createTicket(DemoTicket ticket) {
        if (!client.createDocument(client.userCollection(TICKET_COLLECTION), ticket.getId(), ticketFields(ticket))) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Ticket ID already exists; try submitting again.");
        }
        return ticket;
    }

    @Override
    public DemoTicket cancelTicket(String id, String cancelledAt) {
        DemoTicket current = listTickets().stream().filter(item -> item.getId().equals(id)).findFirst()
            .orElseThrow(() -> new NoSuchElementException("Ticket was not found in this user sandbox."));
        if (!"Open".equals(current.getStatus())) throw new IllegalStateException("Only an open ticket can be cancelled.");
        JsonObject fields = new JsonObject();
        fields.add("status", stringField("Cancelled"));
        fields.add("cancelledAt", timestampField(cancelledAt));
        if (!client.updateDocument(client.userCollection(TICKET_COLLECTION), id, fields,
            java.util.Arrays.asList("status", "cancelledAt"))) {
            throw new NoSuchElementException("Ticket was not found in this user sandbox.");
        }
        return current.cancelled(cancelledAt);
    }

    private static JsonObject leaveFields(DemoLeaveRequest request) {
        JsonObject fields = new JsonObject();
        fields.add("id", stringField(request.getId()));
        fields.add("employeeId", stringField(request.getEmployeeId()));
        fields.add("employeeName", stringField(request.getEmployeeName()));
        fields.add("leaveType", stringField(request.getLeaveType()));
        fields.add("startDate", stringField(request.getStartDate()));
        fields.add("endDate", stringField(request.getEndDate()));
        fields.add("note", stringField(request.getNote()));
        fields.add("status", stringField(request.getStatus()));
        fields.add("submittedAt", timestampField(request.getSubmittedAt()));
        return fields;
    }

    private static JsonObject ticketFields(DemoTicket ticket) {
        JsonObject fields = new JsonObject();
        fields.add("id", stringField(ticket.getId()));
        fields.add("employeeId", stringField(ticket.getEmployeeId()));
        fields.add("employeeName", stringField(ticket.getEmployeeName()));
        fields.add("ticketType", stringField(ticket.getTicketType()));
        fields.add("queue", stringField(ticket.getQueue()));
        fields.add("summary", stringField(ticket.getSummary()));
        fields.add("status", stringField(ticket.getStatus()));
        fields.add("submittedAt", timestampField(ticket.getSubmittedAt()));
        return fields;
    }

    private static DemoLeaveRequest leaveFromDocument(JsonObject document) {
        JsonObject fields = fields(document);
        return new DemoLeaveRequest(documentId(document), value(fields, "employeeId"), value(fields, "employeeName"),
            value(fields, "leaveType"), value(fields, "startDate"), value(fields, "endDate"), value(fields, "note"),
            value(fields, "status"), dateTimeValue(fields, "submittedAt"), dateTimeValue(fields, "cancelledAt"));
    }

    private static DemoTicket ticketFromDocument(JsonObject document) {
        JsonObject fields = fields(document);
        return new DemoTicket(documentId(document), value(fields, "employeeId"), value(fields, "employeeName"),
            value(fields, "ticketType"), value(fields, "queue"), value(fields, "summary"), value(fields, "status"),
            dateTimeValue(fields, "submittedAt"), dateTimeValue(fields, "cancelledAt"));
    }

    private static JsonObject fields(JsonObject document) {
        return document.has("fields") && document.get("fields").isJsonObject()
            ? document.getAsJsonObject("fields") : new JsonObject();
    }

    private static String documentId(JsonObject document) {
        String name = document.has("name") ? document.get("name").getAsString() : "";
        int slash = name.lastIndexOf('/');
        if (slash < 0 || slash == name.length() - 1) throw new IllegalStateException("Firestore workflow document has no ID.");
        return name.substring(slash + 1);
    }

    private static String value(JsonObject fields, String name) {
        JsonElement element = fields.get(name);
        if (element == null || !element.isJsonObject()) return "";
        JsonObject typed = element.getAsJsonObject();
        if (typed.has("stringValue")) return typed.get("stringValue").getAsString();
        if (typed.has("timestampValue")) return typed.get("timestampValue").getAsString();
        return "";
    }

    private static String dateTimeValue(JsonObject fields, String name) {
        return fields.has(name) ? value(fields, name) : "";
    }

    private static JsonObject stringField(String value) {
        JsonObject field = new JsonObject();
        field.addProperty("stringValue", value);
        return field;
    }

    private static JsonObject timestampField(String value) {
        JsonObject field = new JsonObject();
        field.addProperty("timestampValue", value);
        return field;
    }
}
package ph.motorph.web;

import java.time.Instant;
import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.time.format.DateTimeParseException;
import java.util.Arrays;
import java.util.Collections;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Locale;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.NoSuchElementException;
import java.util.UUID;

/** Validates and coordinates safe, non-payroll workflow demonstrations. */
public final class WorkflowService {
    private static final int MAX_TEXT_LENGTH = 240;
    private static final List<String> LEAVE_TYPES = Collections.unmodifiableList(
        Arrays.asList("Vacation", "Medical", "Personal", "Unpaid"));
    private static final Map<String, String> TICKET_QUEUES;
    static {
        Map<String, String> queues = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        queues.put("Overtime request", "Team Lead");
        queues.put("Leave request", "Team Lead");
        queues.put("Timesheet correction", "Team Lead");
        queues.put("Payroll inquiry", "Payroll Staff");
        queues.put("HR inquiry", "HR");
        queues.put("Technical support", "IT Admin");
        TICKET_QUEUES = Collections.unmodifiableMap(queues);
    }

    private final EmployeeService employeeService;
    private final WorkflowStore store;

    public WorkflowService(EmployeeService employeeService, WorkflowStore store) {
        if (employeeService == null || store == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("workflow dependencies must not be null");
        this.employeeService = employeeService;
        this.store = store;
    }

    public List<DemoLeaveRequest> listLeaveRequests() { return store.listLeaveRequests(); }
    public List<DemoTicket> listTickets() { return store.listTickets(); }

    public DemoLeaveRequest createLeaveRequest(String employeeId, String leaveType,
            String startDate, String endDate, String note) {
        Employee employee = requireEmployee(employeeId);
        if (!LEAVE_TYPES.contains(leaveType)) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Choose a valid leave type.");
        LocalDate start = parseDate(startDate, "start date");
        LocalDate end = parseDate(endDate, "end date");
        if (start.isAfter(end)) throw new IllegalArgumentException("The start date must be on or before the end date.");
        String safeNote = optionalText(note, "Note");
        String id = "LV-" + randomSuffix();
        return store.createLeaveRequest(new DemoLeaveRequest(id, employee.getId(), employee.getName(), leaveType,
            start.toString(), end.toString(), safeNote, "Pending review", Instant.now().toString(), ""));
    }

    public DemoLeaveRequest cancelLeaveRequest(String id) {
        requireId(id, "LV-");
        return store.cancelLeaveRequest(id, Instant.now().toString());
    }

    public DemoTicket createTicket(String employeeId, String ticketType, String summary) {
        Employee employee = requireEmployee(employeeId);
        String queue = TICKET_QUEUES.get(ticketType);
        if (queue == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Choose a valid ticket type.");
        String safeSummary = requiredText(summary, "Message");
        String id = "TK-" + randomSuffix();
        return store.createTicket(new DemoTicket(id, employee.getId(), employee.getName(), ticketType, queue,
            safeSummary, "Open", Instant.now().toString(), ""));
    }

    public DemoTicket cancelTicket(String id) {
        requireId(id, "TK-");
        return store.cancelTicket(id, Instant.now().toString());
    }

    private Employee requireEmployee(String employeeId) {
        String id = requiredText(employeeId, "Employee ID");
        return employeeService.findEmployee(id).orElseThrow(() ->
            new NoSuchElementException("Choose an employee from your synthetic demo directory."));
    }

    private static LocalDate parseDate(String value, String field) {
        String text = requiredText(value, field);
        try {
            LocalDate date = LocalDate.parse(text);
            if (!date.toString().equals(text)) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Enter a valid YYYY-MM-DD " + field + ".");
            return date;
        } catch (DateTimeParseException ex) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Enter a valid YYYY-MM-DD " + field + ".");
        }
    }

    private static String requiredText(String value, String field) {
        String text = value == null ? "" : value.trim();
        if (text.isEmpty()) throw new IllegalArgumentException(field + " is required.");
        if (text.length() > MAX_TEXT_LENGTH) throw new IllegalArgumentException(field + " must be " + MAX_TEXT_LENGTH + " characters or fewer.");
        return text;
    }

package ph.motorph.web;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.NoSuchElementException;

/** Process-memory store used only by the unauthenticated local synthetic preview. */
public final class InMemoryWorkflowStore implements WorkflowStore {
    private final Map<String, DemoLeaveRequest> leaveRequests = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    private final Map<String, DemoTicket> tickets = new LinkedHashMap<>();

    @Override
    public synchronized List<DemoLeaveRequest> listLeaveRequests() {
        return new ArrayList<>(leaveRequests.values());
    }

    @Override
    public synchronized DemoLeaveRequest createLeaveRequest(DemoLeaveRequest request) {
        if (leaveRequests.containsKey(request.getId())) throw new IllegalStateException("Request ID already exists.");
        leaveRequests.put(request.getId(), request);
        return request;
    }

    @Override
    public synchronized DemoLeaveRequest cancelLeaveRequest(String id, String cancelledAt) {
        DemoLeaveRequest existing = leaveRequests.get(id);
        if (existing == null) throw new NoSuchElementException("Leave request was not found.");
        if (!"Pending review".equals(existing.getStatus())) throw new IllegalStateException("Only a pending leave request can be cancelled.");
        DemoLeaveRequest cancelled = existing.cancelled(cancelledAt);
        leaveRequests.put(id, cancelled);
        return cancelled;
    }

    @Override
    public synchronized List<DemoTicket> listTickets() {
        return new ArrayList<>(tickets.values());
    }

    @Override
    public synchronized DemoTicket createTicket(DemoTicket ticket) {
        if (tickets.containsKey(ticket.getId())) throw new IllegalStateException("Ticket ID already exists.");
        tickets.put(ticket.getId(), ticket);
        return ticket;
    }

    @Override
    public synchronized DemoTicket cancelTicket(String id, String cancelledAt) {
        DemoTicket existing = tickets.get(id);
        if (existing == null) throw new NoSuchElementException("Ticket was not found.");
        if (!"Open".equals(existing.getStatus())) throw new IllegalStateException("Only an open ticket can be cancelled.");
        DemoTicket cancelled = existing.cancelled(cancelledAt);
        tickets.put(id, cancelled);
        return cancelled;
    }
}
