[NODE 4134]
38-### Attendance read-only model
39-
40-The supplied Data Dictionary lists these Attendance fields:
41-
42-- `attendanceID` — integer primary key;
43:- `scheduleID` — foreign key;
44:- `date` — date, unique in combination with `scheduleID`;
45-- `timeIn` and `timeOut` — time values, with the source check `timeIn <= timeOut`;
46-- `dayType` — enum, with members not specified.
47-
48:The prototype maps these to `AttendanceRecord` and validates positive synthetic identifiers, required values, `timeIn <= timeOut`, and unique `(scheduleID, date)` entries. A minimal employee-to-schedule mapping allows records to be viewed for an employee. The screen provides read-only inclusive date filtering and, following the older MO-IT108 Requirements Analysis, defaults to the selected employee's earliest/latest available record dates. This is a view convenience, not a claimed payroll-period calendar. `dayType` is shown as `DEMO`, not as an official enum value. No work hours, overtime, paid leave, undertime, or pay values are derived.
49-
50:The database-design PDF also describes attendance as tied to Schedule and the DFD routes attendance through Schedule and Time Tracking, then Timesheet Validation. The exact source/import mechanism and MS2 workflow are not asserted by this read-only fixture.
51-
52-### Payroll and payslip fields
53-
54-The source set names payroll components and storage fields, including:
55-
56-- `Payroll`: employee, wage/rebate/summary IDs, month, PTO maximum, hourly/daily/monthly rates, net pay;
57-- `Payslip`: payroll ID, period start/end, regular/overtime/holiday-overtime/PTO/undertime hours, worked days/holidays/rest days, gross income;
58-- `Earnings`: overtime/PTO/holiday/rest-day pay, subsidies/stipends, other incentives, total benefits;
59-- `Deductibles`, `Other Transactions`, `Government Deductibles`, `Contributions`, `Government Tally`, and `Summary` for deduction and contribution amounts/totals.
60-
61-The DFD labels Timesheet Validation, Leave Monetisation, Wage and Adjustments, Government Deductibles, Basic Payroll Computation, Payslip Generation & Distribution, and Monthly Summary Compilation. These descriptions establish the concept names and broad flow, not their exact computation.
62-
63-## Unresolved source conflicts kept open
64-
65-The PDFs disagree on several schema details. The prototype has not chosen a definitive production schema for these:
66-
67:- `Schedule.restDay SET` versus `Schedule.restDayID` plus a separate Rest Day table;
68-- direct Employee `departmentID` / `governmentID` versus deriving department via Position and linking Government via `Government.employeeID`;
69-- Address region stored directly versus derived through City;
70-- presence of `Supervisor.departmentID`;
71:- presence of `Leave.scheduleID`;
72-- key/version fields for Rates and Government Tally;
73-- some Holiday uniqueness and relationship-matrix cardinalities.
74-
75-See Sections 16 and 17 of the full synthesis for the complete discrepancies.
76-
77-## Payroll-rule status
78-
79-The source documents do **not** supply the arithmetic formula or current effective values for gross pay, salary conversion, overtime, holiday/rest-day rates, undertime, paid leave, leave monetisation, SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, withholding tax, deductions, net pay, or rounding. They also do not provide an authoritative worked payslip example. The payroll screen therefore remains intentionally disabled. The nine GitHub submissions' formulas/tests are comparison evidence only, not a policy authority.
80-
81-## Scope boundary
82-
83-MO-IT107's DFD/database design is broad (five actors; employee management, payroll processing, and archival; PII approval intent; many database tables). The current project begins as a narrow web-based Java/OOP slice. Do not add every actor, all tables, two-person PII workflow, monthly reports, or archive deletion unless the active MO-IT110 milestone explicitly requires it. Keep such items traceable to the source and clearly labelled reference-only until scope is confirmed.

# Roadmap to full peer-level MotorPH feature parity

**How to read “100%”:** the nine submitted folders do not share one feature set, so there is no single objective peer-completion percentage. This roadmap uses the richest relevant comparison: the payroll/attendance/leave workflows in the stronger MO-IT110-style submissions (especially folders 6 and 9), plus the user's earlier MO-IT108 Requirements Analysis and System Design. It is a feature-completion target, not a grade.

**Current user constraints remain in force:** synthetic data only; no payroll calculations until authoritative rules are provided; no guessed pay-period calendar; no Firebase Console changes by the assistant. The legacy Terminal Assessment proposal contains template placeholders and is not treated as a detailed specification. `The Code.pdf` is unrelated C++ inventory work and is excluded.

## Practical progression and ownership

This is the shortest safe path from the current prototype to a complete **approved-scope course project**. It does not mean production payroll readiness or guessed business rules.

function renderAttendance(records) {
  state.rawAttendance = [...records].sort((a, b) => String(a.date).localeCompare(String(b.date)));
  const orderedRecords = state.rawAttendance;
  document.getElementById('attendance-export-button').disabled = orderedRecords.length === 0;
  applyDefaultAttendanceRange(orderedRecords);
  renderRawAttendanceSummary(orderedRecords);
  attendanceRows.replaceChildren();
  if (orderedRecords.length === 0) {
    showAttendanceMessage('No attendance entries match this employee and date range.');
  } else {
    orderedRecords.forEach(record => {
      const row = document.createElement('tr');
      [record.date, String(record.attendanceId), String(record.scheduleId), record.timeIn, record.timeOut, record.dayType]
        .forEach(value => row.append(makeCell(value)));
      attendanceRows.append(row);
    });
  }
  attendanceResultCount.textContent = `${orderedRecords.length} raw ${orderedRecords.length === 1 ? 'entry' : 'entries'} loaded`;
}

async function loadAttendance() {
  const employeeId = attendanceEmployee.value;
  if (!employeeId) {
    state.rawAttendance = [];
    renderRawAttendanceSummary([]);
    document.getElementById('attendance-export-button').disabled = true;
    showAttendanceMessage('Load the employee directory first.');
    attendanceResultCount.textContent = 'No records loaded';
    return;
  }
  const requestNumber = ++state.attendanceRequestNumber;
  state.rawAttendance = [];
  renderRawAttendanceSummary([]);
  document.getElementById('attendance-export-button').disabled = true;
  showAttendanceMessage('Loading raw attendance records…');
  attendanceResultCount.textContent = 'Loading';
  const params = new URLSearchParams({ employeeId });
  const from = attendanceFrom.value;
  const to = attendanceTo.value;
  if (from) params.set('from', from);
  if (to) params.set('to', to);
  try {
    const response = await fetch(`/api/attendance?${params.toString()}`, { headers: await apiHeaders() });
    const payload = await response.json();
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(payload.error || `Request failed (${response.status})`);
    if (requestNumber !== state.attendanceRequestNumber) return;
    renderAttendance(Array.isArray(payload.items) ? payload.items : []);
  } catch (error) {
    if (requestNumber !== state.attendanceRequestNumber) return;
    state.rawAttendance = [];
    renderRawAttendanceSummary([]);
    document.getElementById('attendance-export-button').disabled = true;
    showAttendanceMessage(error.message || 'Could not load attendance records.');
    attendanceResultCount.textContent = 'Could not load records';
  }
}

function renderAttendanceReport(items) {
  state.attendanceReport = items;
  const rows = document.getElementById('attendance-report-rows');
  rows.replaceChildren();
  if (!items.length) {
    showWorkflowTableMessage(rows, 6, 'No synthetic employees are available for this report.');
  } else {
    items.forEach(item => {
      const row = document.createElement('tr');
      row.append(makeCell(`${item.employeeName} · ${item.employeeId}`));
      row.append(makeCell(item.hasScheduleMapping ? `Schedule ${item.scheduleId}` : 'No mapping'));
      row.append(makeCell(String(item.rawRecordCount)));
      row.append(makeCell(item.firstRecordDate || '—'));
      row.append(makeCell(item.lastRecordDate || '—'));
      if (item.hasScheduleMapping) {
        const openButton = document.createElement('button');
        openButton.type = 'button';
        openButton.className = 'button button-quiet workflow-report-open';
        openButton.dataset.employeeId = item.employeeId;
        openButton.textContent = 'View rows';
        openButton.setAttribute('aria-label', `View raw entries for ${item.employeeId}`);
        row.append(makeCell(openButton));
      } else {
        row.append(makeCell('—'));
      }
      rows.append(row);
    });
  }
  const totalRawRows = items.reduce((total, item) => total + (Number.isInteger(item.rawRecordCount) ? item.rawRecordCount : 0), 0);
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-count').textContent = `${items.length} employee ${items.length === 1 ? 'row' : 'rows'} · ${totalRawRows} raw ${totalRawRows === 1 ? 'record' : 'records'} in range`;
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-export').disabled = items.length === 0;
}

async function loadAttendanceReport() {
  const requestNumber = ++state.reportRequestNumber;
  const status = document.getElementById('attendance-report-status');
  status.hidden = true;
  status.textContent = '';
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-count').textContent = 'Loading report';
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-export').disabled = true;
  showWorkflowTableMessage(document.getElementById('attendance-report-rows'), 6, 'Loading raw attendance summary…');
  const params = new URLSearchParams();
  const from = document.getElementById('attendance-report-from').value;
  const to = document.getElementById('attendance-report-to').value;
  if (from) params.set('from', from);
  if (to) params.set('to', to);
  const query = params.toString();
  try {
    const response = await fetch(`/api/reports/attendance${query ? `?${query}` : ''}`, { headers: await apiHeaders() });
    const payload = await response.json();
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(payload.error || `Request failed (${response.status})`);
    if (!payload || !Array.isArray(payload.items) || payload.hoursCalculated !== false) {
      throw new Error('Unexpected attendance report response.');
    }
    if (requestNumber !== state.reportRequestNumber) return;
    renderAttendanceReport(payload.items);
    status.textContent = 'Loaded raw record counts and date coverage only; no hours or payroll values were calculated.';
    status.hidden = false;
  } catch (error) {
    if (requestNumber !== state.reportRequestNumber) return;
    state.attendanceReport = [];
    showWorkflowTableMessage(document.getElementById('attendance-report-rows'), 6, error.message || 'Could not load the raw attendance report.');
    document.getElementById('attendance-report-count').textContent = 'Could not load report';
    document.getElementById('attendance-report-export').disabled = true;
    status.textContent = error.message || 'Could not load the raw attendance report.';
    status.hidden = false;
  }
}

const serverChildren = [];

function freePort() {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const server = net.createServer();
    server.once('error', reject);
    server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', () => {
      const { port } = server.address();
      server.close(error => error ? reject(error) : resolve(port));
    });
  });
}

function start(command, args, env, label) {
  const child = spawn(command, args, {
    cwd: projectRoot,
    env,
    detached: process.platform !== 'win32',
    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe']
  });
  child.log = '';
  child.on('error', error => { child.log += `${label}: ${error.message}\n`; });
  for (const stream of [child.stdout, child.stderr]) {
    stream.setEncoding('utf8');
    stream.on('data', chunk => { child.log = (child.log + chunk).slice(-8000); });
  }
  serverChildren.push(child);
  return child;
}

async function waitForServer(url, child, label) {
  const end = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  let lastError = 'no response';
  while (Date.now() < end) {
    if (child.exitCode !== null) throw new Error(`${label} exited early.\n${child.log}`);
    try {
      const response = await fetch(url);
      if (response.ok) return response;
      lastError = `HTTP ${response.status}`;
    } catch (error) {
      lastError = error.message;
    }
    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 150));
  }
  throw new Error(`${label} did not become ready (${lastError}).\n${child.log}`);
}

function setWorkflowStatus(id, message, error = false) {
  const element = document.getElementById(id);
  element.textContent = message;
  element.classList.toggle('workflow-error', error);
  element.classList.toggle('workflow-success', Boolean(message) && !error);
}

function showAttendanceMessage(message) {
    attendanceResultCount.textContent = 'Could not load records';
  }
}

function renderAttendanceReport(items) {
  state.attendanceReport = items;
  const rows = document.getElementById('attendance-report-rows');
  rows.replaceChildren();
  if (!items.length) {
    showWorkflowTableMessage(rows, 6, 'No synthetic employees are available for this report.');
  } else {
    items.forEach(item => {
      const row = document.createElement('tr');
      row.append(makeCell(`${item.employeeName} · ${item.employeeId}`));
      row.append(makeCell(item.hasScheduleMapping ? `Schedule ${item.scheduleId}` : 'No mapping'));
      row.append(makeCell(String(item.rawRecordCount)));
      row.append(makeCell(item.firstRecordDate || '—'));
      row.append(makeCell(item.lastRecordDate || '—'));
      if (item.hasScheduleMapping) {
        const openButton = document.createElement('button');
        openButton.type = 'button';
        openButton.className = 'button button-quiet workflow-report-open';
        openButton.dataset.employeeId = item.employeeId;
        openButton.textContent = 'View rows';
        openButton.setAttribute('aria-label', `View raw entries for ${item.employeeId}`);
        row.append(makeCell(openButton));
      } else {
        row.append(makeCell('—'));
      }
      rows.append(row);
    });
  }
  const totalRawRows = items.reduce((total, item) => total + (Number.isInteger(item.rawRecordCount) ? item.rawRecordCount : 0), 0);
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-count').textContent = `${items.length} employee ${items.length === 1 ? 'row' : 'rows'} · ${totalRawRows} raw ${totalRawRows === 1 ? 'record' : 'records'} in range`;
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-export').disabled = items.length === 0;
}

async function loadAttendanceReport() {
  const requestNumber = ++state.reportRequestNumber;
  const status = document.getElementById('attendance-report-status');
  status.hidden = true;
  status.textContent = '';
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-count').textContent = 'Loading report';
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-export').disabled = true;
  showWorkflowTableMessage(document.getElementById('attendance-report-rows'), 6, 'Loading raw attendance summary…');
  const params = new URLSearchParams();
  const from = document.getElementById('attendance-report-from').value;
  const to = document.getElementById('attendance-report-to').value;
  if (from) params.set('from', from);
  if (to) params.set('to', to);
  const query = params.toString();
  try {
    const response = await fetch(`/api/reports/attendance${query ? `?${query}` : ''}`, { headers: await apiHeaders() });
    const payload = await response.json();
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(payload.error || `Request failed (${response.status})`);
    if (!payload || !Array.isArray(payload.items) || payload.hoursCalculated !== false) {
      throw new Error('Unexpected attendance report response.');
    }
    if (requestNumber !== state.reportRequestNumber) return;
    renderAttendanceReport(payload.items);
    status.textContent = 'Loaded raw record counts and date coverage only; no hours or payroll values were calculated.';
    status.hidden = false;
  } catch (error) {
    if (requestNumber !== state.reportRequestNumber) return;
    state.attendanceReport = [];
    showWorkflowTableMessage(document.getElementById('attendance-report-rows'), 6, error.message || 'Could not load the raw attendance report.');
    document.getElementById('attendance-report-count').textContent = 'Could not load report';
    document.getElementById('attendance-report-export').disabled = true;
    status.textContent = error.message || 'Could not load the raw attendance report.';
    status.hidden = false;
  }
}

function directoryLabelSummaryRows(employees) {
  const counts = new Map();
  employees.forEach(employee => {
    [['Status label', employee.status], ['Department label', employee.department]].forEach(([category, label]) => {
      const key = `${category}\u0000${label}`;
      counts.set(key, (counts.get(key) || 0) + 1);
    });
  });
  return [...counts.entries()]
    .map(([key, count]) => {
      const [category, label] = key.split('\u0000');
      return { category, label, employeeRecords: count };
    })
    .sort((a, b) => a.category.localeCompare(b.category) || a.label.localeCompare(b.label));
}

const WEEKDAYS = ['Monday', 'Tuesday', 'Wednesday', 'Thursday', 'Friday', 'Saturday', 'Sunday'];
const MONTH_FORMAT = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en', { month: 'long', year: 'numeric' });

function dateKey(year, monthIndex, day) {
  return `${String(year).padStart(4, '0')}-${String(monthIndex + 1).padStart(2, '0')}-${String(day).padStart(2, '0')}`;
}

function validIsoDate(value) {
  if (typeof value !== 'string' || !/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(value)) return false;
  const [year, month, day] = value.split('-').map(Number);
  const parsed = new Date(year, month - 1, day);
  return parsed.getFullYear() === year && parsed.getMonth() === month - 1 && parsed.getDate() === day;
}

/** Build a display-only month view of submitted request ranges; this is not an approved leave calendar. */
export function buildLeaveCalendar(monthDate, requests = [], today = new Date()) {
  if (!(monthDate instanceof Date) || Number.isNaN(monthDate.getTime())) {
    throw new TypeError('A valid month date is required.');
  }
  if (!Array.isArray(requests)) throw new TypeError('Requests must be an array.');

  const year = monthDate.getFullYear();
  const monthIndex = monthDate.getMonth();
  const daysInMonth = new Date(year, monthIndex + 1, 0).getDate();
  const mondayOffset = (new Date(year, monthIndex, 1).getDay() + 6) % 7;
  const todayKey = today instanceof Date && !Number.isNaN(today.getTime())
    ? dateKey(today.getFullYear(), today.getMonth(), today.getDate()) : '';

  const validRequests = requests.filter(request => request
    && validIsoDate(request.startDate)
    && validIsoDate(request.endDate)
    && request.startDate <= request.endDate);

  const cells = Array.from({ length: 42 }, (_, index) => {
    const day = index - mondayOffset + 1;
    const inMonth = day >= 1 && day <= daysInMonth;
    const key = inMonth ? dateKey(year, monthIndex, day) : '';
    const dayRequests = inMonth ? validRequests.filter(request => request.startDate <= key && key <= request.endDate) : [];
    return {
      date: key,
      day: inMonth ? day : null,
      inMonth,
      isToday: Boolean(key && key === todayKey),
      requests: dayRequests
    };
  });

  return {
    title: MONTH_FORMAT.format(new Date(year, monthIndex, 1)),
    weekdays: WEEKDAYS.slice(),
    weeks: Array.from({ length: 6 }, (_, index) => cells.slice(index * 7, index * 7 + 7))
  };
}

function renderLeaveCalendar() {
  const tbody = document.getElementById('leave-calendar-grid');
  if (!tbody) return;
  const calendar = buildLeaveCalendar(leaveCalendarMonth, state.workflow.leaveRequests);
  document.getElementById('leave-calendar-month').textContent = calendar.title;
  tbody.replaceChildren();
  calendar.weeks.forEach(week => {
    const row = document.createElement('tr');
    week.forEach(day => {
      const cell = document.createElement('td');
      cell.className = `calendar-day${day.inMonth ? '' : ' outside-month'}${day.isToday ? ' today' : ''}`;
      if (!day.inMonth) {
        cell.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
        row.append(cell);
        return;
      }
      cell.setAttribute('aria-label', `${day.date}${day.requests.length ? `, ${day.requests.length} request date${day.requests.length === 1 ? '' : 's'}` : ''}`);
      const dateNumber = document.createElement('span');
      dateNumber.className = 'calendar-date-number';
      dateNumber.textContent = String(day.day);
      cell.append(dateNumber);
      if (day.requests.length) {
        const list = document.createElement('ul');
        list.className = 'calendar-events';
        day.requests.forEach(request => {

[NODE 4269]
export function filterWorkflowItems(items, { query = '', status = '', searchFields = [] } = {}) {
  if (!Array.isArray(items)) return [];
  const needle = String(query || '').trim().toLowerCase();
  const selectedStatus = String(status || '').trim();
  const fields = Array.isArray(searchFields) ? searchFields : [];
  return items.filter(item => {
    if (!item || typeof item !== 'object') return false;
    if (selectedStatus && item.status !== selectedStatus) return false;
    if (!needle) return true;
    return fields.some(field => {
      const value = item[field];
      return value !== null && value !== undefined && String(value).toLowerCase().includes(needle);
    });
  });
}

Optional live Firebase Auth lifecycle smoke test:

```sh
npm run test:firebase-auth
```

This uses `.env.local`, creates one uniquely named disposable Auth account, verifies sign-in, empty user-scoped reads, and sign-out on localhost, makes **no Firestore writes**, and deletes the Auth account in cleanup. It needs network access and should not be run concurrently with another live Auth test.

The app uses a small vendored Gson JAR for the Java Firestore REST adapter; its license is recorded in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and `third_party/licenses/`.

## Firebase development sandbox

- `.env.local` contains the Firebase **Web** app config used by the browser SDK; `.gitignore` lists this file. The user-supplied Web API key for `motorph-jd` is installed assistant-side. The user does not need to edit `.env.local`.
- The Web API key is a public client identifier, not a server credential. Do not add a service-account key or Admin SDK credentials.
- Authentication uses Email/Password and in-memory browser persistence. Live disposable-account creation/sign-in, empty user-scoped reads, and sign-out now pass on localhost; the test Auth account was deleted. Do not use real staff accounts or data.
- Firestore requests are made by the Java backend through the REST API, forwarding the signed-in user's Firebase ID token. Firestore Security Rules authorize those requests; no privileged server identity bypasses the rules.
- The app uses `users/{uid}/demoEmployees`, `demoAttendance`, `demoLeaveRequests`, and `demoTickets`. Workflow documents are owner-scoped with no reviewer or delete permission in the candidate rules. The opt-in seed writes fictional employee/attendance records only.
- The user published the updated `docs/firestore.rules`. Live Firebase smoke testing with disposable accounts verified owner-scoped employee create/update, leave and ticket create/cancel/read-back, and a cross-user denial (`403`). Both disposable Auth accounts and employee documents were deleted; one cancelled synthetic leave and one cancelled synthetic ticket remain under their deleted test UIDs because workflow deletes are intentionally denied (`LV-3502C01F0E60`, `TK-F05DD2B0D6CC`). No real employee data or credentials were used. These are **development-only** rules, not production role/HR policy.
- If Firebase is not configured locally, the app uses the in-memory synthetic fixture. No Firebase writes are made in that mode.
- `measurementId` / Firebase Analytics is not used.
- Browser auth is verified on `localhost`. The current Arena preview host is `8080-is3s38ic4lxn7e4e77g8b.e2b.app`; its authorized-domain status could not be tested from the sandbox because Arena's traffic-access token is injected only in the user preview session. If the preview reports `auth/unauthorized-domain`, add that exact host under Firebase Console → Authentication → Settings → Authorized domains.

See `docs/firebase-setup-guide.md` for the console checkpoint and `docs/firestore.rules` for the development rules.

## What works

- Overview with live sandbox counts, searchable employee directory/detail, HR directory search/status filters, a synthetic directory-label summary, raw attendance register and coverage report, Requests & tickets, searchable read-only Team roster, and the payroll rules gate. Employee details open from a native keyboard-operable button without overriding table semantics; result counts and form feedback use polite status regions.
- Java employee/attendance services plus a workflow service. Local preview workflow records are held in Java process memory; Firebase mode uses the signed-in user’s Firestore subcollections.
- Leave requests and tickets validate inputs, derive employee names from the caller’s own synthetic directory, show documented queue labels, and support owner-sandbox cancellation. A monthly leave-request calendar displays pending/cancelled request dates only; it does not imply approval or leave balances. Search/status filters narrow history tables only; they do not change the leave calendar or all-record exports. Row details reveal the submitted note/message and UTC timestamps without adding a reviewer workflow. Both local and Firestore workflow histories are ordered newest first. No reviewer/approval/resolve/delete routes exist. The user has published the rules; live tests confirmed leave and ticket create/cancel persistence, plus cross-user denial.
- Read-only Team roster plus a synthetic directory editor. In Firebase mode, signed-in users can create/edit only name, department, role label, location, and demo status in their own sandbox. Local preview has no user authentication and shares one process-memory store for that API process. IDs are server-generated; delete, termination, schedule, salary, and government-ID fields are not exposed. New records receive no schedule mapping, so their raw attendance view is empty. This is not an HR role or a production employee-admin workflow.
- CSV export for currently visible synthetic employee results and Team roster rows, loaded raw attendance rows, attendance coverage reports, and owner-sandbox workflow records. CSV cells are quoted and spreadsheet-formula prefixes are neutralized; exports contain no derived hours or payroll values.
- Server-side employee search/detail, HR table search/status filters, a user-scoped attendance-coverage report (raw row counts and first/last record dates by configured mapping), synthetic directory label counts by status/department, and dynamic overview counts. Unmapped employees are labeled as unmapped, not absent. The attendance date fields default to that employee's earliest/latest available records, following the earlier MO-IT108 Requirements Analysis; the user can narrow the range. This is not a payroll-period calendar. No paid hours, deductions, or pay are calculated.
- Firebase email/password sign-in, development-account creation, and password-reset email UI; reset responses do not disclose whether an email has an account. The app stays behind the sign-in gate when Firebase config is complete.
- `/api/health`, employee list/search/detail plus owner-sandbox create/update, raw attendance query and coverage report, owner-scoped workflow list/create/cancel routes, and opt-in demo seed endpoint.
- Verification: `npm run test:web` passes 20 workflow/calendar/filter/CSV tests; `./test.sh` passes 167 Java checks; `npm run test:e2e` passes the local browser flow for employee create/edit, HR/Team filters and roster CSV, empty unscheduled attendance, raw directory-label summary, reversed-date rejection, leave/ticket submit/cancel and detail disclosures, request-calendar navigation, raw attendance summary/report filtering, drill-through and CSV, simulated workflow authorization/service failure recovery, reload persistence, and mobile width; `npm run build` passes; `npm audit` reports 0 vulnerabilities. An isolated live Firebase auth-lifecycle browser check passed disposable account creation/sign-in, user-scoped empty Firestore reads, and sign-out on localhost; the account was deleted and no Firestore writes were made. The exact Arena preview-origin sign-in remains unverified.

## Not implemented / important limits

- No production hosting, HR authorization roles, admin controls, audit trail, backup, or production security review. The built-in JDK HTTP server is a learning prototype, not a hardened public service.
- No live employee, attendance, or payroll information. Do not use this prototype for payroll processing.
- No work-hour derivation algorithm, payroll formulas, rates, pay-period calendar, payslips, or payroll calculations. The supplied material does not define a complete attendance algorithm or exact semi-monthly cut-offs, so the program will not infer them.
- Leave/ticket records are persistent only in the signed-in user’s sandbox after the updated rules are published; the current local preview uses process memory. There is no supervisor/reviewer role, real queue delivery, approval, notification, audit trail, team assignment, HR lifecycle editing, attendance import, or approved source-system integration.

## Source and attribution

`docs/source-grounding-and-open-rules.md` records supplied-source facts, scope boundaries, and unresolved ambiguities. `docs/acceptance-baseline.md` captures the current source-grounded behavior and gates as a draft, not an approved rubric. `docs/legacy-mo-it108-traceability.md` maps the user's earlier MotorPH requirements/design documents to the current prototype and explains the feature-parity estimate. `docs/peer-parity-roadmap.md` lists the remaining phases and acceptance gates to reach broad peer-level feature parity. The restrained title stripe adapts a small MIT-licensed `system.css` motif; exact attribution and licenses are listed in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

35-
36-The database-design document describes five broad capability areas:
37-
38-1. Employee management, including employment status, department/position, salary structure and personal information.
39:2. Payroll computation using attendance, adjustments, overtime, tax and government contributions; semi-monthly payslips and a monthly summary are named.
40-3. Attendance/leave tracking, including time-in/time-out, leave requests, holidays/rest days and leave benefits.
41-4. Government contributions and compliance, including employer/employee contributions and tax/contribution reporting.
42-5. Role-based access control for system administrators, HR, payroll staff and employees; audit traceability; and protected PII.
43-
44-The overview states that PII access requires approval from **two authorized personnel**, with only corresponding contribution values normally visible/accessed. Treat this as explicit design intent, not as verified repository behavior. The precise approval sequence, approver roles, emergency access, and field-level rules are not specified.
45-
46-### 2. Database-design table inventory (30 tables)
47-
--
93-**Level 1 (PDF page 3):** process 1.0 Employee Management uses an Employee Repository and Logs; process 2.0 Payroll Processing uses a Payroll store; process 3.0 Archival transfers old logs/payroll toward Cold Storage. Employee, supervisor, HR, payroll staff and admin interact with the processes. The diagram labels retrieval/append/modify and backup/archive flows.
94-
95-**Level 2 employee management (PDF page 4):** 1.1 Employee Information Handling; 1.2 Schedule and Time Tracking; 1.3 Government Info Access. Data stores include employee address, job profile, PII, changelog, attendance and leave. PII view/update and employee changes are shown with approval flows. Employee, supervisor, HR, payroll staff and system admin are shown interacting.
96-
97:**Level 2 payroll processing (PDF page 5):** 2.1 Timesheet Validation; 2.2 Leave Monetisation Process; 2.3 Wage and Adjustments; 2.4 Government Deductibles; 2.5 Basic Payroll Computation; 2.6 Payslip Generation & Distribution; 2.7 Monthly Summary Compilation. Data stores include attendance/leave/leave-monetisation logs, wage, benefits & deductibles, tax table/rates, payslip and monthly summary report. The diagram shows supervisory wage/adjustment input and approved leave monetisation, payroll-staff verification, and employee/HR/team viewing paths.
98-
99-**Level 2 archival (PDF page 6):** process 3.1 Appending and process 3.2 Deleting; system admin triggers annual archiving. The image labels one-year records for attendance, leave, changelogs and leave-monetisation logs, two-year payslips, cold storage, and removal of relevant records after an archival trigger/finish. This sequence must not be implemented as destructive production behavior until retention, authorization, restore testing and applicable requirements are confirmed.
100-
101-### 5. Integrated synthesis and diagram-to-schema crosswalk
102-
103-Taken together, the PDFs describe a lifecycle rather than three independent artifacts: establish an employee and their authorized job/schedule information; collect and validate attendance and approved leave; prepare and verify payroll using wage/adjustment and statutory-rule inputs; issue employee/team payslips and monthly aggregates; then preserve records under an archival process. The database-design PDF supplies the intended data structure and capability statements, the dictionary clarifies fields/types/constraints, and the DFD pictures the actors, transformations, stores and approval/archival flows.

122-- **D3 Payroll:** likely maps to `Payroll`, `Payslip`, `Earnings`, `Deductibles`, `Other Transactions`, `Government`, `Government Deductibles`, `Contributions`, `Government Tally`, and `Summary`, with `Rates`, `Tax Table`, `Months`, `Holiday`, and `Leave Type` as reference/configuration data. The DFD's `Monthly Summary Report` is a named store/output; the data design has `Summary` but does not specify a report-file store or output format.

139-Everything below is a **proposed plan**, not an assertion that the missing requirements have been supplied or approved. It uses the PDFs as a starting point and deliberately leaves rule values configurable/unknown.
140-
141-### A. Architecture and boundaries
142-
143:1. **Presentation layer:** separate employee, supervisor, HR, payroll-staff and system-admin views. UI screens collect requests and show only permitted results; they do not contain payroll formulas or direct persistence logic.
144-2. **Application services:** `EmployeeService`, `AttendanceService`, `LeaveService`, `PIIAccessApprovalService`, `PayrollRunService`, `PayslipService`, `MonthlySummaryService`, `AuditService`, and (only after approval) `ArchiveService`. Each service enforces authorization and state transitions.
145-3. **Domain/calculation layer:** explicit models for employee/job/address, schedule/attendance, leave balance/request/accrual/monetisation, payroll period, earnings/deductions, contribution/tax calculation and immutable payroll results. Monetary calculations use fixed-precision decimal arithmetic

403-## Folder-by-folder observations
404-
405-### Folder 1 — SQLite Swing CRUD
406-
407-**Observed:** The sources compile with a matching NetBeans `AbsoluteLayout` library supplied only on the test classpath. The bundled SQLite file is populated. The GUI entry point cannot be meaningfully exercised in this headless environment; startup reaches a Swing `HeadlessException`.
--
421-**Observed:** `CalculateHoursWorked`, `ComputeGrossPay`, `ComputeSemiMonthlySalary`, and `MotorPH_ApplyDeductions` all exited 0 on their built-in examples. The bundled `MotorPH_ReadFromFile` processed 34 rows without an exception.
422-
423-**Observed defect:** The reader's naive comma split is not quote-aware. Every bundled row contains a comma in the quoted address cell. Comparing its 34 printed gross-pay outputs with the correctly parsed CSV salary column at index 17 produced **0 matching values out of 34**. Thus an exit code of zero is not evidence of correct field selection or payroll output.
424-
425:**Inventory test:** Replacing the expected input with the five-column inventory file caused `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`. This is a schema assumption/validation failure, not a payroll formula result.
426-
427-**Data flow:** Each run reads CSV lines into arrays and calculates/prints values in process memory; no durable payroll result store was exercised.
428-
429-### Folder 4 — layered Swing/CSV CP2 application
430-
431-**Observed:** The main `DataRepository`/model/processor subset compiled with the project's Commons CSV 1.9.0 dependency and loaded **35 employee rows** and **5,168 attendance rows** from bundled data. An isolated probe substituting the inventory file returned 0 employees when used as employee data and 0 attendance rows when used as attendance data.
432-
433-**Blocked:** The project targets Java 17. The available Java 11 cannot compile `PayrollService`, which uses `Stream.toList()` (introduced after Java 11). Maven is absent; the full source/test build was not completed. Therefore repository loading was exercised, but service/controller/GUI integration was not.
--
445-**Observed:** The full source compiled under Java 11. `motorph.AllTests` exited 0 with **167 passed, 0 failed**. This is the strongest single bundled suite result among the folders in this run.
446-
447-**Inventory test:** `CSVDataHandler` accepted the file operation but returned **0 employees** when inventory was supplied as employee data, and **0 attendance groups/rows** when supplied as attendance data. No exception or useful error was raised in the probe. The parser's documented shape is 19 columns for employees and 6 for attendance; the uploaded file has five different fields.
448-
449:**Data flow:** CSV data is loaded into employee/attendance objects and collections; payroll computations and role checks operate in memory; result persistence writes output CSV. The tests validate much more than a simple “main exits” check, but the inventory result exposes a silent-empty-data hazard.
450-
451-### Folder 7 — Swing/CSV payroll backend
452-
453-**Observed:** The four reported backend checks all passed. The required employee CSV is absent from the submission, so normal login and UI flows were not exercised.
454-
455-**Inventory test:** `EmployeeData` loaded all 49 records and padded them to 21 fields. This lenient width-padding masks the schema mismatch at the file-loading stage. The next step, `EmployeeMapper.fromCSV`, attempted to interpret inventory text as an employee number and threw `NumberFormatException`.
456-
457-**Data flow:** `EmployeeData.records` is a static shared in-memory list. UI/backend operations modify rows and rewrite CSV. The observed load-then-map failure shows that padding to a target width is not sufficient field validation.

    use probationary-employee behavior
return behavior through the shared Employee interface

### 3. Attendance and pay-period aggregation `[RUN through suite]`

```text

    determine if record belongs to cutoff
    accumulate worked hours/days and applicable time values
return cutoff totals
```

### 4. Payroll and deduction composition `[RUN through 167-check suite]`

```text
receive employee, attendance list, cutoff, and list of Deduction calculators
hours = aggregate matching attendance
gross = calculate employee/cutoff pay, including subtype allowance behavior
for each deduction calculator (SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, tax):
    deductionAmount = calculator.calculate(gross, employee/context)
net = gross - sum(deductionAmount)
create immutable Payslip with period, gross, deductions, net
```

package motorph.model;

import java.time.Duration;
import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.time.LocalTime;
import java.time.format.TextStyle;
import java.util.Locale;

/**
 * One day of attendance for one employee (one row of attendance.csv).
 * <p>
 * The CP2 time rules are hidden inside this class: logins from 8:00 to 8:10
 * count as 8:00 (grace period), and logouts after 5:00 PM count as 5:00 PM
 * (cap). Callers only ask for hours or minutes worked.
 * </p>
 */
public class AttendanceRecord {

    // === TIME RULES (from CP2 computeHoursWorked) ===
    private static final LocalTime WORK_START   = LocalTime.of(8, 0);
    private static final LocalTime GRACE_END    = LocalTime.of(8, 10);
    private static final LocalTime LOGOUT_CAP   = LocalTime.of(17, 0);

    // === CUTOFF RULES (days 1-15 = 1st cutoff, 16-month end = 2nd cutoff) ===
    private static final int FIRST_CUTOFF_END_DAY    = 15;
    private static final int SECOND_CUTOFF_START_DAY = 16;

    private final String employeeId;
    private final LocalDate date;
    private final LocalTime logIn;
    private LocalTime logOut;

    /**
     * Creates an attendance record. Throws IllegalArgumentException if a value
     * is missing or the logout is not after the login.
     */
    public AttendanceRecord(String employeeId, LocalDate date, LocalTime logIn, LocalTime logOut) {
        if (employeeId == null || employeeId.trim().isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Employee ID is required.");
        }
        if (date == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Date is required.");
        }
        if (logIn == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Log in time is required.");
        }
        this.employeeId = employeeId.trim();
        this.date = date;
        this.logIn = logIn;
        setLogOut(logOut);
    }

    // === GETTERS ===

    public String getEmployeeId() { return employeeId; }
    public LocalDate getDate()    { return date; }
    public LocalTime getLogIn()   { return logIn; }
    public LocalTime getLogOut()  { return logOut; }

    /** Updates the logout time. Must be after the login time. */
    public final void setLogOut(LocalTime logOut) {
        if (logOut == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Log out time is required.");
        }
        if (!logOut.isAfter(logIn)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Log out time must be after log in time.");
        }
        this.logOut = logOut;
    }

    // === HOURS ===

    /**
     * Returns the minutes worked after applying the grace period and the
     * logout cap. Never negative. Whole minutes keep payroll math exact.
     */
    public long computeMinutesWorked() {
        long minutes = Duration.between(applyGracePeriod(logIn), applyLogoutCap(logOut)).toMinutes();
        return Math.max(0, minutes);
    }

    /** Returns the hours worked for the day after the time rules. Never negative. */
    public double computeHoursWorked() {
        return computeMinutesWorked() / 60.0;
    }

    /** Treats a login from 8:00 to 8:10 as 8:00. */
    private LocalTime applyGracePeriod(LocalTime time) {
        if (!time.isBefore(WORK_START) && !time.isAfter(GRACE_END)) {
            return WORK_START;
        }
        return time;
    }

    /** Caps a logout after 5:00 PM at 5:00 PM. */
    private LocalTime applyLogoutCap(LocalTime time) {
        return time.isAfter(LOGOUT_CAP) ? LOGOUT_CAP : time;
    }

    // === CUTOFF ===

    /**
     * Returns the payroll cutoff label for this record's date, for example
     * "June 1-15, 2024" or "June 16-30, 2024". Uses the real month length, so
     * February gives "16-29" in leap years and "16-28" otherwise.
     */
    public String getCutoffLabel() {
        String month = date.getMonth().getDisplayName(TextStyle.FULL, Locale.ENGLISH);
        if (date.getDayOfMonth() <= FIRST_CUTOFF_END_DAY) {
            return month + " 1-" + FIRST_CUTOFF_END_DAY + ", " + date.getYear();
        }
        return month + " " + SECOND_CUTOFF_START_DAY + "-" + date.lengthOfMonth() + ", " + date.getYear();
    }
}
package motorph.service;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.math.MathContext;
import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.LinkedHashSet;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Set;
import java.util.TreeMap;
import motorph.deduction.Deduction;
import motorph.model.AttendanceRecord;
import motorph.model.Employee;
import motorph.model.Payslip;

/**
 * Runs the payroll workflow: hours -> gross pay -> deductions -> net pay -> Payslip.
 * <p>
 * Works only with parent types (Employee, Deduction), so there are no checks on
 * employee status or deduction type. The deductions are passed into the
 * constructor: a list of contributions computed on monthly gross (SSS,
 * PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG) and a separate withholding tax computed on taxable
 * income. Adding a new government contribution only needs a new Deduction
 * subclass in that list.
 * </p>
 * <p>
 * Cutoff rule (from CP2): the 1st cutoff (days 1-15) has no deductions and net
 * pay equals gross pay. The 2nd cutoff (day 16 to month end) takes the whole
 * month's deductions once, computed on the combined gross of both cutoffs.
 * </p>
 */
public class PayrollProcessor {

    // === SUMMARY KEYS (computePayrollSummary) ===
    public static final String SUMMARY_TOTAL_EMPLOYEES  = "Total Employees";
    public static final String SUMMARY_TOTAL_GROSS      = "Total Gross Pay";
    public static final String SUMMARY_TOTAL_DEDUCTIONS = "Total Deductions";
    public static final String SUMMARY_TOTAL_NET        = "Total Net Pay";
    public static final String SUMMARY_AVERAGE_NET      = "Average Net Pay";

    // Cutoff labels come from AttendanceRecord.getCutoffLabel(), e.g. "June 16-30, 2024"
    private static final String SECOND_CUTOFF_MARKER  = " 16-";
    private static final String SECOND_CUTOFF_PATTERN = " 16-\\d{2},";
    private static final String FIRST_CUTOFF_DAYS     = " 1-15,";

    private final List<Deduction> contributions;
    private final Deduction withholdingTax;

    /**
     * @param contributions  deductions computed on monthly gross, in payslip order
     * @param withholdingTax deduction computed last, on taxable income
     */
    public PayrollProcessor(List<Deduction> contributions, Deduction withholdingTax) {
        if (contributions == null || withholdingTax == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Contributions and withholding tax are required.");
        }
        for (Deduction contribution : contributions) {
            if (contribution == null) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Contribution list must not contain empty entries.");
            }
        }
        this.contributions = List.copyOf(contributions);
        this.withholdingTax = withholdingTax;
    }

    /** Returns the deduction names in payslip order (contributions, then tax). */
    public List<String> getDeductionNames() {
        List<String> names = new ArrayList<>();
        for (Deduction contribution : contributions) {
            names.add(contribution.getName());
        }
        names.add(withholdingTax.getName());
        return names;
    }

    // === CUTOFFS AND HOURS ===

    /**
     * Returns every cutoff label found in the attendance records, oldest first.
     * Used to fill the cutoff selection list.
     */
    public List<String> getAvailableCutoffs(Map<String, List<AttendanceRecord>> attendanceByEmployee) {
        Map<LocalDate, String> labelsByDate = new TreeMap<>();
        for (List<AttendanceRecord> records : attendanceByEmployee.values()) {
            for (AttendanceRecord record : records) {
                labelsByDate.putIfAbsent(record.getDate(), record.getCutoffLabel());
            }
        }
        Set<String> cutoffs = new LinkedHashSet<>(labelsByDate.values());
        return new ArrayList<>(cutoffs);
    }

    /**
     * Sums the hours worked in one cutoff.
     *
     * @param records     one employee's attendance records
     * @param cutoffLabel the cutoff to total, for example "June 1-15, 2024"
     * @return total hours, or 0 if no records match
     */
    public double computeHoursForCutoff(List<AttendanceRecord> records, String cutoffLabel) {
        long minutes = 0;
        if (records != null) {
            for (AttendanceRecord record : records) {
                if (record.getCutoffLabel().equals(cutoffLabel)) {
                    minutes += record.computeMinutesWorked();
                }
            }
        }
        return minutes / 60.0;
    }

    /**
     * Returns the employees with no hours in the cutoff, so the GUI can warn once
     * before they are computed with 0 hours (CP2 behavior).
     */
    public List<Employee> findEmployeesWithoutAttendance(List<Employee> employees,
            Map<String, List<AttendanceRecord>> attendanceByEmployee, String cutoffLabel) {
        List<Employee> missing = new ArrayList<>();
        for (Employee employee : employees) {
            List<AttendanceRecord> records = attendanceByEmployee.get(employee.getEmployeeId());
            if (computeHoursForCutoff(records, cutoffLabel) <= 0) {
                missing.add(employee);
            }
        }
        return missing;
    }

    // === DEDUCTIONS AND NET PAY ===

    /**
     * Computes each deduction for one month, in order: every contribution on the
     * monthly gross, then withholding tax on taxable income (monthly gross minus
     * the contributions, floored at 0). No type checks: each Deduction runs its
     * own formula.
     *
     * @param monthlyGross combined gross of the 1st and 2nd cutoff
     * @return deduction name to amount, in payslip order
     */
    public Map<String, BigDecimal> computeDeductionBreakdown(BigDecimal monthlyGross) {
        Map<String, BigDecimal> breakdown = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        BigDecimal taxableIncome = monthlyGross;
        for (Deduction contribution : contributions) {
            BigDecimal amount = contribution.computeDeduction(monthlyGross);
            breakdown.put(contribution.getName(), amount);
            taxableIncome = taxableIncome.subtract(amount);
        }
        breakdown.put(withholdingTax.getName(), withholdingTax.computeDeduction(taxableIncome.max(BigDecimal.ZERO)));
        return breakdown;
    }

    /**
     * Totals all government deductions for one month: the sum of
     * computeDeductionBreakdown(), so the total always matches the itemized lines.
     */
    public BigDecimal computeTotalDeductions(BigDecimal monthlyGross) {
        return sum(computeDeductionBreakdown(monthlyGross));
    }

    /** Net pay = cutoff gross - deductions, never below 0. */
    public BigDecimal computeNetPay(BigDecimal cutoffGross, BigDecimal totalDeductions) {
        return cutoffGross.subtract(totalDeductions).max(BigDecimal.ZERO);
    }

    // === PAYSLIPS ===

    /**
     * Builds the payslip for one employee and one cutoff ("One Employee" mode).
     * Accepts any Employee subtype; allowances come from the subclass's own
     * computeAllowances().
     *
     * @param employee    the employee to pay
     * @param records     that employee's attendance records (may be empty)
     * @param cutoffLabel the cutoff to pay
     */
    public Payslip generatePayslip(Employee employee, List<AttendanceRecord> records, String cutoffLabel) {
        if (employee == null || cutoffLabel == null || cutoffLabel.trim().isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Employee and cutoff are required.");
        }
        double hoursWorked = computeHoursForCutoff(records, cutoffLabel);
        BigDecimal grossPay = employee.computeGrossPay(hoursWorked);

        Map<String, BigDecimal> breakdown;
        BigDecimal allowances;
        if (isSecondCutoff(cutoffLabel)) {
            // Monthly items are settled once, here: deductions on the combined gross of both cutoffs,
            // and the month's allowances (listed only; not added to net pay, as in CP2).
            double firstCutoffHours = computeHoursForCutoff(records, getFirstCutoffLabel(cutoffLabel));
            BigDecimal monthlyGross = employee.computeGrossPay(firstCutoffHours + hoursWorked);
            breakdown = computeDeductionBreakdown(monthlyGross);
            allowances = employee.computeAllowances();
        } else {
            breakdown = zeroBreakdown();
            allowances = BigDecimal.ZERO;
        }
        BigDecimal netPay = computeNetPay(grossPay, sum(breakdown));
        return new Payslip(employee, cutoffLabel, hoursWorked, grossPay, breakdown, allowances, netPay);
    }

    /**
     * Runs payroll for every employee in one cutoff ("All Employees" mode).
     * Same steps for every Employee subtype.
     */
    public List<Payslip> processPayroll(List<Employee> employees,
            Map<String, List<AttendanceRecord>> attendanceByEmployee, String cutoffLabel) {
        List<Payslip> payslips = new ArrayList<>();
        for (Employee employee : employees) {
            payslips.add(generatePayslip(employee, attendanceByEmployee.get(employee.getEmployeeId()), cutoffLabel));
        }
        return payslips;
    }

    /**
     * Totals a list of payslips: employee count, total gross, total deductions,
     * total net, and average net. Uses full-precision amounts (as CP2 did), so
     * the totals are rounded only when displayed.
     *
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the list is empty
     */

package motorphemployee;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.nio.file.AtomicMoveNotSupportedException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.nio.file.Paths;
import java.nio.file.StandardCopyOption;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Arrays;
import java.util.List;

/**
 * File-backed leave workflow for the MotorPH payroll screens.
 *
 * <p>The leave screens used to read and write {@code pendingleaves.csv},
 * {@code leaves.csv} and the leave-credit columns of {@code data.csv} on their
 * own. Two places knew the same CSV layout, so a single reversed argument
 * (Pending Leaves wrote the reason where the approval belonged) survived in one
 * call site after the other was fixed, and approving a request updated
 * {@code leaves.csv} while the request stayed in {@code pendingleaves.csv} until
 * somebody remembered to press Save.</p>
 *
 * <p>This class is the single writer for the approve and reject decisions. One call to
 * {@link #decide(int, boolean)} applies the whole decision - the request leaves
 * the pending file, one row is appended to the processed file with the columns
 * in header order, and the employee's leave credits move - and restores all
 * three files if any step fails.</p>
 *
 * <p>No Swing types are used here on purpose: the class can be exercised by a
 * console test without opening a window.</p>
 */
public class LeaveService {

    /** Value written in the {@code Approved?} column for an approved request. */
    public static final String APPROVED = "Yes";
    /** Value written in the {@code Approved?} column for a rejected request. */
    public static final String REJECTED = "No";

    /** Column order of pendingleaves.csv and of the processed leaves.csv. */
    public static final String[] LEAVE_COLUMNS = {"Employee ID", "Leave Type", "Days", "Reason", "Approved?"};

    public static final int COLUMN_EMPLOYEE_ID = 0;
    public static final int COLUMN_LEAVE_TYPE = 1;
    public static final int COLUMN_DAYS = 2;
    public static final int COLUMN_REASON = 3;
    public static final int COLUMN_APPROVAL = 4;

    private static final int COL_EMPLOYEE_ID = COLUMN_EMPLOYEE_ID;
    private static final int COL_LEAVE_TYPE = COLUMN_LEAVE_TYPE;
    private static final int COL_DAYS = COLUMN_DAYS;
    private static final int COL_REASON = COLUMN_REASON;

    private static final int DATA_LEAVE_CREDITS = 21;
    private static final int DATA_APPROVED_LEAVES = 22;
    private static final int DATA_REJECTED_LEAVES = 23;

    private final Path dataFile;
    private final Path pendingFile;
    private final Path leavesFile;

    public LeaveService(String dataFile, String pendingFile, String leavesFile) {
        this.dataFile = Paths.get(dataFile);
        this.pendingFile = Paths.get(pendingFile);
        this.leavesFile = Paths.get(leavesFile);
    }

    /** The three files the GUI uses, relative to the project directory. */
    public static LeaveService forProjectFiles() {
        return new LeaveService(
                "src/motorphemployee/data.csv",
                "src/motorphemployee/pendingleaves.csv",
                "src/motorphemployee/leaves.csv");
    }

    /** Rows of pendingleaves.csv, in file order. */
    public List<String[]> loadPending() throws IOException {
        return readRows(pendingFile);
    }

    /** Rows of leaves.csv (processed requests), in file order. */
    public List<String[]> loadProcessed() throws IOException {
        return readRows(leavesFile);
    }

    /**
     * Applies one decision to the request at {@code pendingIndex}.
     *
     * @param pendingIndex zero-based index into {@link #loadPending()}
     * @param approved     {@code true} to approve, {@code false} to reject
     * @return the row that was written to {@code leaves.csv}: employee id, leave
     *         type, days, reason, {@code Yes}/{@code No}
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException the row is gone, or the employee is unknown
     * @throws IllegalStateException    the employee has no leave credit left
     * @throws IOException              the files could not be written; all three
     *                                  files are restored before this is thrown
     */
    public String[] decide(int pendingIndex, boolean approved) throws IOException {
        return decide(pendingIndex, null, approved);
    }

    /**
     * Same as {@link #decide(int, boolean)}, but refuses when the row at
     * {@code pendingIndex} is not the request the screen showed, which happens
     * when the pending file changed while the window was open.
     *
     * @param expected the four cells the table displayed, or {@code null}
     */
    public String[] decide(int pendingIndex, String[] expected, boolean approved) throws IOException {
        List<String[]> pending = readRows(pendingFile);
        if (pendingIndex < 0 || pendingIndex >= pending.size()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "That leave request is no longer in the pending list. Reopen the window and try again.");
        }
        if (expected != null && !sameRequest(pending.get(pendingIndex), expected)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "The pending leave list changed while this window was open. Reopen the window and try again.");
        }

        String[] request = pending.get(pendingIndex);
        String employeeId = cell(request, COL_EMPLOYEE_ID);
        String leaveType = cell(request, COL_LEAVE_TYPE);
        String reason = reasonOf(request);
        int days = parseDays(cell(request, COL_DAYS));

        List<String[]> employees = readRows(dataFile);
        ensureUniformColumns(employees);
        int employeeRow = indexOfEmployee(employees, employeeId);
        if (employeeRow < 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Employee ID " + employeeId + " is not in the employee data file.");
        }
        String[] employee = employees.get(employeeRow);
        int credits = parseNumber(cell(employee, DATA_LEAVE_CREDITS), "leave credits", employeeId);
        int approvedLeaves = parseNumber(cell(employee, DATA_APPROVED_LEAVES), "approved leaves", employeeId);
        int rejectedLeaves = parseNumber(cell(employee, DATA_REJECTED_LEAVES), "rejected leaves", employeeId);
        if (approved && credits <= 0) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Employee " + employeeId + " has no leave credit left.");
        }

        // New credit values are computed before the first write so a business-rule
        // failure cannot leave the three files half updated.
        employee[DATA_LEAVE_CREDITS] = String.valueOf(approved ? credits - 1 : credits);
        employee[DATA_APPROVED_LEAVES] = String.valueOf(approved ? approvedLeaves + 1 : approvedLeaves);
        employee[DATA_REJECTED_LEAVES] = String.valueOf(approved ? rejectedLeaves : rejectedLeaves + 1);

        String[] processed = new String[] {
            employeeId, leaveType, String.valueOf(days), reason, approved ? APPROVED : REJECTED
        };

        byte[] pendingBefore = readBytes(pendingFile);
        byte[] leavesBefore = readBytes(leavesFile);
        byte[] dataBefore = readBytes(dataFile);
        try {
            pending.remove(pendingIndex);
            writeRows(pendingFile, pending);
            appendRow(leavesFile, processed);
            writeRows(dataFile, employees);
        } catch (IOException | RuntimeException failure) {
            restore(pendingFile, pendingBefore);
            restore(leavesFile, leavesBefore);
            restore(dataFile, dataBefore);
            throw failure;
        }
        return processed;
    }

    /**
     * The reason text of a leave row. Older rows were written with the columns
     * reversed and a reason that can itself contain a comma, so everything from
     * the reason column onwards is joined back into one value.
     */
    public static String reasonOf(String[] row) {
        if (row.length <= COL_REASON) {
            return "";
        }
        String[] tail = Arrays.copyOfRange(row, COL_REASON, row.length);
        return String.join(",", tail).trim();
    }

    /** Pending row (Employee ID, Leave Type, Days, Reason) for the Pending Leaves table. */
    public static Object[] pendingTableRow(String[] row) {
        return new Object[] {
            cell(row, COL_EMPLOYEE_ID), cell(row, COL_LEAVE_TYPE), cell(row, COL_DAYS), reasonOf(row)
        };
    }

    /**
     * Processed row (Employee ID, Leave Type, Days, Reason, Approved?) for the
     * Leave Management table. The approval is the last field and the reason is
     * everything between the days and the approval, so a reason that contains a
     * comma still lands in one cell.
     */
    public static Object[] processedTableRow(String[] row) {
        String approval = row.length > COLUMN_APPROVAL ? row[row.length - 1].trim() : "";
        String reason = row.length > COLUMN_APPROVAL
                ? String.join(",", Arrays.copyOfRange(row, COL_REASON, row.length - 1)).trim()
                : reasonOf(row);
        return new Object[] {
            cell(row, COL_EMPLOYEE_ID), cell(row, COL_LEAVE_TYPE), cell(row, COL_DAYS), reason, approval
        };
    }

    /**
     * Refuses to rewrite an employee file whose rows do not all have the header's
     * column count. A field with an unescaped comma would shift every later
     * column, and writing the parsed rows back would turn that into lost data
     * (known issue 13 - the screens still split on every comma).
     */
    private static void ensureUniformColumns(List<String[]> rows) {
        if (rows.isEmpty()) {
            return;
        }
        int columns = rows.get(0).length;
        for (int i = 1; i < rows.size(); i++) {
            if (rows.get(i).length != columns) {
                throw new IllegalStateException("data.csv row " + (i + 1) + " has " + rows.get(i).length

[NODE 4450]

    private static void approveWritesCorrectColumnsAndRemovesPending() throws IOException {
        start("approve: request leaves pendingleaves.csv, lands in leaves.csv with Yes, credit drops by 1");
        LeaveService service = fixture("23,Sick Leave,2,Sick\r\n13,Emergency Leave,1,Family trip\r\n", "", 5, 0, 0);

        String[] processed = service.decide(0, true);

        check("returned row keeps header order", "23|Sick Leave|2|Sick|Yes", String.join("|", processed));
        check("pending file keeps only the untouched request", "13,Emergency Leave,1,Family trip",
                String.join(" / ", lines(work.resolve("pendingleaves.csv"))));
        check("leaves.csv got one row", 1, lines(work.resolve("leaves.csv")).size());
        check("leaves.csv row has the reason in column 4 and Yes in column 5", "23,Sick Leave,2,Sick,Yes",
                lines(work.resolve("leaves.csv")).get(0));
        List<String> dataRows = lines(work.resolve("data.csv"));
        check("data.csv keeps all 24 columns on the edited row", 24, dataRows.get(1).split(",", -1).length);
        check("leave credits 5 -> 4", "4", creditsOf("23"));
        check("approved leaves 0 -> 1", "1", approvedOf("23"));
        check("rejected leaves unchanged", "0", rejectedOf("23"));
    }

    private static void rejectWritesNoAndKeepsCredits() throws IOException {
        start("reject: same single write, No in the approval column, credit untouched");
        LeaveService service = fixture("13,Emergency Leave,2,Family trip\r\n", "", 5, 0, 0);

        String[] processed = service.decide(0, false);

        check("returned row keeps header order", "13|Emergency Leave|2|Family trip|No", String.join("|", processed));
        check("pending file is empty", 0, lines(work.resolve("pendingleaves.csv")).size());
        check("leaves.csv row has the reason in column 4 and No in column 5", "13,Emergency Leave,2,Family trip,No",
                lines(work.resolve("leaves.csv")).get(0));
        check("leave credits unchanged", "5", creditsOf("13"));
        check("approved leaves unchanged", "0", approvedOf("13"));
        check("rejected leaves 0 -> 1", "1", rejectedOf("13"));
    }

    private static void theSameRequestCannotBeProcessedTwice() throws IOException {
        start("the same request cannot be approved twice (the old duplicate-leave bug)");
        LeaveService service = fixture("23,Sick Leave,2,Sick\r\n", "", 5, 0, 0);

        service.decide(0, true);
        String pendingAfterFirst = String.join("|", lines(work.resolve("pendingleaves.csv")));
        String leavesAfterFirst = String.join("|", lines(work.resolve("leaves.csv")));
        int rowsAfterFirst = lines(work.resolve("leaves.csv")).size();

        boolean refused = false;
        String message = "";
        try {
            service.decide(0, true);
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException expected) {
            refused = true;
            message = expected.getMessage();
        }
        check("second decision on the same index is refused", true, refused);
        check("the refusal explains why", true, message.contains("no longer in the pending list"));
        check("pending file still empty", "", pendingAfterFirst);
        check("leaves.csv still has one row", rowsAfterFirst, lines(work.resolve("leaves.csv")).size());
        check("leaves.csv unchanged", leavesAfterFirst, String.join("|", lines(work.resolve("leaves.csv"))));
        check("leave credit was only deducted once", "4", creditsOf("23"));
    }

    private static void unknownEmployeeLeavesTheFilesUntouched() throws IOException {
        start("unknown employee: refused before any file is written");
        LeaveService service = fixture("99,Sick Leave,2,Sick\r\n", "", 5, 0, 0);
        String pendingBefore = String.join("|", lines(work.resolve("pendingleaves.csv")));
        String dataBefore = String.join("|", lines(work.resolve("data.csv")));

        boolean refused = false;
        try {
            service.decide(0, true);
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException expected) {
            refused = expected.getMessage().contains("not in the employee data file");
        }
        check("refused", true, refused);
        check("pending file untouched", pendingBefore, String.join("|", lines(work.resolve("pendingleaves.csv"))));
        check("data file untouched", dataBefore, String.join("|", lines(work.resolve("data.csv"))));
        check("leaves.csv still empty", 0, lines(work.resolve("leaves.csv")).size());
    }

    private static void employeeWithoutCreditIsRefused() throws IOException {
        start("employee with 0 leave credits: approval refused, nothing written");
        LeaveService service = fixture("23,Sick Leave,2,Sick\r\n", "", 0, 3, 1);
        String pendingBefore = String.join("|", lines(work.resolve("pendingleaves.csv")));

        boolean refused = false;
        try {
            service.decide(0, true);
        } catch (IllegalStateException expected) {
            refused = expected.getMessage().contains("no leave credit left");
        }
        check("refused", true, refused);
        check("pending file untouched", pendingBefore, String.join("|", lines(work.resolve("pendingleaves.csv"))));
        check("data file untouched", "0", creditsOf("23"));
        check("leaves.csv still empty", 0, lines(work.resolve("leaves.csv")).size());
    }

    private static void aStaleRowIsRefusedAfterTheFileChanged() throws IOException {
        start("a row that changed on disk is refused instead of processing the wrong request");
        LeaveService service = fixture("23,Sick Leave,2,Sick\r\n13,Emergency Leave,1,Family trip\r\n", "", 5, 0, 0);
        // The window showed row 0 as employee 23; the file is replaced underneath it.
        Files.write(work.resolve("pendingleaves.csv"),
                "13,Emergency Leave,1,Family trip\r\n".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));

        boolean refused = false;
        try {
            service.decide(0, new String[] {"23", "Sick Leave", "2", "Sick"}, true);
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException expected) {
            refused = expected.getMessage().contains("changed while this window was open");
        }
        check("refused", true, refused);
        check("no processed row was written", 0, lines(work.resolve("leaves.csv")).size());
        check("leave credits untouched", "5", creditsOf("23"));
    }

    private static void aRaggedEmployeeFileIsRefused() throws IOException {
        start("data.csv with a shifted row is refused instead of being rewritten");
        LeaveService service = fixture("23,Sick Leave,2,Sick\r\n", "", 5, 0, 0);
        // The shape a comma inside an address produces: one extra column on row 2.
        String shifted = employee("13", "Valencia", 5, 0, 0).replace(",Test,", ",Test Blk 5, Phase 2,");
        Files.write(work.resolve("data.csv"), (header() + "\r\n"
                + employee("23", "Racimo", 5, 0, 0) + "\r\n" + shifted + "\r\n").getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));

        boolean refused = false;
        try {
            service.decide(0, true);
        } catch (IllegalStateException expected) {
            refused = expected.getMessage().contains("Fix the file before processing leaves");
        }
        check("refused", true, refused);
        check("pending file untouched", 1, lines(work.resolve("pendingleaves.csv")).size());
        check("leaves.csv still empty", 0, lines(work.resolve("leaves.csv")).size());
        check("shifted row kept its extra column (nothing rewritten)", 25,
                lines(work.resolve("data.csv")).get(2).split(",", -1).length);
    }

    private static void reasonWithACommaStaysInTheReasonColumn() throws IOException {
        start("a reason that contains a comma stays in the Reason column");
        LeaveService service = fixture("23,Sick Leave,2,Blk 5, Phase 2\r\n", "", 5, 0, 0);

        String[] processed = service.decide(0, true);

        check("reason rebuilt from the split fields", "Blk 5, Phase 2", processed[LeaveService.COLUMN_REASON]);
        check("approval still last", "Yes", processed[LeaveService.COLUMN_APPROVAL]);
        Object[] pendingCells = LeaveService.pendingTableRow(new String[] {"23", "Sick", "2", "Blk 5", " Phase 2"});
        check("pending table shows the whole reason", "Blk 5, Phase 2", String.valueOf(pendingCells[3]));
    }

    private static void windowsLineEndingsSurviveTheRewrite() throws IOException {
        start("CRLF files keep CRLF after the pending rewrite (no whole-file diff)");
        LeaveService service = fixture("23,Sick Leave,2,Sick\r\n13,Emergency Leave,1,Family trip\r\n", "", 5, 0, 0);

        service.decide(0, true);

        String pending = new String(Files.readAllBytes(work.resolve("pendingleaves.csv")), StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
        check("remaining line still ends with CRLF", true, pending.endsWith("\r\n"));
        check("no bare LF was introduced", false, pending.replace("\r\n", "").contains("\n"));
        String leaves = new String(Files.readAllBytes(work.resolve("leaves.csv")), StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
        check("appended row also uses CRLF", true, leaves.endsWith("\r\n"));
    }

## 1. What the inspected MO-IT110 peer implementation says

The supplied peer review copy at `/home/user/repo_review/full_repo/testingester-main/6/-/` contains an explicit, testable candidate model:

- `src/motorph/model/AttendanceRecord.java`: first cutoff is days 1–15; second cutoff is day 16 through actual month end. Login from 08:00 through 08:10 is treated as 08:00; logout after 17:00 is capped at 17:00. It calculates elapsed time directly from those adjusted times and does **not** subtract a meal interval.

- `src/motorph/model/Employee.java`: gross is hourly rate times the calculated minutes. The course-project fixtures also supply semi-monthly and hourly rates.

[NODE 4506]
A key flaw: its 8:00–17:00 attendance calculation counts nine hours because it doesn’t deduct a meal break. DOLE’s Book III describes an eight-hour normal workday and a meal period of at least 60 minutes off work, so those two attendance times alone don’t establish hours worked. DOLE Book III

[NODE 4507]
I also found a current statutory net-pay reference, ph-payroll. Its documented synthetic example gives ₱22,611.25 net from ₱25,000 monthly basic pay, but it is not an end-to-end attendance or cutoff payroll system. Its annualized withholding result is ₱313.75; reading the rounded threshold in the BIR monthly table gives ₱313.80 for the same taxable amount. That ₱0.05 difference needs resolving before using it as an oracle. The library’s employerCost field is employer contributions only, not salary plus contributions. Library example · BIR Annex E

/home/user/uploads/MotorPH_Payroll_System_Full_Synthesis.md:1935:The database schema describes where records and values are stored and how tables are related. The DFD describes how actors and processes move or update those records. A DFD store such as `D2 Logs` can encompass several relational tables, and a process such as `2.5 Basic Payroll Computation` can consume several stores. Do not assume a DFD data store is exactly one database table unless a source statement confirms it.

1.​   Database Overview
      The MotorPH Payroll System database is built in a way to allow users to automate,
      organise, and streamline MotorPH payroll processes systematically to provide the
      prerogative of having minimal struggle in handling the payroll operations so that users
      may allocate efforts unto more substantially demanding tasks. Through the
      centralisation of most payroll-related data into a singular, secure, and scalable
      repository, the system facilitates rapid data retrieval and processing, which becomes
      indispensable for timely salary computations, tax management, and adherence to legal
      contributions and compliance. Thus, for this instance, we deliver an expectation that
      this database will not just bring about changes in improvement with data derivation
      and the alleviation of unnecessary exertion but also an effective means through which
      future growth of the organisation may be facilitated at incorporation through adaptive
      mechanisms for data expansion.
         1.​ Employee Management – Captures, updates, and maintains employee records,
             including employment status, department affiliation, salary structure, and
             personal information; this module serves as the primary reference for all
             modules, with nearly every module being eventually tied back to this module’s
             unique identifier.
         2.​ Payroll Processing – Automates payroll computation, taking into account
             attendance records, salary adjustments, overtime hours, tax deductions, and
             government-mandated contributions (SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, Withholding
             Tax). The system

import java.util.Scanner;

public class PayrollCalculator {

    public static void calculatePayroll() {

        Scanner input = new Scanner(System.in);

        System.out.println("=== Payroll Calculator ===");

        System.out.print("Enter Hours Worked: ");
        double hoursWorked = input.nextDouble();

        System.out.print("Enter Hourly Rate: ");
        double hourlyRate = input.nextDouble();

        double grossSalary = hoursWorked * hourlyRate;

        double sss = grossSalary * 0.045;
        double philhealth = grossSalary * 0.02;
        double pagibig = 100;

        double totalDeductions = sss + philhealth + pagibig;
        double netSalary = grossSalary - totalDeductions;

        System.out.println("\n--- Payroll Details ---");
        System.out.println("Gross Salary: " + grossSalary);
        System.out.println("SSS Deduction: " + sss);
        System.out.println("PhilHealth Deduction: " + philhealth);
        System.out.println("Pag-IBIG Deduction: " + pagibig);
        System.out.println("Total Deductions: " + totalDeductions);
        System.out.println("Net Salary: " + netSalary);
    }
}
