function renderWorkflow() {
  if (!document.getElementById('leave-request-rows')) return;
  const leaveRequests = state.workflow.leaveRequests;
  const filteredLeaves = sortWorkflowItems(filterWorkflowItems(leaveRequests, {
    query: document.getElementById('leave-filter-search').value,
    status: document.getElementById('leave-filter-status').value,
    type: document.getElementById('leave-filter-type').value,
    typeField: 'leaveType',
    searchFields: ['id', 'employeeId', 'employeeName', 'leaveType', 'startDate', 'endDate'],
    dateRange: {
      from: document.getElementById('leave-filter-from').value,
      to: document.getElementById('leave-filter-to').value,
      startField: 'startDate',
      endField: 'endDate'
    }
  }), {
    field: document.getElementById('leave-sort').value,
    direction: document.getElementById('leave-sort-order').value
  });
  state.visibleLeaveRequests = filteredLeaves;
  const leaveRows = document.getElementById('leave-request-rows');
  leaveRows.replaceChildren();
  if (!leaveRequests.length) {
    showWorkflowTableMessage(leaveRows, 6, 'No session requests yet.');
  } else if (!filteredLeaves.length) {
    showWorkflowTableMessage(leaveRows, 6, 'No requests match these filters.');
  } else {
    filteredLeaves.forEach(request => {
      const row = document.createElement('tr');
      [request.id, `${request.employeeName} · ${request.employeeId}`, request.leaveType,
        `${request.startDate} — ${request.endDate}`].forEach(value => row.append(makeCell(value)));
      row.append(makeCell(makeWorkflowStatus(request.status)));
      const actions = document.createElement('div');
      actions.className = 'workflow-row-actions';
      actions.append(makeWorkflowDetails(request, 'leave'));
      if (request.status === 'Pending review') actions.append(makeCancelButton('cancel-leave', request, request.employeeId, 'Cancel'));
      row.append(makeCell(actions));
      leaveRows.append(row);
    });
  }
  document.getElementById('leave-request-count').textContent = `Showing ${filteredLeaves.length} of ${leaveRequests.length} ${leaveRequests.length === 1 ? 'request' : 'requests'} in this sandbox`;

  const tickets = state.workflow.tickets;
  const filteredTickets = sortWorkflowItems(filterWorkflowItems(tickets, {
    query: document.getElementById('ticket-filter-search').value,
    status: document.getElementById('ticket-filter-status').value,
    type: document.getElementById('ticket-filter-type').value,
    typeField: 'ticketType',
    searchFields: ['id', 'employeeId', 'employeeName', 'ticketType', 'queue', 'summary']
  }), {
    field: document.getElementById('ticket-sort').value,
    direction: document.getElementById('ticket-sort-order').value
  });
  state.visibleTickets = filteredTickets;
  const ticketRows = document.getElementById('ticket-rows');
  ticketRows.replaceChildren();
  if (!tickets.length) {
    showWorkflowTableMessage(ticketRows, 6, 'No session tickets yet.');
  } else if (!filteredTickets.length) {
    showWorkflowTableMessage(ticketRows, 6, 'No tickets match these filters.');
  } else {
    filteredTickets.forEach(ticket => {
      const row = document.createElement('tr');
      [ticket.id, `${ticket.employeeName} · ${ticket.employeeId}`, ticket.ticketType, ticket.queue]
        .forEach(value => row.append(makeCell(value)));
      row.append(makeCell(makeWorkflowStatus(ticket.status)));
      const actions = document.createElement('div');
      actions.className = 'workflow-row-actions';
      actions.append(makeWorkflowDetails(ticket, 'ticket'));
      if (ticket.status === 'Open') actions.append(makeCancelButton('cancel-ticket', ticket, ticket.employeeId, 'Cancel'));
      row.append(makeCell(actions));
      ticketRows.append(row);
    });
  }
  document.getElementById('ticket-count').textContent = `Showing ${filteredTickets.length} of ${tickets.length} ${tickets.length === 1 ? 'ticket' : 'tickets'} in this sandbox`;
  document.getElementById('leave-export-button').disabled = leaveRequests.length === 0;
  document.getElementById('leave-visible-export-button').disabled = filteredLeaves.length === 0;
  document.getElementById('ticket-export-button').disabled = tickets.length === 0;
  document.getElementById('ticket-visible-export-button').disabled = filteredTickets.length === 0;
  const overviewWorkflowCount = document.getElementById('overview-workflow-count');
  if (overviewWorkflowCount) overviewWorkflowCount.textContent = String(leaveRequests.length + tickets.length).padStart(2, '0');
  renderWorkflowSummary();
  renderEmployeeRecordSummary();
  renderLeaveCalendar();
}

function renderWorkflowSummary() {
  const summaryRows = workflowSummaryRows(state.workflow.leaveRequests, state.workflow.tickets);
  const body = document.getElementById('workflow-summary-rows');
  body.replaceChildren();
  if (!summaryRows.length) {
    showWorkflowTableMessage(body, 3, 'No synthetic workflow records are available for this summary.');
  } else {
    summaryRows.forEach(summary => {
      const row = document.createElement('tr');
      [summary.category, summary.label, String(summary.recordCount)].forEach(value => row.append(makeCell(value)));
      body.append(row);
    });
  }
  const recordTotal = state.workflow.leaveRequests.length + state.workflow.tickets.length;
  document.getElementById('workflow-summary-count').textContent = `${summaryRows.length} stored-label rows · ${recordTotal} workflow records`;
  document.getElementById('workflow-summary-export').disabled = summaryRows.length === 0;
}

function renderEmployeeRecordSummary() {
  const summary = employeeRecordSummary(state.allEmployees, state.attendanceReport,
    state.workflow.leaveRequests, state.workflow.tickets);
  state.employeeRecordSummary = summary;
  const visible = filterAndSortEmployeeRecordSummary(summary, {
    query: document.getElementById('employee-record-summary-search').value,
    mapping: document.getElementById('employee-record-summary-mapping').value,
    sortBy: document.getElementById('employee-record-summary-sort').value,
    direction: document.getElementById('employee-record-summary-order').value
  });
  state.visibleEmployeeRecordSummary = visible;
  const body = document.getElementById('employee-record-summary-rows');
  if (!body) return;
  body.replaceChildren();
  if (!summary.length) {
    showWorkflowTableMessage(body, 7, 'No synthetic employees are available for this summary.');
  } else if (!visible.length) {
    showWorkflowTableMessage(body, 7, 'No employee rows match these filters.');
  } else {
    visible.forEach(item => {
      const row = document.createElement('tr');
      [
        `${item.employeeName} · ${item.employeeId}`,
        item.hasScheduleMapping ? 'Mapped' : 'No mapping',
        String(item.rawRecordCount),
        item.firstRecordDate || '—',
        item.lastRecordDate || '—',
        String(item.leaveRequestCount),
        String(item.ticketCount)
      ].forEach(value => row.append(makeCell(value)));
      body.append(row);
    });
  }
  document.getElementById('employee-record-summary-count').textContent = `Showing ${visible.length} of ${summary.length} employee rows · stored counts only`;
  document.getElementById('employee-record-summary-export').disabled = summary.length === 0;
  document.getElementById('employee-record-summary-visible-export').disabled = visible.length === 0;
}

function friendlyAuthError(error) {
  const code = error && error.code || '';
  if (code === 'auth/operation-not-allowed') return 'Email/Password sign-in is disabled. Enable it in Firebase Console → Authentication → Sign-in method.';
  if (code === 'auth/unauthorized-domain') return 'This preview domain is not authorized. Add its host under Firebase Console → Authentication → Settings → Authorized domains, or test on localhost.';
  if (code === 'auth/invalid-api-key' || code === 'auth/api-key-not-valid.-please-pass-a-valid-api-key.') return 'The Firebase Web API key in .env.local is missing or invalid.';
  if (code === 'auth/email-already-in-use') return 'That email already has a Firebase account. Use Sign in instead.';
  if (code === 'auth/weak-password') return 'Use a password with at least six characters.';
  if (code === 'auth/invalid-email') return 'Enter a valid email address.';
  if (code === 'auth/too-many-requests') return 'Too many attempts. Wait a few minutes and try again.';
  if (code === 'auth/invalid-credential' || code === 'auth/wrong-password' || code === 'auth/user-not-found') return 'Email or password is incorrect.';
  return error && error.message ? error.message : 'Firebase sign-in could not be completed.';
}

async function signIn() {
  setAuthError('');
  document.getElementById('auth-reset-status').textContent = '';
  try {
    await signInWithEmailAndPassword(auth, authEmail.value.trim(), authPassword.value);
  } catch (error) {
    setAuthError(friendlyAuthError(error));
  }
}

# MotorPH MS2 — browser payroll foundation

An original browser-based prototype with an HTML/CSS interface and Java 11 backend. Employee and attendance data are synthetic. It includes a disposable, client-only 2026 statutory preview with editable/versioned rules; attendance-derived payroll, persisted runs, and payslips remain gated.

## Run locally

Requires JDK 11+, Node.js 20.19+ (or a current supported Node release), and npm.

```sh
npm install
./run.sh
```

Then open <http://localhost:8080>. `run.sh` builds the Vite frontend and serves it from the Java server. Set `PORT` to choose a different HTTP port.

For development with Vite hot reload, use two terminals:

```sh
# terminal 1: Java backend
./run-api.sh

# terminal 2: frontend
npm run dev
```

Open <http://localhost:5173>. Vite proxies `/api` calls to the Java service at `http://127.0.0.1:8080` by default; set `API_PROXY_TARGET` to use a different backend. Set `HOST=127.0.0.1` for the Java backend when Vite is proxying it locally.

Run Java domain checks:

```sh
./test.sh
```

Run browser end-to-end checks (the suite starts isolated local API/Vite processes, uses only synthetic in-memory records, and cleans them up on exit):

```sh
npx playwright-core install chromium
# Linux, if system libraries are missing:
sudo npx playwright-core install-deps chromium
npm run test:e2e
```

Optional live Firebase Auth lifecycle smoke test:

```sh
npm run test:firebase-auth
```

This uses `.env.local`, creates one uniquely named disposable Auth account, verifies sign-in, empty user-scoped reads, and sign-out on localhost, makes **no Firestore writes**, and deletes the Auth account in cleanup. It needs network access and should not be run concurrently with another live Auth test.

The app uses a small vendored Gson JAR for the Java Firestore REST adapter; its license is recorded in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and `third_party/licenses/`.

## Firebase development sandbox

- `.env.local` contains the Firebase **Web** app config used by the browser SDK; `.gitignore` lists this file. The user-supplied Web API key for `motorph-jd` is installed assistant-side. The user does not need to edit `.env.local`.
- The Web API key is a public client identifier, not a server credential. Do not add a service-account key or Admin SDK credentials.
- Authentication uses Email/Password and in-memory browser persistence. Live disposable-account creation/sign-in, empty user-scoped reads, and sign-out now pass on localhost; the test Auth account was deleted. Do not use real staff accounts or data.
- Firestore requests are made by the Java backend through the REST API, forwarding the signed-in user's Firebase ID token. Firestore Security Rules authorize those requests; no privileged server identity bypasses the rules.
- The app uses `users/{uid}/demoEmployees`, `demoAttendance`, `demoLeaveRequests`, and `demoTickets`. Workflow documents are owner-scoped with no reviewer or delete permission in the candidate rules. The opt-in seed writes fictional employee/attendance records only.
- The user published the updated `docs/firestore.rules`. Live Firebase smoke testing with disposable accounts verified owner-scoped employee create/update, leave and ticket create/cancel/read-back, and a cross-user denial (`403`). Both disposable Auth accounts and employee documents were deleted; one cancelled synthetic leave and one cancelled synthetic ticket remain under their deleted test UIDs because workflow deletes are intentionally denied (`LV-3502C01F0E60`, `TK-F05DD2B0D6CC`). No real employee data or credentials were used. These are **development-only** rules, not production role/HR policy.
- If Firebase is not configured locally, the app uses the in-memory synthetic fixture. No Firebase writes are made in that mode.
- `measurementId` / Firebase Analytics is not used.
- Browser auth is verified on `localhost`. The current Arena preview host is `8080-is3s38ic4lxn7e4e77g8b.e2b.app`; its authorized-domain status could not be tested from the sandbox because Arena's traffic-access token is injected only in the user preview session. If the preview reports `auth/unauthorized-domain`, add that exact host under Firebase Console → Authentication → Settings → Authorized domains.

See `docs/firebase-setup-guide.md` for the console checkpoint and `docs/firestore.rules` for the development rules.

## What works

- Overview with live sandbox counts, searchable employee directory/detail, employee directory sort controls, HR directory search/status filters/sorting, synthetic directory/workflow label-count summaries, searchable/mapped-filterable/sortable employee-linked record counts with all/visible CSV, sortable raw attendance register with a raw-only month calendar and searchable/filterable/sortable coverage report, cross-module sandbox search/export, Requests & tickets, searchable/sortable read-only Team roster with read-only detail view, and a temporary 2026 monthly statutory preview. Employee details open from a native keyboard-operable button without overriding table semantics; result counts and form feedback use polite status regions.
- Java employee/attendance services plus a workflow service. Local preview workflow and raw attendance-entry records are held in Java process memory; Firebase mode uses the signed-in user’s Firestore subcollections. Raw attendance remains read-only in Firebase mode.
- Leave requests and tickets validate inputs, derive employee names from the caller’s own synthetic directory, show documented queue labels, and support owner-sandbox cancellation. A monthly leave-request calendar displays pending/cancelled request dates only and can draft form bounds from two selected dates; it does not imply approval, submit a request, calculate days, or show balances. Search/status/type and inclusive requested-date-overlap filters, plus selectable table sorting, narrow the leave history display only; they do not change the calendar markers. Separate CSV controls export visible or all records. Row details reveal the submitted note/message and UTC timestamps without adding a reviewer workflow. Both local and Firestore workflow histories default to newest first; optional table sorting does not change storage order or all-record exports. Ticket lists also filter by stored type; workflow tables offer visible-only or all-record CSV export. No reviewer/approval/resolve/delete routes exist. The user has published the rules; live tests confirmed leave and ticket create/cancel persistence, plus cross-user denial.
- Read-only Team roster plus a synthetic directory editor. In Firebase mode, signed-in users can create/edit only name, department, role label, location, and demo status in their own sandbox. Local preview has no user authentication and shares one process-memory store for that API process. IDs are server-generated; delete, termination, schedule, salary, and government-ID fields are not exposed. New employees receive no schedule mapping, so attendance queries remain empty and raw capture rejects them rather than assigning one. A local-only attendance form can create a raw DEMO row for existing mapped synthetic employees; it enforces unique schedule/date and time order. Firebase attendance stays read-only; no correction, hours, or payroll calculation is included. This is not an HR role or a production employee-admin workflow.
- Employee detail now includes a read-only employee-specific ledger of raw attendance times and stored leave/ticket labels. The attendance register adds a month calendar showing only loaded raw row dates/times; selecting two dates applies an inclusive raw-record filter. Blank dates do not mean absence or unworked.
- CSV export for currently visible synthetic employee results, filtered HR directory and Team roster rows, loaded raw attendance rows, visible attendance coverage rows, synthetic directory, workflow label-count, and employee-linked count summaries, and either visible or all owner-sandbox workflow records. A read-only workspace JSON bundle and cross-module search use only owner-scoped GETs and include no payroll preview inputs, credentials, calculated hours, or pay. CSV cells are quoted and spreadsheet-formula prefixes are neutralized.
- Temporary monthly 2026 statutory preview: explicit separate fictional bases, SSS MSC/employee/employer/EC, PhilHealth employee/employer shares, Pag-IBIG employee/employer shares, BIR monthly withholding, net estimate and employer contribution cost. Logic is isolated in versioned rules/calculator modules; it is client-side only, is not retained, and can be exported as a clearly labelled preview CSV that is not a payslip.
- Server-side employee search/detail, HR table search/status filters, a user-scoped attendance-coverage report (raw row counts and first/last record dates by configured mapping), synthetic directory label counts by status/department plus workflow label counts by status/type/queue, both with CSV export, and dynamic overview counts. Unmapped employees are labeled as unmapped, not absent. The attendance date fields default to that employee's earliest/latest available records, following the earlier MO-IT108 Requirements Analysis; the user can narrow the range. This is not a payroll-period calendar. The attendance API and reports do not derive hours or pay; the separate statutory preview uses only manually entered synthetic monthly bases.
- Firebase email/password sign-in, development-account creation, and password-reset email UI; reset responses do not disclose whether an email has an account. The app stays behind the sign-in gate when Firebase config is complete.
- `/api/health`, employee list/search/detail plus owner-sandbox create/update, raw attendance query and coverage report, a local-process-memory-only raw attendance create route, owner-scoped workflow list/create/cancel routes, and opt-in demo seed endpoint.
- Verification: `npm run test:web` passes 59 workflow/calendar/filter/sort/summary/CSV/search/workspace-expo

function switchView(view) {
  const labels = { overview: 'Overview', employees: 'Employees', attendance: 'Attendance', requests: 'Requests & tickets', team: 'Team roster', hr: 'HR operations', reports: 'Reports', payroll: 'Payroll' };
  if (!labels[view]) return;
  document.querySelectorAll('.page-view').forEach(page => {
    page.hidden = page.id !== `${view}-view`;
  });
  document.querySelectorAll('.nav-item').forEach(nav => {
    const active = nav.dataset.view === view;
    nav.classList.toggle('active', active);
    if (active) nav.setAttribute('aria-current', 'page');
    else nav.removeAttribute('aria-current');
  });
  document.getElementById('crumb-current').textContent = labels[view];
  document.title = `${labels[view]} — MotorPH Payroll Office`;
  if (view === 'attendance' && attendanceEmployee.value) loadAttendance();
  if (view === 'reports') loadAttendanceReport();
}

document.querySelectorAll('.nav-item').forEach(item => {
  item.addEventListener('click', () => switchView(item.dataset.view));
});

              <p><strong>SSS:</strong> 2025 schedule remains the latest published contribution table found for the 2026 preview; employee 5% and employer 10% apply to MSC up to ₱35,000, with EC ₱10/₱30 paid by employer. <a href="https://www.sss.gov.ph/pay-contribution/">SSS contribution schedule</a></p>
              <p><strong>PhilHealth:</strong> 5% of monthly basic salary with ₱10,000 floor/₱100,000 ceiling, split equally. Commission, overtime and allowances are excluded from the MBS base. <a href="https://www.philhealth.gov.ph/advisories/2025/PA2025-0002.pdf">PA2025-0002</a></p>
              <p><strong>Pag-IBIG:</strong> MFS ceiling ₱10,000; employee 1% at ₱1,500 and below or 2% above; employer 2%. <a href="https://www.pagibigfund.gov.ph/documents/Circular%20No.%20460%20-%20Guidelines%20on%20the%20Pag-IBIG%20Fund's%20Implementation%20of%20Increase%20in%20the%20MFS%20Effective%20February%202024.pdf">Circular No. 460</a></p>
              <p><strong>BIR:</strong> uses the published monthly withholding table from Annex E to RR 11-2018 (effective 2023 onward), not the annualized method used by one third-party library. The monthly/annualized example differs by ₱0.05. <a href="https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/local/pdf/Annex%20E%20RR%2011-2018.pdf">BIR Annex E</a></p>
              <p>All bases are typed separately by the user, and centavo rounding is a provisional half-up rule. No employee status, eligibility, semi-monthly deduction split, non-cash benefits, 13th-month annualisation, or tax adjustment is inferred.</p>

import test from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { buildWorkspaceExport } from '../../web/workspace-export.js';

const date = new Date('2026-11-04T02:00:00.000Z');

test('builds a synthetic sandbox bundle with employee-grouped raw rows and stored workflows', () => {
  const employees = [{ id: 'DEMO-001', name: 'Mara Rivera' }];
  const leaveRequests = [{ id: 'LV-1', employeeId: 'DEMO-001', status: 'Pending review' }];
  const tickets = [{ id: 'TK-1', employeeId: 'DEMO-001', status: 'Open' }];
  const bundle = buildWorkspaceExport({
    mode: 'firebase-user-sandbox',
    employees,
    leaveRequests,
    tickets,
    attendanceByEmployee: {
      'DEMO-001': [{ attendanceId: 5001, employeeId: 'UNTRUSTED', date: '2026-10-01', timeIn: '08:01', timeOut: '17:00', dayType: 'DEMO' }],
      'DEMO-NEW': []
    }
  }, date);

  assert.equal(bundle.formatVersion, 1);
  assert.equal(bundle.exportedAt, '2026-11-04T02:00:00.000Z');
  assert.equal(bundle.storageMode, 'firebase-user-sandbox');
  assert.equal(bundle.syntheticOnly, true);
  assert.equal(bundle.hoursCalculated, false);
  assert.equal(bundle.payrollIncluded, false);
  assert.deepEqual(bundle.employees, employees);
  assert.deepEqual(bundle.attendance, [{ employeeId: 'DEMO-001', attendanceId: 5001, date: '2026-10-01', timeIn: '08:01', timeOut: '17:00', dayType: 'DEMO' }]);
  assert.deepEqual(bundle.leaveRequests, leaveRequests);
  assert.deepEqual(bundle.tickets, tickets);
  assert.ok(!JSON.stringify(bundle).includes('netPay'));
});

test('returns empty arrays for missing data without inventing rows', () => {
  const bundle = buildWorkspaceExport({}, date);
  assert.deepEqual(bundle.employees, []);
  assert.deepEqual(bundle.attendance, []);
  assert.deepEqual(bundle.leaveRequests, []);
  assert.deepEqual(bundle.tickets, []);
  assert.equal(bundle.syntheticOnly, true);
});

test('rejects malformed collections, attendance groups, and timestamps', () => {
  assert.throws(() => buildWorkspaceExport({ employees: {} }, date), /collections must be arrays/);
  assert.throws(() => buildWorkspaceExport({ attendanceByEmployee: [] }, date), /grouped by employee ID/);
  assert.throws(() => buildWorkspaceExport({ attendanceByEmployee: { 'DEMO-001': {} } }, date), /must be an array/);
  assert.throws(() => buildWorkspaceExport({ attendanceByEmployee: { 'DEMO-001': [null] } }, date), /must be an object/);
  assert.throws(() => buildWorkspaceExport({}, '2026-11-04'), /valid export timestamp/);
});

# MotorPH MS2 — persistent-workspace foundation
2
3
An original browser application with a Java 11 HTTP API, Vite frontend, Firebase Authentication, and user-scoped Firestore storage. The current dataset is **synthetic only**. This repository is an in-progress foundation, not a complete payroll or HR product.
4
5
## Runtime policy
6
7
- The normal Java entry point refuses to start without `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID`; it no longer silently serves process-memory data.
8
- The browser refuses to open the workspace when Firebase web configuration is missing. There is no production local-preview fallback.
9
- The test suite has an explicitly isolated synthetic fixture mode bound to loopback. It is not enabled by `run.sh` or `run-api.sh`, and it is used only for automated tests.
10
- No temporary payroll calculator, payroll preview, or downloadable estimated payslip is included. Payroll calculations are disabled until the unresolved rules and authorization boundaries are approved.
… 54 more lines

[NODE 6237]
1
# Build status — persistent-only target
2
3
**This document supersedes earlier statements that a process-memory product mode or a temporary payroll preview is an acceptable deliverable.** The user's current requirement is “No locals, no temps.” No peer implementation or earlier policy candidate changes that requirement.
4
5
## Product behavior now enforced
6
7
- `AppServer.main` requires `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID`. The only no-Firebase entry-point exception is `MOTORPH_TEST_MODE=true` while binding to a loopback host; the production run scripts do not set it. Direct constructor-based local services remain test fixtures used by the isolated test harness, not a supported deployment mode.
8
- `web/app.js` does not open the workspace if Firebase web configuration is missing. It shows a setup error instead. The unauthenticated local workspace is available only in the test build flag `VITE_E2E_TEST_MODE=true` used by the test runner.
9
- Removed the browser-only 2026 payroll preview, rule table, preview CSV, preview UI/CSS, and preview-specific unit tests. The Payroll view now shows a blocking configuration page and calculates nothing.
10
- The test-only synthetic fixture remains intentionally process-memory-backed so the UI/API contract can be exercised without using real staff data or writing test records to a live Firebase project. This is test infrastructure, not a deployable local-data feature.

# Local-only inventory, current behavior, and full-build pseudocode

**Status date:** 2026-11-04  
**Purpose:** identify every behavior that is genuinely local-only, explain its contents and implementation paths, state what would be required to make it durable/non-local, and provide pseudocode for the current build and the remaining full-system work. This is an engineering inventory—not a claim that the app is a complete or production-ready payroll system.

## 1. Current build status

The current project is a working synthetic-data prototype with local process-memory mode and Firebase user-sandbox mode. It has a limited but verified set of employee, raw-attendance, leave/ticket, reporting, and statutory-preview features.

Latest recorded verification: **59 web tests, 181 Java checks, Playwright E2E, production build, and dependency audit with 0 vulnerabilities**. The exact Arena preview-origin Firebase sign-in and production deployment are not verified.

The project’s rough estimate is about **72% broad feature parity**, or about **66% when local-only raw attendance creation and the browser-only statutory preview are excluded**. The user’s earlier 75% non-local target was not met before this documentation request; this estimate is not a grade or code-coverage score. The latest instruction now requests a full non-local build and permits adapting prior submissions as candidate logic. No Firebase Rules, Cloud Functions, or live Firebase data were changed or deployed in response. See `docs/peer-parity-roadmap.md` for the denominator and remaining feature gates.

## 2. What is genuinely local-only

“Local-only” here means that behavior either uses the unauthenticated Java process-memory store or is performed only in the browser without a durable server record. Some screens are available in both modes and therefore are **not** local-only even though their filtering/rendering runs in JavaScript.

| Local-only item | What it does | Contents / implementation | What must change for a non-local or durable version |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Local preview identity/storage mode | Runs without sign-in when Firebase is not configured. Changes are shared by callers of that API process and disappear when it stops. | `AppServer` selects local stores when no Firebase project is configured. `InMemoryEmployeeStore`, `InMemoryWorkflowStore`, and `InMemoryAttendanceStore` hold synthetic records in process memory. The UI labels this `LOCAL PREVIEW` / `Local API memory`. | For multi-user durability, require authenticated Firebase identity, use only `users/{uid}/...` paths, enforce rules on the server, and define a deliberate migration/import process. Do not silently copy shared local rows into a user account; there is no employee-account identity mapping today. |
| Local raw-attendance create | Creates a raw row only in local in-memory demo mode. It does not edit or delete existing rows. | `MutableAttendanceStore.java` exposes create. `InMemoryAttendanceStore.java` synchronizes insertion and checks unique `(scheduleID,date)`. `AttendanceService.createForEmployee` verifies an existing employee and existing schedule mapping, passes the server-selected schedule ID, and fixes `dayType` to `DEMO`. `AppServer.handleAttendanceCreate` accepts exactly employee ID/date/time-in/time-out, returns `201` plus `storage=local-process-memory`, and returns `403` in Firebase mode. UI lives in `web/index.html` and `web/app.js`. | Add a durable, authenticated store implementation; ensure the employee and schedule mapping are owned by the signed-in UID; enforce unique schedule/date atomically under concurrent requests; allocate durable IDs; add security-rule or trusted-server tests; and test deny cases. Firestore rules currently do not make this write path safe/transactional. The current route intentionally rejects Firebase mode. A client-supplied `scheduleID` or `dayType` must remain rejected. **No Firebase attendance write is present in the current build.** |
| Temporary statutory preview | Computes a disposable monthly estimate from values manually entered in the browser. It is not a saved payroll run. | `web/payroll-rules-2026.js` holds a replaceable rules profile; `web/payroll-preview-2026.js` calculates in integer centavos; `web/payroll-preview-ui.js` renders input/result and preview CSV. Inputs and result stay in the browser. The E2E verifies no payroll API request. | This is not “local mode only”: it can appear in the frontend regardless of Firebase configuration, but it is still **browser-only and non-persistent**. Making it a shared cloud payroll service requires approved period, tax/base, rounding, benefit, salary-conversion, attendance, authorization, audit, and persistence decisions; then a versioned backend calculation service, access rules, immutable run inputs/results, and golden expected-value tests. Do not connect it to attendance or save payslips before those decisions are approved. |
| Local-only E2E environment | Proves the local browser flow against a disposable local Java API and test data. | `test/e2e/local-workflows.e2e.js` launches a local API and Vite server with Firebase config blank. It tests UI and API behavior but does not establish that the Arena preview origin or a live Firebase deployment works. | Keep these fast tests, and add Firebase Emulator/API contract tests for signed-in reads/writes and rule denials. A live preview-origin smoke still needs the exact authorized domain and a disposable account. Do not use undeletable workflow records for repeated smoke tests. |
| Downloaded workspace JSON | A client-created file download, not cloud backup/restore. | `web/workspace-export.js` creates a synthetic-only snapshot with employee records, raw attendance rows, leave requests and tickets; it marks `hoursCalculated:false` and `payrollIncluded:false`. `fetchSandboxSnapshot()` obtains data through GET APIs. | No change is needed for reading the current user’s Firebase sandbox; the bundle already uses scoped GETs when signed in. To restore/import the file into Firebase, add a separately designed import path, duplicate-ID handling, schema versioning, per-collection validation, user ownership checks, and preview/confirm/rollback behavior. Current export is not a restore function or automated backup. |

### Local-only feature file contents

- `src/main/java/ph/motorph/web/MutableAttendanceStore.java` — the writable interface limited to creating a raw `AttendanceRecord` from schedule ID, date, times, and fixed day type.
- `src/main/java/ph/motorph/web/InMemoryAttendanceStore.java` — synthetic attendance fixtures and synchronized in-memory create/duplicate check; store lifetime is the Java process.
- `src/main/java/ph/motorph/web/AttendanceService.java` — employee existence check, existing mapping lookup, mutable-store check, fixed `DEMO` assignment; it does not create mappings or calculate hours.
- `src/main/java/ph/motorph/web/AppServer.java` — POST route whitelist, date/time parsing, local-mode guard, JSON response and status codes. Firebase mode is rejected before store access.
- `web/index.html` — the local-only attendance form, explanatory boundary text, raw-record calendar, report/export/search UI.
- `web/app.js` — posts local raw input, loads scoped reads, renders the calendar and reports, cross-module search, JSON export, and employee-linked record details. `showWorkspace(user)` hides the create form for signed-in Firebase users.
- `web/payroll-rules-2026.js`, `web/payroll-preview-2026.js`, `web/payroll-preview-ui.js` — browser-only temporary statutory preview profile/calculator/UI; no persisted run.
- `test/java/ph/motorph/web/AttendanceServiceTest.java` and `AppServerIntegrationTest.java` — domain/API checks for mapping, fixed DEMO label, uniqueness, time order, schedule injection rejection, and Firebase POST rejection.
- `test/e2e/local-workflows.e2e.js` — local browser coverage including create success/rejections, calendars, exports, search, JSON bundle, and no-page-error/mobile checks.
- `docs/local-demo-inventory.md` — shorter local-vs-Firebase summary; this file is the more complete implementation inventory and pseudocode.

## 3. Capabilities that are not local-only

These currently use existing owner-scoped GET APIs and work in local preview and Firebase user-sandbox mode, subject to the user having access to the signed-in sandbox:

- Employee list/search/detail, allowlisted synthetic directory create/update, and HR/Team views.
- Raw attendance GET by employee and optional inclusive date range; Firebase attendance is read-only.
- Owner-scoped leave/ticket GET/create/cancel routes with existing field validation and published user-sandbox rules.
- Attendance coverage report, raw attendance calendar/date selection, employee-linked record detail/count summaries, cross-module search, CSV exports, and the read-only workspace JSON download.
- The local attendance *create* form is not shared; it is hidden in Firebase mode and its API returns `403` there.

No client-side report in this list infers absent/present/tardy status, hours, overtime, leave balances, approval, eligibility, or pay. Stored status/type/queue labels are displayed as labels only.

# Local-only inventory, current behavior, and full-build pseudocode

**Status date:** 2026-11-04  
**Purpose:** identify every behavior that is genuinely local-only, explain its contents and implementation paths, state what would be required to make it durable/non-local, and provide pseudocode for the current build and the remaining full-system work. This is an engineering inventory—not a claim that the app is a complete or production-ready payroll system.

> **Superseding status:** this inventory records code paths and pseudocode from the earlier prototype. Since the current “no locals, no temps” instruction, the normal API entry point now requires Firebase, the browser fails closed without Firebase, and the temporary payroll preview was removed. Process-memory stores and local attendance-entry behavior remain only inside the loopback-isolated test fixture. The active status is `docs/build-status-no-local-no-temp.md`; do not read older rows below as authorization to expose these paths in the product.

## 1. Current build status

The earlier prototype had local process-memory and temporary payroll paths. The current product entry points require Firebase and no longer expose the temporary payroll preview; only the automated loopback fixture exercises in-memory data. Persistent capabilities and outstanding gates are summarized in `docs/build-status-no-local-no-temp.md`.

The earlier 59-test baseline predates the removal of the temporary preview. Current verification is recorded in `docs/build-status-no-local-no-temp.md`; re-run dependency audit after any dependency change. The exact Arena preview-origin Firebase sign-in and production deployment are not verified.

The project’s rough estimate is about **72% broad feature parity**, or about **66% when local-only raw attendance creation and the browser-only statutory preview are excluded**. The user’s earlier 75% non-local target was not met before this documentation request; this estimate is not a grade or code-coverage score. The latest instruction now requests a full non-local build and permits adapting prior submissions as candidate logic. No Firebase Rules, Cloud Functions, or live Firebase data were changed or deployed in response. See `docs/peer-parity-roadmap.md` for the denominator and remaining feature gates.

## 2. What is genuinely local-only

“Local-only” here means that behavior either uses the unauthenticated Java process-memory store or is performed only in the browser without a durable server record. Some screens are available in both modes and therefore are **not** local-only even though their filtering/rendering runs in JavaScript.

| Local-only item | What it does | Contents / implementation | What must change for a non-local or durable version |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Isolated in-memory test fixture | Automated browser/API checks exercise synthetic data without writing to live Firebase. It is not a product runtime. | The E2E harness explicitly sets the loopback-only `MOTORPH_TEST_MODE` and `VITE_E2E_TEST_MODE` flags. Normal run scripts do not set these; the production API and browser fail closed if Firebase is missing. | Keep this isolated to test-only invocation, bind to loopback, and never migrate test rows into a user account. The current test coverage does not prove live Firebase behavior. |
| Local raw-attendance create | Creates a raw row only in local in-memory demo mode. It does not edit or delete existing rows. | `MutableAttendanceStore.java` exposes create. `InMemoryAttendanceStore.java` synchronizes insertion and checks unique `(scheduleID,date)`. `AttendanceService.createForEmployee` verifies an existing employee and existing schedule mapping, passes the server-selected schedule ID, and fixes `dayType` to `DEMO`. `AppServer.handleAttendanceCreate` accepts exactly employee ID/date/time-in/time-out, returns `201` plus `storage=local-process-memory`, and returns `403` in Firebase mode. UI lives in `web/index.html` and `web/app.js`. | Add a durable, authenticated store implementation; ensure the employee and schedule mapping are owned by the signed-in UID; enforce unique schedule/date atomically under concurrent requests; allocate durable IDs; add security-rule or trusted-server tests; and test deny cases. Firestore rules currently do not make this write path safe/transactional. The current route intentionally rejects Firebase mode. A client-supplied `scheduleID` or `dayType` must remain rejected. **No Firebase attendance write is present in the current build.** |

It tests UI and API behavior but does not establish that the Arena preview origin or a live Firebase deployment works. | Keep these fast tests, and add Firebase Emulator/API contract tests for signed-in reads/writes and rule denials. A live preview-origin smoke still needs the exact authorized domain and a disposable account. Do not use undeletable workflow records for repeated smoke tests. |
| Downloaded workspace JSON | A client-created file download, not cloud backup/restore. | `web/workspace-export.js` creates a synthetic-only snapshot with employee records, raw attendance rows, leave requests and tickets; it marks `hoursCalculated:false` and `payrollIncluded:false`. `fetchSandboxSnapshot()` obtains data through GET APIs. | No change is needed for reading the current user’s Firebase sandbox; the bundle already uses scoped GETs when signed in. To restore/import the file into Firebase, add a separately designed import path, duplicate-ID handling, schema versioning, per-collection validation, user ownership checks, and preview/confirm/rollback behavior. Current export is not a restore function or automated backup. |

### Local-only feature file contents

- `src/main/java/ph/motorph/web/MutableAttendanceStore.java` — the writable interface limited to creating a raw `AttendanceRecord` from schedule ID, date, times, and fixed day type.
- `src/main/java/ph/motorph/web/InMemoryAttendanceStore.java` — synthetic attendance fixtures and synchronized in-memory create/duplicate check; store lifetime is the Java process.
- `src/main/java/ph/motorph/web/AttendanceService.java` — employee existence check, existing mapping lookup, mutable-store check, fixed `DEMO` assignment; it does not create mappings or calculate hours.
- `src/main/java/ph/motorph/web/AppServer.java` — POST route whitelist, date/time parsing, local-mode guard, JSON response and status codes. Firebase mode is rejected before store access.
- `web/index.html` — the local-only attendance form, explanatory boundary text, raw-record calendar, report/export/search UI.
- `web/app.js` — posts local raw input, loads scoped reads, renders the calendar and reports, cross-module search, JSON export, and employee-linked record details. `showWorkspace(user)` hides the create form for signed-in Firebase users.
# Candidate policy review from prior submissions and current references

**Status: research only; no calculator is active.** The temporary 2026 browser preview once described in this document has been removed under the current “no temporary features” instruction. No rule table or payroll estimate is shipped by the app. Peer implementations and statutory references below remain candidate research, not MotorPH policy. No official MotorPH payroll rulebook or active grading rubric was found in the supplied set. See `docs/build-status-no-local-no-temp.md` for current behavior.

## 1. What the inspected MO-IT110 peer implementation says

The supplied peer review copy at `/home/user/repo_review/full_repo/testingester-main/6/-/` contains an explicit, testable candidate model:

- `src/motorph/model/AttendanceRecord.java`: first cutoff is days 1–15; second cutoff is day 16 through actual month end. Login from 08:00 through 08:10 is treated as 08:00; logout after 17:00 is capped at 17:00. It calculates elapsed time directly from those adjusted times and does **not** subtract a meal interval.
- `src/motorph/service/PayrollProcessor.java`: the first cutoff has no deductions and net equals cutoff gross. On the second cutoff, it computes monthly contributions from the combined two-cutoff gross, computes withholding tax after those contributions, and subtracts the whole monthly deduction amount from the second-cutoff gross (floored at zero). Allowances are shown on the second-cutoff slip but excluded from net in that implementation.
- `src/motorph/model/Employee.java`: gross is hourly rate times the calculated minutes. The course-project fixtures also supply semi-monthly and hourly rates.
- The peer has substantial tests and CP2 compatibility comparisons, but its own behavior is still an implementation choice, not an authoritative MotorPH payroll rule.
4. calculate net and build an immutable payroll record.

Its NOTES and console tests report this pipeline exercised. But the formulas are hard-coded as Java `double` constants and the source XLSX matrices cited by its verification note were on a personal Windows path, not among the supplied files. The source values are **not a current 2026 ruleset**:

- SSS caps the employee share at ₱1,125, which predates the 2025 schedule (2026 uses the current schedule effective January 2025: 5% employee / 10% employer on MSC up to ₱35,000, plus employer-only EC).
- PhilHealth uses 3%, a ₱10,000 floor/₱60,000 ceiling and a 50/50 split; the current direct-contributor advisory for formal-sector MBS gives 5%, ₱10,000 floor/₱100,000 ceiling, with allowances and overtime excluded from the MBS base.
- Pag-IBIG caps at ₱100, reflecting the former ₱5,000 MFS; Circular 460 moved the MFS ceiling to ₱10,000 effective February 2024, allowing up to ₱200 per side.
- Its first taxable monthly BIR band uses 20%; Annex E uses 15% from ₱20,833 to ₱33,332. The prior project also does not make a semi-monthly tax table part of its calculator API.

A separate folder-7 `ContributionCalculator.java` also computes semi-monthly values, but doubles the pay-period input to a monthly proxy and reuses old CP2 schedules: SSS max ₱1,125, PhilHealth 1.5% employee amount with ₱900 cap, Pag-IBIG cap ₱100, and a 20% first taxable band. Its payroll code labels overtime pricing as temporary pending confirmation. Folder 3 is even simpler (flat 4.5% SSS, 2% PhilHealth, ₱100 Pag-IBIG, no tax schedule). These show earlier mechanical exploration, but none supply a current validated 2026 profile.

The older folder-6 implementation is even more explicitly a CP2/course-project compatibility profile, not a 2026 statutory table. Neither implementation was copied into the current app.

## 7. Withdrawn temporary 2026 preview — historical research only

A temporary synthetic-input monthly preview was previously added during an earlier iteration. It was explicitly non-persistent, but the current user instruction prohibits temporary features, so the preview UI, calculator, rules module, CSV export, styling, and preview-only tests have been removed. None of the numbers in this historical section should be shown or relied upon as a current app result. The official-source links above remain useful research inputs for a future approved, persisted payroll engine; they are not enough to resolve MotorPH's pay-period, eligibility, taxable-base, deduction-allocation, calculation, authorization, or audit rules.

The working application now presents a fail-closed payroll configuration gate and calculates no payroll amount. A durable payroll feature must be implemented only after its policy inputs and independently verified examples are approved. See `docs/build-status-no-local-no-temp.md`.

    private void handleAttendance(HttpExchange exchange) throws IOException {
        if ("POST".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod())) {
            handleAttendanceCreate(exchange);
            return;
        }
        if (!"GET".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod())) {
            sendJson(exchange, 405, "{\"error\":\"Method not allowed\"}");
            return;
        }
        String employeeId = queryParameter(exchange.getRequestURI().getRawQuery(), "employeeId");
        if (employeeId == null || employeeId.trim().isEmpty()) {
            sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"employeeId is required\"}");
            return;
        }
        try {
            RequestServices services = servicesFor(exchange);
            LocalDate from = parseOptionalDate(queryParameter(exchange.getRequestURI().getRawQuery(), "from"));
            LocalDate to = parseOptionalDate(queryParameter(exchange.getRequestURI().getRawQuery(), "to"));
            AttendanceService attendanceService = new AttendanceService(services.employeeService,
                localScheduleStore, services.attendanceStore);
            List<AttendanceRecord> records = attendanceService.findForEmployee(employeeId, from, to);
            sendJson(exchange, 200, attendanceToJson(records));
        } catch (DateTimeParseException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"Dates must use YYYY-MM-DD\"}");
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"" + escapeJson(ex.getMessage()) + "\"}");
        } catch (java.util.NoSuchElementException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 404, "{\"error\":\"Employee not found\"}");
        } catch (FirestoreException ex) {
            sendApiError(exchange, ex);
        }
    }

    private void handleAttendanceCreate(HttpExchange exchange) throws IOException {
        if (!firebaseProjectId.isEmpty()) {
            sendJson(exchange, 403, "{\"error\":\"Raw attendance entry is disabled in Firebase mode; this demo writer is local-memory only.\"}");
            return;
        }
        try {
            JsonObject body = readJsonBody(exchange);
            requireOnlyKeys(body, "employeeId", "date", "timeIn", "timeOut");
            LocalDate date = LocalDate.parse(requiredString(body, "date").trim());
            LocalTime timeIn = parseAttendanceTime(requiredString(body, "timeIn"));
            LocalTime timeOut = parseAttendanceTime(requiredString(body, "timeOut"));
            RequestServices services = servicesFor(exchange);
            AttendanceService attendanceService = new AttendanceService(services.employeeService,
                localScheduleStore, services.attendanceStore);
            AttendanceRecord created = attendanceService.createForEmployee(
                requiredString(body, "employeeId"), date, timeIn, timeOut);
            sendJson(exchange, 201, "{\"item\":" + attendanceRecordToJson(created)
                + ",\"storage\":\"local-process-memory\",\"syntheticOnly\":true,\"hoursCalculated\":false}");
        } catch (DateTimeParseException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"Date must use YYYY-MM-DD and times must use HH:mm\"}");
        } catch (RequestException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, ex.statusCode, "{\"error\":\"" + escapeJson(ex.getMessage()) + "\"}");
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"" + escapeJson(ex.getMessage()) + "\"}");
        } catch (NoSuchElementException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 404, "{\"error\":\"Employee not found\"}");
        } catch (IllegalStateException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 409, "{\"error\":\"" + escapeJson(ex.getMessage()) + "\"}");

# Source-grounded acceptance baseline (draft)

**Purpose:** record observable pass/fail behavior already implemented and define safe candidate acceptance criteria before tailoring. This is a working baseline, **not an approved rubric interpretation**. No standalone active MO-IT110 grading rubric was identified among the supplied files in the workspace; the older MO-IT108/107 documents and peer submissions inform scope, while the Terminal Assessment proposal is treated as placeholder material rather than an authoritative detailed specification.

**Scope rules:** fictional data only; use the signed-in user's sandbox in Firebase mode; Firebase-backed persistence; no production local-memory fallback explicitly process-memory; do not treat inferred attendance/payroll rules, peer-project choices, employee-to-account identity, reviewer authority, or access boundaries as approved policy. At the user's direction, a clearly labelled 2026 monthly statutory preview is now available with synthetic inputs only; its rules are isolated in a changeable module and it has no API/Firestore/payslip path. Attendance-based or persistent payroll, approvals, and reviewer controls remain gated. See `docs/candidate-policy-review.md`. The user-published development rules remain unchanged.

## Candidate acceptance matrix

| Area | Observable acceptance in current prototype | State | Source / boundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Authentication and sandbox | Email/password account creation/sign-in/sign-out on localhost; Firebase requests use the caller's ID token and user-scoped paths. Auth lifecycle smoke uses a disposable account, verifies empty reads, signs out, deletes the account, and makes no Firestore writes. | Verified locally; exact Arena preview origin still unverified | Firebase setup guide, Firestore rules review, browser smoke evidence. No organizational roles or employee-account mapping. |
| Employee directory | Search/detail; selectable field/direction sorting on the employee register; create/update only name, department, role label, location, and demo status; server-generated IDs; HR-table text/status filters, selectable sorting, and filtered CSV export; read-only synthetic label-count summary; employee detail includes that employee's raw rows and stored workflow labels only. | Implemented and browser tested | Legacy MO-IT108 traceability and API contract. No salary/government IDs, termination, employee delete, schedule assignment, or audit history. |
# Prototype API contract

All routes are same-origin JSON endpoints. In local mode, employee/attendance fixtures are synthetic and workflow records live only in the Java process memory (cleared on server restart). When `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID` is configured, employee, attendance, and workflow routes require a signed-in Firebase user and use only that user's Firestore sandbox. The Java backend forwards the Firebase ID token to Firestore REST; Firestore Security Rules authorize every request. The project owner has published `docs/firestore.rules`; live smoke tests verified leave and ticket create/cancel persistence and cross-user denial. The assistant has not changed Firebase Console settings. Future rule-file changes still require owner publication.

In Firebase mode, browser requests include:

```text
Authorization: Bearer <Firebase ID token>
X-Firebase-UID: <signed-in Firebase UID>
```

The UID header is not trusted for authorization: Firestore Rules compare it to the UID in the verified ID token. Do not log or persist ID tokens.
> Historical inventory note: the in-memory runtime described below is no longer available from production entry points. It is confined to the loopback test fixture. The temporary statutory calculator has been removed. See `docs/build-status-no-local-no-temp.md` for current status.

# Local demo inventory

This note separates unauthenticated process-memory behavior from Firebase-backed owner-sandbox behavior. It is not an acceptance rubric or a production-readiness claim.

## Local process-memory mode

- Selected when the API runs without a Firebase project ID. The browser shows `LOCAL PREVIEW`; there is no user sign-in boundary. Directory/workflow/raw records are shared by callers of that local API process and reset when the process stops.
- Synthetic employee create/update is limited to the allowed display fields. IDs are server-generated. New employees receive no schedule mapping.
- Raw attendance queries are read-only as a view; the explicitly authorized **create-only** demo form is the exception. It accepts an existing mapped synthetic employee, date, time-in, and time-out. The server supplies the existing schedule ID and `DEMO` label; the store enforces unique schedule/date and `timeIn <= timeOut`. No correction, delete, schedule assignment, attendance classification, hours, or pay is added.
- Leave/ticket workflows are synthetic, process-memory records with their existing submit/cancel limits; no reviewer, approval, resolution, or delivery action is present.
- The former temporary statutory calculator has been removed; no payroll estimate is available.
- The read-only raw attendance calendar (including its two-date inclusive filter), employee linked-record detail and searchable/mapped-filterable/sortable stored count summary with visible/all CSV, cross-module search, workflow type filters, visible/all CSV exports, and JSON workspace export use the same local demo service. The JSON export includes only the current synthetic records and marks `hoursCalculated:false`, `payrollIncluded:false`; search/export issue reads only.

            String attendanceBody = "{\"employeeId\":\"DEMO-001\",\"date\":\"2026-10-20\",\"timeIn\":\"08:00\",\"timeOut\":\"17:00\"}";
            HttpResponse<String> createdAttendance = postJson(base.resolve("/api/attendance"), attendanceBody);
            check(createdAttendance.statusCode() == 201
                && createdAttendance.body().contains("\"storage\":\"local-process-memory\"")
                && createdAttendance.body().contains("\"syntheticOnly\":true")
                && createdAttendance.body().contains("\"hoursCalculated\":false"),
                "local raw attendance creation advertises ephemeral synthetic storage without calculations");
            check(createdAttendance.body().contains("\"scheduleId\":101")
                && createdAttendance.body().contains("\"dayType\":\"DEMO\"")
                && createdAttendance.body().contains("\"date\":\"2026-10-20\""),
                "server supplies existing schedule mapping and fixed DEMO label");
            HttpResponse<String> duplicateAttendance = postJson(base.resolve("/api/attendance"), attendanceBody);
            check(duplicateAttendance.statusCode() == 409, "local attendance API rejects duplicate schedule/date");
            HttpResponse<String> reversedTimes = postJson(base.resolve("/api/attendance"),
                "{\"employeeId\":\"DEMO-001\",\"date\":\"2026-10-21\",\"timeIn\":\"18:00\",\"timeOut\":\"17:00\"}");
            check(reversedTimes.statusCode() == 400, "local attendance API rejects reversed times");
            HttpResponse<String> clientSchedule = postJson(base.resolve("/api/attendance"),
                "{\"employeeId\":\"DEMO-001\",\"scheduleId\":999,\"date\":\"2026-10-22\",\"timeIn\":\"08:00\",\"timeOut\":\"17:00\"}");
            check(clientSchedule.statusCode() == 400, "client cannot supply a schedule assignment");
            HttpResponse<String> unknownEmployeeAttendance = postJson(base.resolve("/api/attendance"),
                "{\"employeeId\":\"UNKNOWN\",\"date\":\"2026-10-22\",\"timeIn\":\"08:00\",\"timeOut\":\"17:00\"}");
            check(unknownEmployeeAttendance.statusCode() == 404, "attendance creation rejects an unknown employee");
        } finally {
            app.stop();
        }
    }

    private void handleAttendanceCreate(HttpExchange exchange) throws IOException {
        if (!firebaseProjectId.isEmpty()) {
            sendJson(exchange, 403, "{\"error\":\"Raw attendance entry is disabled in Firebase mode; this demo writer is local-memory only.\"}");
            return;
        }
        try {
            JsonObject body = readJsonBody(exchange);
            requireOnlyKeys(body, "employeeId", "date", "timeIn", "timeOut");
            LocalDate date = LocalDate.parse(requiredString(body, "date").trim());
            LocalTime timeIn = parseAttendanceTime(requiredString(body, "timeIn"));
            LocalTime timeOut = parseAttendanceTime(requiredString(body, "timeOut"));
            RequestServices services = servicesFor(exchange);
            AttendanceService attendanceService = new AttendanceService(services.employeeService,
                localScheduleStore, services.attendanceStore);
            AttendanceRecord created = attendanceService.createForEmployee(
                requiredString(body, "employeeId"), date, timeIn, timeOut);
            sendJson(exchange, 201, "{\"item\":" + attendanceRecordToJson(created)
                + ",\"storage\":\"local-process-memory\",\"syntheticOnly\":true,\"hoursCalculated\":false}");
        } catch (DateTimeParseException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"Date must use YYYY-MM-DD and times must use HH:mm\"}");
        } catch (RequestException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, ex.statusCode, "{\"error\":\"" + escapeJson(ex.getMessage()) + "\"}");
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"" + escapeJson(ex.getMessage()) + "\"}");
        } catch (NoSuchElementException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 404, "{\"error\":\"Employee not found\"}");
        } catch (IllegalStateException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 409, "{\"error\":\"" + escapeJson(ex.getMessage()) + "\"}");
        }
    }

    private static LocalTime parseAttendanceTime(String value) {
        String time = value == null ? "" : value.trim();
        if (!time.matches("^([01][0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-5][0-9]$")) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Time values must use 24-hour HH:mm format.");
        }
        return LocalTime.parse(time);
    }

    private void handleAttendanceReport(HttpExchange exchange) throws IOException {
        if (!"GET".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod())) {
            sendJson(exchange, 405, "{\"error\":\"Method not allowed\"}");
            return;
        }
        try {
            RequestServices services = servicesFor(exchange);
            String query = exchange.getRequestURI().getRawQuery();
            LocalDate from = parseOptionalDate(queryParameter(query, "from"));
            LocalDate to = parseOptionalDate(queryParameter(query, "to"));
            AttendanceService attendanceService = new AttendanceService(services.employeeService,
                localScheduleStore, services.attendanceStore);
            List<RawAttendanceSummary> summaries = attendanceService.summarizeRawRecords(from, to);
            sendJson(exchange, 200, attendanceSummaryToJson(summaries, from, to));
        } catch (DateTimeParseException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"Dates must use YYYY-MM-DD\"}");
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"" + escapeJson(ex.getMessage()) + "\"}");
        } catch (FirestoreException ex) {
            sendApiError(exchange, ex);
        }
    }

# Prototype API contract

All routes are same-origin JSON endpoints. In local mode, employee/attendance fixtures are synthetic and workflow records live only in the Java process memory (cleared on server restart). When `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID` is configured, employee, attendance, and workflow routes require a signed-in Firebase user and use only that user's Firestore sandbox. The Java backend forwards the Firebase ID token to Firestore REST; Firestore Security Rules authorize every request. The project owner has published `docs/firestore.rules`; live smoke tests verified leave and ticket create/cancel persistence and cross-user denial. The assistant has not changed Firebase Console settings. Future rule-file changes still require owner publication.

In Firebase mode, browser requests include:

```text
Authorization: Bearer <Firebase ID token>
X-Firebase-UID: <signed-in Firebase UID>
```

The UID header is not trusted for authorization: Firestore Rules compare it to the UID in the verified ID token. Do not log or persist ID tokens.

# Local demo inventory

This note separates unauthenticated process-memory behavior from Firebase-backed owner-sandbox behavior. It is not an acceptance rubric or a production-readiness claim.

## Local process-memory mode

- Selected when the API runs without a Firebase project ID. The browser shows `LOCAL PREVIEW`; there is no user sign-in boundary. Directory/workflow/raw records are shared by callers of that local API process and reset when the process stops.
- Synthetic employee create/update is limited to the allowed display fields. IDs are server-generated. New employees receive no schedule mapping.
- Raw attendance queries are read-only as a view; the explicitly authorized **create-only** demo form is the exception. It accepts an existing mapped synthetic employee, date, time-in, and time-out. The server supplies the existing schedule ID and `DEMO` label; the store enforces unique schedule/date and `timeIn <= timeOut`. No correction, delete, schedule assignment, attendance classification, hours, or pay is added.
- Leave/ticket workflows are synthetic, process-memory records with their existing submit/cancel limits; no reviewer, approval, resolution, or delivery action is present.
- The former temporary statutory calculator has been removed; no payroll estimate is available.
- The read-only raw attendance calendar (including its two-date inclusive filter), employee linked-record detail and searchable/mapped-filterable/sortable stored count summary with visible/all CSV, cross-module search, workflow type filters, visible/all CSV exports, and JSON workspace export use the same local demo service. The JSON export includes only the current synthetic records and marks `hoursCalculated:false`, `payrollIncluded:false`; search/export issue reads only.

## Firebase user-sandbox mode

- The app requires Firebase Email/Password sign-in when client configuration is complete; API reads/writes use the caller's user-scoped paths and existing published rules.
- Employee display fields and owner-scoped workflow routes retain their previously accepted limits. The employee-linked record view, raw attendance calendar, cross-module search, and JSON bundle use user-scoped reads.
- **Firebase attendance stays read-only.** `POST /api/attendance` is rejected with `403` before a storage service is accessed. No Firebase attendance write has been introduced.
- No user roles, employee-account mapping, supervisor/team boundaries, approvals, schedule assignment, attendance calculations, payroll inputs, or persisted pay/payslip workflow are introduced by this slice.

## Local acceptance evidence

- Java domain/service checks cover mapping, fixed day type, unique schedule/date, time order, and unmapped employee rejection.
- Java API integration checks cover the local `201` response metadata, duplicate `409`, invalid `400`, fixed server mapping/classification, client-supplied schedule rejection, and Firebase-mode `403`.
- Browser E2E covers successful local capture, duplicate/mapping/time-order rejection, raw calendar display, employee-linked rows, type-filtered visible exports, cross-module search, JSON export contents, and read-only HTTP methods for bundle/search.
- Latest fully run checks and their counts are recorded in `README.md` and `docs/peer-parity-roadmap.md`.

    private static String queryParameter(String rawQuery, String target) {
        if (rawQuery == null || rawQuery.isEmpty()) return "";
        for (String part : rawQuery.split("&")) {
            int separator = part.indexOf('=');
            String key = separator < 0 ? part : part.substring(0, separator);
            if (target.equals(decode(key))) return separator < 0 ? "" : decode(part.substring(separator + 1));
        }
        return "";
    }

    private static String decode(String value) {
        try {
            return URLDecoder.decode(value, "UTF-8");
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException | java.io.UnsupportedEncodingException ex) {
            return "";
        }
    }

    private static String contentTypeFor(Path path) {
        String name = path.getFileName().toString().toLowerCase();
        if (name.endsWith(".html")) return "text/html; charset=utf-8";
        if (name.endsWith(".css")) return "text/css; charset=utf-8";
        if (name.endsWith(".js")) return "application/javascript; charset=utf-8";
        if (name.endsWith(".svg")) return "image/svg+xml";
        return "application/octet-stream";
    }

    private static String escapeJson(String value) {
        return value.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("\"", "\\\"")
            .replace("\n", "\\n").replace("\r", "\\r").replace("\t", "\\t");
    }

    private static void sendApiError(HttpExchange exchange, FirestoreException exception) throws IOException {
        int status = exception.getStatusCode();
        if (status < 400 || status > 599) status = 500;
        sendJson(exchange, status, "{\"error\":\"" + escapeJson(exception.getMessage()) + "\"}");
    }

    private static String attendanceToJson(List<AttendanceRecord> records) {
        StringBuilder json = new StringBuilder("{\"items\":[");
        for (int i = 0; i < records.size(); i++) {
            AttendanceRecord record = records.get(i);
            if (i > 0) json.append(',');
            json.append(attendanceRecordToJson(record));
        }
        return json.append("],\"count\":").append(records.size())
            .append(",\"hoursCalculated\":false}").toString();
    }

    private static String attendanceRecordToJson(AttendanceRecord record) {
        return "{\"attendanceId\":" + record.getAttendanceId()
            + ",\"scheduleId\":" + record.getScheduleId()
            + ",\"date\":\"" + record.getDate()
            + "\",\"timeIn\":\"" + record.getTimeIn()
            + "\",\"timeOut\":\"" + record.getTimeOut()
            + "\",\"dayType\":\"" + escapeJson(record.getDayType()) + "\"}";
    }

    private static String attendanceSummaryToJson(List<RawAttendanceSummary> summaries, LocalDate from, LocalDate to) {
        StringBuilder json = new StringBuilder("{\"items\":[");
        for (int i = 0; i < summaries.size(); i++) {
            RawAttendanceSummary summary = summaries.get(i);
            if (i > 0) json.append(',');
            json.append("{\"employeeId\":\"").append(escapeJson(summary.getEmployeeId()))
                .append("\",\"employeeName\":\"").append(escapeJson(summary.getEmployeeName()))
                .append("\",\"scheduleId\":").append(summary.getScheduleId() == null ? "null" : summary.getScheduleId())
                .append(",\"hasScheduleMapping\":").append(summary.hasScheduleMapping())
                .append(",\"rawRecordCount\":").append(summary.getRawRecordCount())
                .append(",\"firstRecordDate\":\"").append(escapeJson(summary.getFirstRecordDate()))
                .append("\",\"lastRecordDate\":\"").append(escapeJson(summary.getLastRecordDate())).append("\"}");
        }
        json.append("],\"count\":").append(summaries.size())
            .append(",\"from\":").append(from == null ? "null" : "\"" + from + "\"")
            .append(",\"to\":").append(to == null ? "null" : "\"" + to + "\"")
            .append(",\"hoursCalculated\":false}");
        return json.toString();
    }

    private void handleWorkflows(HttpExchange exchange) throws IOException {
        String path = exchange.getRequestURI().getPath();
        String method = exchange.getRequestMethod();
        try {
            if ("GET".equals(method) && "/api/workflows".equals(path)) {
                WorkflowService service = workflowsFor(exchange);
                sendJson(exchange, 200, workflowsToJson(service.listLeaveRequests(), service.listTickets(),
                    firebaseProjectId.isEmpty() ? "local-process-memory" : "user-scoped-firestore"));
                return;
            }
            if (!"POST".equals(method)) {
                sendJson(exchange, 405, "{\"error\":\"Method not allowed\"}");
                return;
            }

            WorkflowService service = workflowsFor(exchange);
            if ("/api/workflows/leave".equals(path)) {
                JsonObject body = readJsonBody(exchange);
                requireOnlyKeys(body, "employeeId", "leaveType", "startDate", "endDate", "note");
                DemoLeaveRequest request = service.createLeaveRequest(
                    requiredString(body, "employeeId"), requiredString(body, "leaveType"),
                    requiredString(body, "startDate"), requiredString(body, "endDate"), optionalString(body, "note"));
                sendJson(exchange, 201, itemToJson(leaveToJson(request),
                    firebaseProjectId.isEmpty() ? "local-process-memory" : "user-scoped-firestore"));
                return;
            }
            if ("/api/workflows/tickets".equals(path)) {
                JsonObject body = readJsonBody(exchange);
                requireOnlyKeys(body, "employeeId", "ticketType", "summary");
                DemoTicket ticket = service.createTicket(requiredString(body, "employeeId"),
                    requiredString(body, "ticketType"), requiredString(body, "summary"));
                sendJson(exchange, 201, itemToJson(ticketToJson(ticket),
                    firebaseProjectId.isEmpty() ? "local-process-memory" : "user-scoped-firestore"));
                return;
            }
            String[] segments = path.substring("/api/workflows/".length()).split("/");
            if (segments.length == 3 && "cancel".equals(segments[2])) {
                if ("leave".equals(segments[0])) {
                    DemoLeaveRequest request = service.cancelLeaveRequest(segments[1]);
                    sendJson(exchange, 200, itemToJson(leaveToJson(request),
                        firebaseProjectId.isEmpty() ? "local-process-memory" : "user-scoped-firestore"));
                    return;
                }
                if ("tickets".equals(segments[0])) {
                    DemoTicket ticket = service.cancelTicket(segments[1]);
                    sendJson(exchange, 200, itemToJson(ticketToJson(ticket),
                        firebaseProjectId.isEmpty() ? "local-process-memory" : "user-scoped-firestore"));
                    return;
                }
            }
            sendJson(exchange, 404, "{\"error\":\"Workflow endpoint not found\"}");
        } catch (RequestException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, ex.statusCode, "{\"error\":\"" + escapeJson(ex.getMessage()) + "\"}");
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"" + escapeJson(ex.getMessage()) + "\"}");

```

Possible errors: `400` for missing employee ID, invalid date syntax, or reversed range; `404` for an unknown employee; `401` for missing/expired Firebase sign-in; `403` when Firestore Rules deny the request. Raw times only; no hours or pay are derived.

`POST /api/attendance` is a **local-demo-only create operation**. Firebase attendance remains read-only; Firebase-mode POSTs return `403` before accessing a store. The local endpoint accepts exactly the following fields (no client-selected schedule ID or `dayType`):

```json
{
  "employeeId": "DEMO-001",
  "date": "2026-10-20",
  "timeIn": "08:00",
  "timeOut": "17:00"
}
```

The employee must already exist and have a configured synthetic schedule mapping. The server uses that mapping, sets `dayType` to `DEMO`, and stores the raw row in shared process memory. The store atomically enforces unique `(scheduleID, date)`; `timeIn <= timeOut` is validated. Success is `201` with `{"item":{...},"storage":"local-process-memory","syntheticOnly":true,"hoursCalculated":false}`. Errors: `400` for unknown fields, missing/malformed date or time, or reversed time order; `404` for an unknown employee; `409` for an unmapped employee or duplicate schedule/date; `403` in Firebase mode. No hours, classifications, or pay are derived. The local store is ephemeral and this is not a Firebase write path.

### Raw attendance coverage report

`GET /api/reports/attendance`

Optional inclusive ISO date filters: `from=YYYY-MM-DD` and/or `to=YYYY-MM-DD`. Blank filters include all available records; this is not a pay-period boundary. The response includes one row for each employee in the caller's synthetic directory, using the current configured employee-to-schedule mapping. New employees without a mapping are reported as `hasScheduleMapping:false`, `scheduleId:null`, with zero attributed rows; this does **not** mean absent or unworked.

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "employeeId": "DEMO-001",
      "employeeName": "Mara Rivera",
      "scheduleId": 101,

## Leave requests and tickets

`GET /api/workflows` returns only the current user's lists:

```json
{"leaveRequests":[],"tickets":[],"storage":"user-scoped-firestore"}
```

- `POST /api/workflows/leave` accepts `employeeId`, `leaveType`, `startDate`, `endDate`, and optional `note`. The server derives the employee name from the caller's own synthetic directory, validates supported leave types and ISO calendar dates, and creates a `Pending review` record.
- `POST /api/workflows/tickets` accepts `employeeId`, `ticketType`, and `summary`. The server derives the employee name and queue label and creates an `Open` record. No ticket is delivered or assigned to a real handler.
- `POST /api/workflows/leave/{requestId}/cancel` and `POST /api/workflows/tickets/{ticketId}/cancel` allow only the pending/open-to-cancelled transition. Delete, review, approve, reject, and resolve routes do not exist.
- Firebase records use `users/{uid}/demoLeaveRequests/{requestId}` and `users/{uid}/demoTickets/{ticketId}`. The candidate Firestore rules allow owner-only read/create/cancel; they deny deletes and all reviewer actions. Records are limited to the user's synthetic employee directory and contain no payroll calculations.
- Local mode returns `storage:"local-process-memory"`; these records survive page reloads while the Java process is running, but are lost when it stops.

Possible errors: `400` invalid request fields or dates; `401` missing/expired sign-in; `403` Firestore rules deny the operation (publish the updated `docs/firestore.rules`); `404` employee/request/ticket not found in the caller's sandbox; `409` invalid workflow transition.
