`POST /api/demo/seed`

### 4.1 Startup and mode selection

```text
read frontend Firebase configuration
if Firebase configuration is complete:
    initialize Firebase Auth
    show sign-in gate until Firebase reports a signed-in user
    for each API call, send caller ID token and UID headers
else:
    show LOCAL PREVIEW without authentication

Java API startup:
    if Firebase project is absent:
        use shared process-memory employee/workflow/attendance stores
    else:
        require valid-looking Firebase session headers for user-scoped reads/writes
        build Firestore services rooted at users/{uid}/...
        keep attendance store read-only
```

The Firestore Rules, rather than a UI label, are the security boundary. There is no organizational role or employee-account mapping in this build.

### 4.2 Synthetic employee directory

- Employee list, search, and detail selection work; data remains fictional and scoped to the signed-in sandbox.
- Raw attendance records are selectable by employee and inclusive date range; default range spans that employee's earliest/latest available records, following the older Requirements Analysis. The register also displays a month calendar of loaded raw rows with two-date inclusive filter selection, never an absence classification. A separate read-only coverage report summarizes raw row counts and date bounds by configured employee-to-schedule mapping; unmapped is not reported as absent. Firebase attendance remains read-only.
- The Payroll workspace contains a disposable 2026 statutory preview from synthetic values; it is not connected to attendance. The default attendance range is not a pay period.
- Leave request/ticket API routes now validate input, derive employee names from the user's synthetic directory, create records, show status, and allow only cancellation. A display-only personal request calendar shows pending/cancelled date ranges, not approved leave; two date clicks can draft form bounds without submitting. Client-side search/status filters narrow each workflow table, and the leave table additionally filters by inclusive overlap with a requested-date range; native detail disclosures show note/message and submission/cancellation timestamps; local and Firestore lists order newest first; exports remain the full owner-sandbox dataset. Firebase paths are owner-scoped and have no reviewer/approval/delete access; after publication, live smoke testing verified employee create/update, leave and ticket create/cancel/read-back, and cross-user denial. One cancelled leave and one cancelled ticket remain under deleted disposable UIDs because workflow deletion is denied. Local preview stores these records in Java process memory and loses them when the process restarts.
- Team roster is read-only with search/status filters, field/direction sorting, selected-record detail view, and filtered CSV export; the HR directory table also has client-side search/status filters, field/direction sorting, and filtered CSV export. Reports summarizes only stored synthetic directory status/department and workflow status/type/queue labels, with label-count CSV exports; workflow counts do not imply approvals or resolutions. The directory editor creates/updates only fictional name, department, role, location, and demo status. Firebase mode is user-scoped; the old unauthenticated process-memory store is now test-fixture-only; production requires Firebase. Employee detail now shows a read-only linked-record summary, and Reports provides owner-scoped cross-module search and a read-only JSON portability bundle. No team membership, HR authorization, delete, schedules, or lifecycle workflow exists.

    private RequestServices servicesFor(HttpExchange exchange) {
        if (firebaseProjectId.isEmpty()) {
            return new RequestServices(localEmployeeService, localAttendanceStore);
        }
        FirestoreRestClient client = firestoreClientFor(exchange);
        return new RequestServices(new EmployeeService(new FirestoreEmployeeStore(client)), new FirestoreAttendanceStore(client));
    }

    private FirestoreRestClient firestoreClientFor(HttpExchange exchange) {
        String authorization = exchange.getRequestHeaders().getFirst("Authorization");
        String uid = exchange.getRequestHeaders().getFirst("X-Firebase-UID");
        if (authorization == null || !authorization.startsWith("Bearer ") || uid == null || uid.trim().isEmpty()) {
            throw new FirestoreException("Sign in with your Firebase account to continue.", 401);
        }
        String token = authorization.substring("Bearer ".length()).trim();
        if (token.length() > 8192 || uid.length() > 128 || uid.contains("/")) {
            throw new FirestoreException("Invalid Firebase session information.", 401);
        }
        return firestoreApiRoot == null
            ? new FirestoreRestClient(firebaseProjectId, uid, token)
            : new FirestoreRestClient(firebaseProjectId, uid, token, firestoreApiRoot);
    }

    private static LocalDate parseOptionalDate(String value) {
        return value == null || value.trim().isEmpty() ? null : LocalDate.parse(value.trim());
    }

    private static void firebaseModeRejectsPartialAndMalformedSessionsBeforeFirestore() throws Exception {
        AppServer app = new AppServer("motorph-jd", Paths.get("web"));
        HttpServer server = app.start("127.0.0.1", 0);
        try {
            URI employeesUri = URI.create("http://127.0.0.1:" + server.getAddress().getPort() + "/api/employees");
            HttpRequest tokenOnly = HttpRequest.newBuilder(employeesUri).GET()
                .header("Authorization", "Bearer local-test-token").build();
            HttpResponse<String> missingUid = HTTP.send(tokenOnly, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
            check(missingUid.statusCode() == 401, "Firebase ID token without UID header is rejected locally");

            HttpRequest uidOnly = HttpRequest.newBuilder(employeesUri).GET()
                .header("X-Firebase-UID", "synthetic-test-user").build();
            HttpResponse<String> missingToken = HTTP.send(uidOnly, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
            check(missingToken.statusCode() == 401, "UID header without Firebase ID token is rejected locally");

            HttpRequest invalidUid = HttpRequest.newBuilder(employeesUri).GET()
                .header("Authorization", "Bearer local-test-token")
                .header("X-Firebase-UID", "invalid/user").build();
            HttpResponse<String> invalidSession = HTTP.send(invalidUid, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
            check(invalidSession.statusCode() == 401, "malformed UID is rejected locally");
        } finally {
            app.stop();
        }
    }

function showWorkspace(user) {

  authGate.hidden = true;
  appShell.hidden = false;
  document.getElementById('sign-out-button').hidden = !user;
  document.getElementById('operator-label').textContent = user ? 'USER SANDBOX' : 'TEST FIXTURE';

}

rules_version = '2';
service cloud.firestore {
  match /databases/{database}/documents {
    function signedInAs(uid) {
      return request.auth != null && request.auth.uid == uid;
    }

    function validDemoEmployee(employeeId) {
      let d = request.resource.data;
      return d.keys().hasAll(['id', 'name', 'department', 'role', 'location', 'status'])
        && d.keys().hasOnly(['id', 'name', 'department', 'role', 'location', 'status'])
        && d.id is string && d.id == employeeId && d.id.size() <= 40
        && d.name is string && d.name.size() > 0 && d.name.size() <= 100
        && d.department is string && d.department.size() > 0 && d.department.size() <= 100
        && d.role is string && d.role.size() > 0 && d.role.size() <= 100
        && d.location is string && d.location.size() > 0 && d.location.size() <= 100
        && d.status in ['Active', 'On leave'];
    }

    function validDemoScheduleMapping(uid, employeeId) {
      let d = request.resource.data;
      let employeePath = /databases/$(database)/documents/users/$(uid)/demoEmployees/$(employeeId);
      return d.keys().hasAll(['employeeId', 'scheduleId'])
        && d.keys().hasOnly(['employeeId', 'scheduleId'])
        && d.employeeId is string && d.employeeId == employeeId
        && d.scheduleId is int && d.scheduleId > 0
        && exists(employeePath);
    }

    function validDemoAttendance() {
      let d = request.resource.data;
      return d.keys().hasAll(['attendanceId', 'scheduleId', 'date', 'timeIn', 'timeOut', 'dayType'])
        && d.keys().hasOnly(['attendanceId', 'scheduleId', 'date', 'timeIn', 'timeOut', 'dayType'])
        && d.attendanceId is int && d.attendanceId > 0
        && d.scheduleId is int && d.scheduleId > 0
        && d.date is string && d.date.matches('^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$')
        && d.timeIn is string && d.timeIn.matches('^([01][0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-5][0-9]$')
        && d.timeOut is string && d.timeOut.matches('^([01][0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-5][0-9]$')
        && d.dayType == 'DEMO';
    }

    function ownsDemoEmployee(uid, employeeId, employeeName) {
      let employeePath = /databases/$(database)/documents/users/$(uid)/demoEmployees/$(employeeId);
      return employeeId is string
        && (employeeId.matches('^DEMO-[0-9]{3}$') || employeeId.matches('^DEMO-[A-F0-9]{12}$'))
        && employeeName is string
        && exists(employeePath)
        && get(employeePath).data.name == employeeName;
    }

    function validDemoLeaveRequest(uid, requestId) {
      let d = request.resource.data;
      return d.keys().hasAll(['id', 'employeeId', 'employeeName', 'leaveType', 'startDate', 'endDate', 'note', 'status', 'submittedAt'])
        && d.keys().hasOnly(['id', 'employeeId', 'employeeName', 'leaveType', 'startDate', 'endDate', 'note', 'status', 'submittedAt'])
        && d.id is string && d.id == requestId && d.id.matches('^LV-[A-F0-9]{12}$')
        && ownsDemoEmployee(uid, d.employeeId, d.employeeName)
        && d.leaveType in ['Vacation', 'Medical', 'Personal', 'Unpaid']
        && d.startDate is string && d.startDate.matches('^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$')
        && d.endDate is string && d.endDate.matches('^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$')
        && d.startDate <= d.endDate
        && d.note is string && d.note.size() <= 240
        && d.status == 'Pending review'
        && d.submittedAt is timestamp;
    }

    function validDemoLeaveCancellation(uid, requestId) {
      let previous = resource.data;
      let next = request.resource.data;
      return signedInAs(uid)
        && previous.id == requestId
        && previous.status == 'Pending review'
        && next.id == previous.id
        && next.diff(previous).affectedKeys().hasAll(['status', 'cancelledAt'])
        && next.diff(previous).affectedKeys().hasOnly(['status', 'cancelledAt'])
        && next.status == 'Cancelled'
        && next.cancelledAt is timestamp;
    }

    function validTicketQueue(ticketType, queue) {
      return (ticketType in ['Overtime request', 'Leave request', 'Timesheet correction'] && queue == 'Team Lead')
        || (ticketType == 'Payroll inquiry' && queue == 'Payroll Staff')
        || (ticketType == 'HR inquiry' && queue == 'HR')
        || (ticketType == 'Technical support' && queue == 'IT Admin');
    }

    function validDemoTicket(uid, ticketId) {
      let d = request.resource.data;
      return d.keys().hasAll(['id', 'employeeId', 'employeeName', 'ticketType', 'queue', 'summary', 'status', 'submittedAt'])
        && d.keys().hasOnly(['id', 'employeeId', 'employeeName', 'ticketType', 'queue', 'summary', 'status', 'submittedAt'])
        && d.id is string && d.id == ticketId && d.id.matches('^TK-[A-F0-9]{12}$')
        && ownsDemoEmployee(uid, d.employeeId, d.employeeName)
        && validTicketQueue(d.ticketType, d.queue)
        && d.summary is string && d.summary.size() > 0 && d.summary.size() <= 240
        && d.status == 'Open'
        && d.submittedAt is timestamp;
    }

    function validDemoTicketCancellation(uid, ticketId) {
      let previous = resource.data;
      let next = request.resource.data;
      return signedInAs(uid)
        && previous.id == ticketId
        && previous.status == 'Open'
        && next.id == previous.id
        && next.diff(previous).affectedKeys().hasAll(['status', 'cancelledAt'])
        && next.diff(previous).affectedKeys().hasOnly(['status', 'cancelledAt'])
        && next.status == 'Cancelled'
        && next.cancelledAt is timestamp;
    }

    match /users/{uid}/demoEmployees/{employeeId} {
      allow read: if signedInAs(uid);
      allow create, update: if signedInAs(uid) && validDemoEmployee(employeeId);
      allow delete: if signedInAs(uid);
    }

    // Seeded owner-scoped links replace the old code-only employee/schedule map.
    // Read/create only: schedule assignment editing remains disabled until its policy is approved.
    match /users/{uid}/demoEmployeeSchedules/{employeeId} {
      allow read: if signedInAs(uid);
      allow create: if signedInAs(uid) && validDemoScheduleMapping(uid, employeeId);
      allow update, delete: if false;
    }

    match /users/{uid}/demoAttendance/{attendanceId} {
      allow read: if signedInAs(uid);
      allow create, update: if signedInAs(uid) && validDemoAttendance();
      allow delete: if signedInAs(uid);
    }

    // Owner-only demo requests. There are deliberately no reviewer, approval, or delete permissions.
    match /users/{uid}/demoLeaveRequests/{requestId} {
      allow read: if signedInAs(uid);
      allow create: if signedInAs(uid) && validDemoLeaveRequest(uid, requestId);
      allow update: if validDemoLeaveCancellation(uid, requestId);
      allow delete: if false;
    }

    match /users/{uid}/demoTickets/{ticketId} {
      allow read: if signedInAs(uid);
      allow create: if signedInAs(uid) && validDemoTicket(uid, ticketId);
      allow update: if validDemoTicketCancellation(uid, ticketId);
      allow delete: if false;
    }

docs/api-contract.md:53:`POST /api/employees` creates an owner-sandbox fictional record; `PUT /api/employees/{employeeId}` updates its allowed directory fields. Both accept only `name`, `department`, `role`, `location`, and `status` (`Active` or `On leave`). Unknown fields—including client-supplied IDs, payroll values, and government identifiers—are rejected. The server generates IDs in the `DEMO-<12 uppercase hex characters>` form. Responses are `201` and `200`, respectively, with `{"item": {...}}`. Firebase writes use only the caller's `users/{uid}/demoEmployees` path and existing owner rules; they do not grant HR/supervisor roles. Local mode has no user authentication and stores changes in a single process-memory demo store shared by callers of that API process. Delete, termination, schedule assignment, and audit-history routes are not implemented. A new record has no schedule mapping, so attendance returns an empty list until a separately approved schedule mapping is configured.
docs/api-contract.md:88:Optional inclusive ISO date filters: `from=YYYY-MM-DD` and/or `to=YYYY-MM-DD`. Blank filters include all available records; this is not a pay-period boundary. The response includes one row for each employee in the caller's synthetic directory, using the current configured employee-to-schedule mapping. New employees without a mapping are reported as `hasScheduleMapping:false`, `scheduleId:null`, with zero attributed rows; this does **not** mean absent or unworked.

# Source-grounded acceptance baseline (draft)

**Purpose:** record observable pass/fail behavior already implemented and define safe candidate acceptance criteria before tailoring. This is a working baseline, **not an approved rubric interpretation**. No standalone active MO-IT110 grading rubric was identified among the supplied files in the workspace; the older MO-IT108/107 documents and peer submissions inform scope, while the Terminal Assessment proposal is treated as placeholder material rather than an authoritative detailed specification.

**Scope rules:** synthetic data only; Firebase-backed persistence; no production local-memory fallback; no temporary features. Do not treat inferred attendance/payroll rules, peer-project choices, employee-to-account identity, reviewer authority, or access boundaries as approved policy. The earlier temporary 2026 preview has been removed; the Payroll workspace calculates nothing. See `docs/candidate-policy-review.md` and `docs/build-status-no-local-no-temp.md`. The previously published development rules remain unchanged.

# Prototype API contract

All routes are same-origin JSON endpoints. The production entry point requires `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID`; employee, attendance, and workflow routes require a signed-in Firebase user and use only that user's Firestore sandbox. The Java backend forwards the Firebase ID token to Firestore REST; Firestore Security Rules authorize requests. The loopback-only process-memory server is an automated test fixture, not a supported runtime. `POST /api/attendance` is not implemented and returns `405`; attendance is read-only until a persistent schedule/identity design and security rules are implemented. The project owner previously published `docs/firestore.rules`; live smoke tests verified leave and ticket create/cancel persistence and cross-user denial. The assistant has not changed Firebase Console settings. Future rule-file changes still require owner publication.

In Firebase mode, browser requests include:

```text
Authorization: Bearer <Firebase ID token>
X-Firebase-UID: <signed-in Firebase UID>
```

The UID header is not trusted for authorization: Firestore Rules compare it to the UID in the verified ID token. Do not log or persist ID tokens.

## Health

`GET /api/health`

Production mode:

```json
{"status":"ok","mode":"local-synthetic-demo"}
```

Firebase mode reports `firebase-user-sandbox`.

## Employee directory

`GET /api/employees`

`GET /api/employees?q=finance`

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "DEMO-002",
      "name": "Eli Santos",
      "department": "Finance",
      "role": "Payroll Associate",
      "location": "Taguig",
      "status": "Active"
    }
  ],
  "total": 3,
  "matched": 1
}
```

Search is case-insensitive across displayed fields. `total` is the full user-scoped demo directory size; `matched` is the returned count.

`GET /api/employees/{employeeId}` returns `{"item": {...}}` or `404 {"error":"Employee not found"}`.

`POST /api/employees` creates an owner-sandbox fictional record; `PUT /api/employees/{employeeId}` updates its allowed directory fields. Both accept only `name`, `department`, `role`, `location`, and `status` (`Active` or `On leave`). Unknown fields—including client-supplied IDs, payroll values, and government identifiers—are rejected. The server generates IDs in the `DEMO-<12 uppercase hex characters>` form. Responses are `201` and `200`, respectively, with `{"item": {...}}`. Firebase writes use only the caller's `users/{uid}/demoEmployees` path and existing owner rules; they do not grant HR/supervisor roles. Local mode has no user authentication and stores changes in a single process-memory demo store shared by callers of that API process. Delete, termination, schedule assignment, and audit-history routes are not implemented. A new record has no schedule mapping, so attendance returns an empty list until a separately approved schedule mapping is configured.

## Raw attendance

`GET /api/attendance?employeeId=DEMO-001`

Optional ISO date filters: `from=YYYY-MM-DD` and/or `to=YYYY-MM-DD`. If both are supplied, `from` must be on or before `to`; filtering is inclusive. `employeeId` is required.

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "attendanceId": 5001,
      "scheduleId": 101,
      "date": "2026-10-01",
      "timeIn": "08:01",
      "timeOut": "17:00",
      "dayType": "DEMO"
    }
  ],
  "count": 1,
  "hoursCalculated": false
}
```

Possible errors: `400` for missing employee ID, invalid date syntax, or reversed range; `404` for an unknown employee; `401` for missing/expired Firebase sign-in; `403` when Firestore Rules deny the request. Raw times only; no hours or pay are derived.

`POST /api/attendance` returns `405 Method not allowed`. No attendance writer is implemented in any runtime. The former process-memory attendance route/form and mutable-store interface were removed. A future write path requires approved capture semantics, durable schedule/employee assignments, atomic uniqueness, and authorization tests.

Attendance attribution now reads `users/{uid}/demoEmployeeSchedules/{employeeId}`. The opt-in synthetic seed creates only the pre-existing fictional fixture links; these opaque IDs are not shift definitions or approved schedules. Firestore rules permit owner reads and validated creates, and deny mapping update/delete. Publish the updated `docs/firestore.rules` before using this seed/mapping path in Firebase. Existing sandbox records without a persisted mapping are left unlinked; the API does not fall back to a hard-coded mapping.

### Raw attendance coverage report

`GET /api/reports/attendance`

Optional inclusive ISO date filters: `from=YYYY-MM-DD` and/or `to=YYYY-MM-DD`. Blank filters include all available records; this is not a pay-period boundary. The response includes one row for each employee in the caller's synthetic directory, using the current configured employee-to-schedule mapping. New employees without a mapping are reported as `hasScheduleMapping:false`, `scheduleId:null`, with zero attributed rows; this does **not** mean absent or unworked.

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "employeeId": "DEMO-001",
      "employeeName": "Mara Rivera",
      "scheduleId": 101,
      "hasScheduleMapping": true,
      "rawRecordCount": 3,
      "firstRecordDate": "2026-10-01",
      "lastRecordDate": "2026-10-15"
    }
  ],
  "count": 1,
  "from": null,
  "to": null,
  "hoursCalculated": false
}
```

Counts and date bounds summarize stored raw rows only. No hours, worked-day classification, absence, or pay values are calculated. The endpoint is read-only and uses the same user-scoped employee and attendance paths as the raw attendance query. Possible errors: `400` invalid date syntax or reversed range; `401` missing/expired sign-in; `403` when Firestore Rules deny a read.

## Leave requests and tickets

`GET /api/workflows` returns only the current user's lists:

```json
{"leaveRequests":[],"tickets":[],"storage":"user-scoped-firestore"}
```

- `POST /api/workflows/leave` accepts `employeeId`, `leaveType`, `startDate`, `endDate`, and optional `note`. The server derives the employee name from the caller's own synthetic directory, validates supported leave types and ISO calendar dates, and creates a `Pending review` record.
- `POST /api/workflows/tickets` accepts `employeeId`, `ticketType`, and `summary`. The server derives the employee name and queue label and creates an `Open` record. No ticket is delivered or assigned to a real handler.
- `POST /api/workflows/leave/{requestId}/cancel` and `POST /api/workflows/tickets/{ticketId}/cancel` allow only the pending/open-to-cancelled transition. Delete, review, approve, reject, and resolve routes do not exist.
- Firebase records use `users/{uid}/demoLeaveRequests/{requestId}` and `users/{uid}/demoTickets/{ticketId}`. The candidate Firestore rules allow owner-only read/create/cancel; they deny deletes and all reviewer actions. Records are limited to the user's synthetic employee directory and contain no payroll calculations.
- The isolated test fixture returns `storage:"local-process-memory"` only inside automated tests. The production runtime requires Firebase and never selects this store.

Possible errors: `400` invalid request fields or dates; `401` missing/expired sign-in; `403` Firestore rules deny the operation (publish the updated `docs/firestore.rules`); `404` employee/request/ticket not found in the caller's sandbox; `409` invalid workflow transition.

## Opt-in demo seed

`POST /api/demo/seed`

Requires Firebase Authentication and Firestore mode. Creates missing fictional documents only in:

- `users/{uid}/demoEmployees/{employeeId}`
- `users/{uid}/demoAttendance/{attendanceId}`

The endpoint does not overwrite existing records and marks attendance with `dayType: "DEMO"`. It cannot create payroll documents. Firestore Rules are in `docs/firestore.rules`.

## Scope and security

- No production employee or payroll records.
- No service account, Admin SDK, or privileged credentials.
- Current user-owned sandbox rules are development-only, not an organizational role model.
- Payroll formulas, pay-period logic, and calculations remain blocked until specified by supplied course materials.
The prototype now has:

1. Browser email/password sign-in and dev-account creation using Firebase Authentication.
2. In-memory browser auth persistence; this prototype does not persist the Firebase session in local storage.
3. A Java REST adapter that forwards the signed-in ID token to Firestore. Firestore Security Rules remain the access gate; there is no Admin SDK or service-account credential.
4. A per-user development sandbox: `users/{uid}/demoEmployees`, `demoAttendance`, `demoLeaveRequests`, and `demoTickets`; the published workflow rules were live-smoke-tested for leave create/cancel.
5. An explicit **Add synthetic demo data** action that creates fictional employee/attendance records only. The Payroll workspace remains disabled behind a policy gate; it calculates no amounts.

async function seedSyntheticDemoData() {
  seedDemoButton.disabled = true;
  seedDemoButton.textContent = 'Writing synthetic records…';
  try {
    const response = await fetch('/api/demo/seed', { method: 'POST', headers: await apiHeaders() });
    const payload = await response.json();
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(payload.error || `Request failed (${response.status})`);
    resultCount.textContent = `${payload.employeesCreated} employees and ${payload.attendanceCreated} attendance entries added`;
    await loadEmployees();
  } catch (error) {
    showTableMessage(error.message || 'Could not write the synthetic demo records.');
    resultCount.textContent = 'Demo setup failed';
  } finally {
    seedDemoButton.disabled = false;
    seedDemoButton.textContent = 'Add synthetic demo data';
  }
}

function applyWorkflowItem(collection, item, storage) {
  const current = state.workflow[collection];
  const index = current.findIndex(existing => existing.id === item.id);
  const next = [...current];
  if (index < 0) next.unshift(item);
  else next[index] = item;
  state.workflow = { ...state.workflow, [collection]: next };
  setWorkflowStorageMode(storage === 'user-scoped-firestore' ? 'User-scoped Firestore' : 'Isolated test fixture memory');
  renderWorkflow();
}

import com.google.gson.JsonObject;

/** Creates only fictional, clearly marked records in one signed-in user's demo sandbox. */
public final class DemoSeedService {
    private final FirestoreRestClient client;

    public DemoSeedService(FirestoreRestClient client) {
        if (client == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("client must not be null");
        this.client = client;
    }

    public SeedResult seedMissingSyntheticRecords() {
        int employeesCreated = 0;
        for (Employee employee : new InMemoryEmployeeStore().findAll()) {
            if (client.createDocument(client.userCollection("demoEmployees"), employee.getId(), employeeFields(employee))) {
                employeesCreated++;
            }
        }

        int mappingsCreated = 0;
        EmployeeScheduleStore sampleMappings = new InMemoryEmployeeScheduleStore();
        for (Employee employee : new InMemoryEmployeeStore().findAll()) {
            java.util.OptionalInt scheduleId = sampleMappings.findScheduleIdForEmployee(employee.getId());
            if (scheduleId.isPresent() && client.createDocument(client.userCollection("demoEmployeeSchedules"),
                employee.getId(), scheduleMappingFields(employee.getId(), scheduleId.getAsInt()))) {
                mappingsCreated++;
            }
        }

        int attendanceCreated = 0;
        InMemoryAttendanceStore sampleAttendance = new InMemoryAttendanceStore();
        for (int scheduleId : Arrays.asList(101, 102, 103)) {
            for (AttendanceRecord record : sampleAttendance.findByScheduleId(scheduleId)) {
                if (client.createDocument(client.userCollection("demoAttendance"),
                    Integer.toString(record.getAttendanceId()), attendanceFields(record))) {
                    attendanceCreated++;
                }
            }
        }
        return new SeedResult(employeesCreated, mappingsCreated, attendanceCreated);
    }

    private void handleAttendance(HttpExchange exchange) throws IOException {
        if (!"GET".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod())) {
            sendJson(exchange, 405, "{\"error\":\"Method not allowed\"}");
            return;
        }
        String employeeId = queryParameter(exchange.getRequestURI().getRawQuery(), "employeeId");
        if (employeeId == null || employeeId.trim().isEmpty()) {
            sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"employeeId is required\"}");
            return;
        }
        try {
            RequestServices services = servicesFor(exchange);
            LocalDate from = parseOptionalDate(queryParameter(exchange.getRequestURI().getRawQuery(), "from"));
            LocalDate to = parseOptionalDate(queryParameter(exchange.getRequestURI().getRawQuery(), "to"));
            AttendanceService attendanceService = new AttendanceService(services.employeeService,
                services.scheduleStore, services.attendanceStore);
            List<AttendanceRecord> records = attendanceService.findForEmployee(employeeId, from, to);
            sendJson(exchange, 200, attendanceToJson(records));
        } catch (DateTimeParseException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"Dates must use YYYY-MM-DD\"}");
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException ex) {
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"" + escapeJson(ex.getMessage()) + "\"}");
        } catch (java.util.NoSuchElementException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 404, "{\"error\":\"Employee not found\"}");
        } catch (FirestoreException ex) {
            sendApiError(exchange, ex);
        }
    }

    private void handleAttendanceReport(HttpExchange exchange) throws IOException {

            return;
        }

            RequestServices services = servicesFor(exchange);
            String query = exchange.getRequestURI().getRawQuery();
            LocalDate from = parseOptionalDate(queryParameter(query, "from"));
            LocalDate to = parseOptionalDate(queryParameter(query, "to"));
            AttendanceService attendanceService = new AttendanceService(services.employeeService,
                services.scheduleStore, services.attendanceStore);

# Build status — persistent-only target

**This document supersedes earlier statements that a process-memory product mode or a temporary payroll preview is an acceptable deliverable.** The user's current requirement is “No locals, no temps.” No peer implementation or earlier policy candidate changes that requirement.

## Product behavior now enforced

- `AppServer.main` requires `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID`. The only no-Firebase entry-point exception is `MOTORPH_TEST_MODE=true` while binding to a loopback host; the production run scripts do not set it. Direct constructor-based local services remain test fixtures used by the isolated test harness, not a supported deployment mode.
- `web/app.js` does not open the workspace if Firebase web configuration is missing. It shows a setup error instead. The unauthenticated local workspace is available only in the test build flag `VITE_E2E_TEST_MODE=true` used by the test runner.
- Removed the browser-only 2026 payroll preview, rule table, preview CSV, preview UI/CSS, and preview-specific unit tests. The Payroll view now shows a blocking configuration page and calculates nothing.
- The test-only synthetic fixture remains intentionally process-memory-backed so the UI/API contract can be exercised without using real staff data or writing test records to a live Firebase project. This is test infrastructure, not a deployable local-data feature.

## Verified after these changes

- `npm run test:web` — passed, 51 browser/domain tests.
- `./test.sh` — passed 182 Java checks, plus a production-entry-point assertion that startup fails without Firebase configuration.
- `npm run test:e2e` — passed the isolated fixture flow and the browser fail-closed check when Firebase configuration is absent; payroll UI check confirms that no temporary preview/calculator is rendered.
- `npm run build` — passed.
- `npm audit --audit-level=high` — 0 vulnerabilities.
- Live sandbox preview is running on port `8090`; `GET /api/health` returns `firebase-user-sandbox`. This verifies the Firebase-configured server starts, not browser sign-in, cloud reads, or the un-published schedule-mapping rules.
- No Firebase Console action or Firestore write was performed in this slice. Live Firebase integration is not newly re-verified here. The Firestore rules file now includes the owner-scoped schedule-mapping collection; the project owner must publish that rules update before seeded attendance can be linked in Firebase. The rule text was not run through the Firestore emulator or published in this slice.

These are verification results for the code paths exercised, not proof that the full product is complete or deployed.

## Current persistent vertical slices

- Firebase Auth sign-in and caller-token-forwarded Firestore REST access with user-owned paths and reviewed rules.
- Limited synthetic directory read/create/update.
- Raw attendance Firestore reads/reports use owner-scoped `demoEmployeeSchedules` mapping documents; there is no attendance write route/form. The opt-in synthetic seed persists the pre-existing fixture links as data. Schedule assignment editing remains disabled.
- Synthetic leave/ticket create, list, and owner-side cancel; no reviewers, approvals, balances, or notification semantics.
- Search/filter/sort/export over existing sandbox data.

The seeded records are fictional examples and are not copied from the process-memory fixture. The cloud schema is still a per-user development sandbox, not a company tenant or validated production employee database.

## Next implementation slices

1. **Schedule administration and raw attendance capture:** establish an approved schedule model and assignment lifecycle, then a durable attendance writer with authorization/rules tests. The former process-memory attendance writer has been removed; `POST /api/attendance` returns `405`. Current immutable seed mappings are not an editable schedule-management feature. The mappings are copied from the earlier synthetic fixture only; they are not business schedule definitions. `dayType=DEMO` is sample data, not a classification policy.
2. **Identity, organization scope, and roles:** define tenant membership, employee-user mapping, and role-to-action boundaries before adding supervisor or HR review access. Existing owner-only Firebase rules do not support this.
3. **Attendance/timesheet calculation:** keep raw timestamps separate from calculated time until break, shift, timezone, overnight, grace/rounding, correction, holiday, leave, premium, and golden-case rules are approved.
4. **Durable payroll:** after approved examples and statutory period/basis/rounding choices, implement a versioned calculator, immutable input/output snapshots, auditability, saved runs and payslip authorization. Until then, there is no payroll preview or calculation route.
5. **Operations and deployment:** emulator/rules coverage, environment and origin configuration, indexes, backup/retention, error reporting, recovery, accessibility/security review, and a deployment smoke test.

No unresolved rule should be filled from a peer submission without user approval. Keep all test records synthetic and isolated; do not use user or employee production data during development.

# Prototype API contract

All routes are same-origin JSON endpoints. The production entry point requires `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID`; employee, attendance, and workflow routes require a signed-in Firebase user and use only that user's Firestore sandbox. The Java backend forwards the Firebase ID token to Firestore REST; Firestore Security Rules authorize requests. The loopback-only process-memory server is an automated test fixture, not a supported runtime. `POST /api/attendance` is not implemented and returns `405`; attendance is read-only until a persistent schedule/identity design and security rules are implemented. The project owner previously published `docs/firestore.rules`; live smoke tests verified leave and ticket create/cancel persistence and cross-user denial. The assistant has not changed Firebase Console settings. Future rule-file changes still require owner publication.

In Firebase mode, browser requests include:

```text
Authorization: Bearer <Firebase ID token>
X-Firebase-UID: <signed-in Firebase UID>
```

The UID header is not trusted for authorization: Firestore Rules compare it to the UID in the verified ID token. Do not log or persist ID tokens.

## Health

`GET /api/health`

Firebase-backed production mode returns `{"status":"ok","mode":"firebase-user-sandbox"}`. The loopback test fixture reports `local-synthetic-demo`; it is not a production mode.

## Employee directory

`GET /api/employees`

`GET /api/employees?q=finance`

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "DEMO-002",
      "name": "Eli Santos",
      "department": "Finance",
      "role": "Payroll Associate",
      "location": "Taguig",
      "status": "Active"
    }
  ],
  "total": 3,
  "matched": 1
}
```

Search is case-insensitive across displayed fields. `total` is the full user-scoped demo directory size; `matched` is the returned count.

`GET /api/employees/{employeeId}` returns `{"item": {...}}` or `404 {"error":"Employee not found"}`.

`POST /api/employees` creates an owner-sandbox fictional record; `PUT /api/employees/{employeeId}` updates its allowed directory fields. Both accept only `name`, `department`, `role`, `location`, and `status` (`Active` or `On leave`). Unknown fields—including client-supplied IDs, payroll values, and government identifiers—are rejected. The server generates IDs in the `DEMO-<12 uppercase hex characters>` form. Responses are `201` and `200`, respectively, with `{"item": {...}}`. Firebase writes use only the caller's `users/{uid}/demoEmployees` path and existing owner rules; they do not grant HR/supervisor roles. The isolated test fixture has no user authentication and stores changes in process memory; it is not exposed by the production entry point. Delete, termination, schedule assignment editing, and audit-history routes are not implemented. A new employee has no schedule mapping; mappings are read from persistent owner-scoped `demoEmployeeSchedules` documents.

## Raw attendance

`GET /api/attendance?employeeId=DEMO-001`

Optional ISO date filters: `from=YYYY-MM-DD` and/or `to=YYYY-MM-DD`. If both are supplied, `from` must be on or before `to`; filtering is inclusive. `employeeId` is required.

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "attendanceId": 5001,
      "scheduleId": 101,
      "date": "2026-10-01",
      "timeIn": "08:01",
      "timeOut": "17:00",
      "dayType": "DEMO"
    }
  ],
  "count": 1,
  "hoursCalculated": false
}
```

Possible errors: `400` for missing employee ID, invalid date syntax, or reversed range; `404` for an unknown employee; `401` for missing/expired Firebase sign-in; `403` when Firestore Rules deny the request. Raw times only; no hours or pay are derived.

`POST /api/attendance` returns `405 Method not allowed`. No attendance writer is implemented in any runtime. The former process-memory attendance route/form and mutable-store interface were removed. A future write path requires approved capture semantics, durable schedule/employee assignments, atomic uniqueness, and authorization tests.

Attendance attribution now reads `users/{uid}/demoEmployeeSchedules/{employeeId}`. The opt-in synthetic seed creates only the pre-existing fictional fixture links; these opaque IDs are not shift definitions or approved schedules. Firestore rules permit owner reads and validated creates, and deny mapping update/delete. Publish the updated `docs/firestore.rules` before using this seed/mapping path in Firebase. Existing sandbox records without a persisted mapping are left unlinked; the API does not fall back to a hard-coded mapping.

### Raw attendance coverage report

`GET /api/reports/attendance`

Optional inclusive ISO date filters: `from=YYYY-MM-DD` and/or `to=YYYY-MM-DD`. Blank filters include all available records; this is not a pay-period boundary. The response includes one row for each employee in the caller's synthetic directory, using the caller-scoped persisted `demoEmployeeSchedules` mapping. New employees without a mapping are reported as `hasScheduleMapping:false`, `scheduleId:null`, with zero attributed rows; this does **not** mean absent or unworked.

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "employeeId": "DEMO-001",
      "employeeName": "Mara Rivera",
      "scheduleId": 101,
      "hasScheduleMapping": true,
      "rawRecordCount": 3,
      "firstRecordDate": "2026-10-01",
      "lastRecordDate": "2026-10-15"
    }
  ],
  "count": 1,
  "from": null,
  "to": null,
  "hoursCalculated": false
}
```

Counts and date bounds summarize stored raw rows only. No hours, worked-day classification, absence, or pay values are calculated. The endpoint is read-only and uses the same user-scoped employee and attendance paths as the raw attendance query. Possible errors: `400` invalid date syntax or reversed range; `401` missing/expired sign-in; `403` when Firestore Rules deny a read.

## Leave requests and tickets

`GET /api/workflows` returns only the current user's lists:

```json
{"leaveRequests":[],"tickets":[],"storage":"user-scoped-firestore"}
```

- `POST /api/workflows/leave` accepts `employeeId`, `leaveType`, `startDate`, `endDate`, and optional `note`. The server derives the employee name from the caller's own synthetic directory, validates supported leave types and ISO calendar dates, and creates a `Pending review` record.
- `POST /api/workflows/tickets` accepts `employeeId`, `ticketType`, and `summary`. The server derives the employee name and queue label and creates an `Open` record. No ticket is delivered or assigned to a real handler.
- `POST /api/workflows/leave/{requestId}/cancel` and `POST /api/workflows/tickets/{ticketId}/cancel` allow only the pending/open-to-cancelled transition. Delete, review, approve, reject, and resolve routes do not exist.
- Firebase records use `users/{uid}/demoLeaveRequests/{requestId}` and `users/{uid}/demoTickets/{ticketId}`. The candidate Firestore rules allow owner-only read/create/cancel; they deny deletes and all reviewer actions. Records are limited to the user's synthetic employee directory and contain no payroll calculations.
- The isolated test fixture returns `storage:"local-process-memory"` only inside automated tests. The production runtime requires Firebase and never selects this store.

Possible errors: `400` invalid request fields or dates; `401` missing/expired sign-in; `403` Firestore rules deny the operation (publish the updated `docs/firestore.rules`); `404` employee/request/ticket not found in the caller's sandbox; `409` invalid workflow transition.

## Opt-in demo seed

`POST /api/demo/seed`

Requires Firebase Authentication and Firestore mode. Creates missing fictional documents only in:

- `users/{uid}/demoEmployees/{employeeId}`
- `users/{uid}/demoEmployeeSchedules/{employeeId}`
- `users/{uid}/demoAttendance/{attendanceId}`

The response includes `employeesCreated`, `scheduleMappingsCreated`, and `attendanceCreated`. The endpoint preflights the mapping collection permission before writing, does not overwrite existing records, and marks seeded attendance with `dayType: "DEMO"`. It cannot create payroll documents. Firestore Rules are in `docs/firestore.rules`.

## Scope and security

- No production employee or payroll records.
- No service account, Admin SDK, or privileged credentials.
- Current user-owned sandbox rules are development-only, not an organizational role model.
- Payroll formulas, pay-period logic, and calculations remain blocked until specified by supplied course materials.

No standalone active MO-IT110 grading rubric was identified among the supplied files in the workspace; the older MO-IT108/107 documents and peer submissions inform scope, while the Terminal Assessment proposal is treated as placeholder material rather than an authoritative detailed specification.

Do not treat inferred attendance/payroll rules, peer-project choices, employee-to-account identity, reviewer authority, or access boundaries as approved policy. The earlier temporary 2026 preview has been removed; the Payroll workspace calculates nothing. See `docs/candidate-policy-review.md` and `docs/build-status-no-local-no-temp.md`. Some screens are available in both modes and therefore are **not** local-only even though their filtering/rendering runs in JavaScript.

### Earlier local-only feature file contents (some files have since been removed)

- `MutableAttendanceStore.java` and the attendance-create service/route/form have been deleted; older references in this inventory describe history, not current files.
- `src/main/java/ph/motorph/web/InMemoryAttendanceStore.java` — synthetic attendance fixtures and synchronized in-memory create/duplicate check; store lifetime is the Java process.
- `src/main/java/ph/motorph/web/AttendanceService.java` — employee existence check, existing mapping lookup, mutable-store check, fixed `DEMO` assignment; it does not create mappings or calculate hours.
- `src/main/java/ph/motorph/web/AppServer.java` — POST route whitelist, date/time parsing, local-mode guard, JSON response and status codes. Firebase mode is rejected before store access.
- `web/index.html` — the local-only attendance form, explanatory boundary text, raw-record calendar, report/export/search UI.
- `web/app.js` — posts local raw input, loads scoped reads, renders the calendar and reports, cross-module search, JSON export, and employee-linked record details. `showWorkspace(user)` hides the create form for signed-in Firebase users.
- The former payroll preview modules were deleted; no browser calculator is present.
- `test/java/ph/motorph/web/AttendanceServiceTest.java` and `AppServerIntegrationTest.java` — domain/API checks for mapping, fixed DEMO label, uniqueness, time order, schedule injection rejection, and Firebase POST rejection.
- `test/e2e/synthetic-fixture.e2e.js` — local browser coverage including create success/rejections, calendars, exports, search, JSON bundle, and no-page-error/mobile checks.
- `docs/local-demo-inventory.md` — shorter local-vs-Firebase summary; this file is the more complete implementation inventory and pseudocode.

## 3. Capabilities that are not local-only

These currently use existing owner-scoped GET APIs and work in local preview and Firebase user-sandbox mode, subject to the user having access to the signed-in sandbox:

- Employee list/search/detail, allowlisted synthetic directory create/update, and HR/Team views.
- Raw attendance GET by employee and optional inclusive date range; Firebase attendance is read-only.
- Owner-scoped leave/ticket GET/create/cancel routes with existing field validation and published user-sandbox rules.
- Attendance coverage report, raw attendance calendar/date selection, employee-linked record detail/count summaries, cross-module search, CSV exports, and the read-only workspace JSON download.
- Attendance capture is not available in the product; `POST /api/attendance` returns `405` in all modes.

No client-side report in this list infers absent/present/tardy status, hours, overtime, leave balances, approval, eligibility, or pay. Stored status/type/queue labels are displayed as labels only.

## 4. Current system pseudocode — what works today

### 4.1 Startup and mode selection

```text
read frontend Firebase configuration
if Firebase configuration is complete:
    initialize Firebase Auth
    show sign-in gate until Firebase reports a signed-in user
    for each API call, send caller ID token and UID headers
else:
    show LOCAL PREVIEW without authentication

Java API startup:
    if Firebase project is absent:
        use shared process-memory employee/workflow/attendance stores
    else:
        require valid-looking Firebase session headers for user-scoped reads/writes
        build Firestore services rooted at users/{uid}/...
        keep attendance store read-only
```

The Firestore Rules, rather than a UI label, are the security boundary. There is no organizational role or employee-account mapping in this build.

### 4.2 Synthetic employee directory

```text
GET /api/employees [optional search]
    select local store OR current user's Firestore employee collection
    return allowed synthetic fields and total count

POST /api/employees
    reject unknown fields and client-supplied ID
    validate name, department, role label, location, demo status
    generate synthetic ID on server
    save to local process store OR owner-scoped Firestore collection

PUT /api/employees/{id}
    reject unknown fields
    validate allowlisted directory fields
    update local process store OR owner-scoped Firestore document

UI
    search/sort/filter/list/detail
    HR/Team views display the same synthetic directory; no HR role is inferred
```

### 4.3 Raw attendance query, local create, and reports

```text
GET /api/attendance?employeeId=...&from=...&to=...
    require an existing employee
    find only the existing configured schedule mapping
    read rows from local store OR caller's Firestore collection
    apply inclusive optional dates; reject reversed range
    return raw attendanceID/scheduleID/date/timeIn/timeOut/dayType
    return hoursCalculated=false

POST /api/attendance (isolated test fixture only)
    if Firebase project configured: return 403 before reading the body/store
    reject all fields except employeeId/date/timeIn/timeOut
    parse ISO date and strict 24-hour HH:mm times
    find employee and pre-existing schedule mapping; never assign one
    construct AttendanceRecord with server-fixed dayType=DEMO
    synchronized store insertion rejects duplicate (scheduleID,date)
    model validation rejects timeIn > timeOut
    return 201; no hours/classification/pay output

GET /api/reports/attendance
    enumerate caller's synthetic employees and configured mappings
    count stored raw rows/date bounds for optional inclusive date range
    unmapped => hasScheduleMapping=false, count=0; do not call it absence

Browser
    raw table/calendar shows only loaded record dates/times
    two calendar clicks apply an inclusive selected range
    employee-linked summary joins raw row counts and stored workflow counts by ID
    no date without a row is classified
```

### 4.4 Leave and ticket demonstrations

```text
GET /api/workflows
    read only current sandbox's leaveRequests and tickets

POST /api/workflows/leave
    accept validated synthetic employee ID, leave type, ordered dates, optional bounded note
    derive employee name from current sandbox directory
    assign only the existing demonstration status
    save only under current UID Firestore path; fail closed without Firebase

POST /api/workflows/tickets
    accept validated synthetic employee ID, documented ticket type, bounded summary
    derive employee name and documented queue label
    assign only existing demonstration status
    save only under current UID Firestore path; fail closed without Firebase

# Local-only inventory, current behavior, and full-build pseudocode

**Status date:** 2026-11-04  
**Purpose:** identify every behavior that is genuinely local-only, explain its contents and implementation paths, state what would be required to make it durable/non-local, and provide pseudocode for the current build and the remaining full-system work. This is an engineering inventory—not a claim that the app is a complete or production-ready payroll system.

> **Superseding status:** this inventory records code paths and pseudocode from the earlier prototype. Since the current “no locals, no temps” instruction, the normal API entry point now requires Firebase, the browser fails closed without Firebase, and the temporary payroll preview was removed. Process-memory employee/workflow stores remain only inside the loopback-isolated test fixture. The former attendance-entry form, route, and mutable store contract have been removed entirely. The active status is `docs/build-status-no-local-no-temp.md`; do not read older rows below as authorization to expose these paths in the product.

## 1. Current build status

The earlier prototype had local process-memory and temporary payroll paths. The current product entry points require Firebase and no longer expose the temporary payroll preview; only the automated loopback fixture exercises in-memory data. Persistent capabilities and outstanding gates are summarized in `docs/build-status-no-local-no-temp.md`.

The earlier 59-test baseline predates the removal of the temporary preview. Current verification is recorded in `docs/build-status-no-local-no-temp.md`; re-run dependency audit after any dependency change. The exact Arena preview-origin Firebase sign-in and production deployment are not verified.

Prior feature-parity estimates in older docs are not current completion claims. The current acceptance target is a persistent, non-temporary product; see `docs/build-status-no-local-no-temp.md`. The current Firestore rules file was edited to add schedule-link documents, but no Console publication or live Firebase data change was made in this slice.

## 2. What is genuinely local-only

“Local-only” here means that behavior either uses the unauthenticated Java process-memory store or is performed only in the browser without a durable server record. Some screens are available in both modes and therefore are **not** local-only even though their filtering/rendering runs in JavaScript.

| Local-only item | What it does | Contents / implementation | What must change for a non-local or durable version |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Isolated in-memory test fixture | Automated browser/API checks exercise synthetic data without writing to live Firebase. It is not a product runtime. | The E2E harness explicitly sets the loopback-only `MOTORPH_TEST_MODE` and `VITE_E2E_TEST_MODE` flags. Normal run scripts do not set these; the production API and browser fail closed if Firebase is missing. | Keep this isolated to test-only invocation, bind to loopback, and never migrate test rows into a user account. The current test coverage does not prove live Firebase behavior. |
| Removed local raw-attendance create path | Previously created a row only in memory. Removed on 2026-11-04; no UI, route, mutation service, or mutable-store interface remains. | Historical implementation is documented below only for traceability; tests now assert `POST /api/attendance` is `405`. | A future persistent implementation requires a durable mapping source, approved capture schema, unique-key design, authorized rules, and integration tests. Do not reintroduce an in-memory version as a product feature. |
| Withdrawn temporary payroll preview | Was a client-only synthetic calculator; it was removed on 2026-11-04 under the no-temporary-features instruction. | The former calculator/UI/rules/CSS/CSV and preview-only tests are no longer shipped. The Payroll view now calculates nothing. | Implement only a persistent, versioned payroll feature after policy, security, approval, retention, and independently verified example decisions are approved. |
| Local-only E2E environment | Proves the local browser flow against a disposable local Java API and test data. | `test/e2e/synthetic-fixture.e2e.js` launches a loopback-only synthetic API and Vite fixture with explicit test-only flags and also checks production fail-closed behavior. It tests UI and API behavior but does not establish that the Arena preview origin or a live Firebase deployment works. | Keep these fast tests, and add Firebase Emulator/API contract tests for signed-in reads/writes and rule denials. A live preview-origin smoke still needs the exact authorized domain and a disposable account. Do not use undeletable workflow records for repeated smoke tests. |
| Downloaded workspace JSON | A client-created file download, not cloud backup/restore. | `web/workspace-export.js` creates a synthetic-only snapshot with employee records, raw attendance rows, leave requests and tickets; it marks `hoursCalculated:false` and `payrollIncluded:false`. `fetchSandboxSnapshot()` obtains data through GET APIs. | No change is needed for reading the current user’s Firebase sandbox; the bundle already uses scoped GETs when signed in. To restore/import the file into Firebase, add a separately designed import path, duplicate-ID handling, schema versioning, per-collection validation, user ownership checks, and preview/confirm/rollback behavior. Current export is not a restore function or automated backup. |

### Earlier local-only feature file contents (some files have since been removed)

- `MutableAttendanceStore.java` and the attendance-create service/route/form have been deleted; older references in this inventory describe history, not current files.
- `src/main/java/ph/motorph/web/InMemoryAttendanceStore.java` — synthetic attendance fixtures and synchronized in-memory create/duplicate check; store lifetime is the Java process.
- `src/main/java/ph/motorph/web/AttendanceService.java` — employee existence check, existing mapping lookup, mutable-store check, fixed `DEMO` assignment; it does not create mappings or calculate hours.
- `src/main/java/ph/motorph/web/AppServer.java` — POST route whitelist, date/time parsing, local-mode guard, JSON response and status codes. Firebase mode is rejected before store access.
- `web/index.html` — the local-only attendance form, explanatory boundary text, raw-record calendar, report/export/search UI.
- `web/app.js` — posts local raw input, loads scoped reads, renders the calendar and reports, cross-module search, JSON export, and employee-linked record details. `showWorkspace(user)` hides the create form for signed-in Firebase users.
- The former payroll preview modules were deleted; no browser calculator is present.
- `test/java/ph/motorph/web/AttendanceServiceTest.java` and `AppServerIntegrationTest.java` — domain/API checks for mapping, fixed DEMO label, uniqueness, time order, schedule injection rejection, and Firebase POST rejection.
- `test/e2e/synthetic-fixture.e2e.js` — local browser coverage including create success/rejections, calendars, exports, search, JSON bundle, and no-page-error/mobile checks.
- `docs/local-demo-inventory.md` — shorter local-vs-Firebase summary; this file is the more complete implementation inventory and pseudocode.

## 3. Capabilities that are not local-only

These currently use existing owner-scoped GET APIs and work in local preview and Firebase user-sandbox mode, subject to the user having access to the signed-in sandbox:

- Employee list/search/detail, allowlisted synthetic directory create/update, and HR/Team views.
- Raw attendance GET by employee and optional inclusive date range; Firebase attendance is read-only.
- Owner-scoped leave/ticket GET/create/cancel routes with existing field validation and published user-sandbox rules.
- Attendance coverage report, raw attendance calendar/date selection, employee-linked record detail/count summaries, cross-module search, CSV exports, and the read-only workspace JSON download.
- Attendance capture is not available in the product; `POST /api/attendance` returns `405` in all modes.

No client-side report in this list infers absent/present/tardy status, hours, overtime, leave balances, approval, eligibility, or pay. Stored status/type/queue labels are displayed as labels only.

===== web/attendance-calendar.js
const WEEKDAYS = ['Monday', 'Tuesday', 'Wednesday', 'Thursday', 'Friday', 'Saturday', 'Sunday'];
const MONTH_FORMAT = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en', { month: 'long', year: 'numeric' });

function dateKey(year, monthIndex, day) {
  return `${String(year).padStart(4, '0')}-${String(monthIndex + 1).padStart(2, '0')}-${String(day).padStart(2, '0')}`;
}

function isIsoDate(value) {
  if (typeof value !== 'string' || !/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(value)) return false;
  const [year, month, day] = value.split('-').map(Number);
  const parsed = new Date(year, month - 1, day);
  return parsed.getFullYear() === year && parsed.getMonth() === month - 1 && parsed.getDate() === day;
}

/** Build a calendar of stored raw rows only; a blank date has no absence or work-status meaning. */
export function buildAttendanceCalendar(monthDate, records = []) {
  if (!(monthDate instanceof Date) || Number.isNaN(monthDate.getTime())) {
    throw new TypeError('A valid month date is required.');
  }
  if (!Array.isArray(records)) throw new TypeError('Attendance records must be an array.');

  const year = monthDate.getFullYear();
  const monthIndex = monthDate.getMonth();
  const daysInMonth = new Date(year, monthIndex + 1, 0).getDate();
  const mondayOffset = (new Date(year, monthIndex, 1).getDay() + 6) % 7;
  const byDate = new Map();
  records.filter(record => record && isIsoDate(record.date) && record.date.startsWith(`${year}-${String(monthIndex + 1).padStart(2, '0')}-`))
    .forEach(record => {
      if (!byDate.has(record.date)) byDate.set(record.date, []);
      byDate.get(record.date).push(record);
    });

  const cells = Array.from({ length: 42 }, (_, index) => {
    const day = index - mondayOffset + 1;
    const inMonth = day >= 1 && day <= daysInMonth;
    const date = inMonth ? dateKey(year, monthIndex, day) : '';
    return {
      date,
      day: inMonth ? day : null,
      inMonth,
      records: inMonth ? (byDate.get(date) || []).slice() : []
    };
  });

  return {
    title: MONTH_FORMAT.format(new Date(year, monthIndex, 1)),
    weekdays: WEEKDAYS.slice(),
    weeks: Array.from({ length: 6 }, (_, index) => cells.slice(index * 7, index * 7 + 7))
  };
}
===== web/leave-calendar.js
const WEEKDAYS = ['Monday', 'Tuesday', 'Wednesday', 'Thursday', 'Friday', 'Saturday', 'Sunday'];
const MONTH_FORMAT = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en', { month: 'long', year: 'numeric' });

function dateKey(year, monthIndex, day) {
  return `${String(year).padStart(4, '0')}-${String(monthIndex + 1).padStart(2, '0')}-${String(day).padStart(2, '0')}`;
}

function validIsoDate(value) {
  if (typeof value !== 'string' || !/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(value)) return false;
  const [year, month, day] = value.split('-').map(Number);
  const parsed = new Date(year, month - 1, day);
  return parsed.getFullYear() === year && parsed.getMonth() === month - 1 && parsed.getDate() === day;
}

/** Build a display-only month view of submitted request ranges; this is not an approved leave calendar. */
export function buildLeaveCalendar(monthDate, requests = [], today = new Date()) {
  if (!(monthDate instanceof Date) || Number.isNaN(monthDate.getTime())) {
    throw new TypeError('A valid month date is required.');
  }
  if (!Array.isArray(requests)) throw new TypeError('Requests must be an array.');

  const year = monthDate.getFullYear();
  const monthIndex = monthDate.getMonth();
  const daysInMonth = new Date(year, monthIndex + 1, 0).getDate();
  const mondayOffset = (new Date(year, monthIndex, 1).getDay() + 6) % 7;
  const todayKey = today instanceof Date && !Number.isNaN(today.getTime())
    ? dateKey(today.getFullYear(), today.getMonth(), today.getDate()) : '';

  const validRequests = requests.filter(request => request
    && validIsoDate(request.startDate)
    && validIsoDate(request.endDate)
    && request.startDate <= request.endDate);

  const cells = Array.from({ length: 42 }, (_, index) => {
    const day = index - mondayOffset + 1;
    const inMonth = day >= 1 && day <= daysInMonth;
    const key = inMonth ? dateKey(year, monthIndex, day) : '';
    const dayRequests = inMonth ? validRequests.filter(request => request.startDate <= key && key <= request.endDate) : [];
    return {
      date: key,
      day: inMonth ? day : null,
      inMonth,
      isToday: Boolean(key && key === todayKey),
      requests: dayRequests
    };
  });

  return {
    title: MONTH_FORMAT.format(new Date(year, monthIndex, 1)),
    weekdays: WEEKDAYS.slice(),
    weeks: Array.from({ length: 6 }, (_, index) => cells.slice(index * 7, index * 7 + 7))
  };
}
===== web/employee-record-summary.js
/** Joins stored row counts and workflow counts by existing employee ID; derives no attendance status or pay. */
export function employeeRecordSummary(employees, attendanceSummaries = [], leaveRequests = [], tickets = []) {
  if (!Array.isArray(employees)) return [];
  const attendanceByEmployee = new Map((Array.isArray(attendanceSummaries) ? attendanceSummaries : [])
    .filter(item => item && typeof item.employeeId === 'string')
    .map(item => [item.employeeId, item]));
  const countByEmployee = records => {
    const counts = new Map();
    (Array.isArray(records) ? records : []).forEach(item => {
      if (item && typeof item.employeeId === 'string') counts.set(item.employeeId, (counts.get(item.employeeId) || 0) + 1);
    });
    return counts;
  };
  const leaveCounts = countByEmployee(leaveRequests);
  const ticketCounts = countByEmployee(tickets);
  return employees.filter(employee => employee && typeof employee.id === 'string').map(employee => {
    const attendance = attendanceByEmployee.get(employee.id);
    return {
      employeeId: employee.id,
      employeeName: String(employee.name || employee.id),
      department: String(employee.department || ''),
      hasScheduleMapping: Boolean(attendance && attendance.hasScheduleMapping),
      rawRecordCount: attendance && Number.isInteger(attendance.rawRecordCount) ? attendance.rawRecordCount : 0,
      firstRecordDate: attendance && typeof attendance.firstRecordDate === 'string' ? attendance.firstRecordDate : '',
      lastRecordDate: attendance && typeof attendance.lastRecordDate === 'string' ? attendance.lastRecordDate : '',
      leaveRequestCount: leaveCounts.get(employee.id) || 0,
      ticketCount: ticketCounts.get(employee.id) || 0
    };
  });
}

  employees.forEach(employee => {
    if (!employee || typeof employee !== 'object') return;
    [['Status label', employee.status], ['Department label', employee.department]].forEach(([category, label]) => {
      if (typeof label !== 'string' || !label.trim()) return;
      const key = `${category}\u0000${label}`;
      counts.set(key, (counts.get(key) || 0) + 1);
    });
  });
  return [...counts.entries()]
    .map(([key, count]) => {
      const [category, label] = key.split('\u0000');
      return { category, label, employeeRecords: count };
    })
    .sort((a, b) => a.category.localeCompare(b.category) || a.label.localeCompare(b.label));
}

===== web/workspace-export.js
/** Builds a user-sandbox-only JSON portability bundle without derived hours or payroll fields. */
export function buildWorkspaceExport({ mode = 'local-synthetic-demo', employees = [], leaveRequests = [], tickets = [], attendanceByEmployee = {} } = {}, exportedAt = new Date()) {
  if (!Array.isArray(employees) || !Array.isArray(leaveRequests) || !Array.isArray(tickets)) {
    throw new TypeError('Workspace export collections must be arrays.');
  }
  if (!attendanceByEmployee || typeof attendanceByEmployee !== 'object' || Array.isArray(attendanceByEmployee)) {
    throw new TypeError('Attendance export data must be grouped by employee ID.');
  }
  if (!(exportedAt instanceof Date) || Number.isNaN(exportedAt.getTime())) {
    throw new TypeError('A valid export timestamp is required.');
  }
  const records = [];
  for (const [employeeId, items] of Object.entries(attendanceByEmployee)) {
    if (!Array.isArray(items)) throw new TypeError(`Attendance rows for ${employeeId} must be an array.`);
    items.forEach(item => {
      if (!item || typeof item !== 'object' || Array.isArray(item)) {
        throw new TypeError(`Attendance row for ${employeeId} must be an object.`);
      }
      records.push({ ...item, employeeId });
    });
  }
  return {
    formatVersion: 1,
    exportedAt: exportedAt.toISOString(),
    storageMode: String(mode),
    syntheticOnly: true,
    hoursCalculated: false,
    payrollIncluded: false,
    employees: employees.slice(),
    attendance: records,
    leaveRequests: leaveRequests.slice(),
    tickets: tickets.slice()
  };
}
===== web/employee-record-summary-view.js
const SORT_KEYS = new Set(['employeeName', 'rawRecordCount', 'firstRecordDate', 'lastRecordDate', 'leaveRequestCount', 'ticketCount']);

/** Filters and sorts stored employee-linked counts without assigning business meaning. */
export function filterAndSortEmployeeRecordSummary(rows, { query = '', mapping = 'all', sortBy = 'employeeName', direction = 'asc' } = {}) {
  if (!Array.isArray(rows)) return [];
  const needle = String(query || '').trim().toLowerCase();
  const selectedMapping = ['all', 'mapped', 'unmapped'].includes(mapping) ? mapping : 'all';
  const field = SORT_KEYS.has(sortBy) ? sortBy : 'employeeName';
  const sign = direction === 'desc' ? -1 : 1;
  return rows.filter(row => {
    if (!row || typeof row !== 'object') return false;
    if (selectedMapping === 'mapped' && row.hasScheduleMapping !== true) return false;
    if (selectedMapping === 'unmapped' && row.hasScheduleMapping !== false) return false;
    if (!needle) return true;
    return [row.employeeId, row.employeeName, row.department]
      .some(value => value !== null && value !== undefined && String(value).toLowerCase().includes(needle));
  }).slice().sort((a, b) => {
    const left = a[field];
    const right = b[field];
    let result;
    if (typeof left === 'number' && typeof right === 'number') result = left - right;
    else result = String(left || '').localeCompare(String(right || ''), undefined, { sensitivity: 'base', numeric: true });
    return result === 0 ? String(a.employeeId).localeCompare(String(b.employeeId), undefined, { numeric: true }) : sign * result;
  });
}
===== web/workflow-filter.js
export function filterWorkflowItems(items, { query = '', status = '', type = '', typeField = '', searchFields = [], dateRange = null } = {}) {
  if (!Array.isArray(items)) return [];
  const needle = String(query || '').trim().toLowerCase();
  const selectedStatus = String(status || '').trim();
  const selectedType = String(type || '').trim();
  const categoryField = String(typeField || '').trim();
  const fields = Array.isArray(searchFields) ? searchFields : [];
  const from = dateRange ? String(dateRange.from || '') : '';
  const to = dateRange ? String(dateRange.to || '') : '';
  const startField = dateRange && dateRange.startField || 'startDate';
  const endField = dateRange && dateRange.endField || 'endDate';
  if (from && to && from > to) return [];
  return items.filter(item => {
    if (!item || typeof item !== 'object') return false;
    if (selectedStatus && item.status !== selectedStatus) return false;
    if (selectedType && (!categoryField || item[categoryField] !== selectedType)) return false;
    if (from && (typeof item[endField] !== 'string' || item[endField] < from)) return false;
    if (to && (typeof item[startField] !== 'string' || item[startField] > to)) return false;
    if (!needle) return true;
    return fields.some(field => {
      const value = item[field];
      return value !== null && value !== undefined && String(value).toLowerCase().includes(needle);
    });
  });
}

  if (!Array.isArray(items)) return [];

      { numeric: true, sensitivity: 'base' });

export function filterAttendanceCoverage(items, { query = '', mapping = 'all' } = {}) {
  if (!Array.isArray(items)) return [];
  const normalizedQuery = String(query).trim().toLocaleLowerCase();
  return items.filter(item => {
    if (!item || typeof item !== 'object') return false;
    if (typeof item.employeeId !== 'string' && typeof item.employeeName !== 'string') return false;
    const hasMapping = item.hasScheduleMapping === true;
    if (mapping === 'mapped' && !hasMapping) return false;
    if (mapping === 'unmapped' && hasMapping) return false;
    if (!['all', 'mapped', 'unmapped'].includes(mapping)) return false;
    if (!normalizedQuery) return true;
    const searchable = [item.employeeId, item.employeeName,
      hasMapping ? `schedule ${item.scheduleId}` : 'no mapping']
      .filter(value => value !== undefined && value !== null)
      .join(' ')
      .toLocaleLowerCase();
    return searchable.includes(normalizedQuery);
  });

===== web/attendance-coverage-sort.js
const FIELDS = new Set(['employeeId', 'employeeName', 'scheduleId', 'rawRecordCount', 'firstRecordDate', 'lastRecordDate']);
const NUMERIC_FIELDS = new Set(['scheduleId', 'rawRecordCount']);

export function sortAttendanceCoverage(items, { field = 'employeeId', direction = 'asc' } = {}) {
  if (!Array.isArray(items)) return [];
  const key = FIELDS.has(field) ? field : 'employeeId';
  const multiplier = direction === 'desc' ? -1 : 1;
  return [...items].sort((left, right) => {
    const leftValue = left?.[key];
    const rightValue = right?.[key];
    let primary;
    if (NUMERIC_FIELDS.has(key)) {
      const a = Number.isFinite(Number(leftValue)) ? Number(leftValue) : Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY;
      const b = Number.isFinite(Number(rightValue)) ? Number(rightValue) : Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY;
      primary = a === b ? 0 : a < b ? -1 : 1;
    } else {
      primary = String(leftValue ?? '').localeCompare(String(rightValue ?? ''), undefined,
        { numeric: true, sensitivity: 'base' });
    }
    if (primary) return primary * multiplier;
    return String(left?.employeeId ?? '').localeCompare(String(right?.employeeId ?? ''), undefined,
      { numeric: true, sensitivity: 'base' });
  });
}

package ph.motorph.web;

import java.time.Instant;

/** Validates and coordinates safe, non-payroll workflow demonstrations. */
public final class WorkflowService {
    private static final int MAX_TEXT_LENGTH = 240;
    private static final List<String> LEAVE_TYPES = Collections.unmodifiableList(
        Arrays.asList("Vacation", "Medical", "Personal", "Unpaid"));
    private static final Map<String, String> TICKET_QUEUES;
    static {
        Map<String, String> queues = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        queues.put("Overtime request", "Team Lead");
        queues.put("Leave request", "Team Lead");
        queues.put("Timesheet correction", "Team Lead");
        queues.put("Payroll inquiry", "Payroll Staff");
        queues.put("HR inquiry", "HR");
        queues.put("Technical support", "IT Admin");
        TICKET_QUEUES = Collections.unmodifiableMap(queues);
    }

    private final EmployeeService employeeService;
    private final WorkflowStore store;

    public WorkflowService(EmployeeService employeeService, WorkflowStore store) {
        if (employeeService == null || store == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("workflow dependencies must not be null");
        this.employeeService = employeeService;
        this.store = store;
    }

    public List<DemoLeaveRequest> listLeaveRequests() { return store.listLeaveRequests(); }
    public List<DemoTicket> listTickets() { return store.listTickets(); }

    public DemoLeaveRequest createLeaveRequest(String employeeId, String leaveType,
            String startDate, String endDate, String note) {
        Employee employee = requireEmployee(employeeId);
        if (!LEAVE_TYPES.contains(leaveType)) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Choose a valid leave type.");
        LocalDate start = parseDate(startDate, "start date");
        LocalDate end = parseDate(endDate, "end date");
        if (start.isAfter(end)) throw new IllegalArgumentException("The start date must be on or before the end date.");
        String safeNote = optionalText(note, "Note");
        String id = "LV-" + randomSuffix();
        return store.createLeaveRequest(new DemoLeaveRequest(id, employee.getId(), employee.getName(), leaveType,
            start.toString(), end.toString(), safeNote, "Pending review", Instant.now().toString(), ""));
    }

    public DemoLeaveRequest cancelLeaveRequest(String id) {
        requireId(id, "LV-");
        return store.cancelLeaveRequest(id, Instant.now().toString());
    }

    public DemoTicket createTicket(String employeeId, String ticketType, String summary) {
        Employee employee = requireEmployee(employeeId);
        String queue = TICKET_QUEUES.get(ticketType);
        if (queue == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Choose a valid ticket type.");
        String safeSummary = requiredText(summary, "Message");
        String id = "TK-" + randomSuffix();
        return store.createTicket(new DemoTicket(id, employee.getId(), employee.getName(), ticketType, queue,
            safeSummary, "Open", Instant.now().toString(), ""));
    }

    public DemoTicket cancelTicket(String id) {
        requireId(id, "TK-");
        return store.cancelTicket(id, Instant.now().toString());
    }

    private Employee requireEmployee(String employeeId) {
        String id = requiredText(employeeId, "Employee ID");
        return employeeService.findEmployee(id).orElseThrow(() ->
            new NoSuchElementException("Choose an employee from your synthetic demo directory."));
    }

    private static LocalDate parseDate(String value, String field) {
        String text = requiredText(value, field);
        try {
            LocalDate date = LocalDate.parse(text);
            if (!date.toString().equals(text)) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Enter a valid YYYY-MM-DD " + field + ".");
            return date;
        } catch (DateTimeParseException ex) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Enter a valid YYYY-MM-DD " + field + ".");
        }
    }

    private static String requiredText(String value, String field) {
        String text = value == null ? "" : value.trim();
        if (text.isEmpty()) throw new IllegalArgumentException(field + " is required.");
        if (text.length() > MAX_TEXT_LENGTH) throw new IllegalArgumentException(field + " must be " + MAX_TEXT_LENGTH + " characters or fewer.");
        return text;
    }

    private static String optionalText(String value, String field) {
        String text = value == null ? "" : value.trim();
        if (text.length() > MAX_TEXT_LENGTH) throw new IllegalArgumentException(field + " must be " + MAX_TEXT_LENGTH + " characters or fewer.");
        return text;
    }

    private static String randomSuffix() {
        return UUID.randomUUID().toString().replace("-", "").substring(0, 12).toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
    }

    private static void requireId(String id, String prefix) {
        if (id == null || !id.matches(prefix + "[A-F0-9]{12}")) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Workflow record ID is invalid.");
    }
