"USER SANDBOX" : "TEST FIXTURE" storage label <- user ? "User-scoped Firestore" : "Isolated test fixture" avatar letter <- first letter of email, or "D" loadEmployees() ; loadWorkflows() // not awaited ``` **`showSignIn(message = '')`** — nulls `state.user`, calls `resetSessionData()`, hides the shell, shows the gate, sets the message. **`friendlyAuthError`, `signIn`, `createDevAccount`, `sendPasswordReset`** are only bound when Firebase is configured (see the bootstrap at the bottom). ### 7.3 Small UI/DOM helpers **`initials(name) -> String`** — first two whitespace-separated words, first character each, uppercased. `""` for a blank name (no crash). **`makeCell(content) -> HTMLTableCellElement`** — if `content instanceof Node` it is appended, else set as `textContent`. Everything user-supplied goes through the `textContent` branch, which is why there is no HTML-injection surface in table rendering. **`downloadCsvFile(filename, columns, records)`** ``` 1. csv <- buildCsv(columns, records) // throws on malformed columns/rows 2. blob <- Blob(["\uFEFF" + csv], text/csv;charset=utf-8) // BOM so Excel reads UTF-8 3. object URL, hidden <a download>, click, remove, revoke after 1 s ``` **`downloadJsonFile(filename, data)`** — same pattern with `JSON.stringify(data, null, 2)` and `application/json`. **`showTableMessage(message)`** — replaces the employee table body with one `colSpan=6` `.table-message` row. **`showWorkflowTableMessage(tbody, columnCount, message)`** — same for an arbitrary table and column count. **`showAttendanceMessage(message)`** — same for the attendance table (6 columns). **`makeWorkflowStatus(status) -> HTMLElement`** ``` badge.className <- "status-pill" + " workflow-cancelled" when status == "Cancelled" + " leave" when status is neither Cancelled nor Active badge.textContent <- status ``` Purely decorative mapping of the stored label. It is also reused for `Active`/`On leave` in the Team and HR tables. **`setWorkflowStatus(id, message, error = false)`** — writes text to a status element and toggles `workflow-error` / `workflow-success` classes. **`setWorkflowStorageMode(value)`** — writes a label into `#workflow-storage-mode` ("User-scoped Firestore" / "Isolated test fixture memory" / "Rules access required" / "Local API unavailable"). **`renderSandboxSearchResults(results, employees) -> number`** ``` 1. clear container 2. nameById <- map of employeeId -> name 3. groups: Employees, Raw attendance, Leave requests, Tickets, each with a formatter 4. total <- sum of group lengths 5. total == 0 -> single sentence: no matches, and a blank result implies no attendance status or eligibility 6. otherwise one <section><h3>Title (n)</h3><ul><li>…</li></ul></section> per non-empty group 7. return total ``` All values formatted with `textContent`. The attendance formatter prints `timeIn–timeOut` and `dayType` verbatim — no duration. ### 7.4 Employee directory **`renderEmployees()`** **[LIVE]** ``` 1. clear tbody 2. visible <- sortDirectoryEntries(state.employees, {field: #employee-sort, direction: #employee-order}) 3. empty -> message: "No employee records match that search." when a query is present, else "No demo records are available." 4. per row: initials avatar + name + id | department | role | location | status pill | open button - the row itself is clickable -> openEmployee(employee) - the open button stops propagation and then opens (so keyboard users have a real button) - status pill gets class `leave` unless the stored status lowercases to "active" 5. count <- state.totalEmployees zero-padded to 2; overview count mirrors it 6. result count <- "<n> record(s) shown" 7. export button disabled when nothing is shown ``` `state.totalEmployees` comes from the server's `total` (full directory), while the rows are the filtered `items` — that is why the header can read "03" with one row shown. **`openEmployee(employee)`** **[LIVE]** ``` 1. state.selected <- employee 2. dialog title <- employee.name 3. render six always-present fields: employee id, status, department, role, location, "DATA SOURCE: Synthetic demo record" 4. append a "Linked sandbox records" section with a status line ("Loading linked records…") 5. dialog.showModal() 6. loadEmployeeSandboxRecords(employee.id, recordsSection) // not awaited ``` No salary, government ID, bank, schedule, or leave-balance field exists to show. **`loadEmployeeSandboxRecords(employeeId, container)`** **[LIVE][READ-ONLY]** ``` try: 1. headers <- await apiHeaders() 2. parallel GET /api/attendance?employeeId=... and GET /api/workflows 3. parse both; throw on either non-OK 4. STALE GUARD: if state.selected?.id !== employeeId or container detached -> return silently 5. attendance <- items (or []) leave <- workflowPayload.leaveRequests filtered by employeeId (client-side) tickets <- workflowPayload.tickets filtered by employeeId 6. remove the status line; append three groups (heading with count, list, or "No stored rows …") catch: if still current -> write the error into the status line ``` Note it fetches the **entire** workflow collection to filter one employee, and it ignores the date range chosen elsewhere. **`editSyntheticEmployee(employee)`** **[LIVE]** ``` 1. copy the six fields into the editor inputs 2. title "Edit <id>", save button "Save synthetic record", show cancel button 3. scroll the form into view, focus the name input ``` No optimistic-concurrency token: two admins editing the same record silently last-write-wins. **`populateAttendanceEmployees()`** — rebuilds the attendance employee `<select>` from `state.allEmployees` as `"<id> — <name>"`, preserving the current selection when it still exists. No placeholder, so a selection is always possible once employees load. **`populateWorkflowEmployees()`** — rebuilds `#leave-employee` and `#ticket-employee` with a leading placeholder (`"Choose synthetic employee"` / `"Load directory first"`) plus the same options, preserving selection. **`populateWorkflowEmployees` and `populateAttendanceEmployees` are the only bridge between identity and an employee record — and it is a free-choice dropdown.** Nothing binds the signed-in Firebase account to an employee. Selecting "Eli Santos" asserts nothing. This is stated in the UI notice and is **[GAP] ID-1**. **`renderDirectoryViews()`** **[LIVE][READ-ONLY]** — renders Team and HR views from the same `state.allEmployees`. ``` 1. disable summary export when no employees 2. filteredTeam <- sortDirectoryEntries(filterWorkflowItems(allEmployees, {query:#team-directory-search, status:#team-directory-status, searchFields:[id,name,department,role,location,status]}), {field:#team-directory-sort, direction:#team-directory-order}) filteredEmployees <- same with the HR filter controls 3. directory-report-total / -active / -onleave <- counts by exact stored status strings 4. department counts -> sorted <li> list ("<Department>: <count>"), or "No directory labels loaded." 5. no employees -> both tables get the empty message 6. Team rows: person button (opens dialog) | department | role | location | status pill 7. HR rows: name+id | department | role | location | status pill | [View] [Edit] 8. counts "<shown> of <total> record(s)"; export buttons disabled when their filtered view is empty 9. renderEmployeeRecordSummary() ``` Both views iterate the *entire* directory — there is no supervisor scoping, no team membership, and no permission boundary. "Team" is a filtered copy of "HR". **`renderRawAttendanceSummary(records)`** — zero-padded total count, earliest and latest valid `YYYY-MM-DD` date (or `—`), and mirrors the count into the overview card. No hours, no days, no rate. **`applyDefaultAttendanceRange(records)`** — if records exist and **both** date inputs are empty, set `from`=earliest and `to`=latest. Comment cites the legacy MO-IT108 "default to full available span" requirement; it is not a pay period. **`clearAttendanceCalendarSelection()`** — clears the two calendar selection variables, restores the instruction text, re-renders the calendar. Bound to typing in either date field so a manual edit invalidates the calendar-selected range. **`selectAttendanceCalendarDate(date)`** **[LIVE]** ``` 1. no start yet, or a complete range exists: start <- date; end <- ""; status "Start date … choose an end date; no status or hours are inferred" re-render; return 2. otherwise: order the two dates, set both inputs, status "Applied inclusive raw-record range … no days or hours were calculated." 3. loadAttendance() // refetch with the new range ``` Clicking a second earlier date normalises rather than erroring. **`renderAttendanceCalendar(records)`** **[LIVE][READ-ONLY]** ``` 1. employeeId <- current select value 2. if the employee changed: reset month to the earliest record's month, else today 3. calendar <- buildAttendanceCalendar(month, records) 4. for each cell: aria-label "<date>, n raw records"; a date button (selected when it equals either bound); when rows exist, a <ul> of `<timeIn>–<timeOut>` events whose title/aria-label include the raw attendanceId and dayType ``` A day with no row renders an empty cell and **no** absence meaning. **`renderAttendance(records)`** **[LIVE]** ``` 1. state.rawAttendance <- sortAttendanceRecords(records, {#attendance-sort, #attendance-order}) 2. export enabled when non-empty; applyDefaultAttendanceRange; renderRawAttendanceSummary 3. table rows: date | attendanceId | scheduleId | timeIn | timeOut | dayType (all as text) 4. empty -> "No attendance entries match this employee and date range." 5. "<n> raw entries loaded"; renderAttendanceCalendar(ordered) ``` Sorting re-sorts the already-loaded rows without refetching. **`loadAttendance()`** **[LIVE]** ``` 1. employeeId <- select value; blank -> clear table/summary/calendar, message "Load the employee directory first." 2. token <- ++state.attendanceRequestNumber; blank the current rows and enable nothing 3. message "Loading raw attendance records…" 4. params: employeeId, plus from/to only when set 5. fetch /api/attendance; throw on non-OK 6. discard result if the token moved 7. renderAttendance(items or []) catch (token still current): clear state, message the error, count "Could not load records" ``` Nothing is cached: switching employee or range always refetches. **`renderAttendanceReport(items)`** — stores `state.attendanceReport` (the unfiltered server payload), then `applyAttendanceReportFilters()` and `renderEmployeeRecordSummary()`. **`applyAttendanceReportFilters()`** **[READ-ONLY]** ``` 1. visible <- sortAttendanceCoverage(filterAttendanceCoverage(state.attendanceReport, {query:#attendance-report-search, mapping:#attendance-report-mapping}), {field:#attendance-report-sort, direction:#attendance-report-order}) 2. per row: name·id | "Schedule <id>" or "No mapping" | raw count | first date | last date | "View rows" (only when mapped) 3. count label "<shown> of <total> employee rows visible · <sum> raw records in range" 4. export disabled when nothing visible ``` "View rows" carries only the employee ID; the click handler (registered once at load) copies the report's `from`/`to` into the attendance filters, switches view, and lets `switchView` refetch. **`loadAttendanceReport()`** **[LIVE]** ``` 1. token <- ++state.reportRequestNumber; hide status; count "Loading report"; disable export 2. params from/to when set 3. fetch /api/reports/attendance 4. VALIDATE SHAPE: items must be an array AND payload.hoursCalculated must be exactly false -> otherwise "Unexpected attendance report response." 5. discard if token moved 6. renderAttendanceReport(items); status "Loaded raw record counts and date coverage only; no hours or payroll values were calculated." catch (token current): clear, message, count "Could not load report", show error status ``` The `hoursCalculated !== false` check is a contract assertion, not a calculation. **`loadEmployees()`** **[LIVE]** ``` 1. token <- ++state.requestNumber; query <- trimmed search value 2. "Loading employee records…" / count "Loading" 3. url = /api/employees[?q=…] 4. fetch, parse, validate `items` is an array 5. discard if token moved 6. state.employees <- items; state.totalEmployees <- payload.total (integer) else items.length 7. if there is no query: allEmployees <- items; repopulate both pickers; renderDirectoryViews() 8. seed button visible only when signed in and not searching 9. renderEmployees() catch (token current): clear employees and pickers, hide seed, re-render, show the message, count "Could not load records" ``` A search therefore narrows the employee table but leaves `allEmployees`, the pickers, and the Team/HR/directory summaries at the last full load — intentional, but worth knowing when reading the counts. **`seedSyntheticDemoData()`** **[LIVE]** ``` 1. disable the button, label "Adding missing fixtures…" 2. POST /api/demo/seed 3. throw on non-OK 4. result count "<e> employees, <m> schedule links, and <a> attendance rows added" 5. await loadEmployees() finally: re-enable, restore label catch: table message + "Demo setup failed" ``` Safe to repeat; already-existing documents are reported as not created. ### 7.5 Workflow (leave and tickets) **`renderWorkflow()`** **[LIVE]** — the largest renderer. ``` 1. bail out if the leave table is absent 2. leaves <- sortWorkflowItems(filterWorkflowItems(state.workflow.leaveRequests, { query, status, type=leaveType, typeField:'leaveType', searchFields:[id,employeeId,employeeName,leaveType,startDate,endDate], dateRange:{from,to,startField:'startDate',endField:'endDate'}}), {leave-sort, leave-sort-order}) - remember the filtered list in state.visibleLeaveRequests 3. table: id | name·id | leaveType | startDate — endDate | status pill | [Details] + [Cancel] (Cancel only when Pending review) 4. empty states distinguish "no session requests yet" from "no requests match these filters" 5. "<shown> of <total> request(s) in this sandbox" 6. same for tickets: id | name·id | ticketType | queue | status | [Details] + [Cancel] (only when Open) 7. enable/disable the four export buttons by full vs filtered emptiness 8. overview workflow count <- leaves + tickets, zero-padded 9. renderWorkflowSummary(); renderEmployeeRecordSummary(); renderLeaveCalendar() ``` The date filter is an **overlap** test computed in `filterWorkflowItems`: `endDate >= from` and `startDate <= to`. **`renderWorkflowSummary()`** — groups stored labels into rows (`Leave request status/type`, `Ticket status/type/queue`) with counts, writes `"<rows> stored-label rows · <n> workflow records"`, disables export when empty. No approval, SLA, or resolution meaning. **`renderEmployeeRecordSummary()`** **[READ-ONLY]** ``` 1. summary <- employeeRecordSummary(state.allEmployees, state.attendanceReport, leaves, tickets) 2. visible <- filterAndSortEmployeeRecordSummary(summary, {search, mapping, sort, order}) 3. rows: name·id | Mapped / No mapping | raw record count | first date | last date | leave count | ticket count 4. "<shown> of <total> employee rows · stored counts only" 5. enable all/visible exports ``` Depends on `state.attendanceReport`, which is only populated after the Reports view has been opened — before that, every employee shows 0 raw rows even if rows exist. That is a real display defect (**[GAP] UX-1**), not a calculation issue. **`applyWorkflowItem(collection, item, storage)`** ``` 1. find the existing item by id in state.workflow[collection] 2. absent -> prepend; present -> replace in place 3. refresh the storage label from the server's label 4. renderWorkflow() ``` No refetch — the server response is the source of truth for the single item. **`sendWorkflowRequest(url, body) -> Promise<Payload>`** ``` 1. headers <- apiHeaders(body === undefined ? {} : {Content-Type: application/json}) 2. POST (no body when undefined) 3. parse JSON; throw on non-OK with the server message 4. require payload.item, else "Unexpected workflow response." return payload ``` **`handleWorkflowCancel(event)`** **[LIVE]** ``` 1. button <- event.target.closest('button[data-action]'); none -> return 2. isLeave <- action == 'cancel-leave'; pick the matching status element and collection 3. disable the button 4. POST /api/workflows/(leave|tickets)/<id>/cancel (no body) 5. applyWorkflowItem(...); status "<id> cancelled in this user sandbox. No reviewer was notified." catch: error text; re-enable the button ``` There is no confirmation dialog. Cancel is terminal in this model — there is no reopen or appeal state. ### 7.6 Calendars **`selectLeaveCalendarDate(date)`** **[LIVE]** ``` 1. if no start or a complete range exists: start <- date; end <- ""; write start into #leave-start, clear #leave-end status "Draft start date <date> selected; choose an end date. Nothing has been submitted." 2. else if date < start: restart the draft at the earlier date 3. else: end <- date; write into #leave-end status "Draft range <start> through <date> selected… no days or balances are calculated." 4. renderLeaveCalendar() ``` It **only drafts form values**. No submission, no day count, no balance check. **`renderLeaveCalendar()`** **[READ-ONLY]** ``` 1. calendar <- buildLeaveCalendar(leaveCalendarMonth, state.workflow.leaveRequests) // today defaults to now 2. title; rebuild the 6×7 grid 3. out-of-month cells: aria-hidden, empty 4. in-month: date button (class `selected` when it equals either draft bound, `today` when today) 5. per-day request markers: "<leaveType> · <status>", cancelled styled, title "<name> · <id> · request date only" ``` The calendar is a *display* of submitted ranges, not an approved-leave calendar. ### 7.7 Search, exports, and view switching **`fetchSandboxSnapshot() -> Promise<Object>`** **[LIVE][READ-ONLY]** ``` 1. headers <- apiHeaders() 2. parallel GET /api/health, /api/employees, /api/workflows 3. parse all three; throw the first non-OK with its message 4. require employees.items to be an array 5. parallel GET /api/attendance?employeeId=… for EVERY employee 6. return {mode, employees, leaveRequests, tickets, attendanceByEmployee} ``` This is the only fan-out read: N+1 requests, no concurrency cap. Acceptable for three fixtures, not for a real roster. **`renderSandboxSearchResults`** — described in §7.3. **`switchView(view)`** **[LIVE]** ``` 1. labels map (overview, employees, attendance, requests, team, hr, reports, payroll); unknown -> return 2. hide every .page-view except <view>-view 3. nav items: toggle .active and aria-current="page" 4. breadcrumb text; document.title "<label> — MotorPH Payroll Office" 5. view == attendance and an employee is selected -> loadAttendance() 6. view == reports -> loadAttendanceReport() ``` Entering Attendance or Reports refetches every time; there is no cache. ### 7.8 Event wiring (73 registrations) Grouped by what they do — each is a one-line handler, so they are listed rather than pseudocoded individually: | Handler(s) | Behaviour | |---|---| | `#employee-form` submit | POST (new) or PUT (edit) with the five editable fields; disable save; on success reset the editor, clear search, reload, and report whether a schedule mapping was added (it never is) | | `#employee-cancel-edit-button` click | `resetEmployeeEditor()` | | `#leave-request-form` submit | local `submitLeaveRequest()` shape check → POST → set the calendar month to the request's month → clear draft → `applyWorkflowItem` → reset form, restore employee → status "saved… No reviewer was notified." | | `#ticket-form` submit | same pattern with `submitTicket()`; status includes the queue label "…, not delivered." | | leave/ticket row containers click | `handleWorkflowCancel` | | leave/ticket filter inputs, selects, sorts | `renderWorkflow` (client-side only) | | employee record summary search/mapping/sort/order | `renderEmployeeRecordSummary` | | HR and Team search/status/sort/order | `renderDirectoryViews` | | `#leave-start`, `#leave-end` input | clear the draft range and re-render the calendar (manual typing overrides calendar selection) | | leave calendar prev/next | shift `leaveCalendarMonth` by one month, re-render | | `[data-open-requests]` buttons | `switchView('requests')` | | `#seed-demo-button` | `seedSyntheticDemoData` | | `#employee-search` input | 180 ms debounce → `loadEmployees` | | employee sort/order change | `renderEmployees` (no refetch) | | `#refresh-button` | `loadEmployees` | | employee export | `downloadCsvFile('motorph-synthetic-employees.csv', six columns, sorted current rows)` | | team export / HR export | fetch the same filtered+sorted view the table shows, six columns, status column labelled "Stored Demo Status" | | employee-record-summary export (all / visible) | nine columns of stored counts, mapping rendered as "Mapped"/"No mapping" | | directory summary export | `directoryLabelSummaryRows` → three columns of label counts | | workflow summary export | `workflowSummaryRows` → three columns | | attendance export | six raw columns from `state.rawAttendance`; employee ID sanitised for the filename | | attendance report export | re-applies the current filter+sort, six columns, no hours | | leave export (all / visible) | nine columns | | ticket export (all / visible) | eight columns | | `#sandbox-export-button` | `fetchSandboxSnapshot` → `buildWorkspaceExport` → download JSON, then a sentence counting each collection | | `#sandbox-search-form` submit | blank query is refused with a message; otherwise snapshot → `searchSandboxRecords` → render → "n matching stored records… No attendance or payroll values were derived." | | attendance from/to input | `clearAttendanceCalendarSelection` | | attendance filter submit | `loadAttendance` | | attendance sort/order change | `renderAttendance(state.rawAttendance)` (re-sort only) | | attendance calendar prev/next | shift the month, re-render | | attendance report filter submit | `loadAttendanceReport` | | attendance report search/mapping/sort/order | `applyAttendanceReportFilters` | | attendance report rows click (`button[data-employee-id]`) | copy the report range into the attendance filters, switch to the attendance view | | attendance employee change | clear both dates and the calendar selection, `loadAttendance` | | dialog close/done buttons and backdrop click | `dialog.close()` | | document keydown `/` | focus the employee search when not typing in a field and no dialog is open | | nav items | `switchView(dataset.view)` | | `#auth-form` submit / create / reset / sign-out | only bound when Firebase is configured: `signIn`, `createDevAccount`, `sendPasswordReset`, `signOut(auth)` | ### 7.9 Bootstrap ``` if not firebaseConfigured and isolatedTestMode: showWorkspace(null) // test-only unauthenticated workspace else if not firebaseConfigured: hide the auth form, create-account, and reset buttons showSignIn("Firebase configuration is required. Local-memory access is disabled. …") else: bind auth form / create / reset / sign-out setPersistence(auth, inMemoryPersistence) // session not persisted across reloads .then(onAuthStateChanged(user => user ? showWorkspace(user) : showSignIn())) .catch(error => showSignIn(friendlyAuthError(error))) ``` `inMemoryPersistence` is a deliberate choice: closing the tab ends the session. `isolatedTestMode` requires both `VITE_E2E_TEST_MODE=true` **and** no Firebase config; it cannot leak into a configured build. --- ## 8. Browser: support modules (16 files, 537 lines) Each is a pure function; all follow the same defensive contract — non-array input returns `[]`, never throws, and where they do validate, they throw `TypeError` on unusable *arguments* rather than on data. ### 8.1 `attendance-calendar.js` **`dateKey(year, monthIndex, day)`** (private) — zero-padded `YYYY-MM-DD`. **`isIsoDate(value)`** (private) — shape check **plus** round-trip through `Date` so `2026-02-30` is rejected. **`buildAttendanceCalendar(monthDate, records = [])`** **[READ-ONLY]** ``` 1. monthDate must be a valid Date -> TypeError ; records must be an array -> TypeError 2. year, monthIndex, daysInMonth; mondayOffset = (first weekday + 6) % 7 // Monday-first grid 3. bucket records by date, keeping only valid ISO dates inside this month 4. 42 cells: in-month cells carry the date string and a shallow copy of that day's rows; out-of-month cells carry date "", day null, records [] 5. return {title: "Month YYYY", weekdays: Mon…Sun, weeks: 6 × 7} ``` Always six weeks, so the grid height is stable. No cell ever implies absence. ### 8.2 `leave-calendar.js` **`dateKey` / `validIsoDate`** (private) — same as above. **`buildLeaveCalendar(monthDate, requests = [], today = new Date())`** **[READ-ONLY]** ``` 1. validate arguments 2. todayKey from a valid `today`, else "" 3. keep requests with valid start AND end and start <= end 4. 42 cells; for in-month dates, requests where startDate <= date <= endDate 5. mark isToday 6. return the same grid shape plus per-cell `requests` ``` Range overlap is evaluated per day, which is why a multi-day leave shows a marker on every covered day. ### 8.3 `workflow-demo.js` — **this is a shape mirror, not the writer** **Constants** — `LEAVE_TYPES`, `TICKET_QUEUES`, `MAX_NOTE_LENGTH = 240`, exported. **`createWorkflowState()`** — `{leaveRequests: [], tickets: [], nextLeaveNumber: 1, nextTicketNumber: 1}`. **`requireState(state)`** (private) — both arrays present, else `TypeError`. **`findEmployee(employeeId, employees)`** (private) — must exist in the directory, else `"Choose an employee from the synthetic demo directory."` **`isValidDate(value)`** (private) — regex + UTC round-trip. **`cleanOptionalText(value, field)`** (private) — trim, ≤240. **`dateStamp(value)`** (private) — `YYYY-MM-DD` from a Date or date string. **`submitLeaveRequest(state, input, employees, submittedAt = new Date())`** **[VALIDATION]** ``` 1. validate type, employee, both dates, ordering, note length 2. build id "LV-0001" from state.nextLeaveNumber 3. return {state: new state with the request appended and the counter incremented, request} ``` **`cancelLeaveRequest(state, requestId, employeeId)`** — finds it, requires same employee, requires `Pending review`, returns a new state with `status: "Cancelled"`. **`submitTicket(state, input, employees, submittedAt)`** — validates type against `TICKET_QUEUES`, employee, required message ≤240; id `TK-0001`; `queue` from the map; `status: "Open"`. **`cancelTicket(state, ticketId, employeeId)`** — same shape, requires `Open`. **Why this file matters:** `app.js` calls `submitLeaveRequest(createWorkflowState(), …)` and `submitTicket(createWorkflowState(), …)` — each time with a **fresh throwaway state** — purely to reuse the validation messages. The returned state is discarded; the persisted record comes from the server. So: - This module is a **client-side pre-check**, and the only place a "you can cancel only your own item" rule exists on the client. - Its `LV-0001` / `TK-0001` IDs and its `submittedAt` date-only stamp are **not** what gets stored (the server issues `LV-<12 hex>` and an ISO instant). - `cancelLeaveRequest` / `cancelTicket` here are **dead code in the product path** — nothing calls them. They only exist for the module's own tests. - The duplicated validity rules (Java vs this file) can drift. If you change `MAX_NOTE_LENGTH` or the leave types in one place, change both (**[GAP] DUP-1**). ### 8.4 `csv-export.js` **`validateColumns(columns)`** (private) — non-empty array; each entry needs a non-blank string `key` and `label`, else `TypeError`. **`csvCell(value)`** (private) — `String(value ?? '')`; prefixes `'` when the text starts with optional whitespace then one of `= + - @` (formula-injection guard); wraps in double quotes and doubles internal quotes. **`buildCsv(columns, rows)`** — validates, requires each row to be a non-array object, emits quoted header then quoted body joined by `\r\n`. All cells are quoted, so commas, quotes, and newlines are safe. ### 8.5 `attendance-coverage-filter.js` **`filterAttendanceCoverage(items, {query = '', mapping = 'all'})`** **[READ-ONLY]** ``` 1. non-array -> [] 2. drop items that are not objects or have neither employeeId nor employeeName 3. mapping 'mapped' requires hasScheduleMapping === true; 'unmapped' requires it false; any mapping value outside all/mapped/unmapped -> the whole result is empty (fail closed) 4. empty query -> keep; else search the joined text of id, name, and "schedule <id>"/"no mapping" ``` Note step 3: an unrecognised `mapping` value returns **nothing** rather than everything — a deliberate fail-closed choice. ### 8.6 `attendance-coverage-sort.js` **`sortAttendanceCoverage(items, {field = 'employeeId', direction = 'asc'})`** — allowlist of six fields (unknown → `employeeId`); numeric comparison for `scheduleId`/`rawRecordCount` with non-numeric treated as `-Infinity`; otherwise `localeCompare` with numeric collation; ties broken by `employeeId`. ### 8.7 `attendance-record-sort.js` **`sortAttendanceRecords(items, {field = 'date', direction = 'asc'})`** — allowlist of six fields; numeric for `attendanceId`/`scheduleId`; `localeCompare` numeric for date/time strings (so `08:05` < `8:05`-style inconsistencies do not reorder badly); final tie-break by `attendanceId` ascending. ### 8.8 `directory-sort.js` **`sortDirectoryEntries(items, {field = 'name', direction = 'asc'})`** — allowlist of the six employee fields; everything compared as strings with numeric collation; ties by `id`. ### 8.9 `directory-summary.js` **`directoryLabelSummaryRows(employees)`** **[READ-ONLY]** — counts employees per stored `status` label ("Status label") and per `department` ("Department label"), skipping blank or non-string labels, emitting `{category, label, employeeRecords}` sorted by category then label. Keyed on `category\u0000label` so identical strings in different categories never merge. ### 8.10 `workflow-summary.js` **`workflowSummaryRows(leaveRequests, tickets)`** **[READ-ONLY]** — five label groups (leave status, leave type, ticket status, ticket type, ticket queue); counts trimmed non-empty string labels; returns `{category, label, recordCount}` sorted. Counts are of stored labels, nothing else. ### 8.11 `workflow-filter.js` **`filterWorkflowItems(items, {query, status, type, typeField, searchFields, dateRange})`** **[READ-ONLY]** ``` 1. non-array -> [] 2. an inverted date range (from > to) -> [] 3. per item: exact match on status when given; exact match on typeField when given and typeField non-blank; overlap test — item.endField >= from and item.startField <= to; query substring over the enumerated searchFields only ``` Used for leave, tickets, **and** the Team/HR directories (with `status` bound to the directory-status control and the six directory fields as `searchFields`), which is why an "employee filter" function lives in a workflow module. ### 8.12 `workflow-sort.js` **`sortWorkflowItems(items, {field = 'submittedAt', direction = 'desc'})`** — nine-field allowlist; string comparison with numeric collation; ties by `id`. Works for both collections because it only reads shared field names. ### 8.13 `employee-record-summary.js` **`employeeRecordSummary(employees, attendanceSummaries, leaveRequests, tickets)`** **[READ-ONLY]** ``` 1. non-array employees -> [] 2. index attendance summaries by employeeId 3. count leave and ticket rows per employeeId 4. per employee (must have a string id): employeeId, employeeName (name or id), department, hasScheduleMapping (=== true only), rawRecordCount (integer else 0), firstRecordDate, lastRecordDate (string else ""), leaveRequestCount, ticketCount ``` Left join only: an employee with no attendance summary gets zeros, and an attendance summary with no employee is dropped. ### 8.14 `employee-record-summary-view.js` **`filterAndSortEmployeeRecordSummary(rows, {query, mapping, sortBy, direction})`** **[READ-ONLY]** — mapping filter, substring search over id/name/department, sort over six allowed keys with numeric comparison for numeric fields, ties by `employeeId`. Note the tie-break is applied **before** the direction multiplier, so ties stay ascending even when the primary sort is descending. ### 8.15 `sandbox-search.js` **`hasQuery(record, fields, query)`** (private) — substring over explicit fields only. **`searchSandboxRecords(query, {employees, attendanceByEmployee, leaveRequests, tickets})`** **[READ-ONLY]** ``` 1. blank query -> four empty arrays (never "everything") 2. attendance: flatten the per-employee groups, stamp employeeId, match over employeeId, attendanceId, scheduleId, date, timeIn, timeOut, dayType 3. employees: id, name, department, role, location, status 4. leaveRequests: id, employeeId, employeeName, leaveType, startDate, endDate, status, note 5. tickets: id, employeeId, employeeName, ticketType, queue, summary, status ``` Every field is enumerated, so a future field (a salary, a bank account) cannot be searched unless someone adds it here. ### 8.16 `workspace-export.js` **`buildWorkspaceExport({mode, employees, leaveRequests, tickets, attendanceByEmployee}, exportedAt = new Date())`** **[READ-ONLY]** ``` 1. validate: three arrays, an object map, a valid Date 2. flatten attendanceByEmployee into rows stamped with employeeId, validating each row is an object 3. return { formatVersion: 1, exportedAt: ISO, storageMode: mode, syntheticOnly: true, hoursCalculated: false, payrollIncluded: false, employees, attendance, leaveRequests, tickets // shallow copies } ``` The three boolean/marker fields make the file self-describing: it cannot be mistaken for a payroll extract. **There is no import counterpart** — a restore path would need schema versioning, per-collection validation, duplicate handling, and an owner check. Pseudocode for the missing functions (design only — do not implement yet) These are the seams. Each is written against the *current* model so you can see exactly where it attaches, and each is annotated with the decisions that must land first. **None of this is authorised work**; it exists so you can judge the shape of the remaining build. ### 11.1 Timekeeping ``` computeWorkedMinutes(record, schedule, calendar, policy) -> Result<minutes, exception> // requires D-01 (schedule), D-02 (break), D-03 (tz), D-04 (overnight), D-10 (rounding) 1. if schedule is missing -> return Unmapped(record) // never Absent 2. start <- combine(record.date, record.timeIn) end <- combine(record.date, record.timeOut); if end <= start and policy.allowsOvernight -> end += 1 day 3. rounded <- roundPunches(record.timeIn, record.timeOut, policy.punchRounding) 4. gross <- minutesBetween(rounded.in, rounded.out) 5. breakM <- policy.breakFor(schedule, gross) // fixed, punch-based, or zero 6. paid <- max(0, gross - breakM) 7. cap <- policy.capPerDay ?? infinity 8. return Worked(min(paid, cap), overtimeCandidate: max(0, paid - schedule.standardMinutes)) ``` ``` classifyAttendance(worked, schedule, calendar, policy) -> Classification // requires D-05 (dayType enum), D-11 (grace), D-12 (undertime), D-13 (no row), D-14 (OT) Present | Late(minutes) | Undertime(minutes) | Absent | RestDay | Holiday(type) | OnLeave(type) | NoSchedule // rule: a day with no row is only Absent when the schedule says it is a workday AND no approved leave covers it // rule: an unapproved overtime minute is reported, never paid, until D-14 says otherwise ``` ### 11.2 Leave ``` computeLeaveDays(startDate, endDate, leaveType, calendar, policy) -> days // requires D-20 (calendar vs working days, half days), D-05 (holiday calendar) filter the inclusive date range by policy.countsWeekends / policy.countsHolidays for the type subtract half-day markers if the type supports them ``` ``` applyLeaveRequest(current, request, balances, approver, policy) -> newState | Rejection // requires D-19, D-21, D-23, D-24 guard: requester may act for this employee (D-23/D-24) guard: balance sufficient, or policy allows negative (D-20) guard: no overlapping approved leave or approved OT on the same dates (D-17) transition Pending review -> Approved | Rejected, recording approver, timestamp, reason on Approval: deduct from the balance atomically (transaction) and emit an audit event ``` ### 11.3 Payroll (the gated engine) ``` buildPayrollRun(period, employees, attendance, leave, ruleset) -> Run | Blocked(reasons) // requires D-34, D-36, D-43, D-46…D-51 1. assert ruleset covers period (D-51); if not -> Blocked("no ruleset for period") // fail closed 2. for each employee with an approved payroll profile: inputs <- PayrollInputs{ cashPay, sssCompensation, philHealthMbs, pagibigFundSalary, taxableCompensation } // the five INDEPENDENT bases if any base missing -> Blocked(employee, "missing base") // never infer one from another 3. compute components per employee, each a pure function of (input base, ruleset) 4. persist an immutable snapshot: inputs, ruleset version, computed components, timestamps return Run ``` ``` computeSss(base, ruleset) -> {employee, employer, ec} msc <- clamp(base, floor, ceiling); msc <- roundToStep(msc, step) // D-46 employee<- msc * employeeRate employer<- msc * employerRate ec <- bracketLookup(msc, ecTable) // employer-only ``` ``` computePhilHealth(base, ruleset) -> {employee, employer} b <- clamp(base, floor, ceiling) // D-47 total <- b * rate return { employee: total / 2, employer: total / 2 } // each share rounded per D-39 ``` ``` computePagIbig(base, ruleset) -> {employee, employer} fund <- min(base, maxFundSalary) // D-48 employeeRate <- fund <= lowThreshold ? lowRate : highRate return { employee: fund * employeeRate, employer: fund * employerRate } ``` ``` computeWithholding(taxableBase, ruleset) -> amount // requires D-49 (which table + base definition) and D-50 (boundary convention) band <- last band whose lowerBound < taxableBase // strict, whole-peso bound return band.baseTax + (taxableBase - band.floor) * band.rate ``` ``` computeNet(run, policy) -> {net, employerCost} // requires D-41 (order/allocation), D-42 (floor) employeeStatutory <- sss.employee + philHealth.employee + pagibig.employee taxableBase <- policy.taxBaseOf(cashPay, allowances, employeeStatutory) // <-- THE open assumption withholding <- computeWithholding(taxableBase, ruleset) net <- cashPay - employeeStatutory - withholding - otherDeductions if net < 0 and policy.floorAtZero -> net <- 0 and record a carry-forward employerCost <- cashPay + sss.employer + sss.ec + philHealth.employer + pagibig.employer ``` The single most important line above is `policy.taxBaseOf(...)`. The handoff's own document says its choice — subtract employee statutory shares before withholding — is "a documented implementation assumption". **That is exactly the line you have to decide (D-49), and it is why no calculator should exist yet.** ### 11.4 Golden examples you will need to supply Before any engine is switched on, you need a signed-off table like this — filled by you or by payroll, not by me: | Case | Period | Inputs (five bases) | Expected SSS ee/er/ec | PhilHealth ee/er | Pag-IBIG ee/er | Taxable base | Withholding | Net | Employer cost | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | Monthly minimum wage | monthly | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | | Below SSS floor | monthly | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | | At each bracket boundary ±₱0.50 | monthly | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | | Above all ceilings | monthly | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | | Semi-monthly cutoff 1 / cutoff 2 pair | semi-monthly | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | | Zero-pay period with active benefits | any | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | Boundary cases matter more than mid-band cases: every historical 0.01 discrepancy in the peer evidence came from a boundary or a rounding choice. --- ## 12. Every payroll amount passes through here so rounding * happens in exactly one place. Firestore has no decimal type, so amounts are stored * as plain decimal strings and parsed back into BigDecimal. */ public final class Money { public static final BigDecimal ZERO = new BigDecimal("0.00"); private static final BigDecimal HUNDRED = new BigDecimal("100"); private Money() { } /** Two-decimal, half-up: the convention that reproduces the supplied MotorPH payslip. */ public static BigDecimal round(BigDecimal value) { if (value == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("amount must not be null"); return value.setScale(2, RoundingMode.HALF_UP); } /** Parse a user/CSV amount, tolerating currency marks, spaces and thousands separators. */ public static BigDecimal parse(String raw) { if (raw == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("amount must not be null"); String cleaned = raw.replace('\u20B1', ' ').replace(",", "").replace("\u00A0", " ").trim(); if (cleaned.isEmpty()) throw new IllegalArgumentException("amount must not be blank"); try { return round(new BigDecimal(cleaned)); } catch (NumberFormatException ex) { throw new IllegalArgumentException("Not a valid amount: " + raw.trim()); } } /** Parse, treating blank as zero; used for optional allowance columns. */ public static BigDecimal parseOrZero(String raw) { return raw == null || raw.trim().isEmpty() ? Available: 2025, 2026. Refusing to calculate outside a covered year."); } public String id() { return id; } public String effectiveFrom() { return effectiveFrom; } public String effectiveTo() { return effectiveTo; } public BigDecimal sssEmployeeRate() { return sssEmployeeRate; } public BigDecimal sssEmployerRate() { return sssEmployerRate; } public BigDecimal sssMinMsc() { return sssMinMsc; } public BigDecimal sssMaxMsc() { return sssMaxMsc; } public BigDecimal sssMscStep() { return sssMscStep; } public BigDecimal sssEcLow() { return sssEcLow; } public BigDecimal sssEcHigh() { return sssEcHigh; } public BigDecimal sssEcThreshold() { return sssEcThreshold; } public BigDecimal sssMpfThreshold() { return sssMpfThreshold; } public BigDecimal phRate() { return phRate; } public BigDecimal phFloor() { return phFloor; } public BigDecimal phCeiling() { return phCeiling; } public BigDecimal pagibigMaxFund() { return pagibigMaxFund; } public BigDecimal pagibigLowThreshold() { return pagibigLowThreshold; } public BigDecimal pagibigEmployeeLow() { return pagibigEmployeeLow; } public BigDecimal pagibigEmployeeHigh() { return pagibigEmployeeHigh; } public BigDecimal pagibigEmployerRate() { return pagibigEmployerRate; } public List<TaxBracket> taxBrackets(Period period) { List<TaxBracket> source = period == Period.SEMI_MONTHLY ? [NODE 7443]
Actually cleanest & verified: basePay = dailyRate × daysWorked. With dailyRate = 2675 and days 10 → 26,750 ✓. And for a full monthly period, daysWorked = 21.75 → dailyRate × 21.75 = 58,181 ≠ 53,500. So "days worked" in a monthly period should be 20 (53,500/2,675). The divisor depends on period. MotorPH's 2026 Jan 1-15 period used 10 days → so they count only actual working days in the period (Jan 2-15: Jan 2,5,6,7,8,9,12,13,14,15 = 10 working days; Jan 1 holiday, weekends 3,4,10,11 → yes exactly 10!).

[NODE 7444]
basePay = dailyRate × daysWorked

BASIC_ONLY reproduces the supplied payslip. */ public enum TaxBasis { BASIC_ONLY, BASIC_PLUS_TAXABLE_ALLOWANCE } /** How a monthly statutory amount is applied to a pay period. */ public enum StatutoryBasis { FULL_MONTHLY_EACH_PERIOD, SPLIT_EVENLY } public static final class Input { public String employeeId; public String employeeName = ""; public String position = ""; public String department = ""; public String payPeriod = "MONTHLY"; public String periodStart = ""; public String periodEnd = ""; public BigDecimal monthlyBasic; public BigDecimal nightDifferentialRatePercent = new BigDecimal("10"); public BigDecimal riceSubsidy = Money.ZERO; public BigDecimal phoneAllowance = Money.ZERO; public BigDecimal clothingAllowance = Money.ZERO; public BigDecimal taxableAllowance = Money.ZERO; public BigDecimal otherDeductions = Money.ZERO; public String taxBasis = TaxBasis.BASIC_ONLY.name(); public String statutoryBasis = StatutoryBasis.FULL_MONTHLY_EACH_PERIOD.name(); } public Payslip compute(Input input, PayrollRuleset ruleset) { validate(input); PayrollRuleset.Period period = PayrollRuleset.Period.parse(input.payPeriod); TaxBasis taxBasis = parseTaxBasis(input.taxBasis); BigDecimal nightDifferentialPay = Money.round(hourlyRate.multiply(input.nightDifferentialHours) .multiply(input.nightDifferentialRatePercent).divide(new BigDecimal("100"), 6, RoundingMode.HALF_UP)); BigDecimal grossIncome = Money.round(basePay.add(overtimePay).add(nightDifferentialPay)); BigDecimal nonTaxable = Money.round(input.riceSubsidy.add(input.phoneAllowance).add(input.clothingAllowance)); BigDecimal taxableAllowance = Money.round(input.taxableAllowance); BigDecimal totalBenefits = Money.round(nonTaxable.add(taxableAllowance)); // Statutory amounts are monthly figures; the split decides how much lands in this period. BigDecimal divisor = statutoryBasis == StatutoryBasis.SPLIT_EVENLY && period == PayrollRuleset.Period.SEMI_MONTHLY ? new BigDecimal(period.periodsPerMonth()) : BigDecimal.ONE; BigDecimal sss = perPeriod(ruleset.sssEmployee(monthlyBasic), divisor); BigDecimal philHealth = perPeriod(ruleset.philHealthEmployee(monthlyBasic), divisor); BigDecimal pagibig = perPeriod(ruleset.pagibigEmployee(monthlyBasic), divisor); BigDecimal monthlyStatutory = Money.round(ruleset.sssEmployee(monthlyBasic) .add(ruleset.philHealthEmployee(monthlyBasic)).add(ruleset.pagibigEmployee(monthlyBasic))); BigDecimal taxableMonthly = taxBasis == TaxBasis.BASIC_PLUS_TAXABLE_ALLOWANCE ? Correct the inputs before saving this run."); } BigDecimal employerSss = perPeriod(ruleset.sssEmployer(monthlyBasic), divisor); BigDecimal employerEc = perPeriod(ruleset.sssEc(monthlyBasic), divisor); BigDecimal employerPhilHealth = perPeriod(ruleset.philHealthEmployer(monthlyBasic), divisor); BigDecimal employerPagibig = perPeriod(ruleset.pagibigEmployer(monthlyBasic), divisor); BigDecimal employerCost = Money.round(grossIncome.add(totalBenefits) .add(employerSss).add(employerEc).add(employerPhilHealth).add(employerPagibig)); rows.add(new String[]{"PhilHealth", Money.format(ph)}); rows.add(new String[]{"Pag-IBIG", Money.format(pi)}); rows.add(new String[]{"BIR withholding", Money.format(tax)}); return rows; } private static BigDecimal divideMonths(BigDecimal monthly, BigDecimal divisor) { return monthly.divide(divisor, 2, RoundingMode.HALF_UP); } private static BigDecimal perPeriod(BigDecimal monthlyAmount, BigDecimal divisor) { if (divisor.compareTo(BigDecimal.ONE) == 0) return monthlyAmount; return Money.round(monthlyAmount.divide(divisor, 4, RoundingMode.HALF_UP)); $ cd /home/user/motorph-ms2 && cat > web/payroll.js <<'EOF' /** * Payroll presentation helpers. All money arithmetic happens on the server; these functions * only format amounts, build the payslip layout, and assemble CSV columns. */ const AMOUNT_FIELDS = Object.freeze([ ['monthlyBasic', 'Monthly Salary'], ['dailyRate', 'Daily Rate'], ['hourlyRate', 'Hourly Rate'], ['overtimePay', 'Overtime'], ['nightDifferentialPay', 'Night Differential'], ['grossIncome', 'GROSS INCOME'], ['riceSubsidy', 'Rice Subsidy'], ['phoneAllowance', 'Phone Allowance'], ['clothingAllowance', 'Clothing Allowance'], ['taxableAllowance', 'Taxable Allowance'], ['totalBenefits', 'TOTAL BENEFITS'], ['sssEmployee', 'Social Security System'], ['philHealthEmployee', 'PhilHealth'], ['pagibigEmployee', 'Pag-IBIG'], ['withholdingTax', 'Withholding Tax'], ['totalDeductions', 'TOTAL DEDUCTIONS'], ['takeHomePay', 'TAKE HOME PAY'], ['sssEmployer', 'SSS employer share'], ['sssEc', "Employer EC"], ['philHealthEmployer', 'PhilHealth employer share'], ['pagibigEmployer', 'Pag-IBIG employer share'], ['employerCost', 'EMPLOYER COST'] ]); /** Money text for display: "26,750.00". Never used for arithmetic. */ export function formatAmount(value) { const number = Number(value); if (!Number.isFinite(number)) return '0.00'; return number.toLocaleString('en-PH', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 }); $ cd /home/user/motorph-ms2 && rm -f ui-check.tmp.mjs diag.tmp.mjs golden-ui.tmp.mjs && cat > docs/payroll-ruleset-and-golden-case.md <<'EOF' # Payroll ruleset, golden case, and what the supplied data settled **Status date:** 2026-11-05. **Supersedes** the "payroll gated, no calculation" statements in `docs/build-status-no-local-no-temp.md` and the research-only status in `docs/candidate-policy-review.md`. Payroll now calculates, saves runs, and is verified against a document MotorPH produced. ## 1. What closed the gap The supplied documents contain a **MotorPH payslip with every line item**, and a **timecard with break punches**. That payslip is a controlling example: any ruleset that does not reproduce it is wrong, regardless of what a summary table says. The engine in `PayrollService` + `PayrollRuleset` reproduces it to the centavo, and `PayrollGoldenTest` fails the build if that ever stops being true. **Source documents** | Document | What it settled | |---|---| | `Copy of MotorPH Payslip - MotorPH Payslip.csv` | The full arithmetic chain: gross, benefits, four deductions, totals, take-home | | `Copy of MotorPH Sample Timecard - MotorPH Payslip.csv` | Break out / break in punches, the 8-hour day, weekend and holiday rows at 0 hrs | | `Copy of MotorPH_Employee Data - Employee Details.csv` | Monthly basic, the three allowances, and the 20-day / 168-hour divisors | | sweldongpinoy.com (rates: 2026) | The rate *structure*: basic pay + taxable/non-taxable allowance + night differential + overtime → statutory → withholding | ## 2. The golden case Payslip `15-2026-01-15`, employee 15, period 2026-01-02 → 2026-01-15, monthly basic ₱53,500, 10 days worked, benefits ₱4,500. | Line | MotorPH | Engine | |---|---:|---:| | Daily rate (53,500 ÷ 20) | 2,675.00 | 2,675.00 | | Gross income (× 10 days) | 26,750.00 | 26,750.00 | | Rice / phone / clothing | 1,500 / 2,000 / 1,000 | same | | Benefits total | 4,500.00 | 4,500.00 | | SSS employee | 1,750.00 | 1,750.00 | | PhilHealth | 1,337.50 | 1,337.50 | | Pag-IBIG | 200.00 | 200.00 | | Taxable base | *not printed* | 50,212.50 | | Withholding tax | 5,250.83 | 5,250.83 | | Total deductions | 8,538.33 | 8,538.33 | | **Take home pay** | **22,711.67** | **22,711.67** | Two MotorPH conventions are now **implemented as evidenced**, not guessed: 1. **Statutory amounts are monthly and are deducted in full inside a semi-monthly cutoff.** The payslip deducts a full month's SSS (₱1,750 = 5% of the ₱35,000 ceiling) from one cutoff. This is the default (`FULL_MONTHLY_EACH_PERIOD`); a `SPLIT_EVENLY` mode exists but does not reproduce the payslip. 2. **Withholding is computed on monthly basic less employee statutory shares**, using the monthly Annex E table. This is `BASIC_ONLY`, the default. `BASIC_PLUS_TAXABLE_ALLOWANCE` exists for comparison and changes the answer. ## 3. Rate decisions that are now evidenced rather than assumed **Bracket floors are the annual thresholds divided by 12, not the whole-peso rendering.** This is the one finding that could not have been guessed: ``` 50,212.50 taxable floor 33,333.00 (whole peso) -> 1,875 + (50,212.50 - 33,333.00) × 20% = 5,250.90 ✗ floor 33,333.33 (400,000/12) -> 1,875 + (50,212.50 - 33,333.33) × 20% = 5,250.83 ✓ ``` The same applies to the semi-monthly table, which uses the annual thresholds over 24 and is **not** the monthly table halved. Both tables are in `PayrollRuleset`. **Divisors are `monthly ÷ 20` and `monthly ÷ 168`.** Every row of the supplied salary table satisfies these to the centavo (₱24,000 → ₱1,200 daily and ₱142.86 hourly; ₱41,850 → ₱2,092.50 / ₱249.11). **SSS MSC rounds up to the next ₱500 step and is then clamped** to ₱5,000–₱35,000. At ₱53,500 both readings give ₱1,750, so the payslip cannot settle rounding; the round-up rule is the standard SSS method and is flagged as such in the ruleset. **Timekeeping uses punches, not a fixed lunch.** The supplied timecard reports 08:00–12:00 / 13:00–17:00 as **8 hrs**, i.e. out − in − meal. `WorkedTime` implements exactly that, and `TimesheetServiceTest` asserts the supplied row shape. Consequence worth stating plainly: a row with **no** break punches yields 9 hours, so missing meal punches inflate paid hours. That is a data requirement, not a rule the app can invent. ## 4. What is implemented - `Money`, `PayrollRuleset` (2025 and 2026, effective-dated, fail-closed outside them), `PayrollService`, `Payslip`, `PayrollRun`, `PayrollStore` + `InMemory`/`Firestore` adapters, `TimesheetService`, `WorkedTime`, break-aware `AttendanceRecord`. - Routes: `GET /api/payroll/rules`, `GET /api/payroll/timesheet`, `POST /api/payroll/preview`, `POST /api/payroll/runs`, `GET /api/payroll/runs`, `GET /api/payroll/runs/{id}`. - Employee records carry monthly basic, rice subsidy, phone allowance and clothing allowance; the payroll picker only offers employees that have a pay profile. - UI: payslip in MotorPH's layout, remittance summary (both shares), statutory rate table, run history with saved snapshots, payslip CSV export, "use stored timesheet days". - Saved runs are **immutable snapshots**: inputs, ruleset version, both calculation assumptions, and every computed line are stored, so a reprint never recalculates. ## 5. What is still not done | Gap | Why it is still open | |---|---| | Attendance → days worked → payslip, automatically | The UI has "use stored timesheet days", but days worked is still an operator-confirmed field. Absence, tardiness and undertime have no approved rule. | | Overtime and night-differential **hours** from punches | Rates are parameterised (125% / 10%); the qualifying hours are not derived. Overtime approval is not modelled. | | Leave pay, holiday/rest-day premiums, 13th month, other earnings | No rule supplied. | | A **multi-employee** run | API and store support many payslips per run; the UI computes one employee at a time. | | Approval, roles, audit, payslip access control | Owner-only Firestore paths; no role model. | | Ruleset for years before 2025 | `forYear` throws outside 2025–2026 rather than borrowing an adjacent table. | ## 6. What the remaining questions now are (short list) 1. **Cutoff convention:** confirm `FULL_MONTHLY_EACH_PERIOD` is company policy, or supply the split rule. This is the largest remaining per-payslip difference. 2. **Withholding base:** confirm `BASIC_ONLY` (as the payslip shows) or include taxable allowances. 3. **MSC rounding:** round up to the bracket, or use the bracket containing the salary? Both give ₱1,750 at the ceiling, so only a mid-range payslip can settle it. 4. **Overtime and night-differential hours:** how are they qualified and approved? 5. **Absence/tardiness/undertime:** which day is "no work" versus "no record"? 6. **2027 tables:** the effective-dating mechanism works; next year's rates must be added when published. ## 7. Non-negotiable test `PayrollGoldenTest` reproduces the supplied payslip (14 amounts), the bracket boundaries, the MSC steps, the semi-monthly table, the split and allowance variants, the rejections (uncovered year, negative pay, too many days, negative take-home, bad dates, unknown period), and the remittance totals. If a future rule change breaks the golden case, the test fails the build on purpose. rules_version = '2';
service cloud.firestore {
  match /databases/{database}/documents {
    function signedInAs(uid) {
      return request.auth != null && request.auth.uid == uid;
    }

    function validDemoEmployee(employeeId) {
      let d = request.resource.data;
      return d.keys().hasAll(['id', 'name', 'department', 'role', 'location', 'status'])
        && d.keys().hasOnly(['id', 'name', 'department', 'role', 'location', 'status'])
        && d.id is string && d.id == employeeId && d.id.size() <= 40
        && d.name is string && d.name.size() > 0 && d.name.size() <= 100
        && d.department is string && d.department.size() > 0 && d.department.size() <= 100
        && d.role is string && d.role.size() > 0 && d.role.size() <= 100
        && d.location is string && d.location.size() > 0 && d.location.size() <= 100
        && d.status in ['Active', 'On leave'];
    }

    function validDemoScheduleMapping(uid, employeeId) {
      let d = request.resource.data;
      let employeePath = /databases/$(database)/documents/users/$(uid)/demoEmployees/$(employeeId);
      return d.keys().hasAll(['employeeId', 'scheduleId'])
        && d.keys().hasOnly(['employeeId', 'scheduleId'])
        && d.employeeId is string && d.employeeId == employeeId
        && d.scheduleId is int && d.scheduleId > 0
        && exists(employeePath);
    }

    function validDemoAttendance() {
      let d = request.resource.data;
      return d.keys().hasAll(['attendanceId', 'scheduleId', 'date', 'timeIn', 'timeOut', 'dayType'])
        && d.keys().hasOnly(['attendanceId', 'scheduleId', 'date', 'timeIn', 'timeOut', 'dayType'])
        && d.attendanceId is int && d.attendanceId > 0
        && d.scheduleId is int && d.scheduleId > 0
        && d.date is string && d.date.matches('^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$')
        && d.timeIn is string && d.timeIn.matches('^([01][0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-5][0-9]$')
        && d.timeOut is string && d.timeOut.matches('^([01][0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-5][0-9]$')
        && d.dayType == 'DEMO';
    }

    function ownsDemoEmployee(uid, employeeId, employeeName) {
      let employeePath = /databases/$(database)/documents/users/$(uid)/demoEmployees/$(employeeId);
      return employeeId is string
        && (employeeId.matches('^DEMO-[0-9]{3}$') || employeeId.matches('^DEMO-[A-F0-9]{12}$'))
        && employeeName is string
        && exists(employeePath)
        && get(employeePath).data.name == employeeName;
    }

    function validDemoLeaveRequest(uid, requestId) {
      let d = request.resource.data;
      return d.keys().hasAll(['id', 'employeeId', 'employeeName', 'leaveType', 'startDate', 'endDate', 'note', 'status', 'submittedAt'])
        && d.keys().hasOnly(['id', 'employeeId', 'employeeName', 'leaveType', 'startDate', 'endDate', 'note', 'status', 'submittedAt'])
        && d.id is string && d.id == requestId && d.id.matches('^LV-[A-F0-9]{12}$')
        && ownsDemoEmployee(uid, d.employeeId, d.employeeName)
        && d.leaveType in ['Vacation', 'Medical', 'Personal', 'Unpaid']
        && d.startDate is string && d.startDate.matches('^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$')
        && d.endDate is string && d.endDate.matches('^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$')
        && d.startDate <= d.endDate
        && d.note is string && d.note.size() <= 240
        && d.status == 'Pending review'
        && d.submittedAt is timestamp;
    }

    function validDemoLeaveCancellation(uid, requestId) {
      let previous = resource.data;
      let next = request.resource.data;
      return signedInAs(uid)
        && previous.id == requestId
        && previous.status == 'Pending review'
        && next.id == previous.id
        && next.diff(previous).affectedKeys().hasAll(['status', 'cancelledAt'])
        && next.diff(previous).affectedKeys().hasOnly(['status', 'cancelledAt'])
        && next.status == 'Cancelled'
        && next.cancelledAt is timestamp;
    }

    function validTicketQueue(ticketType, queue) {
      return (ticketType in ['Overtime request', 'Leave request', 'Timesheet correction'] && queue == 'Team Lead')
        || (ticketType == 'Payroll inquiry' && queue == 'Payroll Staff')
        || (ticketType == 'HR inquiry' && queue == 'HR')
        || (ticketType == 'Technical support' && queue == 'IT Admin');
    }

    function validDemoTicket(uid, ticketId) {
      let d = request.resource.data;
      return d.keys().hasAll(['id', 'employeeId', 'employeeName', 'ticketType', 'queue', 'summary', 'status', 'submittedAt'])
        && d.keys().hasOnly(['id', 'employeeId', 'employeeName', 'ticketType', 'queue', 'summary', 'status', 'submittedAt'])
        && d.id is string && d.id == ticketId && d.id.matches('^TK-[A-F0-9]{12}$')
        && ownsDemoEmployee(uid, d.employeeId, d.employeeName)
        && validTicketQueue(d.ticketType, d.queue)
        && d.summary is string && d.summary.size() > 0 && d.summary.size() <= 240
        && d.status == 'Open'
        && d.submittedAt is timestamp;
    }

    function validDemoTicketCancellation(uid, ticketId) {
      let previous = resource.data;
      let next = request.resource.data;
      return signedInAs(uid)
        && previous.id == ticketId
        && previous.status == 'Open'
        && next.id == previous.id
        && next.diff(previous).affectedKeys().hasAll(['status', 'cancelledAt'])
        && next.diff(previous).affectedKeys().hasOnly(['status', 'cancelledAt'])
        && next.status == 'Cancelled'
        && next.cancelledAt is timestamp;
    }

    match /users/{uid}/demoEmployees/{employeeId} {
      allow read: if signedInAs(uid);
      allow create, update: if signedInAs(uid) && validDemoEmployee(employeeId);
      allow delete: if signedInAs(uid);
    }

    // Seeded owner-scoped links replace the old code-only employee/schedule map.
    // Read/create only: schedule assignment editing remains disabled until its policy is approved.
    match /users/{uid}/demoEmployeeSchedules/{employeeId} {
      allow read: if signedInAs(uid);
      allow create: if signedInAs(uid) && validDemoScheduleMapping(uid, employeeId);
      allow update, delete: if false;
    }

    match /users/{uid}/demoAttendance/{attendanceId} {
      allow read: if signedInAs(uid);
      allow create, update: if signedInAs(uid) && validDemoAttendance();
      allow delete: if signedInAs(uid);
    }

    // Owner-only demo requests. There are deliberately no reviewer, approval, or delete permissions.
    match /users/{uid}/demoLeaveRequests/{requestId} {
      allow read: if signedInAs(uid);
      allow create: if signedInAs(uid) && validDemoLeaveRequest(uid, requestId);
      allow update: if validDemoLeaveCancellation(uid, requestId);
      allow delete: if false;
    }

    match /users/{uid}/demoTickets/{ticketId} {
      allow read: if signedInAs(uid);
      allow create: if signedInAs(uid) && validDemoTicket(uid, ticketId);
      allow update: if validDemoTicketCancellation(uid, ticketId);
      allow delete: if false;
    }

    // Default-deny: no other Firestore document paths are available to clients.
    match /{document=**} {
      allow read, write: if false;
    }
  }
}

    private static void localModeServesSyntheticEmployeeAndAttendanceResponses() throws Exception {
        AppServer app = new AppServer("", Paths.get("web"));

        try {

            check(noMatches.statusCode() == 200 && noMatches.body().contains("\"items\":[]"), "empty employee search is a valid empty result");

            HttpResponse<String> employee = get(base.resolve("/api/employees/DEMO-001"));
            check(employee.statusCode() == 200 && employee.body().contains("\"name\":\"Mara Rivera\""), "employee detail returns selected record over HTTP");
            HttpResponse<String> missingEmployee = get(base.resolve("/api/employees/UNKNOWN"));
            check(missingEmployee.statusCode() == 404, "unknown employee detail returns not found");

            HttpResponse<String> attendance = get(base.resolve("/api/attendance?employeeId=DEMO-001&from=2026-10-01&to=2026-10-15"));

            HttpResponse<String> oneDay = get(base.resolve("/api/attendance?employeeId=DEMO-001&from=2026-10-02&to=2026-10-02"));

            check(noAttendance.statusCode() == 200 && noAttendance.body().contains("\"count\":0"), "empty selected period returns an empty attendance result");

            HttpResponse<String> missingAttendanceEmployee = get(base.resolve("/api/attendance"));

            check(invalidRange.statusCode() == 400, "reversed date range returns client error");

                "report returns raw row count and date bounds");

    private static void localModeCreatesAndUpdatesOnlySyntheticDirectoryFields() throws Exception {
        AppServer app = new AppServer("", Paths.get("web"));
        HttpServer server = app.start("127.0.0.1", 0);
        try {
            URI base = URI.create("http://127.0.0.1:" + server.getAddress().getPort());

            HttpResponse<String> attendance = get(base.resolve("/api/attendance?employeeId=" + id));
            check(attendance.statusCode() == 200 && attendance.body().contains("\"count\":0"),
                "new synthetic employees have no attendance until a schedule mapping is supplied");

            HttpResponse<String> injectedId = postJson(base.resolve("/api/employees"),
                "{\"id\":\"REAL-001\",\"name\":\"Fake\",\"department\":\"Ops\",\"role\":\"Role\",\"location\":\"City\",\"status\":\"Active\"}");
            check(injectedId.statusCode() == 400, "client cannot choose or inject an employee ID");
            HttpResponse<String> invalidStatus = postJson(base.resolve("/api/employees"),
                "{\"name\":\"Bad Status\",\"department\":\"Ops\",\"role\":\"Role\",\"location\":\"City\",\"status\":\"Terminated\"}");
            check(invalidStatus.statusCode() == 400, "unsupported synthetic status is rejected");

            HttpResponse<String> updated = putJson(base.resolve("/api/employees/" + id),
                "{\"name\":\"Ira Rivera\",\"department\":\"Operations\",\"role\":\"Lead\",\"location\":\"Makati\",\"status\":\"On leave\"}");
            check(updated.statusCode() == 200 && updated.body().contains("Ira Rivera"), "owner sandbox can update synthetic directory fields");
            HttpResponse<String> search = get(base.resolve("/api/employees?q=ira+rivera"));
            check(search.statusCode() == 200 && search.body().contains(id) && search.body().contains("On leave"),
                "updated synthetic employee appears in search results");
            HttpRequest delete = HttpRequest.newBuilder(base.resolve("/api/employees/" + id)).DELETE().build();
            HttpResponse<String> deleteResponse = HTTP.send(delete, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
            check(deleteResponse.statusCode() == 405, "employee deletion is not exposed");
        } finally {
            app.stop();
        }
    }

    private static void localModeStoresScopedWorkflowRequestsWithValidatedStateChanges() throws Exception {
        AppServer app = new AppServer("", Paths.get("web"));
        HttpServer server = app.start("127.0.0.1", 0);
        try {
            URI base = URI.create("http://127.0.0.1:" + server.getAddress().getPort());
            HttpResponse<String> empty = get(base.resolve("/api/workflows"));
            check(empty.statusCode() == 200 && empty.body().contains("\"leaveRequests\":[]")
                && empty.body().contains("\"tickets\":[]"), "local workflow lists start empty");

            HttpResponse<String> invalid = postJson(base.resolve("/api/workflows/leave"),
                "{\"employeeId\":\"DEMO-001\",\"leaveType\":\"Vacation\",\"startDate\":\"2026-02-30\",\"endDate\":\"2026-03-01\",\"note\":\"\"}");
            check(invalid.statusCode() == 400, "invalid leave date is rejected");

            HttpResponse<String> createdLeave = postJson(base.resolve("/api/workflows/leave"),

    private static final class FakeFirestoreServer implements AutoCloseable {
        private static final String SCHEDULE_MAPPING_DOCUMENT = "{\"name\":\"projects/demo-project/databases/(default)/documents/users/user-77/demoEmployeeSchedules/DEMO-001\",\"fields\":{\"employeeId\":{\"stringValue\":\"DEMO-001\"},\"scheduleId\":{\"integerValue\":\"101\"}}}";
        private static final String EMPLOYEE_DOCUMENT = "{\"name\":\"projects/demo-project/databases/(default)/documents/users/user-77/demoEmployees/DEMO-001\","
            + "\"fields\":{\"id\":{\"stringValue\":\"DEMO-001\"},\"name\":{\"stringValue\":\"Mara Rivera\"},"
            + "\"department\":{\"stringValue\":\"People Operations\"},\"role\":{\"stringValue\":\"HR Coordinator\"},"
            + "\"location\":{\"stringValue\":\"Makati\"},\"status\":{\"stringValue\":\"Active\"}}}";
        private final HttpServer server;
        private final List<String> paths = new ArrayList<>();
        private final List<String> methods = new ArrayList<>();
        private final List<String> authorizations = new ArrayList<>();
        private final List<String> requestBodies = new ArrayList<>();

        FakeFirestoreServer() throws Exception {
            server = HttpServer.create(new java.net.InetSocketAddress("127.0.0.1", 0), 0);
            server.createContext("/", this::handle);
            server.start();
        }

        String apiRoot() { return "http://127.0.0.1:" + server.getAddress().getPort() + "/v1/projects/"; }

        private synchronized void handle(HttpExchange exchange) throws java.io.IOException {
            paths.add(exchange.getRequestURI().toString());
            methods.add(exchange.getRequestMethod());
            authorizations.add(exchange.getRequestHeaders().getFirst("Authorization"));
            String body = new String(exchange.getRequestBody().readAllBytes(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
            requestBodies.add(body);
            String path = exchange.getRequestURI().getPath();
            String response;
            int status = 200;
            if ("GET".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod()) && path.contains("/demoEmployees")) {
                response = "{\"documents\":[" + EMPLOYEE_DOCUMENT + "]}";
            } else if ("GET".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod()) && path.contains("/demoEmployeeSchedules")) {
                response = "{\"documents\":[" + SCHEDULE_MAPPING_DOCUMENT + "]}";
            } else if ("GET".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod()) && path.contains("/demoAttendance")) {
                response = "{\"documents\":[]}";
            } else if ("POST".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod()) && path.contains("/demoLeaveRequests")) {
                response = "{\"name\":\"projects/demo-project/databases/(default)/documents/users/user-77/demoLeaveRequests/LV-012345ABCDEF\"}";
            } else if ("POST".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod()) && path.contains("/demoEmployees")) {
                response = "{\"name\":\"projects/demo-project/databases/(default)/documents/users/user-77/demoEmployees/DEMO-FAKE000000\"}";
            } else if ("POST".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod()) && (path.contains("/demoEmployeeSchedules") || path.contains("/demoAttendance"))) {
                response = "{\"name\":\"projects/demo-project/databases/(default)/documents" + path.substring(path.indexOf("/users/")) + "\"}";
            } else if ("PATCH".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod()) && path.endsWith("/DEMO-001")) {
                response = EMPLOYEE_DOCUMENT;
            } else {
                status = 404;
                response = "{\"error\":{\"status\":\"NOT_FOUND\"}}";
            }
            byte[] bytes = response.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
            exchange.getResponseHeaders().set("Content-Type", "application/json");
            exchange.sendResponseHeaders(status, bytes.length);
            exchange.getResponseBody().write(bytes);
            exchange.close();
        }

        @Override public void close() { server.stop(0); }
    }

    private static void check(boolean condition, String message) {
        checks++;
        if (!condition) throw new AssertionError(message);
    }

    private void handlePayroll(HttpExchange exchange) throws IOException {
        String path = exchange.getRequestURI().getPath();
        String method = exchange.getRequestMethod();
        try {
            if ("GET".equals(method) && "/api/payroll/rules".equals(path)) {
                int year = parseIntYear(queryParameter(exchange.getRequestURI().getRawQuery(), "year"));
                PayrollRuleset ruleset = PayrollRuleset.forYear(year);
                sendJson(exchange, 200, rulesetToJson(ruleset));
                return;
            }
            if ("GET".equals(method) && "/api/payroll/timesheet".equals(path)) {
                String employeeId = queryParameter(exchange.getRequestURI().getRawQuery(), "employeeId");
                if (employeeId == null || employeeId.trim().isEmpty()) {
                    sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"employeeId is required\"}");
                    return;
                }
                RequestServices services = servicesFor(exchange);
                AttendanceService attendance = new AttendanceService(services.employeeService,
                    services.scheduleStore, services.attendanceStore);
                LocalDate from = parseOptionalDate(queryParameter(exchange.getRequestURI().getRawQuery(), "from"));
                LocalDate to = parseOptionalDate(queryParameter(exchange.getRequestURI().getRawQuery(), "to"));
                TimesheetService.Summary summary = new TimesheetService(attendance).summarise(employeeId, from, to);
                sendJson(exchange, 200, timesheetToJson(summary));
                return;
            }
            if ("POST".equals(method) && ("/api/payroll/preview".equals(path) || "/api/payroll/runs".equals(path))) {
                PayrollService.Input input = payrollInputFrom(readJsonBody(exchange));
                PayrollRuleset ruleset = PayrollRuleset.forYear(periodYear(input));
                Payslip slip = new PayrollService().compute(input, ruleset);
                if ("/api/payroll/preview".equals(path)) {
                    sendJson(exchange, 200, "{\"payslip\":" + PayslipJson.toJson(slip).toString()
                        + ",\"saved\":false,\"ruleset\":" + rulesetToJson(ruleset) + "}");
                    return;
                }
                PayrollRun saved = payrollStoreFor(exchange).create(new PayrollRun(runId(input), input.payPeriod,
                    input.periodStart, input.periodEnd, ruleset.id(), input.taxBasis, input.statutoryBasis,
                    java.time.Instant.now().toString(), java.util.Collections.singletonList(slip)));
                sendJson(exchange, 201, "{\"run\":" + runToJson(saved, true) + ",\"saved\":true}");
                return;
            }
            if ("GET".equals(method) && ("/api/payroll/runs".equals(path) || "/api/payroll/runs/".equals(path))) {
                StringBuilder items = new StringBuilder();
                int count = 0;
                for (PayrollRun run : payrollStoreFor(exchange).findAll()) {
                    if (count > 0) items.append(',');
                    items.append(runToJson(run, false));
                    count++;
                }
                sendJson(exchange, 200, "{\"items\":[" + items + "],\"count\":" + count + "}");
                return;
            }
            if ("GET".equals(method) && path.startsWith("/api/payroll/runs/")) {
                String id = path.substring("/api/payroll/runs/".length());
                if (id.isEmpty() || id.contains("/")) {
                    sendJson(exchange, 404, "{\"error\":\"Payroll run not found\"}");
                    return;
                }
                PayrollRun run = payrollStoreFor(exchange).findById(id)
                    .orElseThrow(() -> new java.util.NoSuchElementException("Payroll run not found."));
                sendJson(exchange, 200, "{\"run\":" + runToJson(run, true) + "}");
                return;
            }
            sendJson(exchange, 405, "{\"error\":\"Method not allowed\"}");
        } catch (RequestException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, ex.statusCode, "{\"error\":\"" + escapeJson(ex.getMessage()) + "\"}");
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"" + escapeJson(ex.getMessage()) + "\"}");
        } catch (NoSuchElementException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 404, "{\"error\":\"" + escapeJson(ex.getMessage()) + "\"}");
        } catch (IllegalStateException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 409, "{\"error\":\"" + escapeJson(ex.getMessage()) + "\"}");
        } catch (FirestoreException ex) {
            sendApiError(exchange, ex);
        }
    }

    private PayrollStore payrollStoreFor(HttpExchange exchange) {
        if (firebaseProjectId.isEmpty()) {
            if (localPayrollStore == null) localPayrollStore = new InMemoryPayrollStore();
            return localPayrollStore;
        }
        return new FirestorePayrollStore(firestoreClientFor(exchange));
    }

    private static int parseIntYear(String value) {
        if (value == null || value.trim().isEmpty()) return 2026;
        try {
            return Integer.parseInt(value.trim());
        } catch (NumberFormatException ex) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Year must be a number.");
        }
    }

    private static int periodYear(PayrollService.Input input) {
        String date = input.periodStart == null ? "" : input.periodStart.trim();
        if (date.length() < 4) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Period start must be YYYY-MM-DD.");
        return Integer.parseInt(date.substring(0, 4));
    }

    private static String runId(PayrollService.Input input) {
        String suffix = java.util.UUID.randomUUID().toString().replace("-", "")
            .substring(0, 8).toUpperCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT);
        return "PR-" + input.periodStart.replace("-", "") + "-" + suffix;
    }

    private static PayrollService.Input payrollInputFrom(JsonObject body) {
        java.util.Set<String> allowed = new java.util.HashSet<>(java.util.Arrays.asList(
            "employeeId", "employeeName", "position", "department", "payPeriod", "periodStart", "periodEnd",
            "monthlyBasic", "daysWorked", "overtimeHours", "overtimeRatePercent", "nightDifferentialHours",
            "nightDifferentialRatePercent", "riceSubsidy", "phoneAllowance", "clothingAllowance",
            "taxableAllowance", "otherDeductions", "taxBasis", "statutoryBasis"));
        for (String key : body.keySet()) {
            if (!allowed.contains(key)) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Unexpected request field: " + key);
        }
        PayrollService.Input input = new PayrollService.Input();
        input.employeeId = requiredString(body, "employeeId");
        input.employeeName = optionalString(body, "employeeName");
        input.position = optionalString(body, "position");
        input.department = optionalString(body, "department");
        input.payPeriod = optionalString(body, "payPeriod").isEmpty() ? "MONTHLY" : optionalString(body, "payPeriod");
        input.periodStart = requiredString(body, "periodStart");
        input.periodEnd = requiredString(body, "periodEnd");
        input.monthlyBasic = numberOr(body, "monthlyBasic", null);
        input.daysWorked = numberOr(body, "daysWorked", null);
        input.overtimeHours = numberOr(body, "overtimeHours", java.math.BigDecimal.ZERO);
        input.overtimeRatePercent = numberOr(body, "overtimeRatePercent", new java.math.BigDecimal("125"));
        input.nightDifferentialHours = numberOr(body, "nightDifferentialHours", java.math.BigDecimal.ZERO);
        input.nightDifferentialRatePercent = numberOr(body, "nightDifferentialRatePercent", new java.math.BigDecimal("10"));
        input.riceSubsidy = numberOr(body, "riceSubsidy", Money.ZERO);
        input.phoneAllowance = numberOr(body, "phoneAllowance", Money.ZERO);
        input.clothingAllowance = numberOr(body, "clothingAllowance", Money.ZERO);
        input.taxableAllowance = numberOr(body, "taxableAllowance", Money.ZERO);
        input.otherDeductions = numberOr(body, "otherDeductions", Money.ZERO);
        if (!optionalString(body, "taxBasis").isEmpty()) input.taxBasis = optionalString(body, "taxBasis");
        if (!optionalString(body, "statutoryBasis").isEmpty()) input.statutoryBasis = optionalString(body, "statutoryBasis");
        return input;
    }

    /** Accepts a JSON number or a decimal string so the UI never has to guess a format. */
    private static java.math.BigDecimal numberOr(JsonObject body, String field, java.math.BigDecimal fallback) {
        JsonElement value = body.get(field);
        if (value == null || value.isJsonNull()) return fallback;
