Attendance and timesheets ### 7.1 `AttendanceRecord` ``` FIELDS attendanceId, scheduleId, date, timeIn, breakOut?, breakIn?, timeOut, dayType, hoursWorked hasBreak() → breakOut and breakIn are both present ``` `hoursWorked` is **stored**, not computed on read — the raw timecard already contains the column and the app does not silently redefine it. `WorkedTime` is used when a value must be derived (tests, and any future capture path). ### 7.2 `AttendanceService` — reading raw rows ``` FUNCTION findForEmployee(employeeId, from, to): IF employee unknown: fail 404 "employee not found" IF from > to: fail 400 "from date must be on or before to date" scheduleId ← scheduleStore.findScheduleIdForEmployee(employeeId) IF no mapping: → [] # unmapped, not an error → attendanceStore.findByScheduleId(n) .filter(date ≥ from) # both bounds inclusive .filter(date ≤ to) FUNCTION summarizeRawRecords(from, to): # used by the coverage report FOR each employee in listEmployees(): schedule ← mapping or null IF null: summary(employee, schedule=null, count=0, "", "") # "unmapped" is explicit ELSE: matched ← all records for that schedule within [from, to] summary(employee, schedule, matched.size, min(date), max(date)) → summaries sorted by employeeId # Describes coverage. Never classifies absence, never derives pay hours. ``` ### 7.3 `TimesheetService` — the bridge to payroll ``` FUNCTION summarise(employeeId, from, to): IF from or to missing: fail 400 "A timesheet period needs both a start and an end date." records ← attendanceService.findForEmployee(employeeId, from, to) byDate ← {} ; total ← 0 FOR each record: hours ← record.hoursWorked IF hours ≤ 0: CONTINUE # weekend/holiday zero rows never inflate days worked byDate[date] += hours # duplicate rows on one date merge into one day total += hours days ← byDate sorted by date → Summary { employeeId, from, to, daysWorked = days.size, totalHours = round(total), days } ``` **The counting rule that matters:** a day counts when it has a **positive** hour total. The supplied December timecard has 22 rows but only **19** working days — 12-08, 12-25 and 12-30 are zero-hour rows, correctly excluded. That is exactly why the golden case can say "19 day(s), 152.00 paid hours". ### 7.4 Attendance HTTP handlers ``` handleAttendance(exchange): GET: employeeId ← query param, required → 400 "employeeId is required" from, to ← optional ISO dates → 400 on malformed or reversed items ← attendanceService.findForEmployee(...) → 404 when the employee is unknown → { items: [attendanceRecordToJson…], count, hoursCalculated: false } # hoursCalculated:false is a promise: nothing here turned punches into pay. POST → 405 # there is no attendance capture or correction in this product other → 405 handleAttendanceReport(exchange): GET only from, to ← optional; reversed → 400 summaries ← attendanceService.summarizeRawRecords(from, to) → { employees:[{employeeId, employeeName, scheduleId, mapped, rawRecordCount, firstRecordDate, lastRecordDate}…], totalRecords, from, to } ``` `attendanceRecordToJson` emits every stored field, including `breakOut`, `breakIn` and `hoursWorked`, so the UI can show the raw row without guessing. --- ## 8. Workflow (leave requests and tickets) **Scope, stated plainly:** these are validated request records with a queue label and a cancel action. There is no reviewer, no approval, no notification, no balance, and no payroll effect. ### 8.1 `WorkflowService` ``` LEAVE_TYPES = [Vacation, Medical, Personal, Unpaid] TICKET_QUEUES = { "Overtime request": Team Lead, "Leave request": Team Lead, "Timesheet correction": Team Lead, "Payroll inquiry": Payroll Staff, "HR inquiry": HR, "Technical support": IT Admin } MAX_TEXT_LENGTH = 240 listLeaveRequests() / listTickets() → store lists (newest first) FUNCTION createLeaveRequest(employeeId, leaveType, startDate, endDate, note): employee ← requireEmployee(employeeId) # must exist in this sandbox → 404 otherwise IF leaveType not in LEAVE_TYPES: fail 400 "Choose a valid leave type." start ← parseDate(startDate); Payroll — the core This is the part that was missing before 2026-11-05 and is now the most tested part of the system. ### 9.1 `PayrollService.Input` — everything a computation may depend on ``` employeeId, employeeName, position, department # §9.3 — all of it, before any arithmetic period ← Period.parse(input.payPeriod) taxBasis ← parseTaxBasis(input.taxBasis) statutoryBasis ← parseStatutoryBasis(input.statutoryBasis) ── 1. rates ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── monthlyBasic ← round(input.monthlyBasic) dailyRate ← round(monthlyBasic / 20, 2) # Correct the inputs…" # Explicitly refused rather than stored as a negative payslip. ── 7. employer side (cost, never deducted from the employee) ──────────── employerSss ← perPeriod(ruleset.sssEmployer(monthlyBasic), divisor) employerEc ← perPeriod(ruleset.sssEc(monthlyBasic), divisor) employerPhilHealth ← perPeriod(ruleset.philHealthEmployer(monthlyBasic), divisor) employerPagibig ← perPeriod(ruleset.pagibigEmployer(monthlyBasic), divisor) employerCost ← round(grossIncome + totalBenefits + the four employer amounts above) → Payslip { identity, period, rulesetId, rates, days, premiums, benefits, employee deductions, employer shares, taxableMonthly, takeHomePay } ``` Two conventions are deliberately exposed as **assumption switches**, because the supplied payslip cannot settle them on its own: | Switch | Default (matches MotorPH) | Alternative | What changes | |---|---|---|---| | `statutoryBasis` | `FULL_MONTHLY_EACH_PERIOD` — deduct the full monthly SSS/PhilHealth/Pag-IBIG in a semi-monthly cutoff | `SPLIT_EVENLY` — half in each cutoff | SSS 1,750 vs 875; PhilHealth 1,337.50 vs 668.75; Pag-IBIG 200 vs 100 | | `taxBasis` | `BASIC_ONLY` — tax on basic less statutory | `BASIC_PLUS_TAXABLE_ALLOWANCE` | taxable base, therefore withholding | Both are stored on every saved run, so a reprint always says which convention produced it. ### 9.3 `validate(input)` — every rejection, in order ``` null input → "Payroll input is required." employeeId blank → "Employee ID is required." monthlyBasic null / negative → "Monthly basic pay is required." / "…must not be negative." daysWorked null / negative → "Days worked is required." / "…must not be negative." daysWorked > 20 AND MONTHLY → "Days worked cannot exceed 20 in one monthly period." daysWorked > 10 AND SEMI_MONTHLY→ "Days worked cannot exceed 10 in one semi-monthly period." overtimeHours, ndHours, rice, phone, clothing, taxableAllowance, otherDeductions, otRate%, ndRate% negative → "<field> must not be negative." payPeriod unparseable → "Pay period must be Monthly or Semi-monthly." periodStart / periodEnd → must be real YYYY-MM-DD (round-tripped through LocalDate) periodStart > periodEnd → "Period start must be on or before period end." ``` The payload itself was already filtered upstream: unknown JSON fields are rejected by `requireOnlyKeys`, and a non-JSON `Content-Type` never reaches the service. ### 9.4 The golden case, number by number Input: monthly basic **53,500**, semi-monthly, 2026-01-02 → 2026-01-15, **10** days, rice 1,500, phone 2,000, clothing 1,000, defaults for both switches. ``` dailyRate 53,500 / 20 = 2,675.00 hourlyRate 53,500 / 168 = 318.45 basePay 2,675.00 × 10 = 26,750.00 grossIncome = 26,750.00 benefits 1,500 + 2,000 + 1,000 = 4,500.00 MSC ceil(53,500/500)×500 → 54,000, clamp → 35,000 SSS employee 35,000 × 5% = 1,750.00 PhilHealth 53,500 × 5% = 2,675 ÷ 2 = 1,337.50 Pag-IBIG min(53,500, 10,000) × 2% = 200.00 monthlyStatutory = 3,287.50 taxableMonthly 53,500 − 3,287.50 = 50,212.50 withholding 1,875 + (50,212.50 − 33,333.33)×20% = 5,250.83 totalDeductions 1,750 + 1,337.50 + 200 + 5,250.83 = 8,538.33 takeHomePay 26,750 + 4,500 − 8,538.33 = 22,711.67 employer SSS 3,500.00 + EC 30.00 + PhilHealth 1,337.50 + Pag-IBIG 200.00 employerCost 31,250.00 + 5,067.50 = 36,317.50 ``` Every one of those thirteen figures is asserted in `PayrollGoldenTest` (61 checks) and re-asserted over HTTP in `AppServerIntegrationTest`, then again in a real browser by the e2e suite. ### 9.5 `remittanceRows(payslips)` — what the employer must remit ``` FOR each payslip: sss += sssEmployee + sssEmployer ec += sssEc ph += philHealthEmployee + philHealthEmployer pi += pagibigEmployee + pagibigEmployer tax += withholdingTax → [ ("Social Security System", …), ("Employees' Compensation", …), ("PhilHealth", …), ("Pag-IBIG", …), ("BIR withholding", …) ] ``` ### 9.6 `Payslip` and `PayslipJson` `Payslip` is an immutable value object built through a builder with seven groups: `employee`, `period`, `ruleset`, `salary`, `premiums`, `benefits`, `deductions`, `employer`, `result` — 33 accessors, no logic. `PayslipJson` is the *only* serializer/deserializer for it: ``` toJson(slip): 33 fields; money → 2-decimal strings; hours/days → plain decimal strings fromJson(node): reverse; missing numeric field → 0.00 (a truncated snapshot reads as zero, never as a crash) ; missing text field → "" ``` Round-trip equality is tested in `FirestorePayrollStoreTest`, which is what makes "a reprint is a read, not a recalculation" a verified claim rather than a comment. ### 9.7 `PayrollRun` — the immutable snapshot ``` FIELDS id ("PR-YYYYMMDD-XXXXXXXX"), payPeriod, periodStart, periodEnd, rulesetId, taxBasis, statutoryBasis, createdAt, payslips[] ``` The run stores the **inputs' meaning** (`rulesetId`, `taxBasis`, `statutoryBasis`) and the **outputs** (every payslip line). Nothing about it can be recomputed differently later: the statutory tables can change next year and last year's payslip still prints what was paid. ### 9.8 Payroll HTTP handlers, in order ``` handlePayroll(exchange): GET /api/payroll/rules?year=YYYY year ← query param; blank → 2026; non-numeric → 400 ruleset ← PayrollRuleset.forYear(year) # uncovered year → 400, never a guess → rulesetToJson(ruleset) { id, currency:"PHP", effectiveFrom, effectiveTo, daysPerMonth:"20", hoursPerMonth:"168", sss:{employeeRate, employerRate, minMsc, maxMsc, mscStep, ecLow, ecHigh, ecThreshold, mpfThreshold}, philHealth:{rate, floor, ceiling}, pagibig:{maxFund, lowThreshold, employeeLowRate, employeeHighRate, employerRate}, monthlyTaxBrackets:[…], semiMonthlyTaxBrackets:[…] } GET /api/payroll/timesheet?employeeId=&from=&to= employeeId required → 400 from/to parsed; TimesheetService.summarise → Summary → { employeeId, from, to, daysWorked, totalHours, days:[{date, dayType, hours}…] } POST /api/payroll/preview input ← payrollInputFrom(readJsonBody) # §9.9 ruleset ← forYear(year of periodStart) slip ← new PayrollService().compute(input, ruleset) → 200 { payslip, saved:false, ruleset } # nothing written POST /api/payroll/runs identical computation, then: run ← payrollStoreFor(exchange).create({ id: "PR-" + periodStart without dashes + "-" + 8 random hex, payPeriod, periodStart, periodEnd, rulesetId, taxBasis, statutoryBasis, createdAt: now, payslips: [slip] }) → 201 { run (with payslips), saved:true } # 409 if that id already exists GET /api/payroll/runs runs ← store.findAll() # sorted newest first → { items:[ runToJson(run, includePayslips=false)… ], count } # history stays a summary: no payslip bodies in the list GET /api/payroll/runs/{id} reject empty id or an id containing "/" → 404 run ← store.findById(id) or 404 → { run } # with payslips DELETE /api/payroll/runs/{id} → 405 # immutable by design anything else → 405 FUNCTION runToJson(run, includePayslips): id, payPeriod, periodStart, periodEnd, rulesetId, taxBasis, statutoryBasis, createdAt employeeCount ← payslips.size totalGross ← Σ grossIncome # payroll gross only totalBenefits ← Σ totalBenefits totalEarnings ← totalGross + totalBenefits # what a payslip prints as total earnings totalDeductions, totalNet, totalEmployerCost ← Σ of each IF includePayslips: payslips:[PayslipJson…] ``` `totalGross`, `totalBenefits` and `totalEarnings` are three separate numbers on purpose: an earlier version folded benefits into "gross" and reported 31,250 where the payslip said 26,750. ### 9.9 `payrollInputFrom(body)` — the request contract ``` requireOnlyKeys(body, [employeeId, employeeName, position, department, payPeriod, periodStart, periodEnd, monthlyBasic, daysWorked, overtimeHours, overtimeRatePercent, nightDifferentialHours, nightDifferentialRatePercent, riceSubsidy, phoneAllowance, clothingAllowance, taxableAllowance, otherDeductions, taxBasis, statutoryBasis]) # A field like "bonus" is a 400. Typos cannot be silently ignored. employeeId, periodStart, periodEnd required strings payPeriod default "MONTHLY" money and hours fields accept a JSON number or a decimal string, default 0 overtimeRatePercent default 125 ; nightDifferentialRatePercent default 10 taxBasis / statutoryBasis default BASIC_ONLY / FULL_MONTHLY_EACH_PERIOD ``` ### 9.10 Saved-run lifecycle ``` 1. UI computes a preview POST /preview → figures shown, nothing stored 2. Operator reviews payslip + remittance + rate table on screen 3. Operator saves POST /runs → 201, run id PR-20260102-77BC9231 4. History lists summaries GET /runs → totals per run, newest first 5. Anyone reprints GET /runs/{id} → stored payslip lines, no recomputation 6. Nobody can alter or delete DELETE → 405; Firestore rules allow create+read only ``` --- ## 10. Demo seeding `POST /api/demo/seed` — the only way fixture data ever reaches a real Firestore project. ``` FUNCTION seedMissingSyntheticRecords(client): employeesCreated ← 0 FOR each employee in a FRESH InMemoryEmployeeStore: IF createDocument("users/{uid}/demoEmployees", id, employeeFields): employeesCreated++ # existing documents are left untouched mappingsCreated ← 0 FOR each employee with a fixture schedule mapping: IF createDocument("users/{uid}/demoEmployeeSchedules", id, {employeeId, scheduleId}): mappingsCreated++ attendanceCreated ← 0 FOR scheduleId in [101, 102, 103, 104]: FOR each fixture row on that schedule: IF createDocument("users/{uid}/demoAttendance", attendanceId, fields): attendanceCreated++ → { employeesCreated, scheduleMappingsCreated, attendanceCreated } ``` Properties worth knowing: - **Idempotent.** A second call reports `0, 0, 0` because `createDocument` refuses to overwrite. - **Additive.** It never updates or deletes anything already in the sandbox. - **Synthetic only.** The fixtures are the fictional MotorPH training set; pay profiles are marked as demo values. It is the only writer that can create attendance rows — there is no capture form. - **Owner-scoped.** `client.userCollection(...)` puts everything under the caller's `uid`. --- ## 11. The browser `web/index.html` is one page with eight views toggled by `switchView()`; `web/app.js` holds all the wiring. Fifteen small modules hold the pure logic so it can be unit-tested in Node with no browser. ### 11.1 Module map | Module | Functions | What they do | |---|---|---| | `app.js` | 66 | All DOM wiring, fetch calls, rendering, auth screens | | `payroll.js` | 8 | Payslip layout, CSV columns, run summaries, formatting | | `workflow-demo.js` | 10 | Client-side leave/ticket state machine (used with fixtures) | | `attendance-calendar.js` | 3 | Month grid from raw rows | | `leave-calendar.js` | 3 | Month grid + date validation | | `csv-export.js` | 3 | RFC-4180-safe CSV construction | | `attendance-coverage-*.js`, `attendance-record-sort.js` | 3 | Filter and sort raw coverage rows | | `directory-sort.js`, `directory-summary.js` | 2 | Employee sorting, label totals | | `workflow-filter.js`, `workflow-sort.js`, `workflow-summary.js` | 3 | Request/ticket filtering, sorting, summary | | `employee-record-summary*.js` | 2 | One employee's cross-record summary | | `sandbox-search.js` | 2 | Search across employees and requests | | `workspace-export.js` | 1 | Whole-sandbox JSON export | ### 11.2 Auth (`app.js`) ``` FUNCTION apiHeaders(): # every fetch goes through this user ← firebaseAuth.currentUser IF user: → { "Content-Type":"application/json", "Authorization":"Bearer " + await user.getIdToken(), "X-Firebase-UID": user.uid } ELSE: → { "Content-Type":"application/json" } # the API answers 401 FUNCTION signIn(email, password) → setPersistence(NONE) → signInWithEmailAndPassword FUNCTION createDevAccount(email, pw) → createUserWithEmailAndPassword FUNCTION sendPasswordReset(email) → sendPasswordResetEmail FUNCTION showWorkspace() / showSignIn() → swap the two top-level screens FUNCTION friendlyAuthError(code) → plain-English message per Firebase error code ``` Persistence is `in-memory`: closing the tab signs you out. private static String itemToJson(JsonObject item, String storage) {
        JsonObject response = new JsonObject();
        response.add("item", item);
        response.addProperty("storage", storage);
        return response.toString();
    }
    private static String workflowsToJson(List<DemoLeaveRequest> leaveRequests, List<DemoTicket> tickets, String storage) {
        JsonObject response = new JsonObject();
        JsonArray leaves = new JsonArray();
        for (DemoLeaveRequest request : leaveRequests) leaves.add(leaveToJson(request));
        JsonArray ticketItems = new JsonArray();
        for (DemoTicket ticket : tickets) ticketItems.add(ticketToJson(ticket));
        response.add("leaveRequests", leaves);
        response.add("tickets", ticketItems);
        response.addProperty("storage", storage);
        return response.toString();
    }
    private static String attendanceSummaryToJson(List<RawAttendanceSummary> summaries, LocalDate from, LocalDate to) {
        StringBuilder json = new StringBuilder("{\"items\":[");
        for (int i = 0; i < summaries.size(); i++) {
            RawAttendanceSummary summary = summaries.get(i);
            if (i > 0) json.append(',');
            json.append("{\"employeeId\":\"").append(escapeJson(summary.getEmployeeId()))
                .append("\",\"employeeName\":\"").append(escapeJson(summary.getEmployeeName()))
                .append("\",\"scheduleId\":").append(summary.getScheduleId() == null ? "null" : summary.getScheduleId())
                .append(",\"hasScheduleMapping\":").append(summary.hasScheduleMapping())
                .append(",\"rawRecordCount\":").append(summary.getRawRecordCount())
                .append(",\"firstRecordDate\":\"").append(escapeJson(summary.getFirstRecordDate()))
                .append("\",\"lastRecordDate\":\"").append(escapeJson(summary.getLastRecordDate())).append("\"}");
        }
        json.append("],\"count\":").append(summaries.size())
            .append(",\"from\":").append(from == null ? "null" : "\"" + from + "\"")
            .append(",\"to\":").append(to == null ? "null" : "\"" + to + "\"")
            .append(",\"hoursCalculated\":false}");
        return json.toString();
    }
    private static String employeesToJson(List<Employee> employees, int total) {
        StringBuilder json = new StringBuilder("{\"items\":[");
        for (int i = 0; i < employees.size(); i++) {
            if (i > 0) json.append(',');
            json.append(employeeToJson(employees.get(i)));
        }
        return json.append("],\"total\":").append(total)
            .append(",\"matched\":").append(employees.size()).append('}').toString();
    }
    private static String queryParameter(String rawQuery, String target) {
        if (rawQuery == null || rawQuery.isEmpty()) return "";
        for (String part : rawQuery.split("&")) {
            int separator = part.indexOf('=');
            String key = separator < 0 ? part : part.substring(0, separator);
            if (target.equals(decode(key))) return separator < 0 ? "" : decode(part.substring(separator + 1));
        }
        return "";
    }
    private static String decode(String value) {
        try {
            return URLDecoder.decode(value, "UTF-8");
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException | java.io.UnsupportedEncodingException ex) {
            return "";
        }
    }
    private static String contentTypeFor(Path path) {
        String name = path.getFileName().toString().toLowerCase();
        if (name.endsWith(".html")) return "text/html; charset=utf-8";
        if (name.endsWith(".css")) return "text/css; charset=utf-8";
        if (name.endsWith(".js")) return "application/javascript; charset=utf-8";
        if (name.endsWith(".svg")) return "image/svg+xml";
        return "application/octet-stream";
    }

private static void sendText(HttpExchange exchange, int status, String type, String body) throws IOException {
        byte[] bytes = body.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);

        exchange.getResponseHeaders().set("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff");

    private static String employeesToJson(List<Employee> employees, int total) {
        StringBuilder json = new StringBuilder("{\"items\":[");
        for (int i = 0; i < employees.size(); i++) {
            if (i > 0) json.append(',');
            json.append(employeeToJson(employees.get(i)));
        }
        return json.append("],\"total\":").append(total)
            .append(",\"matched\":").append(employees.size()).append('}').toString();
    }

Let me also check the 13th-month tax premise: "It only matters above ₱90,000 basic." That's a claim from Claude's side perhaps. Under Philippine law, 13th month pay is exempt up to ₱90,000 (combined with other benefits). So "only matters above ₱90,000" — meaning the 13th month itself only becomes taxable above 90k. But if the site's 13th month assumption is about including it in the tax base... Let me think about this claim carefully. 13th month pay ≤ ₱90,000 is exempt from income tax (RA 10963/TRAIN). So the excess over 90,000 is taxable. Claude says "It only matters above ₱90,000 basic" — the threshold is on the 13th month amount itself, not the basic. Actually the ₱90,000 exemption applies to 13th month pay and other benefits. 13th month = basic/12, so basic would need to be > ₱1,080,000 for the 13th month alone to exceed ₱90,000. Saying "above ₱90,000 basic" is imprecise — it's the benefit amount, not the basic salary. Worth flagging.

[NODE 9072]

[NODE 9073]
Important nuance for OT: OT is beyond 8 hours in a day, not "after 17:00" per se. But operationally, for a shift 08:00–17:00 with a 1-hour unpaid break, 8 hours are done at 17:00, so both coincide. The rule should be "beyond the scheduled/regular 8 hours", computed from punches, not from a clock time. If someone starts at 07:00, they finish 8 hours at 16:00 — work from 16:00–17:00 is already OT. So "after 17:00" is wrong as a general rule; it's right only for the standard 08:00–17:00 shift.

[NODE 9074]
And "should log-in before 08:00 earn extra?" — Under the Labor Code, no; arriving early isn't automatically paid. It's only paid if the contract/policy says so or if work was authorized/required. Also DOLE: work before the scheduled start is not "overtime" (overtime = beyond normal hours worked in a day). If the employee actually works 07:00–17:00 with a 1-hour break = 9 hours... hmm, then under the punch-based rule they'd have 9 hours worked, and OT would be the 9th hour. But if they just arrive early and wait, they're not working. The punch record can't distinguish. Practical answer: don't pay "early arrival" as OT automatically; require an approved OT request (which the product doesn't have yet) and base OT on hours beyond 8 worked in the day.

[NODE 9075]
13th month tax: The ₱90,000 threshold — law says 13th month pay and other benefits are exempt up to ₱90,000 per year (RA 10963/TRAIN). Above that, the excess is taxable as part of the annual taxable income. Important: it's not a separate flat rate; the excess is added to taxable income and taxed by the annual brackets. The site's assumption of "only matters above ₱90,000 basic" is imprecise — the threshold applies to 13th month + other benefits (not basic pay), and the excess is taxed at the marginal brackets, typically in December true-up or annualized. Since our app doesn't compute 13th month at all, the answer is: not applicable yet; and when implemented, treat it as an annual income item subject to the ₱90,000 exemption, not a per-period line. Also annualization: the correct approach is annualized tax computation (total annual taxable income incl. 13th month minus 90k exempt) rather than "tax 13th month separately".

[NODE 9076]
Also worth noting: withholding tax on regular pay is computed per period using the annualized table; a year-end annualization adjusts. Our engine computes the monthly Annex E table each run without annualization — that's consistent with MotorPH's payslip (5,250.83) but is a simplification worth flagging: if 13th month or variable pay is added, you must annualize, otherwise the tax will be wrong.

[NODE 9192]
Two separate questions, and the first one matters more than the rate.

[NODE 9193]
What counts. Overtime is work beyond 8 hours in a workday (Labor Code Art. 87), not "any time
after 17:00". A 10:00–19:00 shift with an hour's meal performs 8 hours and earns no overtime; a
06:00–15:00 shift earns none either. The test is productive hours in the day, not the clock.

[NODE 9194]
Rates (DOLE matrix — the premium applies on top of the day's own rate):

[NODE 9195]
Night differential (+10%, Art. 86) applies to hours between 22:00 and 06:00 and stacks on top of
whichever rate already applies — it is 10% of the applicable rate, not of plain basic.

[NODE 9196]
What the code does today: overtime hours are an operator-entered field multiplied by
hourlyRate × rate% with the rate defaulting to 125%. That part is correct for an ordinary day. Two
gaps:

Answers are in docs/statutory-and-policy-questions.md (open in your viewer). Short version — and one correction to the framing first: four of the eight premises don't describe this codebase, so I checked each against the source before answering.

[NODE 9233]
docs/statutory-and-policy-questions.md

[NODE 9234]
1. ₱150/₱160/₱200 hourly rates — premise doesn't apply. No flat rate table exists here. Hourly rate is derived: monthlyBasic ÷ 168. That divisor reproduces every row of MotorPH's own employee file (₱90,000 → ₱535.71; ₱60,000 → ₱357.14). Their lowest rate is ₱313.51. Don't add flat rates — at ₱150/h the golden case would pay 22,800 instead of 26,750, a ₱3,950 error.

[NODE 9235]
monthlyBasic ÷ 168

[NODE 9236]
2. Leave credits 5/5/3 — premise doesn't apply. No balances exist; the UI says "no days or balances are calculated." Fine as labelled demo policy, but keep it out of payroll — a balance only becomes money through the leave-pay rule, which is undecided.

[NODE 9237]
3. 13th-month ₱90,000 — premise doesn't apply (no 13th month is computed). The figure is right, but it's a threshold on the benefit, and it's annual/cumulative — undecidable inside a semi-monthly run.

[NODE 9238]
4. Pag-IBIG at exactly ₱1,500 — already follows the circular (1%). Code: fund ≤ 1,500 → 1%, pinned by a test ("Pag-IBIG 1% at 1,500 = 15.00"). HDMF Circular 460 says "at or below ₱1,500" → 1%. If the site says 2%, the site is the outlier. No change needed.

[NODE 9239]
fund ≤ 1,500 → 1%

[NODE 9240]
5. Overtime — beyond 8 productive hours, not "after 17:00". A 10:00–19:00 shift with a meal is 8 hours, no OT. Rates: 125% ordinary day, 169% rest/special day, 195%, 260% regular holiday, 338% holiday+rest day; night diff +10% for 22:00–06:00, stacked. Our engine has only the 125% multiplier, and nothing stops double pay (days worked and OT hours are independent inputs).

[NODE 9241]
6. Paid leave — a paid day, not paid hours. Counts toward pay, never toward hours worked (so it can't generate OT). Not implementable yet: leave approval doesn't exist, so "approved leave" isn't a state the data can hold.

[NODE 9242]
7. Early login — the premise is backwards: it already earns extra time, and that's a defect. I ran our own WorkedTime: in 07:00 / break 12–13 / out 17:00 → 9.00 h; 07:00 with no break punches → 10.00 h. So early arrival pays straight time at 100% while manual evening OT pays 125%. Recommended rule: paid = min(worked, scheduled), unapproved overage shown separately. This is the only real bug in the eight.

[NODE 9243]
WorkedTime

[NODE 9244]
paid = min(worked, scheduled)

[NODE 9245]
8. Self-approval — never. Enforce on the server by identity, not role, plus the Firestore rule. Blocked in practice because every collection lives under users/{uid} today, so the only available approver is the owner — which is why approval isn't built.

[NODE 9307]
Idea 1 — The browser never does maths.
Every number on screen came from the server. The browser only prints it.
So if a number is wrong, the bug is on the server. Always.

[NODE 9308]
Idea 2 — The server never says "yes" to the database.
The server passes your login token to Firebase, and Firebase's rules decide what you can see.
Your uid comes from your token — you cannot ask for someone else's data even by editing the request.

[NODE 9309]
uid

[NODE 9310]
Idea 3 — Money is never a float.
Decimals are stored as text ("26750.00") and calculated exactly. Rounding happens in exactly one
place: Money.round() — 2 decimals, round half up. That's how the centavos match.

[NODE 9318]
Why "frozen" matters: tax tables change. If 2027's tables change, last year's payslip must still
print what was actually paid. That's why saved runs can't be edited or deleted.

[NODE 9319]
Inputs: monthly salary, days worked, allowances, overtime hours, night-diff hours.

[NODE 9320]
The 6 formulas:

[NODE 9321]
text
daily rate    = monthly salary ÷ 20
hourly rate   = monthly salary ÷ 168
gross         = daily rate × days worked   (+ overtime + night diff)
SSS           = 5% of salary, capped between ₱5,000 and ₱35,000
PhilHealth    = 5% of salary, split in half
Pag-IBIG      = 2% of salary, capped at ₱10,000
tax           = BIR table, applied to (salary − the three contributions above)
take home     = gross + allowances − (SSS + PhilHealth + Pag-IBIG + tax)

B. Magic numbers — answer: MotorPH's own file proves ÷20 and ÷168 (both columns exist: Basic Salary → Hourly Rate = /168). The 20 is MotorPH policy (5-day week × 4 weeks), not law. Law (DOLE) says daily rate = monthly × 12 / 261 for a 5-day workweek. So there are two valid conventions; ours reproduces MotorPH's payslip, which is the acceptance criterion. Make it configurable with the divisor as policy input, not hardcoded.

[NODE 9393]
Actually — is ÷168 = ÷(20×8) consistent? Yes: 20 days × 8 hours. And 261 = 261 working days/year; 261/12 = 21.75 days/month; ×8 = 174 hours/month. So DOLE convention would be ÷21.75 and ÷174. MotorPH uses ÷20 and ÷168 (their own table). This is a real finding worth presenting as a table.

[NODE 9394]

[NODE 9395]

Propose: server is authoritative; if API down, UI shows cached last-known payslip read-only and blocks save. That's the honest engineering answer, and it matches their "no local-only features" constraint.

## 3. Can we use this directly in your payroll application?

Yes, technically.

There are three relevant ways to call it:

| Method | Feasibility |
|---|---|
| Python backend → Sweldong Pinoy | Yes, subject to session and server restrictions |
| PHP backend → Sweldong Pinoy | Yes, same HTTP form submission |
| Browser frontend → Sweldong Pinoy | Potential CORS restrictions |

I'd favour a backend request rather than calling it directly from JavaScript.

One caveat: this is an **undocumented internal endpoint**, not an officially supported API. There are no guarantees regarding availability, rate limits, backwards compatibility, or permission for automated commercial use.

Also, the cURL contains a live-looking `JSESSIONID`. Treat that as a session credential, and clear the site's cookies before continuing to use your browser session.

## 4. What we should investigate next

The most useful discovery now is whether the endpoint accepts different combinations of parameters without requiring a browser session.

I'd test the following:

| Test | Purpose |
|---|---|
| POST without cookies | Determine whether session cookies are mandatory |
| POST with a fresh session | Determine whether visiting the homepage is sufficient |
| Private Employee | Inspect SSS computation |
| Government Employee | Inspect GSIS computation |
| Different salary brackets | Identify contribution bracket boundaries |
| Semi-monthly and daily | Identify payroll-period adjustments |
| Taxable and non-taxable allowances | Identify their treatment |
| Overtime and night differential | Identify supplementary compensation rules |

**One particularly interesting detail:** Both `result` and `altresult` appeared in your response, and they were identical. I'd investigate whether `altresult` is simply a legacy response field or represents an alternative computation that only differs under certain conditions.

At this point, we have enough information to build a working API client around the endpoint. The remaining uncertainty is its session requirements and whether the returned calculations remain consistent across different employee types and payroll periods.

## [20] CHATGPT (gpt-6-t-mini)

## 1. What actually matters in this request

Your cURL reveals the following:

| Component | Finding |
|---|---|
| Endpoint | `POST https://www.sweldongpinoy.com/` |
| Content type | `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` |
| Authentication | No explicit API key or bearer token |
| Session | `JSESSIONID` cookie |
| Request body | 12 form parameters |
| Response | JSON |
| CSRF token | None visible in the captured request |

The `JSESSIONID` is important. It is a server-side session identifier, so we should test whether the server requires it or automatically creates a new session when the homepage is accessed.

Most of the other headers are browser-generated and probably unnecessary:

- `sec-ch-ua`
- `sec-fetch-*`
- `sec-ch-ua-platform`
- `sec-ch-ua-mobile`
- `priority`
- `dnt`
- `sec-gpc`
- `accept-language`

I would retain `Origin`, `Referer`, and `User-Agent` initially, then remove unnecessary headers during testing.

## 2. Python implementation matching your request

Rather than hardcoding your browser's session cookie, the following creates a fresh session by visiting the homepage first.

<CodeBlock language="python" editable>
import requests
from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation

URL = "https://www.sweldongpinoy.com/"

PAYLOAD = {
    "employment_type": "Private Employee",
    "pay_period": "Monthly",
    "payroll_period_daily_days": "20",
    "basic_pay": "10,000.00",
    "taxable_allowance": "1,000.00",
    "nontaxable_allowance": "0.00",
    "night_differential_hours": "",
    "night_differential_rate": "",
    "overtime_hours": "",
    "overtime_rate": "",
    "work_schedule": "5"
}

HEADERS = {
    "Accept": "*/*",
    "Origin": "https://www.sweldongpinoy.com",
    "Referer": URL,
    "User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0"
}

def money(value):
    try:
        return Decimal(str(value or "0"))
    except InvalidOperation:
        return Decimal("0")

def main():
    with requests.Session() as session:
        session.headers.update(HEADERS)

        page = session.get(URL, timeout=30)
        page.raise_for_status()

        response = session.post(
            URL,
            data=PAYLOAD,
            timeout=30
        )

[NODE 9898]
The checkbox (§6) is a verification aid, never the calculation. If the network is down, the app
still pays everyone correctly — which is the whole point of not outsourcing the maths.

[NODE 9899]
"Wouldn't local be better?" Local calculation is exactly what we do; the maths runs on the
server the app already owns, with no external call in the path. What we must never do is calculate in
the browser: the client would then own money logic, and any user could edit it.

[NODE 10124]
Your spec has Supervisor "handle timesheet edits" and Payroll "process payroll". If both can edit the
inputs a payslip is computed from, you need to decide which one wins and keep an audit trail of
every change. Otherwise two people can produce two different payslips for the same period and neither
is provably the one that was paid.

[NODE 10125]
The current design sidesteps this by making attendance read-only and payroll runs immutable. Keep that
property when you add editing: never mutate an attendance row in place — append a correction with an
approver and a timestamp, and let the run snapshot record which corrections it included.

## 1. "What if the work month isn't 20 work days?" — the divisor

Date: 2026-11-06 · Answers to "what if the month isn't 20 days?", "168 is a magic number",

[NODE 10129]
It already can be. MotorPH's own file has a Gross Semi-monthly Rate column, and the daily rate is
defined as monthly ÷ 2 ÷ semi-monthly gross ÷ … — formally:

[NODE 10130]
Gross Semi-monthly Rate

[NODE 10131]
monthly ÷ 2 ÷ semi-monthly gross ÷ …

[NODE 10132]
text
daily rate = (monthly basic × 12) ÷ (work days per year)

[NODE 10133]
daily rate = (monthly basic × 12) ÷ (work days per year)

[NODE 10134]
daily rate = (monthly basic × 12) ÷ (work days per year)

[NODE 10135]
which, for MotorPH's stated 5-day week (261 working days a year, 313 in a 6-day week), gives 20 days a
month = 240 days a year. The 20 is not a guess: it is 240 ÷ 12, and it reproduces every row of the
employee file (₱24,000 → ₱1,200.00; ₱41,850 → ₱2,092.50; ₱53,500 → ₱2,675.00).

[NODE 10136]
20

[NODE 10137]
240 ÷ 12

[NODE 10138]
What we should add is not a different constant but a per-employee workDaysPerMonth — 20 for the
5-day staff, 26 for a 6-day staff, 22 for a 5.5-day staff — defaulting to 20 so nothing changes for the
34 existing employees. Then:

[NODE 10139]
workDaysPerMonth

[NODE 10140]
text
daily rate  = monthly basic ÷ workDaysPerMonth
hourly rate = daily rate ÷ 8

[NODE 10141]
daily rate  = monthly basic ÷ workDaysPerMonth
hourly rate = daily rate ÷ 8

[NODE 10142]
daily rate  = monthly basic ÷ workDaysPerMonth
hourly rate = daily rate ÷ 8

[NODE 10143]
That single change replaces the ÷20 and ÷168 pair and makes the divisor explicit and defensible.
It is a ruleset/employee-field change, not a maths change: the golden case uses 20, so it keeps
passing unchanged.

[NODE 10144]
÷20

[NODE 10145]
÷168

[NODE 10146]
One caveat that matters more than the divisor: whatever constant you pick, a monthly employee is
paid the same monthly basic whether the month has 18, 20 or 22 working days. The divisor only exists to
price a partial month (days worked, absences, OT hours). Do not let it decide full-month pay.

[NODE 10147]
text
168 = 20 days × 8.4 hours   ← the real definition
    = 240 work days × 8.4 hours ÷ 12

[NODE 10148]
168 = 20 days × 8.4 hours   ← the real definition
    = 240 work days × 8.4 hours ÷ 12

[NODE 10149]
168 = 20 days × 8.4 hours   ← the real definition
    = 240 work days × 8.4 hours ÷ 12

[NODE 10150]
8.4 hours (8h + a 1-hour unpaid meal, prorated to a 5-day week) is the standard Philippine
"8.4-hour working day" used by DOLE. The cleaner presentation:

[NODE 10151]
text
hourly rate = daily rate ÷ 8          ← 8 paid hours per day
daily rate  = monthly ÷ 20
    ⇒ hourly = monthly ÷ 160

[NODE 10152]
hourly rate = daily rate ÷ 8          ← 8 paid hours per day
daily rate  = monthly ÷ 20
    ⇒ hourly = monthly ÷ 160

[NODE 10153]
hourly rate = daily rate ÷ 8          ← 8 paid hours per day
daily rate  = monthly ÷ 20
    ⇒ hourly = monthly ÷ 160

[NODE 10154]
But ÷160 ≠ ÷168: ₱53,500 ÷ 160 = ₱334.38, while MotorPH's file says ₱318.45 (= ÷168). The 8.4
hour divisor includes the meal hour and therefore pays less per hour. That is a real policy choice,
not a rounding detail:

[NODE 10155]
÷160 ≠ ÷168

[NODE 10156]
Recommendation: keep ÷168 because it is what MotorPH's own file and the supplied payslip use, but
stop calling it magic: expose it as hoursPerMonth = workDaysPerMonth × 8.4 in the ruleset, so a
6-day-week employee automatically gets ÷218.4. Anyone reading the code then sees where the number
comes from and can change it once, in one place.

[NODE 10157]
hoursPerMonth = workDaysPerMonth × 8.4

[NODE 10158]

[NODE 10181]
The optimal path: keep the Java service as the only calculator, add the optional comparison checkbox
(§5), and if offline resilience is required later, cache the last computed payslip client-side and
label it "cached — not recalculated". Never a second calculator.

[NODE 10182]
Feasible, with one important design point: the browser must not call their site directly. Reasons:
CORS, the JSESSIONID handshake, and — decisively — you would be sending salary data from the user's
machine to a third party where you cannot log it.

[NODE 10183]
JSESSIONID

[NODE 10184]
The correct shape is a server-side proxy on our own API:

[NODE 10185]
text

  → our API posts the form to sweldongpinoy with a short timeout
  → returns { ours: {...}, theirs: {...}, differences: [...] }
  → if their site is slow or down: { theirs: null, reason: "reference unavailable" }

private PayrollStore payrollStoreFor(HttpExchange exchange) {
        if (firebaseProjectId.isEmpty()) {
            if (localPayrollStore == null) localPayrollStore = new InMemoryPayrollStore();
            return localPayrollStore;
        }
        return new FirestorePayrollStore(firestoreClientFor(exchange));
    }

    private static int parseIntYear(String value) {
        if (value == null || value.trim().isEmpty()) return 2026;
        try {
            return Integer.parseInt(value.trim());
        } catch (NumberFormatException ex) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Year must be a number.");
        }
    }

    private static int periodYear(PayrollService.Input input) {
        String date = input.periodStart == null ? "" : input.periodStart.trim();
        if (date.length() < 4) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Period start must be YYYY-MM-DD.");
        return Integer.parseInt(date.substring(0, 4));
    }

    private static String runId(PayrollService.Input input) {
        String suffix = java.util.UUID.randomUUID().toString().replace("-", "")
            .substring(0, 8).toUpperCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT);
        return "PR-" + input.periodStart.replace("-", "") + "-" + suffix;
    }

    private static PayrollService.Input payrollInputFrom(JsonObject body) {
        java.util.Set<String> allowed = new java.util.HashSet<>(java.util.Arrays.asList(
            "employeeId", "employeeName", "position", "department", "payPeriod", "periodStart", "periodEnd",
            "monthlyBasic", "daysWorked", "overtimeHours", "overtimeRatePercent", "nightDifferentialHours",
            "nightDifferentialRatePercent", "riceSubsidy", "phoneAllowance", "clothingAllowance",
            "taxableAllowance", "otherDeductions", "taxBasis", "statutoryBasis"));
        for (String key : body.keySet()) {
            if (!allowed.contains(key)) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Unexpected request field: " + key);
        }
        PayrollService.Input input = new PayrollService.Input();
        input.employeeId = requiredString(body, "employeeId");
        input.employeeName = optionalString(body, "employeeName");

[NODE 10298]
private void handleSeedDemo(HttpExchange exchange) throws IOException {
        if (!"POST".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod())) {
            sendJson(exchange, 405, "{\"error\":\"Method not allowed\"}");
            return;
        }
        if (firebaseProjectId.isEmpty()) {
            sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"Firebase is not configured for this server.\"}");
            return;
        }
        try {
            FirestoreRestClient client = firestoreClientFor(exchange);
            DemoSeedService.SeedResult result = new DemoSeedService(client).seedMissingSyntheticRecords();
            sendJson(exchange, 200, "{\"employeesCreated\":" + result.getEmployeesCreated()
                + ",\"scheduleMappingsCreated\":" + result.getScheduleMappingsCreated()
                + ",\"attendanceCreated\":" + result.getAttendanceCreated()
                + ",\"syntheticOnly\":true}");
        } catch (FirestoreException ex) {
            sendApiError(exchange, ex);
        }
    }

    private RequestServices servicesFor(HttpExchange exchange) {
        if (firebaseProjectId.isEmpty()) {
            return new RequestServices(localEmployeeService, localScheduleStore, localAttendanceStore);
        }
        FirestoreRestClient client = firestoreClientFor(exchange);
        return new RequestServices(new EmployeeService(new FirestoreEmployeeStore(client)),
            new FirestoreEmployeeScheduleStore(client), new FirestoreAttendanceStore(client));
    }

    private FirestoreRestClient firestoreClientFor(HttpExchange exchange) {
        String authorization = exchange.getRequestHeaders().getFirst("Authorization");
        String uid = exchange.getRequestHeaders().getFirst("X-Firebase-UID");
        if (authorization == null || !authorization.startsWith("Bearer ") || uid == null || uid.trim().isEmpty()) {
            throw new FirestoreException("Sign in with your Firebase account to continue.", 401);
        }
        String token = authorization.substring("Bearer ".length()).trim();
        if (token.length() > 8192 || uid.length() > 128 || uid.contains("/")) {
            throw new FirestoreException("Invalid Firebase session information.", 401);
        }
        return firestoreApiRoot == null
            ? new FirestoreRestClient(firebaseProjectId, uid, token)
            : new FirestoreRestClient(firebaseProjectId, uid, token, firestoreApiRoot);
    }

package ph.motorph.web;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.util.Objects;

/** A directory record: identity, placement and the pay inputs MotorPH's payslip needs. */
public final class Employee {
    private final String id;
    private final String name;
    private final String department;
    private final String role;
    private final String location;
    private final String status;
    private final BigDecimal monthlyBasic;
    private final BigDecimal riceSubsidy;
    private final BigDecimal phoneAllowance;
    private final BigDecimal clothingAllowance;

    /** Directory-only record with no pay data; used where salary is irrelevant. */
    public Employee(String id, String name, String department, String role, String location, String status) {
        this(id, name, department, role, location, status, null, null, null, null);
    }

    public Employee(String id, String name, String department, String role, String location, String status,
                    BigDecimal monthlyBasic, BigDecimal riceSubsidy, BigDecimal phoneAllowance, BigDecimal clothingAllowance) {
        this.id = requireText(id, "id");
        this.name = requireText(name, "name");
        this.department = requireText(department, "department");
        this.role = requireText(role, "role");
        this.location = requireText(location, "location");
        this.status = requireText(status, "status");
        this.monthlyBasic = nonNegative(monthlyBasic, "Monthly basic pay");
        this.riceSubsidy = nonNegative(riceSubsidy, "Rice subsidy");
        this.phoneAllowance = nonNegative(phoneAllowance, "Phone allowance");
        this.clothingAllowance = nonNegative(clothingAllowance, "Clothing allowance");
    }

    public Employee withPay(BigDecimal basic, BigDecimal rice, BigDecimal phone, BigDecimal clothing) {
        return new Employee(id, name, department, role, location, status, basic, rice, phone, clothing);
    }

    private static String requireText(String value, String field) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(value, field + " must not be null");
        if (value.trim().isEmpty()) throw new IllegalArgumentException(field + " must not be blank");
        return value.trim();
    }

    private static BigDecimal nonNegative(BigDecimal value, String field) {
        if (value != null && value.signum() < 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException(field + " must not be negative");
        return value == null ? null : Money.round(value);
    }

    public String getId() { return id; }
    public String getName() { return name; }
    public String getDepartment() { return department; }
    public String getRole() { return role; }
    public String getLocation() { return location; }
    public String getStatus() { return status; }
    public BigDecimal getMonthlyBasic() { return monthlyBasic; }
    public BigDecimal getRiceSubsidy() { return riceSubsidy; }
    public BigDecimal getPhoneAllowance() { return phoneAllowance; }
    public BigDecimal getClothingAllowance() { return clothingAllowance; }

    /** True when this record carries enough pay data to be included in a payroll run. */
    public boolean hasPayProfile() {
        return monthlyBasic != null && monthlyBasic.signum() > 0
            && riceSubsidy != null && phoneAllowance != null && clothingAllowance != null;
    }
}

package ph.motorph.web;

import java.util.Collections;
import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.OptionalInt;

/** Synthetic employee-to-schedule mapping; replace with the approved source later. */
public final class InMemoryEmployeeScheduleStore implements EmployeeScheduleStore {
    private final Map<String, Integer> scheduleByEmployee;

    public InMemoryEmployeeScheduleStore() {
        Map<String, Integer> values = new HashMap<>();
        values.put("DEMO-001", 101);
        values.put("DEMO-002", 102);
        values.put("DEMO-003", 103);
        values.put("DEMO-015", 104);
        scheduleByEmployee = Collections.unmodifiableMap(values);
    }

    @Override
    public OptionalInt findScheduleIdForEmployee(String employeeId) {
        Integer scheduleId = employeeId == null ? null : scheduleByEmployee.get(employeeId);
        return scheduleId == null ? OptionalInt.empty() : OptionalInt.of(scheduleId);
    }
}

        new EmployeeServiceTest().run();

    private void run() {
        EmployeeService service = new EmployeeService(new InMemoryEmployeeStore());

        List<Employee> all = service.listEmployees();
        equal(4, all.size(), "the demo directory has four records");
        equal("DEMO-001", all.get(0).getId(), "directory order is stable");

        List<Employee> finance = service.searchEmployees("finance");
        equal(1, finance.size(), "search matches department case-insensitively");
        equal("Eli Santos", finance.get(0).getName(), "department search returns correct person");

        List<Employee> city = service.searchEmployees("TAGUIG");
        equal(1, city.size(), "search matches location case-insensitively");
        equal("DEMO-002", city.get(0).getId(), "location search returns correct record");

        equal(1, service.searchEmployees("demo-003").size(), "search matches employee ID");
        equal(4, service.searchEmployees("  ").size(), "blank search returns all employees");
        equal(0, service.searchEmployees("not a person").size(), "no match returns an empty list");

        Optional<Employee> found = service.findEmployee(" DEMO-002 ");
        check(found.isPresent(), "employee lookup trims the supplied ID");
        equal("Finance", found.get().getDepartment(), "employee lookup returns the expected record");
        check(!service.findEmployee("MISSING").isPresent(), "unknown ID has no employee");

        expectIllegalArgument(() -> new Employee(" ", "Name", "Dept", "Role", "Place", "Active"),
            "employee ID cannot be blank");
        System.out.println("PASS: " + checks + " employee-domain checks");
    }

    private void run() {
        EmployeeService employees = new EmployeeService(new InMemoryEmployeeStore());
        InMemoryAttendanceStore attendanceStore = new InMemoryAttendanceStore();
        AttendanceService service = new AttendanceService(employees,
            new InMemoryEmployeeScheduleStore(), attendanceStore);

        List<AttendanceRecord> all = service.findForEmployee("10001", null, null);
        equal(3, all.size(), "employee gets only their synthetic schedule entries");
        equal(101, all.get(0).getScheduleId(), "attendance is linked by schedule ID");
        equal("2026-10-01", all.get(0).getDate().toString(), "date is preserved without deriving hours");

        List<RawAttendanceSummary> summaries = service.summarizeRawRecords(null, null);
        RawAttendanceSummary firstSummary = summaries.stream()
            .filter(item -> item.getEmployeeId().equals("10001")).findFirst().orElseThrow(AssertionError::new);
        equal(3, firstSummary.getRawRecordCount(), "summary counts raw rows only");
        equal("2026-10-01", firstSummary.getFirstRecordDate(), "summary exposes earliest raw date");
        equal("2026-10-15", firstSummary.getLastRecordDate(), "summary exposes latest raw date");
        check(firstSummary.hasScheduleMapping() && firstSummary.getScheduleId() == 101,
            "summary reports the configured synthetic schedule mapping");
        Employee unmapped = employees.createEmployee("Unmapped Sample", "Demo", "Tester", "Taguig", "Active");
        RawAttendanceSummary unmappedSummary = service.summarizeRawRecords(null, null).stream()
            .filter(item -> item.getEmployeeId().equals(unmapped.getId())).findFirst().orElseThrow(AssertionError::new);
        check(!unmappedSummary.hasScheduleMapping() && unmappedSummary.getRawRecordCount() == 0,
            "unmapped employee is identified without implying absence");
        List<RawAttendanceSummary> oneDaySummary = service.summarizeRawRecords(
            LocalDate.parse("2026-10-02"), LocalDate.parse("2026-10-02"));
        RawAttendanceSummary filteredSummary = oneDaySummary.stream()
            .filter(item -> item.getEmployeeId().equals("10001")).findFirst().orElseThrow(AssertionError::new);
        equal(1, filteredSummary.getRawRecordCount(), "report date range is inclusive");
        expectIllegalArgument(() -> service.summarizeRawRecords(LocalDate.parse("2026-10-15"),
            LocalDate.parse("2026-10-01")), "report rejects reversed date range");

        List<AttendanceRecord> oneDay = service.findForEmployee("10001",
            LocalDate.parse("2026-10-02"), LocalDate.parse("2026-10-02"));
        equal(1, oneDay.size(), "date filtering is inclusive at both ends");
        equal(5002, oneDay.get(0).getAttendanceId(), "date filter returns the right entry");

        equal(0, service.findForEmployee("10002", LocalDate.parse("2026-10-10"), null).size(),
            "open-ended lower date filter works");
        equal(1, service.findForEmployee("10003", null, LocalDate.parse("2026-10-02")).size(),
            "open-ended upper date filter works");
        equal(0, service.findForEmployee("10001", LocalDate.parse("2026-11-01"), null).size(),
            "no matches returns an empty list");

package ph.motorph.web;

import com.google.gson.JsonObject;

import java.util.Arrays;

/** Creates only fictional, clearly marked records in one signed-in user's demo sandbox. */
public final class DemoSeedService {
    private final FirestoreRestClient client;

    public DemoSeedService(FirestoreRestClient client) {
        if (client == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("client must not be null");
        this.client = client;
    }

    public SeedResult seedMissingSyntheticRecords() {
        // Preflight the new rules path before any writes so an unpublished ruleset cannot leave a partial seed.
        client.listDocuments(client.userCollection("demoEmployeeSchedules"));
        int employeesCreated = 0;
        for (Employee employee : new InMemoryEmployeeStore().findAll()) {
            if (client.createDocument(client.userCollection("demoEmployees"), employee.getId(), employeeFields(employee))) {
                employeesCreated++;
            }
        }

        int mappingsCreated = 0;
        EmployeeScheduleStore sampleMappings = new InMemoryEmployeeScheduleStore();
        for (Employee employee : new InMemoryEmployeeStore().findAll()) {
            java.util.OptionalInt scheduleId = sampleMappings.findScheduleIdForEmployee(employee.getId());
            if (scheduleId.isPresent() && client.createDocument(client.userCollection("demoEmployeeSchedules"),
                employee.getId(), scheduleMappingFields(employee.getId(), scheduleId.getAsInt()))) {
                mappingsCreated++;
            }
        }

        int attendanceCreated = 0;
        InMemoryAttendanceStore sampleAttendance = new InMemoryAttendanceStore();
        for (int scheduleId : Arrays.asList(101, 102, 103, 104)) {
            for (AttendanceRecord record : sampleAttendance.findByScheduleId(scheduleId)) {
                if (client.createDocument(client.userCollection("demoAttendance"),
                    Integer.toString(record.getAttendanceId()), attendanceFields(record))) {
                    attendanceCreated++;
                }
            }
        }
        return new SeedResult(employeesCreated, mappingsCreated, attendanceCreated);
    }

    private static JsonObject employeeFields(Employee employee) {
        JsonObject fields = new JsonObject();

        private void savePayrollRun(String path, String body) {
            String documentId = "";
            int query = path.indexOf('?');
            if (query >= 0) {
                for (String pair : path.substring(query + 1).split("&")) {
                    if (pair.startsWith("documentId=")) documentId = pair.substring("documentId=".length());
                }
            }

            com.google.gson.JsonObject parsed = com.google.gson.JsonParser.parseString(body).getAsJsonObject();
            storedRunFields = parsed.getAsJsonObject("fields").toString();
            storedRunName = "projects/demo-project/databases/(default)/documents"
                + cleanPath.substring(cleanPath.indexOf("/users/")) + "/" + documentId;
        }

        private String storedPayrollRun() {

const items = [
  { id: 'LV-101', employeeId: '10001', employeeName: 'Avery Sample', leaveType: 'Vacation', startDate: '2026-11-12', status: 'Pending review' },

];

test('filters case-insensitively across explicitly selected fields', () => {
  const results = filterWorkflowItems(items, { query: 'aVeRy', searchFields: ['employeeName', 'id'] });
  assert.deepEqual(results.map(item => item.id), ['LV-101', 'TK-201']);
});

test('combines text and exact status filters', () => {
  const results = filterWorkflowItems(items, { query: 'demo-001', status: 'Open', searchFields: ['employeeId', 'employeeName'] });
  assert.deepEqual(results.map(item => item.id), ['TK-201']);
});

test('filters exact leave or ticket type only through the explicitly selected type field', () => {
  assert.deepEqual(filterWorkflowItems(items, { type: 'Vacation', typeField: 'leaveType' }).map(item => item.id), ['LV-101']);
  assert.deepEqual(filterWorkflowItems(items, { type: 'Technical support', typeField: 'ticketType' }).map(item => item.id), ['TK-201']);
  assert.deepEqual(filterWorkflowItems(items, { type: 'Vacation' }), []);
});

test('ignores text in fields not configured for the list', () => {
  const results = filterWorkflowItems(items, { query: '2026-11-12', searchFields: ['id', 'employeeName'] });
  assert.deepEqual(results, []);
});

/** Reads the payslip form into the API request body. */
function payrollFormInput() {
  const employee = state.payrollEmployees.find(item => item.id === document.getElementById('payroll-employee').value);
  const value = id => document.getElementById(id).value;
  return {
    employeeId: value('payroll-employee'),
    employeeName: employee ? employee.name : '',
    position: employee ? employee.role : '',
    department: employee ? employee.department : '',
    payPeriod: value('payroll-period'),
    periodStart: value('payroll-start'),
    periodEnd: value('payroll-end'),
    monthlyBasic: employee ? employee.monthlyBasic : '',
    daysWorked: value('payroll-days'),
    overtimeHours: value('payroll-ot-hours') || '0',
    overtimeRatePercent: value('payroll-ot-rate') || '125',
    nightDifferentialHours: value('payroll-nd-hours') || '0',
    nightDifferentialRatePercent: value('payroll-nd-rate') || '10',
    riceSubsidy: employee ? employee.riceSubsidy : '0',
    phoneAllowance: employee ? employee.phoneAllowance : '0',
    clothingAllowance: employee ? employee.clothingAllowance : '0',
    taxableAllowance: value('payroll-taxable-allowance') || '0',
    otherDeductions: value('payroll-other-deductions') || '0',
    taxBasis: value('payroll-tax-basis'),
    statutoryBasis: value('payroll-statutory-basis')
  };
}

/** Reads the stored timesheet for the selected employee and period, then fills days worked. */
async function useStoredTimesheet() {
  const employeeId = document.getElementById('payroll-employee').value;
  const from = document.getElementById('payroll-start').value;
  const to = document.getElementById('payroll-end').value;
  if (!employeeId || !from || !to) {
    setWorkflowStatus('payroll-status', 'Choose an employee and a period start and end first.', true);
    return;
  }
  try {
    const params = new URLSearchParams({ employeeId, from, to });
    const response = await fetch(`/api/payroll/timesheet?${params.toString()}`, { headers: await apiHeaders() });
    const payload = await response.json();
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(payload.error || `Request failed (${response.status})`);
    document.getElementById('payroll-days').value = String(payload.daysWorked);
    const hours = formatAmount(payload.totalHours);
    setWorkflowStatus('payroll-status', payload.daysWorked
      ? `Stored timecard: ${payload.daysWorked} day(s), ${hours} paid hours. Days worked filled in; hours are informational only.`
      : 'No stored timecard rows with positive hours in this period; days worked left at 0.');

/** Loads the selected employee's salary into the form so every run starts from stored data. */
function applyPayrollEmployee() {
  const employeeId = document.getElementById('payroll-employee').value;
  const employee = state.payrollEmployees.find(item => item.id === employeeId);
  const status = document.getElementById('payroll-status');
  if (!employee) {
    document.getElementById('payroll-days').value = '';
    status.textContent = 'Add a monthly basic pay to an employee record before running payroll.';
    return;
  }
  document.getElementById('payroll-days').value = document.getElementById('payroll-days').value || '10';
  status.textContent = `${employee.name}: monthly basic ${formatAmount(employee.monthlyBasic)}, `
    + `rice ${formatAmount(employee.riceSubsidy)}, phone ${formatAmount(employee.phoneAllowance)}, `
    + `clothing ${formatAmount(employee.clothingAllowance)}.`;
}

## 4. Where we deliberately differ from the site

| Area | Site | Us | Why ours is right |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SSS brackets** | Range table: below ₱5,250 → MSC ₱5,000 | ⌈basic/500⌉ → same result | **Verified identical for every input tested.** The official schedule is bracket-based; ceil-to-500 happens to reproduce it because brackets are ₱500 wide with a ₱250 offset. We keep the closed form (it is testable in one line) and now assert it equals the bracket definition at the edges. |
| **Pag-IBIG at exactly ₱1,500** | **2%** (₱30.00) | **1%** (₱15.00) | HDMF Circular 460: employee pays 1% *at or below* ₱1,500. The site applies "at least ₱1,500". Ours matches the circular — and MotorPH's employee file has nobody at that boundary, so real payslips are unaffected. |
| **`payroll_period_daily_days`** | **Ignored** (20/21/22/26 all produce identical output) | Day count drives pay | The parameter is cosmetic on their side: monthly pay is flat regardless of days worked. We take days worked because a payslip that pays a full month for 3 days worked is not a payslip. |
| **`work_schedule` (5/6/4)** | **Ignored** | Not modelled | Same finding — no effect on any output. |
| **Daily pay period** | Multiplies basic × `days` | Supported via `daysWorked` | Semantics differ: theirs is "daily rate × days" in one step; ours is "monthly basic ÷ 20 × days". |
| **Semi-monthly** | Doubles basic (treats input as the cutoff amount) | Deducts full-month statutory per cutoff or splits | Two defensible readings; the supplied MotorPH payslip settles ours. |
| **Tax 95k–100k** | 13-centavo variant | Annual÷12 exact | Our fix above. |
| **Tax above ~100k** | Diverges sharply (₱2,750 higher at 200k) | Annex E cumulative | The site's curve applies a ~27% marginal rate directly after ₱66,666, which does not match any published band. It appears to add the lower brackets' tax on top. **Unresolved on their side** — worth one more probe before treating their high-income output as authoritative. |
| **Year selector** | UI only; `year`/`tax_year`/`yy` params ignored | `forYear` refuses uncovered years | Ours fails closed rather than silently using the wrong table. |
| **Self-employed / minimum wage / kasambahay** | Fall through to the private-employee formula | Not implemented | Their branches are cosmetic too. |

# MotorPH — the short guide

You don't need the 1,500-line version to understand this app.
**Read this file. Skim section 5. Look things up in the big file only when you want.**

---

## 1. What this app is, in 5 lines

1. It's a payroll app for MotorPH: people, timecards, leave, and payslips.
2. You sign in with your own account. You only ever see your own data.
3. It calculates a payslip **exactly like MotorPH's own sample payslip** — same numbers to the centavo.
4. It saves each payroll run permanently. You can reprint it later.
5. Everything is **fake data**. No real people, no real money.

---

## 2. The 3 ideas that explain everything else

**Idea 1 — The browser never does maths.**
Every number on screen came from the server. The browser only prints it.
So if a number is wrong, the bug is on the server. Always.

**Idea 2 — The server never says "yes" to the database.**
The server passes your login token to Firebase, and **Firebase's rules** decide what you can see.
Your `uid` comes from your token — you cannot ask for someone else's data even by editing the request.

**Idea 3 — Money is never a float.**
Decimals are stored as text (`"26750.00"`) and calculated exactly. Rounding happens in exactly one
place: `Money.round()` — 2 decimals, round half up. That's how the centavos match.

---

Left nav, top to bottom. Only the first and last matter much:

| Screen | What it does | Notes |

| **Reports** | Who has how many attendance rows | Coverage, not pay |
| **Payroll** | **The main event** | See §5 |

## 4. One payslip, start to finish

This is the whole app in one path.

```
You pick an employee            →  salary comes from their record (not typed in)
        ↓
You enter or fetch days worked  →  "Use stored timesheet days" reads their timecard
        ↓
Server calculates               →  daily rate, gross, SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, tax

[NODE 11118]
Server calculates               →  daily rate, gross, SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, tax
        ↓
You see the payslip             →  nothing saved yet
        ↓
You click "Save as payroll run" →  frozen forever, with the rules version stamped on it
        ↓
Later you click "Open"          →  it prints the STORED numbers, it does not recalculate
```

**Why "frozen" matters:** tax tables change. If 2027's tables change, last year's payslip must still
print what was actually paid. That's why saved runs can't be edited or deleted.

## 5. The payroll numbers (the part worth knowing)

**Inputs:** monthly salary, days worked, allowances, overtime hours, night-diff hours.

**The 6 formulas:**

```
daily rate    = monthly salary ÷ 20
hourly rate   = monthly salary ÷ 168
gross         = daily rate × days worked   (+ overtime + night diff)
SSS           = 5% of salary, capped between ₱5,000 and ₱35,000
PhilHealth    = 5% of salary, split in half
Pag-IBIG      = 2% of salary, capped at ₱10,000
tax           = BIR table, applied to (salary − the three contributions above)
take home     = gross + allowances − (SSS + PhilHealth + Pag-IBIG + tax)
```

**Worked example** (this is MotorPH's real sample — the test that must always pass):

```
Salary ₱53,500, 10 days, semi-monthly
  gross        26,750.00
  SSS           1,750.00
  PhilHealth    1,337.50
  Pag-IBIG        200.00
  tax           5,250.83
  ─────────────────────
  take home    22,711.67   ← must be exactly this
```

If a change makes this number move, the change is wrong. A test enforces it.

## 6b. What the sweldongpinoy test found (2026-11-06)

We ran MotorPH's 34 real employees through both systems:

- **SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG: identical on all 34**, to the centavo.
- **Tax: they caught a bug in ours.** Three bracket bases were 13 centavos too high
  (8,541.80 instead of 102,500÷12 = 8,541.67). Anyone above ~₱90,000 basic was overcharged 13c.
  **Fixed**, with tests.
- **Two places where we are right and they are wrong:** Pag-IBIG at exactly ₱1,500 (they use 2%,
  the circular says 1%), and their tax curve above ~₱100,000 doesn't match any published band.
- **Their `days` and `schedule` settings do nothing** — output is identical for 15, 20, 22 days.
- **There is no public API**, just an undocumented form post. We added an optional
  "compare with sweldongpinoy.com" checkbox that calls it **through our server**, side by side.
  If their site is down, the payslip is unaffected.

## 7. The 8 questions from the review, in one line each

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| ₱150/₱160/₱200 hourly rates? | Not used. Rate = salary ÷ 168. Don't add flat rates. |
| Leave credits 5/5/3? | Fine as demo policy. Keep out of payroll. |
| 13th month + ₱90,000 tax? | No 13th month exists. It's a separate annual feature. |
| Pag-IBIG at exactly ₱1,500? | **Already follows the law (1%).** Nothing to do. |
| Overtime — what counts? | Past **8 hours**, not past 17:00. 125% on normal days. |
| Paid leave in payroll? | It's a paid **day**, not paid hours. Blocked — no approvals yet. |
| Log in before 08:00 = extra pay? | **It does today, and it shouldn't.** This is a real bug. |
| Approve your own leave? | Never. |

---

## 8. What's missing (don't go looking for it)

- No attendance clock-in/out screen (records come from the seed only)
- No automatic "days worked" — you confirm the number
- No overtime/night-diff **hours** from punches (you type the hours)
- No leave pay, no holidays, no 13th month
- No approvals, no roles, no managers
- No multi-employee run in the UI

The app **says** these are missing instead of pretending. That's deliberate. If a screen implies a
feature works when it doesn't, that's a bug worth reporting.

---

## 9. Three sentences that are safe to say out loud

1. "Payroll reproduces MotorPH's sample payslip to the centavo, with tests at every layer."
2. "Every saved run is permanent and reprints from stored numbers."
3. "It's a synthetic demo: no real employees, no real money, and gaps are labelled."

            if (!parsed.isJsonObject()) return Comparison.unavailable("Reference calculator returned no result.");
            JsonObject root = parsed.getAsJsonObject();
            JsonObject result = root.has("result") && root.get("result").isJsonObject()
                ? root.getAsJsonObject("result") : root;
            if (!result.has("net_pay")) return Comparison.unavailable("Reference calculator returned no figures.");

        } catch (java.net.http.HttpTimeoutException ex) {
            return Comparison.unavailable("Reference calculator timed out.");
        } catch (InterruptedException ex) {
            Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
            return Comparison.unavailable("Reference calculation was interrupted.");
        } catch (IOException | IllegalArgumentException | com.google.gson.JsonParseException ex) {
            return Comparison.unavailable("Reference calculator could not be reached.");
        }
    }

### `POST /api/payroll/compare` — optional reference check

Computes the payslip exactly as `/preview` does, then **additionally** asks sweldongpinoy.com for its
own figures. Returns both side by side.

```json
{
  "reference": "sweldongpinoy.com",
  "referenceNote": "Undocumented third-party calculator, used for comparison only. Never used to compute or save a payslip.",
  "ours":   { "grossPay":"58000.00","sss":"1750.00","philHealth":"1337.50","pagibig":"200.00",
              "withholdingTax":"5250.83","totalDeductions":"8538.33","netPay":"49461.67" },
  "available": true,
  "theirs": { "…same shape…" },
  "differences": [ {"field":"sss","ours":"1750.00","theirs":"1750.00","delta":"0.00"} ],
  "matches": true
}
```

When the reference is unreachable the route still answers `200` with:

```json
{ "ours": {…}, "available": false, "reason": "Reference calculator timed out.",
  "theirs": null, "differences": [] }
```

Rules that make this safe:

- It never changes the payslip. `ours` is produced by our ruleset before the reference is contacted.
- A timeout, an HTTP error or a malformed answer is reported, never thrown — payroll cannot break because
  a third-party site is down.
- It runs **server-side** (`SweldongPinoyClient`), so salary data is never posted from the browser, and
  CORS/the session handshake stay out of the client.
- `./test.sh` pins `MOTORPH_SWP_ENDPOINT` to a closed port, so the build never touches the internet.

# Build status — persistent-only target

> **Payroll status update (2026-11-05):** payroll now calculates against an effective-dated
> ruleset and reproduces the supplied MotorPH payslip to the centavo. See
> `docs/payroll-ruleset-and-golden-case.md`. The statements below about a removed *temporary
> preview* remain historically accurate; what replaced it is a durable, saved-run feature, not a
> browser-only estimate.

**This document supersedes earlier statements that a process-memory product mode or a temporary payroll preview is an acceptable deliverable.** The user's current requirement is “No locals, no temps.” No peer implementation or earlier policy candidate changes that requirement.

## Product behavior now enforced

- `AppServer.main` requires `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID`. The only no-Firebase entry-point exception is `MOTORPH_TEST_MODE=true` while binding to a loopback host; the production run scripts do not set it. Direct constructor-based local services remain test fixtures used by the isolated test harness, not a supported deployment mode.
- `web/app.js` does not open the workspace if Firebase web configuration is missing. It shows a setup error instead. The unauthenticated local workspace is available only in the test build flag `VITE_E2E_TEST_MODE=true` used by the test runner.
- Removed the browser-only 2026 payroll preview that existed on 2026-11-04. On 2026-11-05 it was replaced by a server-side, effective-dated payroll service grounded in MotorPH's supplied payslip and timecard: `PayrollService`, `PayrollRuleset`, `TimesheetService`, saved `PayrollRun` snapshots in Firestore, and payslip rendering in the Payroll view. The removed artefact was a synthetic-input estimate; the replacement stores its inputs, ruleset version and assumptions with every run.
- The test-only synthetic fixture remains intentionally process-memory-backed so the UI/API contract can be exercised without using real staff data or writing test records to a live Firebase project. This is test infrastructure, not a deployable local-data feature.

## Verified after these changes

- **Withholding-table correction (2026-11-06):** the 25/30/35% bands used `8,541.80 / 33,541.80 /
  183,541.80` as their base instead of the annual amounts over 12 (`102,500/12 = 8,541.67`,
  `402,500/12 = 33,541.67`, `2,202,500/12 = 183,541.67`). A 13-centavo error on every payslip above
  ~₱90,000 basic. Found by comparing against sweldongpinoy.com, fixed, and pinned by three new tests
  (`PayrollGoldenTest` 61 → 65). The ₱53,500 golden case was never affected.
- **Reference comparison added:** `POST /api/payroll/compare` plus a "compare with sweldongpinoy.com"
  checkbox. Optional, server-side, read-only; a failure can never affect a payslip. Verified live:
  all six statutory lines match.

`"0.00"` — that is why the payroll picker filters on it.

1. Introduction This document outlines the business requirements for the MotorPH payroll system. The main objective of this system is to streamline and automate payroll processing, ensuring accurate and timely payment of employees while maintaining compliance with relevant laws and regulations. 2. Business Objectives The key objectives of implementing the MotorPH payroll system are as follows: ● Efﬁciency: Automate manual payroll processes to reduce administrative workload and minimize errors. ● Accuracy: Ensure precise and error-free salary calculations and tax deductions. ● Compliance: Meet all legal and regulatory requirements related to payroll management. ● Security: Implement robust security measures to safeguard sensitive payroll data. ● Scalability: Design a system to accommodate the company's growth and evolving payroll needs. ● Employee Self-Service: Allow employees to access and manage their payroll information securely. 3. Project Scope The MotorPH payroll system is composed of the following key features and functionalities: 3.1. Employee Information Management Maintain a centralized database of employee information, including personal details, salary structure, tax information, and relevant documents. 3.2. Time and Attendance Tracking Integrate with a time and attendance system to capture accurate work hours for each employee. MO-IT107 Information Management 6 Last Updated: 11/28/2025

--- page 7 ---
3.3. Salary Calculation Automate salary calculations based on work hours, overtime, bonuses, deductions, and taxes, compliant with local tax laws and regulations. 3.4. Employee Self-Service Portal Provide a secure portal for employees to access their payroll information, such as payslips, tax forms, and annual statements. 3.5. Payroll Administrator Roles Implement various user roles and permissions to control access and maintain data security. 4. Stakeholders The main stakeholders involved in the MotorPH payroll system implementation are: 1. HR Department: To manage employee information, attendance records, and leave management. 2. Finance Department: To oversee payroll processing, tax calculations, and reporting. 3. Employees: To access their payroll information and manage personal details securely. 4. IT Department: To oversee system integration, maintenance, and data security. 5. Constraints The development of the MotorPH payroll system considers the following constraints: 1. Budget: The project adheres to the allocated budget for development and implementation of ₱500,000 2. Timeline: The system is developed and deployed within the agreed-upon timeframe. 6. Assumptions 1. Employees input their time and attendance data accurately through manual entry or automated systems. 2. The company provides the necessary resources, including hardware, software, and infrastructure, to support the payroll system. MO-IT107 Information Management 7 Last Updated: 11/28/2025

--- page 8 ---
3. The IT department ensures data backup and implements disaster recovery measures. 7. Risks 1. Data Security: Unauthorized access to sensitive employee data and ﬁnancial information. 2. Integration Challenges: Difﬁculties integrating the payroll system with existing HR and ﬁnancial systems. 3. Data Inaccuracies: Errors in payroll calculations leading to incorrect salary disbursement. 4. Regulatory Compliance: Failure to comply with changing tax and labor regulations. 8. Reporting Requirements The MotorPH payroll system generates the following reports: 1. Monthly Payroll Summary Report: An overview of monthly payroll expenses. See an example in the Data Repository - Sample Documents on our website. 2. Payslips: Detailed pay statements for individual employees.
