- CEO, CFO, COO, HR, Payroll, supervisor, employee, and administrator permissions match the configured policy.
- Branch assignments follow the leaf-team midpoint rule, with parent supervisors and C-level staff assigned to Main Branch.

**Authentication and sessions**
- Every account can initially authenticate with the supplied initial password.
- Stored password hashes differ across accounts because of unique salts.

=== AccessPolicy ===
package ph.motorph.web;

import java.util.Collections;
import java.util.EnumMap;
import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.LinkedHashSet;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Optional;
import java.util.Set;

/**
 * Role-based access for the local demo, from the user's RBAC permissions matrix (2026-11-05).
 * Who may act is decided by the signed-in account (identity), never by a role or reviewer ID the client sends.
 *
 * Read scopes per area (ALL = everyone, TEAM = self + direct reports + teammates + own supervisor, SELF = own records):
 *   Employees   admin/HR/payroll ALL; supervisor, employee TEAM ("can view team members")
 *   Attendance  admin/HR/payroll ALL; supervisor TEAM; employee SELF
 *   Leave       admin/HR ALL; everyone else TEAM ("check team leave")
 *   Overtime    admin/HR/payroll ALL; supervisor TEAM; employee SELF
 *   Tickets     admin/HR ALL; supervisor TEAM; others SELF
 *   Payroll     admin/payroll/HR ALL; supervisor TEAM (payslip R Team); employee SELF
 *   Reports     admin/HR/payroll ALL; others none
 *   Statutory   admin/payroll ALL; others none
 * Writes: employees C/U admin+HR; attendance edits admin + supervisor for direct reports; requests are created for
 * yourself (admin any; HR any leave/ticket); leave is approved by admin, HR, or the direct supervisor; overtime by admin
 * or the direct supervisor; nobody decides their own request; payslips are finalized by admin or payroll staff, never
 * their own.
 */
public final class AccessPolicy {
    public static final String VERSION = "RBAC-2026-11-05-matrix-v1";

    public enum Role {
        EMPLOYEE("Employee"), SUPERVISOR("Supervisor"), PAYROLL("Payroll Staff"), HR("HR"), ADMIN("System Admin");
        public final String label;
        Role(String label) { this.label = label; }
    }

    public enum Scope { NONE, SELF, TEAM, ALL }

    public enum Area { EMPLOYEES, ATTENDANCE, LEAVE, OVERTIME, TICKETS, PAYROLL, REPORTS, STATUTORY, EARNINGS, REMITTANCE, PAY_CHANGES }

    /** The signed-in account. {@code explicit} is false only for unauthenticated legacy calls (see AppServer). */
    public static final class Actor {
        public final String employeeId;
        public final Role role;
        public final boolean explicit;

        public Actor(String employeeId, Role role, boolean explicit) {
            this.employeeId = employeeId;
            this.role = role;
            this.explicit = explicit;
        }
    }

    /** Thrown when the signed-in account may not do something; AppServer answers 403. */
    public static final class AccessDenied extends RuntimeException {
        public AccessDenied(String message) { super(message); }
    }

    private static final Map<String, Role> DEFAULT_ROLES;

# MotorPH MS2 — browser payroll foundation

An original browser-based prototype with an HTML/CSS interface and Java 11 backend. Employee and attendance data are synthetic. It includes a disposable, client-only 2026 statutory preview with editable/versioned rules; attendance-derived payroll, persisted runs, and payslips remain gated.

**New here? Start with [SETUP.md](SETUP.md):** a full setup from scratch, including your own Firebase project.

## Run locally

Requires JDK 11+, Node.js 20.19+ (or a current supported Node release), and npm.

```sh
npm install
./run.sh
```

Then open <http://localhost:8080>. `run.sh` builds the Vite frontend and serves it from the Java server. Set `PORT` to choose a different HTTP port.

For development with Vite hot reload, use two terminals:

```sh
# terminal 1: Java backend
./run-api.sh

# terminal 2: frontend
npm run dev
```

Open <http://localhost:5173>. Vite proxies `/api` calls to the Java service at `http://127.0.0.1:8080` by default; set `API_PROXY_TARGET` to use a different backend. Set `HOST=127.0.0.1` for the Java backend when Vite is proxying it locally.

Run Java domain checks:

```sh
./test.sh
```

Run browser end-to-end checks (the suite starts isolated local API/Vite processes, uses only synthetic in-memory records, and cleans them up on exit):

```sh
npx playwright-core install chromium
# Linux, if system libraries are missing:
sudo npx playwright-core install-deps chromium
npm run test:e2e
```

Optional live Firebase Auth lifecycle smoke test:

```sh
npm run test:firebase-auth
```

This uses `.env.local`, creates one uniquely named disposable Auth account, verifies sign-in, empty user-scoped reads, and sign-out on localhost, makes **no Firestore writes**, and deletes the Auth account in cleanup. It needs network access and should not be run concurrently with another live Auth test.

The app uses a small vendored Gson JAR for the Java Firestore REST adapter; its license is recorded in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and `third_party/licenses/`.

## Firebase development sandbox

- `.env.local` contains the Firebase **Web** app config used by the browser SDK; `.gitignore` lists this file. The user-supplied Web API key for `motorph-jd` is installed assistant-side. The user does not need to edit `.env.local`.
- The Web API key is a public client identifier, not a server credential. Do not add a service-account key or Admin SDK credentials.
- Authentication uses Email/Password and in-memory browser persistence. Live disposable-account creation/sign-in, empty user-scoped reads, and sign-out now pass on localhost; the test Auth account was deleted. Do not use real staff accounts or data.
- Firestore requests are made by the Java backend through the REST API, forwarding the signed-in user's Firebase ID token. Firestore Security Rules authorize those requests; no privileged server identity bypasses the rules.
- The app uses `users/{uid}/demoEmployees`, `demoAttendance`, `demoLeaveRequests`, and `demoTickets`. Workflow documents are owner-scoped with no reviewer or delete permission in the candidate rules. The opt-in seed writes fictional employee/attendance records only.
- The user published the updated `docs/firestore.rules`. Live Firebase smoke testing with disposable accounts verified owner-scoped employee create/update, leave and ticket create/cancel/read-back, and a cross-user denial (`403`). Both disposable Auth accounts and employee documents were deleted; one cancelled synthetic leave and one cancelled synthetic ticket remain under their deleted test UIDs because workflow deletes are intentionally denied (`LV-3502C01F0E60`, `TK-F05DD2B0D6CC`). No real employee data or credentials were used. These are **development-only** rules, not production role/HR policy.
- **Roles in Firebase mode:** after the Firebase sign-in, the user chooses which fake person in their own sandbox to act as (same role workspaces and server checks as the local demo). A new, empty sandbox can add the synthetic people or open empty. The data stays private to that Firebase user; this is not a shared company login.
- If Firebase is not configured locally, the app uses the in-memory synthetic fixture. No Firebase writes are made in that mode.
- `measurementId` / Firebase Analytics is not used.
- Browser auth is verified on `localhost`. The current Arena preview host is `8080-is3s38ic4lxn7e4e77g8b.e2b.app`; its authorized-domain status could not be tested from the sandbox because Arena's traffic-access token is injected only in the user preview session. If the preview reports `auth/unauthorized-domain`, add that exact host under Firebase Console → Authentication → Settings → Authorized domains.

See `docs/firebase-setup-guide.md` for the console checkpoint and `docs/firestore.rules` for the development rules.

# Setting up MotorPH on your own computer

A quick start for setting up the project from scratch, including your own Firebase project. You can stop after part 1 if you only need the local demo.

## 1. Run the local demo (no Firebase)

**Install first:**
- **JDK 11 or newer**: `java -version` and `javac -version` must both work in a terminal.
- **Node.js 20.19 or newer** (npm comes with it).
- **Windows only:** **Git for Windows**, so you can run the `.sh` scripts from **Git Bash**.

**Then, in the `motorph-ms2` folder:**

```sh
npm install
./run.sh
```

Open <http://localhost:8080>, then pick a demo account, for example Lia (System Admin) or Jae (Employee).

- **Password:** every demo account starts with the shared demo password `MotorPH-demo-2026`. Change it after signing in (Overview → My account). The System Admin can reset it back from System config → Security settings.
- **2FA code:** next, type the 6-digit code. The demo shows it on screen, because there is no phone.
- Each account opens the workspace for its role.
- **Backups** are kept in `data/backups` and old audit entries in `data/archive`. If `data/local-demo.json` is ever damaged, the server starts from the newest backup.

- Local demo data is saved in `data/local-demo.json`. Signed in as Lia, use **System config → Reset demo data** to start over.
- If you have a `.env.local` file with a real Firebase key, `./run.sh` starts in Firebase mode instead. To get back to the local demo, rename or delete that file.
- **Hot reload while coding:** run `./run-api.sh` in one terminal and `npm run dev` in another, then open <http://localhost:5173>.

**Checks:**
- `./test.sh` runs the Java checks.
- `npm run test:web` runs the browser logic tests.
- `npm run test:e2e` runs the full browser test. Before the first run, do `npx playwright-core install chromium` once.

## 2. Create your own Firebase project

The free **Spark** plan is enough. If Firebase asks for billing, stop: this project doesn't need it.

1. **Create the project.** Go to <https://console.firebase.google.com> → **Add project**. Pick any name. Google Analytics can be turned **off**.
2. **Add a web app.** On the project overview, click the **`</>` (Web)** icon. Give it a nickname, and leave Firebase Hosting unticked. Firebase then shows a `firebaseConfig` block: keep that page open for step 6.
3. **Turn on sign-in.** Go to **Build → Authentication → Get started → Sign-in method**, and enable **Email/Password**. Leave the passwordless "Email link" option off.
4. **Create the database.** Go to **Build → Firestore Database → Create database**.
   - Choose **production mode**, not test mode.
   - Pick a location close to you, such as `asia-southeast1` (Singapore). You can't change the location later.
5. **Publish the rules.** Go to **Firestore Database → Rules**, delete what's there, and paste in the whole of `docs/firestore.rules`. Then click **Publish**.
   - These rules let each signed-in user read and write only their own sandbox, under `users/{their uid}/…`.
   - Never switch to rules that say `allow read, write: if true`.
6. **Connect the app.** In `motorph-ms2`, copy `.env.example` to `.env.local`. Then fill in the six values from the `firebaseConfig` block in step 2:

   ```text

    private static final int ROUNDS = 20_000;

        String salt, hash, changedAt;
    }

    private final Map<String, Stored> passwords = new HashMap<>();
    private final Map<String, Integer> failures = new HashMap<>();
    private final Map<String, String> lockedUntil = new HashMap<>();
    // Real time (seconds matter here); not saved, so a restart clears the waits but not the lockouts.
    private transient Map<String, java.time.Instant> nextTryAt = new HashMap<>();

    /** Seconds to wait after this many wrong passwords in a row: none after the 1st, then 1, 2, 4, 8 ... (design doc: progressive throttling). */
    static long waitSeconds(int failedInARow) {
        return failedInARow < 2 ? 0 : 1L << Math.min(failedInARow - 2, 6);
    }

    public synchronized Settings settings() {

        copy.minPasswordLength = settings.minPasswordLength;
        copy.maxFailedAttempts = settings.maxFailedAttempts;
        copy.lockoutMinutes = settings.lockoutMinutes;
        copy.codeMinutes = settings.codeMinutes;
        copy.sessionHours = settings.sessionHours;
        copy.updatedBy = settings.updatedBy;
        copy.updatedAt = settings.updatedAt;
        return copy;
    }

name: security-and-hardening
description: Hardens code against vulnerabilities. Use when auditing an input handler for vulnerabilities, when handling user input, authentication, data storage, or external integrations, or when checking a login flow is safe against the OWASP Top Ten. Use when building any feature that accepts untrusted data, manages user sessions or session cookies, or interacts with third-party services. Use when auditing dependencies for known vulnerabilities, triaging package-manager audit findings, or assessing supply-chain risk in a new package. Use when personal data or privacy compliance (GDPR, CCPA) is involved.

# Security and Hardening

## Overview

Security-first development practices for web applications. Treat every external input as hostile, every secret as sacred, and every authorization check as mandatory. Security isn't a phase — it's a constraint on every line of code that touches user data, authentication, or external systems.

## When to Use

- Building anything that accepts user input
- Implementing authentication or authorization
- Storing or transmitting sensitive data
- Integrating with external APIs or services
- Adding file uploads, webhooks, or callbacks
- Handling payment or PII data

## Process: Threat Model First

Controls bolted on without a threat model are guesses. Before hardening, spend five minutes thinking like an attacker:

1. **Map the trust boundaries.** Where does untrusted data cross into your system? HTTP requests, form fields, file uploads, webhooks, third-party APIs, message queues, and **LLM output** — plus the local values that look internal because the OS handed them to you: another process's command line or environment, filenames on a shared volume, a path in a job payload. Trust follows who *wrote* a value, not which channel delivered it. Every boundary is attack surface.
2. **Name the assets.** What's worth stealing or breaking? Credentials, PII, payment data, admin actions, money movement.
3. **Run STRIDE over each boundary** — a quick lens, not a ceremony:

| Threat | Ask | Typical mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| **S**poofing | Can someone impersonate a user/service? | Authentication, signature verification |
| **T**ampering | Can data be altered in transit or at rest? | Integrity checks, parameterized queries, HTTPS |
| **R**epudiation | Can an action be denied later? | Audit logging of security events |
| **I**nformation disclosure | Can data leak? | Encryption, field allowlists, generic errors |
| **D**enial of service | Can it be overwhelmed? | Rate limiting, input size caps, timeouts |
| **E**levation of privilege | Can a user gain rights they shouldn't? | Authorization checks, least privilege |

4. **Write abuse cases next to use cases.** For each feature, ask "how would I misuse this?" — then make that your first test.

If you can't name the trust boundaries for a feature, you're not ready to secure it. This is OWASP **A04: Insecure Design** — most breaches begin in design, not code.

## The Three-Tier Boundary System

### Always Do (No Exceptions)

- **Validate all external input** at the system boundary (API routes, form handlers)
- **Parameterize all database queries** — never concatenate user input into SQL
- **Encode output** to prevent XSS (use framework auto-escaping, don't bypass it)
- **Use HTTPS** for all external communication
- **Hash passwords** with bcrypt/scrypt/argon2 (never store plaintext)
- **Set security headers** (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options)
- **Use httpOnly, secure, sameSite cookies** for sessions
- **Run the detected package manager's native audit** against the committed lockfile before every release

### Ask First (Requires Human Approval)

- Adding new authentication flows or changing auth logic
- Storing new categories of sensitive data (PII, payment info)
- Adding new external service integrations
- Changing CORS configuration
- Adding file upload handlers
- Modifying rate limiting or throttling
- Granting elevated permissions or roles

### Never Do

- **Never commit secrets** to version control (API keys, passwords, tokens)
- **Never log sensitive data** (passwords, tokens, full credit card numbers)
- **Never trust client-side validation** as a security boundary
- **Never disable security headers** for convenience
- **Never use `eval()` or `innerHTML`** with user-provided data
- **Never store sessions in client-accessible storage** (localStorage for auth tokens)
- **Never expose stack traces** or internal error details to users

## Hardening Controls

The rules below are the workflow; a concrete implementation of each lives in [references/hardening-patterns.md](references/hardening-patterns.md). Open the section you need when you reach that code, not before.

### Injection, XSS, and access control

- Parameterize every query. Never build SQL, NoSQL, or shell commands from input strings.
- Encode output through the framework's auto-escaping. If raw HTML is unavoidable, sanitize with an allowlist sanitizer first.
- Check **authorization** on every request, not just authentication: the authenticated user must own, or be permitted on, the specific resource (A01, IDOR).

Patterns: [Injection](references/hardening-patterns.md#injection), [XSS](references/hardening-patterns.md#cross-site-scripting-xss), [Access control](references/hardening-patterns.md#broken-access-control).

### Authentication and sessions

- Hash passwords with bcrypt (≥12 rounds), scrypt, or argon2. The session secret comes from the environment, never from code.
- Session cookies are `httpOnly`, `secure`, and `sameSite: 'lax'` or `'strict'` (the CSRF defense; `'none'` sends the cookie on cross-site requests), with a bounded `maxAge`.

Pattern: [Authentication](references/hardening-patterns.md#broken-authentication).

### Headers, CORS, and responses

- Security headers on every response (helmet or the framework equivalent); CSP starts from `default-src 'self'` and is tightened, not loosened.
- CORS restricted to an explicit origin list from configuration. Never `*` with credentials.
- Strip sensitive fields (`passwordHash`, reset tokens) before any response. Error bodies are generic; internals go to server logs only.

Patterns: [Misconfiguration](references/hardening-patterns.md#security-misconfiguration), [Sensitive data exposure](references/hardening-patterns.md#sensitive-data-exposure).

### Input validation and uploads

- Validate at the boundary with a schema: allowlisted shape, lengths, enums, formats. Reject with 422 and structured details; downstream code uses only the parsed, typed value.
- Uploads: allowlist MIME types, cap size, verify content (magic bytes) when it matters. The extension proves nothing.

Patterns: [Schema validation](references/hardening-patterns.md#schema-validation-at-boundaries), [File upload](references/hardening-patterns.md#file-upload-safety).

### Server-side fetches (SSRF)

    /** The audit log is loaded from the data file but kept through a demo reset or a backup restore (the restore is logged). */
    private void importAudit(JsonObject stores) {
        if (!stores.has("auditLog")) return;
        AuditLog saved = (dataFile != null ? dataFile : new LocalStateFile(Paths.get("unused.json"))).gson().fromJson(stores.get("auditLog"), AuditLog.class);
        if (saved != null) auditLog = saved;
    }

    /** One audit entry per change request: the signed-in account (from the session), method, path, target and result. */
    private void audit(HttpExchange exchange, int status) {
        String session = exchange.getRequestHeaders().getFirst("X-Demo-Session");
        String named = String.valueOf(exchange.getRequestHeaders().getFirst("X-Demo-User") == null ? "" : exchange.getRequestHeaders().getFirst("X-Demo-User")).trim();
        String actor = twoFactor.sessionOwner(session).orElse(named.isEmpty() ? "no account" : named + " (not signed in)");
        Object target = exchange.getAttribute("auditTarget");
        auditLog.record(clockService.now().toString(), actor, exchange.getRequestMethod(), exchange.getRequestURI().getPath(),
            target == null ? "" : target.toString(), status, oldest -> {
                if (dataFile == null) return null;
                try {
                    return dataFile.writeArchive("audit", dataFile.gson().toJsonTree(oldest));
                } catch (IOException ex) {
                    System.err.println("Could not archive old audit entries: " + ex);
                    return null;
                }
            });
    }

    /** After a successful change in the local demo, write the data file. A failed save is logged, never hidden. */
    private void saveDataFile() {
        if (dataFile == null) return;
        try {
            dataFile.save(exportState());
        } catch (IOException | RuntimeException ex) {
            System.err.println("Could not save local demo data to " + dataFile.path() + ": " + ex);
        }
    }

    /** Wraps each API handler so a successful change (or a logged full view of government numbers) is saved. */
    private void context(String path, com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpHandler handler) {
        server.createContext(path, exchange -> {
            boolean change = !"GET".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod())
                || String.valueOf(exchange.getRequestURI().getRawQuery()).contains("reveal=true");
            if (!change) {
                handler.handle(exchange);
                return;
            }
            // Changes run one at a time, so the saved file is never a half-applied mix of two requests.
            synchronized (stateLock) {
                handler.handle(exchange);
                int status = exchange.getResponseCode();
                if (firebaseProjectId.isEmpty()) audit(exchange, status);
                // Saved after every change request, refused ones too, so failed sign-ins stay in the audit log.
                if (firebaseProjectId.isEmpty()) saveDataFile();
            }
        });
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        int port = Integer.parseInt(System.getenv().getOrDefault("PORT", "8080"));
        String host = System.getenv().getOrDefault("HOST", "0.0.0.0");
        AppServer app = new AppServer();
        app.start(host, port);
        Runtime.getRuntime().addShutdownHook(new Thread(app::stop));
    }

    HttpServer start(String host, int port) throws IOException {
        if (server != null) throw new IllegalStateException("server is already started");
        server = HttpServer.create(new InetSocketAddress(host, port), 0);
        context("/api/health", this::handleHealth);
        context("/api/employees", this::handleEmployees);
        context("/api/attendance", this::handleAttendance);

        context("/api/team/today", this::handleTeamToday);
        server.createContext("/", this::handleStaticFiles);
        executor = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(8);
        server.setExecutor(executor);
        server.start();
        System.out.println("MotorPH Java API listening on " + host + ":" + server.getAddress().getPort());
        System.out.println("Mode: " + (firebaseProjectId.isEmpty() ? "local synthetic demo" : "Firebase-authenticated user sandbox"));
        System.out.println("Serving browser files from " + webRoot);
        System.out.println("Local demo data: " + (dataFile == null ? "in memory only" : dataFile.path()));
        return server;
    }

    void stop() {
        // Waits for a change that is being saved, so shutting down never cuts the data file short.
        synchronized (stateLock) {
            if (server != null) {
                server.stop(0);
                server = null;
            }
        }
        if (executor != null) {
            executor.shutdownNow();
            executor = null;
        }
    }

    private void handleHealth(HttpExchange exchange) throws IOException {
        if (!"GET".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod())) {
            sendJson(exchange, 405, "{\"error\":\"Method not allowed\"}");
            return;
        }
        String mode = firebaseProjectId.isEmpty() ? "local-synthetic-demo" : "firebase-user-sandbox";
        sendJson(exchange, 200, "{\"status\":\"ok\",\"mode\":\"" + mode + "\",\"persistence\":\"" + (dataFile == null ? "memory" : "file") + "\"}");
    }

    private void handleEmployees(HttpExchange exchange) throws IOException {
        String path = exchange.getRequestURI().getPath();
        String method = exchange.getRequestMethod();
        try {
            if ("GET".equals(method)) {
                RequestServices services = servicesFor(exchange);
                if ("/api/employees".equals(path) || "/api/employees/".equals(path)) {
                    String query = queryParameter(exchange.getRequestURI().getRawQuery(), "q");
                    AccessPolicy.Actor actor = actorFor(exchange);
                    List<Employee> matches = new java.util.ArrayList<>();
                    for (Employee item : services.employeeService.searchEmployees(query)) {
                        if (AccessPolicy.canRead(actor, AccessPolicy.Area.EMPLOYEES, item.getId())) matches.add(item);
                    }
                    int total = (int) services.employeeService.listEmployees().stream()
                        .filter(item -> AccessPolicy.canRead(actor, AccessPolicy.Area.EMPLOYEES, item.getId())).count();
                    sendJson(exchange, 200, employeesToJson(matches, total));
                    return;
                }
                if (!path.startsWith("/api/employees/")) {
                    sendJson(exchange, 404, "{\"error\":\"Employee not found\"}");
                    return;
                }
                String id = path.substring("/api/employees/".length());
                if (id.isEmpty() || id.contains("/")) {
                    sendJson(exchange, 404, "{\"error\":\"Employee not found\"}");
                    return;
                }
                Optional<Employee> employee = services.employeeService.findEmployee(id);
                if (!employee.isPresent()) {
                    sendJson(exchange, 404, "{\"error\":\"Employee not found\"}");
                    return;
                }
                AccessPolicy.Actor reader = actorFor(exchange);
                guard(() -> AccessPolicy.requireRead(reader, AccessPolicy.Area.EMPLOYEES, id));

/** Branch page rows (GET /api/branches): counts only, no names. */
export function branchRows(payload) {
  if (!payload || !Array.isArray(payload.branches)) throw new TypeError('Unexpected branch response.');
  return payload.branches.map(branch => [branch.name === payload.mine ? `${branch.name} (yours)` : branch.name, String(branch.headcount), String(branch.active),
    String(branch.onLeaveToday), String(branch.clockedInNow), String(branch.onsiteToday)]);
}

/**
     * Branch pages (requirement 1, "redirect to the branch page"): counts for the signed-in person's branch (their
     * directory location), or every branch for Payroll Staff, HR and the System Admin. Counts only, no names.
     */
    private void handleBranches(HttpExchange exchange) throws IOException {
        if (!firebaseProjectId.isEmpty()) {
            sendError(exchange, 403, "Branch pages are local-demo only.");
            return;
        }
        if (!"GET".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod())) {
            sendError(exchange, 405, "Method not allowed");
            return;
        }
        try {
            AccessPolicy.Actor actor = actorFor(exchange);
            String mine = actor.explicit ? localEmployeeService.findEmployee(actor.employeeId).map(Employee::getLocation).orElse("") : "";
            boolean all = actor.role == AccessPolicy.Role.ADMIN || actor.role == AccessPolicy.Role.HR || actor.role == AccessPolicy.Role.PAYROLL;
            LocalDate today = clockService.now().toLocalDate();
            List<DemoLeaveRequest> leaves = localWorkflowStore.listLeaveRequests();
            Map<String, int[]> counts = new java.util.TreeMap<>(); // headcount, active, on leave today, clocked in, onsite
            for (Employee employee : localEmployeeService.listEmployees()) {
                String id = employee.getId();
                if (hrRecords.isSeparated(id, today)) continue;
                if (!all && !employee.getLocation().equals(mine)) continue;
                int[] row = counts.computeIfAbsent(employee.getLocation(), key -> new int[5]);
                row[0]++;
                if ("Active".equals(employee.getStatus())) row[1]++;
                boolean onLeave = leaves.stream().anyMatch(leave -> leave.getEmployeeId().equals(id) && "Approved".equals(leave.getStatus())
                    && !today.isBefore(LocalDate.parse(leave.getStartDate())) && !today.isAfter(LocalDate.parse(leave.getEndDate())));
                if (onLeave) row[2]++;
                if (clockService.openShift(id).isPresent()) row[3]++;
                if (clockService.onsiteAt(id, today).isPresent()) row[4]++;
            }
            JsonArray branches = new JsonArray();
            for (Map.Entry<String, int[]> entry : counts.entrySet()) {
                JsonObject item = new JsonObject();
                item.addProperty("name", entry.getKey());
                item.addProperty("headcount", entry.getValue()[0]);
                item.addProperty("active", entry.getValue()[1]);
                item.addProperty("onLeaveToday", entry.getValue()[2]);
                item.addProperty("clockedInNow", entry.getValue()[3]);
                item.addProperty("onsiteToday", entry.getValue()[4]);
                branches.add(item);
            }
            JsonObject response = new JsonObject();
            response.addProperty("mine", mine);
            response.addProperty("today", today.toString());
            response.add("branches", branches);
            sendJson(exchange, 200, response.toString());
        } catch (RequestException ex) {
            sendError(exchange, ex.statusCode, ex.getMessage());
        }
    }

async function apiHeaders(extra = {}) {
  const headers = { Accept: 'application/json', ...extra };
  if (state.account) headers['X-Demo-User'] = state.account.employeeId;
  if (state.session) headers['X-Demo-Session'] = state.session;
  if (state.user) {
    const token = await state.user.getIdToken();
    headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${token}`;
    headers['X-Firebase-UID'] = state.user.uid;
  }
  return headers;
}

/** Local demo 2FA: the server "texts" a code (shown here, since there is no phone); the right code gives a session. */
function askPassword(account) {
  const form = document.getElementById('password-form');
  document.getElementById('account-error').hidden = true;
  document.getElementById('account-list').hidden = true;
  form.hidden = false;
  form.dataset.employeeId = account.employeeId;
  document.getElementById('password-who').textContent = `${account.name} (${account.roleLabel})`;
  document.getElementById('signin-password').value = '';
  document.getElementById('signin-password').focus();
}

document.getElementById('password-back').addEventListener('click', () => showAccountList());
document.getElementById('password-form').addEventListener('submit', event => {
  event.preventDefault();
  startTwoFactor(accountFrom(state.accounts, event.currentTarget.dataset.employeeId), document.getElementById('signin-password').value);
});

async function startTwoFactor(account, password) {
  const form = document.getElementById('twofa-form');
  const message = document.getElementById('account-error');
  message.hidden = true;
  try {
    const challenge = await postAuth('/api/auth/2fa/start', { employeeId: account.employeeId, password });
    document.getElementById('account-list').hidden = true;
    document.getElementById('password-form').hidden = true;
    form.hidden = false;
    form.dataset.challengeId = challenge.challengeId;
    form.dataset.employeeId = account.employeeId;
    document.getElementById('twofa-sent').textContent = `${account.name}: we sent a 6-digit code to ${challenge.sentTo}. It expires at ${challenge.expiresAt}.`;
    document.getElementById('twofa-demo').textContent = `Demo only (there is no phone): your code is ${challenge.demoCode}.`;
    document.getElementById('twofa-code').value = '';
    document.getElementById('twofa-code').focus();
  } catch (error) {
    message.textContent = error.message;
    message.hidden = false;
  }
}

async function postAuth(url, body, session = '') {
  const headers = { Accept: 'application/json', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' };
  if (session) headers['X-Demo-Session'] = session;
  const response = await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers, body: JSON.stringify(body) });
  const payload = await response.json();
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(payload.error || `Request failed (${response.status})`);
  return payload;
}

function showAccountList() {
  document.getElementById('twofa-form').hidden = true;
  document.getElementById('password-form').hidden = true;
  document.getElementById('account-list').hidden = false;
}

document.getElementById('twofa-back').addEventListener('click', showAccountList);
document.getElementById('twofa-form').addEventListener('submit', async event => {
  event.preventDefault();
  const form = event.currentTarget;
  const message = document.getElementById('account-error');
  try {
    const { session, defaultPassword } = await postAuth('/api/auth/2fa/verify', { challengeId: form.dataset.challengeId, code: document.getElementById('twofa-code').value });
    state.session = session;
    state.defaultPassword = defaultPassword;
    sessionStorage.setItem(SESSION_KEY, session);
    showAccountList();
    const signedIn = accountFrom(state.accounts, form.dataset.employeeId);
    playSignInSplash(signedIn);
    enterAs(signedIn);
  } catch (error) {
    message.textContent = error.message;
    message.hidden = false;
    if (!/tries left/.test(error.message)) showAccountList();
  }
});

# Kubai Icons

这个 skill 自带完整的实现：引擎、一整套范例图标、展示页、自检脚本和静态导出脚本。你的工作是按规则写新图标，不是重写引擎。

## 包里有什么

- `PROMPT.md`：全部设计规则，每一条都是硬性要求。动手前完整读一遍。
- `src/engine.js`：引擎。颜色推导、外描边遮罩、厚度带渐变、投影和内发光滤镜、插值动画、色板都在这里。直接复用，不要改。
- `src/icons.js`：范例图标。新图标按同样的格式追加。
- `src/app.js`、`index.html`：展示页。`ORDER` 决定展示哪些图标、按什么顺序排。
- `scripts/check.mjs`：自检脚本。在无头 Chrome 里截出静止、悬停、悬停过程的中间帧、24px、28px 和所有色板，并读出每一页的脚本报错。临时文件都放在输出目录里，跑完自动清理。
- `scripts/export.mjs`：静态导出。把图标渲染成不依赖脚本和样式表的独立 SVG 文件，可以指定色板、主色和静止或悬停状态。

## 流程

1. 读 `PROMPT.md`。
2. 确定交付形式。用户没说清楚时先问一句：
   - 动态（默认）：SVG + JS，悬停时形变，靠 `src/engine.js` 在页面里运行。适合网页和能跑 JS 的界面。
   - 静态：独立的 `.svg` 文件，没有动效，任何地方都能用：设计工具、原生 App、文档、`<img>`。用户提到"切图""SVG 文件""放进 Figma""App 里用"等，就是要静态。
   - 两者都要：按动态做，最后再导出一份静态。
3. 确定在哪里做：
   - 新做一套：把本 skill 的 `index.html`、`src/`、`scripts/` 复制到目标位置（一个新目录或新仓库），在那份副本里工作。保留每个文件开头的版权声明；`PROMPT.md` 和 `SKILL.md` 只留在 skill 里，不要复制进去（见 `LICENSE` 第 3 条）。
   - 往已有的一套里加：直接在那份 `src/icons.js` 里追加。
   - 只要静态：同样复制一份到工作目录里画，最后只把导出的 SVG 交给用户。
4. 读产品代码，列出功能。动态版每个功能写一句"物体 + 悬停动作"；静态版只需要确定物体（`PROMPT.md` 第 1 节）。
5. 每写一个图标之前，先在 `src/icons.js` 里找一两个结构最接近的范例读一遍（例如翻开的东西看信封和日历，切出前片的看下载和上传，会旋转的看齿轮和星标），照它们的写法来。
6. 把名字加进 `src/app.js` 的 `ORDER`。用不到的范例，不放进 `ORDER` 就不会显示。
7. 运行自检，把新图标和几个现有图标放在一起看：

   ```bash
   node scripts/check.mjs --only 新图标A,新图标B --with 文件夹,邮件,下载
   ```

   截图在 `check-out/`。逐条对照 `PROMPT.md` 第 10 节的清单检查；脚本报出错误时先修错误。往复类动作看 `frames.png`；查细缝时加 `--scale 3`；查浅主色上的标记时加 `--accent #F59E0B`，把所有图标换成同一个主色。不加 `--only` 就检查整套。静态版看 `rest.png`、`size-24.png`、`size-28.png` 和 `palettes.png` 就够了。
8. 改到全部通过后，更新 README 里提到的图标数量，以及展示页每个断点的列数（列数要能整除图标总数，断点可以增删）。
9. 要静态时，导出到用户指定的目录，并告诉用户用的是哪个色板：

   ```bash
   node scripts/export.mjs --only 新图标A,新图标B --palette 彩色 --out 目标目录
   ```

   `--palette` 按名字选色板（彩色、蓝灰、青瓷、薄荷、薰衣草、杏色、黑色），`--accent #hex` 把所有图标换成一个主色，`--state hover` 导出悬停结束时的样子，`--size` 设定像素尺寸，`--pad` 给投影留出边距。每个图标一个 `名字.svg`。

## 环境

- Node 18 以上，以及 Chrome。浏览器路径可以用环境变量 `CHROME` 覆盖。
- 所有检查都在无头模式下进行，不会打开任何可见窗口，也不会动用户正在用的浏览器。

// Copyright (c) 2026 Kubai087. Licensed under the Kubai Icons License; see LICENSE.
// The icon set. Each entry: svg(u) builds the layers, target(hover, state) returns the
// numbers for rest or hover, draw(p, E) writes the interpolated numbers back. A contributed
// icon also names its designer's GitHub handle in `by`.

// ---------- Icons ----------
// Fills: u.lo(h) / u.up(h) carry the thin bottom band. Use them only on a flat-bottomed
// rectangle of height h whose bottom is clear: nothing within about 3 units of the edge
// and the piece itself not short. Everything else, and curved shapes, use u.loS / u.upS.
// Marks: on a mid-tone (back) body they are white; on a light (front) body or white
// content they take the deep tint; a supporting object laid over the subject (the
// lens) is deep so it reads as separate. Weights: content lines 1.6, glyphs 2.2.
const OL = 'class="ol" data-t="stroke:#5393FF"';
const LINE = 'class="ln" data-t="stroke:#D3E2FC"';

const FOLDER_BACK_R = [KR, 1.4, 1.4, KR, KR, KR];
// Keylines (fills; outside strokes add 1 all round), all centred on (15.5, 12.5) and scaled from the folder's 23-wide body
// (Material's 20 / 18 / 20×16 grid × 1.15): circle Ø23, square 20.6, landscape 23×18.4,
// portrait 18.4×23. Outlines sit 1 unit outside a shape; a coloured band around white
// content keeps 2+ units or is dropped so the content meets the edge.
const TRASH_LID = rp([[5.4, 6.6], [5.4, 4], [12.4, 4], [12.4, 1.6], [18.6, 1.6], [18.6, 4], [25.6, 4], [25.6, 6.6]], [1, 1, 0.5, 0.8, 0.8, 0.5, 1, 1]);
const GEAR = gear(6, 11.4, 9);
  const MAIL_T = 3.3;
const today = new Date();
const tomorrow = new Date(today.getTime() + 86400000);

// A capsule ring centred on the origin: outer w×h, wall t (fill-rule evenodd).
const capsuleRing = (w, h, t) => rr(-w / 2, -h / 2, w, h, h / 2) + rr(-w / 2 + t, -h / 2 + t, w - 2 * t, h - 2 * t, (h - 2 * t) / 2);
const LINK_RING = capsuleRing(15.6, 9.6, 2.8);
// An arc of radius r round the origin from angle a0 to a1 (degrees, clockwise), and a
// solid arrowhead whose base covers the arc's end. Strokes never overlap one another,
// so the head stays crisp instead of clotting where strokes would cross.
function arcArrow(a0, a1, r) {
  const rad = (d) => d * Math.PI / 180;
  const pt = (a) => [r * Math.cos(rad(a)), r * Math.sin(rad(a))];
  const s = pt(a0), e = pt(a1);
  const t = [-Math.sin(rad(a1)), Math.cos(rad(a1))], n = [Math.cos(rad(a1)), Math.sin(rad(a1))];
  const tip = [e[0] + t[0] * 3, e[1] + t[1] * 3];

// Copyright (c) 2026 Kubai087. Licensed under the Kubai Icons License; see LICENSE.
// Kubai Icons: colour derivation, motion, geometry, gradients and filters, and the
// runtime that mounts, paints and animates an icon. Loaded before icons.js and app.js.

// ---------- Color: the same tint rule as Lumno's tintFolderColor ----------
const REF = [83, 147, 255];
const hex = (c) => '#' + c.map((v) => Math.max(0, Math.min(255, Math.round(v))).toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join('').toUpperCase();
const rgb = (h) => [1, 3, 5].map((i) => parseInt(h.slice(i, i + 2), 16));
function tint(src, sel) {
  const s = rgb(src);
  return hex([0, 1, 2].map((i) => {
    const amt = i === 2 ? (s[0] - REF[0]) / (255 - REF[0]) : (s[i] - REF[i]) / (255 - REF[i]);
    return amt >= 0 ? sel[i] + (255 - sel[i]) * amt : sel[i] * (1 + amt);
  }));
}

// ---------- Motion: 460ms, cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1), number by number ----------
function bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2) {
  const cx = 3 * x1, bx = 3 * (x2 - x1) - cx, ax = 1 - cx - bx;
  const cy = 3 * y1, by = 3 * (y2 - y1) - cy, ay = 1 - cy - by;
  const sx = (t) => ((ax * t + bx) * t + cx) * t;
  const sy = (t) => ((ay * t + by) * t + cy) * t;
  const dx = (t) => (3 * ax * t + 2 * bx) * t + cx;
  return (x) => {
    if (x <= 0) return 0;
    if (x >= 1) return 1;
    let t = x;
    for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
      const e = sx(t) - x;
      if (Math.abs(e) < 1e-5) break;
      const d = dx(t);
      if (Math.abs(d) < 1e-6) break;
      t -= e / d;
    }
    return sy(t);
  };
}
const EASE = bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1);
const DUR = 460;
let REDUCED = false;
try { REDUCED = matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches; } catch (e) {}
function interp(a, b, t) {
  if (typeof b === 'number') return typeof a === 'number' ? a + (b - a) * t : b;
  if (Array.isArray(b)) return b.map((v, i) => interp(a ? a[i] : v, v, t));
  if (b && typeof b === 'object') {
    const o = {};
    for (const k in b) o[k] = interp(a ? a[k] : undefined, b[k], t);
    return o;
  }
  return b;
}

// ---------- Geometry. Canvas 31×29, live area x 4–27 / y 2–23, baseline y=23. ----------
// Fill radii. Outside strokes add 1, so the corner you see is 3.2, the folder's.
const KR = 2.2, CR = 1.2;
const f = (n) => +n.toFixed(3);
const R = (x, y, w, h) => [[x, y], [x + w, y], [x + w, y + h], [x, y + h]];
// `full` lets a corner use a whole edge when its neighbour on that edge is small.
function rp(pts, r, full) {
  const n = pts.length;
  let d = '';
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    const v = pts[i], a = pts[(i + n - 1) % n], b = pts[(i + 1) % n];
    const ri = Array.isArray(r) ? r[i] : r;
    const la = Math.hypot(a[0] - v[0], a[1] - v[1]) || 1e-6;
    const lb = Math.hypot(b[0] - v[0], b[1] - v[1]) || 1e-6;
    const lim = full ? 1 : 0.5;
    const k1 = Math.min(ri, la * lim) / la, k2 = Math.min(ri, lb * lim) / lb;
    d += (i ? 'L' : 'M') + f(v[0] + (a[0] - v[0]) * k1) + ' ' + f(v[1] + (a[1] - v[1]) * k1)
      + 'Q' + f(v[0]) + ' ' + f(v[1]) + ' ' + f(v[0] + (b[0] - v[0]) * k2) + ' ' + f(v[1] + (b[1] - v[1]) * k2);

// ---------- Runtime ----------
const SVG_NS = 'http://www.w3.org/2000/svg';
const ICON_VIEWBOX = '0 -2 31 29';
const runtime = { palette: null };

// Builds one icon inside `host` and returns its live instance.
function mountIcon(icon, i, host) {
  const k = 'i' + i;
  const u = makeU(k);
  const body = icon.svg(u);
  host.innerHTML = `<svg viewBox="${ICON_VIEWBOX}" fill="none" aria-hidden="true">${defs(k, u.grads)}${body}</svg>`;
  const svg = host.querySelector('svg');
  const E = {};
  svg.querySelectorAll('[data-n]').forEach((el) => { E[el.dataset.n] = el; });
  const tints = [...svg.querySelectorAll('[data-t]')].map((el) => { const [attr, src] = el.dataset.t.split(':'); return [el, attr, src]; });
  // Outside strokes: each 2-unit outline is masked by its own shape, so only the outer
  // 1 unit shows and the fill keeps its full size.
  const defsEl = svg.querySelector('defs');
  const clips = [...svg.querySelectorAll('.ol')].map((el, j) => {
    const mask = document.createElementNS(SVG_NS, 'mask');
    mask.id = `ol-${k}-${j}`;
    at(mask, { maskUnits: 'userSpaceOnUse', x: -40, y: -40, width: 111, height: 109 });
    mask.innerHTML = '<rect x="-40" y="-40" width="111" height="109" fill="#fff"/>';
    const shape = document.createElementNS(SVG_NS, 'path');
    shape.setAttribute('fill', '#000');
    shape.setAttribute('fill-rule', el.getAttribute('fill-rule') || 'nonzero');
    mask.appendChild(shape);
    defsEl.appendChild(mask);
    el.setAttribute('mask', `url(#${mask.id})`);
    return [el, shape];
  });
  const inst = {
    icon, i, E, tints, clips,
    whites: [...svg.querySelectorAll('[data-w]')],
    pures: [...svg.querySelectorAll('[data-pure]')],
    shadow: svg.querySelector('[data-sh]'),
    s: {}, raf: 0, painted: '', hover: 0
  };
  inst.cur = targetOf(inst);
  render(inst);
  return inst;
}

function targetOf(inst) {
  const pal = runtime.palette;
  const h = Boolean(inst.hover > 0 || inst.pin || inst.demo);
  const t = inst.icon.target(h, inst.s);
  t.c = rgb(pal.colors[inst.i]);
  t.e = rgb((pal.edges || pal.colors)[inst.i]);
  return t;
}

function render(inst) {
  const p = inst.cur;
  inst.icon.draw(p, inst.E, inst);
  for (const [el, shape] of inst.clips) {
    const d = el.getAttribute('d');
    if (d && shape.getAttribute('d') !== d) shape.setAttribute('d', d);
  }
  const deep = Boolean(runtime.palette.deepMarks);
  const key = hex(p.c) + hex(p.e) + deep;
  if (inst.painted === key) return;
  inst.painted = key;
  // Gradients and light marks follow the fill colour; outlines and deep marks follow the
  // edge colour, which stays strong when the fill is lifted.
  const pick = (src) => (rgb(src)[0] <= REF[0] ? p.e : p.c);
  for (const [el, attr, src] of inst.tints) el.setAttribute(attr, tint(src, el.tagName !== 'stop' ? pick(src) : p.c));
  // White marks sit on mid-tone bodies; on a light body they turn deep to stay legible.
  for (const el of inst.whites) el.setAttribute(el.dataset.w, deep ? tint('#2F6FE0', p.e) : '#fff');
  // Large solid fills: solid normally; a light palette fades them from near-white at the top.
  for (const stop of inst.pures) {
    const base = tint(stop.dataset.src, pick(stop.dataset.src));
    stop.setAttribute('stop-color', deep && stop.dataset.pure === '0' ? soften(base, 0.72) : base);
  }
  const sh = rgb(tint('#8AB6FF', p.c));
  inst.shadow.setAttribute('values', `0 0 0 0 ${f(sh[0] / 255)} 0 0 0 0 ${f(sh[1] / 255)} 0 0 0 0 ${f(sh[2] / 255)} 0 0 0 0.21 0`);
}

// Starts from what is on screen, so reversing mid-way carries on smoothly.
function go(inst) {
  const to = targetOf(inst);
  cancelAnimationFrame(inst.raf);
  if (REDUCED) { inst.cur = to; render(inst); return; }
  const from = inst.cur, t0 = performance.now();
  const tick = (now) => {
    const t = Math.min(1, (now - t0) / DUR);
    inst.cur = interp(from, to, EASE(t));
    render(inst);
    if (t < 1) inst.raf = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
  };
  inst.raf = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
}

package ph.motorph.web;

import java.util.Objects;

/** A small employee view model for the first synthetic-data prototype. */
public final class Employee {
    private final String id;
    private final String name;
    private final String department;
    private final String role;
    private final String location;
    private final String status;

    public Employee(String id, String name, String department, String role, String location, String status) {
        this.id = requireText(id, "id");
        this.name = requireText(name, "name");
        this.department = requireText(department, "department");
        this.role = requireText(role, "role");
        this.location = requireText(location, "location");
        this.status = requireText(status, "status");
    }

    private static String requireText(String value, String field) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(value, field + " must not be null");
        if (value.trim().isEmpty()) throw new IllegalArgumentException(field + " must not be blank");
        return value.trim();
    }

    public String getId() { return id; }
    public String getName() { return name; }
    public String getDepartment() { return department; }
    public String getRole() { return role; }
    public String getLocation() { return location; }
    public String getStatus() { return status; }
}

package ph.motorph.web;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.NoSuchElementException;
import java.util.Optional;

/** Process-memory store containing only fictional demo employees. */
public final class InMemoryEmployeeStore implements MutableEmployeeStore {
    private final Map<String, Employee> employees = new LinkedHashMap<>();

    public InMemoryEmployeeStore() {
        addFixture(new Employee("DEMO-001", "Mara Rivera", "People Operations", "HR Coordinator", "Makati", "Active"));
        addFixture(new Employee("DEMO-002", "Eli Santos", "Finance", "Payroll Associate", "Taguig", "Active"));
        addFixture(new Employee("DEMO-003", "Noa Reyes", "Operations", "Operations Lead", "Quezon City", "On leave"));
        addFixture(new Employee("DEMO-004", "Jae Cruz", "Operations", "Operations Associate", "Pasig", "Active"));
        addFixture(new Employee("DEMO-005", "Lia Torres", "IT", "System Administrator", "Makati", "Active"));
    }

    @Override
    public synchronized List<Employee> findAll() {
        return new ArrayList<>(employees.values());
    }

    @Override
    public synchronized Optional<Employee> findById(String id) {
        return Optional.ofNullable(id == null ? null : employees.get(id.trim()));
    }

    @Override
    public synchronized Employee create(Employee employee) {
        if (employees.containsKey(employee.getId())) throw new IllegalStateException("Employee ID already exists.");
        employees.put(employee.getId(), employee);
        return employee;
    }

    @Override
    public synchronized Employee update(Employee employee) {
        if (!employees.containsKey(employee.getId())) throw new NoSuchElementException("Employee not found.");
        employees.put(employee.getId(), employee);
        return employee;
    }

package ph.motorph.o_oop;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.Locale;
import java.util.Optional;
import java.util.UUID;
import java.util.NoSuchElementException;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;

/** Employee use cases, separated from HTTP handling and the storage implementation. */
public final class EmployeeService {
    private final EmployeeStore store;

    public EmployeeService(EmployeeStore store) {
        if (store == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("store must not be null");
        this.store = store;
    }

    public List<Employee> listEmployees() {
        return store.findAll();
    }

    public Optional<Employee> findEmployee(String id) {
        return store.findById(id == null ? null : id.trim());
    }

    /** Creates a fictional directory record inside the current owner's sandbox only. */
    public Employee createEmployee(String name, String department, String role, String location, String status) {
        MutableEmployeeStore mutable = mutableStore();
        Employee employee = validatedEmployee("DEMO-" + UUID.randomUUID().toString().replace("-", "")
            .substring(0, 12).toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT), name, department, role, location, status);
        return mutable.create(employee);
    }

    /** Updates only fields present in the synthetic directory model; no payroll/PII fields exist here. */
    public Employee updateEmployee(String id, String name, String department, String role, String location, String status) {
        String safeId = id == null ? "" : id.trim();
        if (!safeId.matches("DEMO-(?:[0-9]{3}|[A-F0-9]{12})")) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Employee ID is invalid.");
        if (!findEmployee(safeId).isPresent()) throw new NoSuchElementException("Employee not found.");
        return mutableStore().update(validatedEmployee(safeId, name, department, role, location, status));
    }

    private MutableEmployeeStore mutableStore() {
        if (!(store instanceof MutableEmployeeStore)) throw new IllegalStateException("This employee store is read-only.");
        return (MutableEmployeeStore) store;
    }

    private static Employee validatedEmployee(String id, String name, String department,
            String role, String location, String status) {
        return new Employee(id, requiredDirectoryText(name, "Name"), requiredDirectoryText(department, "Department"),
            requiredDirectoryText(role, "Role"), requiredDirectoryText(location, "Location"), validStatus(status));
    }

    private static String requiredDirectoryText(String value, String field) {
        String text = value == null ? "" : value.trim();
        if (text.isEmpty()) throw new IllegalArgumentException(field + " is required.");
        if (text.length() > 100) throw new IllegalArgumentException(field + " must be 100 characters or fewer.");
        return text;
    }

That is far more precision than a * nearest-branch decision between offices 10–15 km apart needs. */ public final class Locality { private Locality() {} /** Lower-case "city" → {latitude, longitude}. */ private static final Map<String, double[]> PLACES = new LinkedHashMap<>(); [NODE 14814]
More important: the results are meaningless — nearly every team centroid is hundreds of km away from all four branches (because the "cities" are nationwide fictional), so nearest-branch collapses to "Taguig" by coincidence (Taguig just happens to be the southernmost of the four). The centroid of e.g. De Leon's team (Visayas/Mindanao) is 384km from Taguig. The rule still yields a deterministic answer but it's semantically garbage.

[NODE 14815]
The brief says: "If an address cannot be geocoded reliably, use the most precise shared locality supported by the CSV... mark the assignment as approximate in engineering documentation rather than pretending it is exact."

[NODE 14816]
So the honest approach: the CSV's addresses are not real Metro Manila addresses at all (they're synthetic nationwide streets). What the file DOES support: the province/city names. Given branches exist only in Metro Manila (Makati/QC/Taguig/Pasig), the nearest-branch rule applied to nationwide addresses is degenerate.

[NODE 14817]
Better approach that is both faithful and sane: compute the centroid of each leaf team from municipality coordinates, and pick the branch nearest the centroid. But since the branches are all in Metro Manila and teams are scattered nationwide, tie-breaking is essentially arbitrary.

[NODE 14818]
Alternative interpretation that's more useful: the branch set should perhaps not be limited to Metro Manila. But brief says use the branch list already present in Claude's implementation — which is effectively "whatever the location strings were": Makati, Taguig, Quezon City, Pasig (the seeded employees' locations). That's the set. So those four branches.

[NODE 14819]

package ph.motorph.o_oop;

import com.google.gson.JsonElement;
import com.google.gson.JsonObject;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Optional;

/** User-scoped demo employee records read through the Firestore REST API. */
public final class FirestoreEmployeeStore implements MutableEmployeeStore {
    private final FirestoreRestClient client;

    public FirestoreEmployeeStore(FirestoreRestClient client) {
        if (client == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("client must not be null");
        this.client = client;
    }

    @Override
    public List<Employee> findAll() {
        List<Employee> employees = new ArrayList<>();
        for (JsonObject document : client.listDocuments(client.userCollection("demoEmployees"))) {
            employees.add(fromDocument(document));
        }
        return employees;
    }

    @Override
    public Optional<Employee> findById(String id) {
        if (id == null) return Optional.empty();
        return findAll().stream().filter(employee -> employee.getId().equals(id)).findFirst();
    }

    @Override
    public Employee create(Employee employee) {
        if (!client.createDocument(client.userCollection("demoEmployees"), employee.getId(), employeeFields(employee))) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Employee ID already exists; refresh the directory and retry.");
        }
        return employee;
    }

[NODE 14887]
fields.add("department", stringField(employee.getDepartment()));
        fields.add("role", stringField(employee.getRole()));
        fields.add("location", stringField(employee.getLocation()));
        fields.add("status", stringField(employee.getStatus()));

    private static JsonObject stringField(String value) {
        JsonObject field = new JsonObject();
        field.addProperty("stringValue", value);
        return field;
    }

    private static Employee fromDocument(JsonObject document) {
        JsonObject fields = document.has("fields") ? document.getAsJsonObject("fields") : new JsonObject();
        return new Employee(
            stringValue(fields, "id"), stringValue(fields, "name"), stringValue(fields, "department"),
            stringValue(fields, "role"), stringValue(fields, "location"), stringValue(fields, "status"));
    }

    static String stringValue(JsonObject fields, String name) {
        JsonElement element = fields.get(name);
        if (element == null || !element.isJsonObject()) return "";
        JsonElement value = element.getAsJsonObject().get("stringValue");
        return value == null || value.isJsonNull() ? "" : value.getAsString();
    }
}

A naive * {@code split(",")} turns one employee into three. */ public final class CsvLine { private CsvLine() {} public static List<String> fields(String line) { List<String> out = new ArrayList<>(); StringBuilder cell = new StringBuilder(); boolean quoted = false; for (int i = 0; i < line.length(); i++) { char c = line.charAt(i); if (quoted) { if (c == '"') { if (i + 1 < line.length() && line.charAt(i + 1) == '"') { cell.append('"'); i++; } else quoted = false; } else cell.append(c); } else if (c == '"') { quoted = true; } else if (c == ',') { out.add(cell.toString()); cell.setLength(0); } else if (c != '\r') { cell.append(c); } } out.add(cell.toString()); return out; } /** Money as the file writes it: "53,500" or "1,500.00" → 53500.00. } if (counted == 0) { notes.add(team + ": no recognised municipality, assigned Main Branch."); return Branch.MAIN.label(); } double[] centre = { lat / counted, lon / counted }; Branch best = null; double bestDistance = Double.MAX_VALUE; # Compile every main source (all packages under ph/motorph) and, optionally, the tests.

mkdir -p target/classes target/test-classes
find src/main/java -name '*.java' > target/main-sources.txt
# Resources travel with the classes: the employee file is read from the classpath at startup.

A **leaf team** is a supervisor who has direct reports and no supervisor reporting to them. Each leaf team gets one branch. 2. The branch is the **nearest existing office to the team's geographic centre**, where the centre is the mean of its members' home municipalities. 3. **Supervisors who lead other supervisors**, and **every C-level executive**, go to **Main Branch**. 4. Members inherit their leaf team's branch. ## The honest caveat about the addresses The file's addresses are street-level but fictional, and they are spread across the whole country — Batanes to Sulu. Nobody can geocode them exactly, so the finest truthful grain is the **municipality or city** each address names. `Locality.java` holds approximate municipality centres for those places; the centroid is the mean of those. The consequence is worth stating plainly: **most teams' centroids are hundreds of kilometres from all four offices.** The rule still decides (there is always a nearest), but for those teams it is deciding by a few kilometres out of several hundred — that is, by little more than chance. The one team where the answer is genuinely local is the executive team, whose centroid sits 4 km from Makati. import org.bouncycastle.crypto.params.Argon2Parameters; /** * Password storage: <b>Argon2id</b> over {@code salt + password + pepper}, with a fresh random salt per account. * * Three properties this class is responsible for, and how each is met: * <ul> * <li><b>Two people with the same password get different stored values.</b> Every hash carries 16 random bytes of * salt, so the derived keys differ even when the passwords do not.</li> * <li><b>The pepper never touches the database, and never comes from the person.</b> It is read once from the * environment ({@link PasswordPolicy#PEPPER_VARIABLE}); if it is missing the application refuses to start. * It is not derived from an employee number, name, birthday, email or timestamp.</li> * <li><b>Comparison is constant-time</b> and performed by this class, never by string equality on the caller's * side.</li> * </ul> * * The stored format is self-describing, so parameters can be raised later without invalidating old hashes: * {@code argon2id$v=19$m=65536,t=3,p=1$<salt-b64>$<hash-b64>}. */ public final class PasswordHasher { private static final int VERSION = 19; // Argon2 version 1.3 private static final int MEMORY_KIB = 64 * 1024; // 64 MiB — deliberate, and the reason login is not instant private static final int ITERATIONS = 3; private static final int PARALLELISM = 1; private static final int HASH_BYTES = 32; private static final int SALT_BYTES = 16; private static final SecureRandom RANDOM = new SecureRandom(); private final byte[] pepperBytes; public PasswordHasher(String pepper) { if (pepper == null || pepper.trim().length() < 32) { throw new IllegalStateException(PasswordPolicy.PEPPER_VARIABLE + " must be set to at least 32 characters; " + "refusing to start with a weak or missing pepper."); } this.pepperBytes = pepper.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8); } /** Hash for storage. The result includes the salt and parameters; the pepper is not recoverable from it. */ public String hash(String password) { byte[] salt = new byte[SALT_BYTES]; RANDOM.nextBytes(salt); byte[] digest = derive(password, salt, MEMORY_KIB, ITERATIONS, PARALLELISM); Base64.Encoder b64 = Base64.getEncoder().withoutPadding(); return "argon2id$v=" + VERSION + "$m=" + MEMORY_KIB + ",t=" + ITERATIONS + ",p=" + PARALLELISM + "$" + b64.encodeToString(salt) + "$" + b64.encodeToString(digest); } /** True when {@code password} reproduces the stored hash. Wrong password and malformed hash both return false. */ public boolean verify(String password, String stored) { if (password == null || stored == null) return false; String[] parts = stored.split("\\$"); return MessageDigest.isEqual(expected, actual); } catch (RuntimeException malformed) { return false; } } /** True when a stored value needs re-hashing because the parameters have since been raised. */ public boolean needsRehash(String stored) { return stored == null || !stored.startsWith("argon2id$v=" + VERSION + "$m=" + MEMORY_KIB + ",t=" + ITERATIONS + ",p=" + PARALLELISM + "$"); } private byte[] derive(String password, byte[] salt, int memoryKib, int iterations, int parallelism) { // salt ‖ pepper: the pepper is concatenated into the salt input so a stolen table cannot be attacked // offline without it, while the per-account salt keeps identical passwords distinct. byte[] passwordBytes = password.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8); Argon2Parameters params = new Argon2Parameters.Builder(Argon2Parameters.ARGON2_id) .withVersion(VERSION) .withMemoryAsKB(memoryKib) .withIterations(iterations) .withParallelism(parallelism) .withSalt(combinedSalt) .build(); Argon2BytesGenerator generator = new Argon2BytesGenerator(); generator.init(params); byte[] out = new byte[HASH_BYTES]; generator.generateBytes(passwordBytes, out); Arrays.fill(passwordBytes, (byte) 0); return out; } /** * A PBKDF2 stand-in used only when the pepper is deliberately absent in a test process. It is not the * production path and is flagged as such wherever it appears. */ static String testOnlyHash(String password, String saltText) { try { byte[] salt = saltText.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8); PBEKeySpec spec = new PBEKeySpec(password.toCharArray(), salt, 1000, 256); byte[] key = SecretKeyFactory.getInstance("PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256").generateSecret(spec).getEncoded(); return Base64.getEncoder().withoutPadding().encodeToString(key); } catch (Exception ex) { throw new IllegalStateException(ex); } } } JAVA echo ok

It must be an unpredictable value supplied by the deployment (environment * variable or secret manager) — never derived from an employee number, name, birthday, email, location or time, * because all of those are either guessable or already in the database. */ public static final String PEPPER_VARIABLE = "MOTORPH_PASSWORD_PEPPER"; public static final int MIN_LENGTH = 12; private PasswordPolicy() {} /** Reasons the password is unacceptable; empty when it is fine. */ public static java.util.List<String> problems(String password) { java.util.List<String> problems = new java.util.ArrayList<>(); String value = password == null ? $ cd /home/user/motorph-v3 && cat > src/main/java/ph/motorph/sp_secpol/SessionStore.java <<'JAVA' package ph.motorph.sp_secpol; import java.security.SecureRandom; import java.time.Clock; import java.time.Duration; import java.time.Instant; import java.util.ArrayList; import java.util.Base64; import java.util.LinkedHashMap; import java.util.List; import java.util.Map; import java.util.Optional; /** * Server-side session table with lazy, request-driven expiry. * * The brief's three requirements, and how they are met without a background loop: * <ol> * <li><b>Opaque token.</b> 32 bytes from {@link SecureRandom}, base64url encoded. It contains no employee number, * timestamp or expiry — nothing a holder could decode or forge.</li> * <li><b>Stored hashed.</b> Only SHA-256 of the token is kept. The browser holds the raw token in an HttpOnly * cookie; the server cannot leak what it does not have.</li> * <li><b>Expiry checked on every protected request</b> ({@link #resolve}), never on a timer. Expired rows are * pruned on write and by {@link #sweep}, which a caller may run daily; correctness does not depend on it.</li> * </ol> * * Sessions are also invalidated by password changes ({@link #revokeAllFor}) so a changed password cannot leave an * older browser signed in. */ public final class SessionStore { public static final int IDLE_MINUTES = 15; public static final int ABSOLUTE_HOURS = 8; private static final SecureRandom RANDOM = new SecureRandom(); private final Map<String, SessionRecord> byTokenHash = java.util.Collections.synchronizedMap(new LinkedHashMap<>()); private final Clock clock; private final int idleMinutes, absoluteHours; public SessionStore() { this(Clock.systemDefaultZone(), IDLE_MINUTES, ABSOLUTE_HOURS); } public SessionStore(Clock clock) { this(clock, IDLE_MINUTES, ABSOLUTE_HOURS); } public SessionStore(Clock clock, int idleMinutes, int absoluteHours) { this.clock = clock; this.idleMinutes = idleMinutes; this.absoluteHours = absoluteHours; } public int idleMinutes() { return idleMinutes; } public int absoluteHours() { return absoluteHours; } /** Issues a session and returns the raw token — the only moment it exists outside the browser. */ public String issue(String employeeId) { byte[] raw = new byte[32]; RANDOM.nextBytes(raw); String token = Base64.getUrlEncoder().withoutPadding().encodeToString(raw); Instant now = clock.instant(); byTokenHash.put(hash(token), new SessionRecord(hash(token), employeeId, now, now.plus(Duration.ofHours(absoluteHours)), idleMinutes)); prune(now); return token; } /** * Resolves a token to its owner, or empty when the token is unknown, revoked, idle-expired or past its hard * deadline. A successful resolve counts as activity. */ public Optional<SessionRecord> resolve(String token) { if (token == null || token.isEmpty()) return Optional.empty(); SessionRecord record = byTokenHash.get(hash(token)); if (record == null) return Optional.empty(); Instant now = clock.instant(); String expired = record.expiredReason(now); if (expired != null) { byTokenHash.remove(record.tokenHash); return Optional.empty(); } record.touch(now); return Optional.of(record); } /** Sign-out: the session stops working immediately, not when the cookie happens to be dropped. */ public void revoke(String token) { if (token == null) return; byTokenHash.remove(hash(token)); } /** Password change: every other session for the account dies with it. */ public int revokeAllFor(String employeeId) { int removed = 0; List<String> keys = new ArrayList<>(byTokenHash.keySet()); for (String key : keys) { SessionRecord record = byTokenHash.get(key); if (record != null && record.employeeId.equals(employeeId)) { byTokenHash.remove(key); removed++; } } return removed; } /** Remaining seconds on the idle clock, for the browser's countdown. */ public long idleSecondsLeft(String token) { SessionRecord record = byTokenHash.get(hash(token)); if (record == null) return 0; long seconds = Duration.between(clock.instant(), record.lastActive().plusSeconds(idleMinutes * 60L)).getSeconds(); return Math.max(0, seconds); } /** Housekeeping only; expiry is already enforced by {@link #resolve}. */ public int sweep() { Instant now = clock.instant(); int before = byTokenHash.size(); prune(now); return before - byTokenHash.size(); } public int size() { return byTokenHash.size(); } private void prune(Instant now) { byTokenHash.values().removeIf(record -> record.expiredReason(now) != null); } /** SHA-256 of the token, hex. Storing the hash means a database dump cannot be replayed as a login. */ static String hash(String token) { try { byte[] digest = java.security.MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256").digest(token.getBytes(java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.UTF_8)); StringBuilder hex = new StringBuilder(digest.length * 2); for (byte b : digest) hex.append(String.format("%02x", b)); return hex.toString(); } catch (java.security.NoSuchAlgorithmException ex) { throw new IllegalStateException("SHA-256 is required", ex); } } } JAVA cat > src/main/java/ph/motorph/sp_secpol/Account.java <<'JAVA' package ph.motorph.sp_secpol; /** * A sign-in account: an employee number, the stored Argon2id hash and the first-login flag. * * The employee number is the login name. There is no email, no external identity provider, and no second account * per role — one person, one account, whatever their role. */ public final class Account { public final String employeeId; private String passwordHash; private boolean mustChangePassword; private int failedAttempts; private String lockedUntil; // ISO instant, empty when not locked private String lastSignIn; // ISO instant, empty when never public Account(String employeeId, String passwordHash, boolean mustChangePassword) { this.employeeId = employeeId; this.passwordHash = passwordHash; this.mustChangePassword = mustChangePassword; this.lockedUntil = ""; this.lastSignIn = ""; } public String passwordHash() { return passwordHash; } public boolean mustChangePassword() { return mustChangePassword; } public int failedAttempts() { return failedAttempts; } public String lockedUntil() { return lockedUntil; } public String lastSignIn() { return lastSignIn; } void replaceHash(String newHash) { this.passwordHash = newHash; this.mustChangePassword = false; } void recordFailure(int maxAttempts, java.time.Instant now, java.time.Duration lockFor) { failedAttempts++; if (failedAttempts >= maxAttempts) { lockedUntil = now.plus(lockFor).toString(); failedAttempts = 0; } } void recordSuccess(java.time.Instant now) { failedAttempts = 0; lockedUntil = ""; lastSignIn = now.toString(); } boolean locked(java.time.Instant now) { if (lockedUntil == null || lockedUntil.isEmpty()) return false; return now.isBefore(java.time.Instant.parse(lockedUntil)); } } JAVA echo ok

$ cd /home/user/motorph-v3 && cat > src/main/java/ph/motorph/sp_secpol/CredentialStore.java <<'JAVA' package ph.motorph.sp_secpol; import java.time.Clock; import java.time.Duration; import java.time.Instant; import java.util.ArrayList; import java.util.LinkedHashMap; import java.util.List; import java.util.Map; import java.util.Optional; /** * The account table: who can sign in, with what hash, and whether they have changed their first password. * * Provisioning is done from the employee file, so there is exactly one account per employee number and no account * for anyone who is not on the roster. A missing employee is not created on demand — that would let a typo mint an * account. * * Failed sign-ins are throttled per account with a growing lockout. The error the caller sees is identical for * "no such employee" and "wrong password", so the form cannot be used to enumerate who works here. */ public final class CredentialStore { public static final int MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5; public static final Duration LOCK_FOR = Duration.ofMinutes(15); private final Map<String, Account> accounts = new LinkedHashMap<>(); private final PasswordHasher hasher; private final Clock clock; public CredentialStore(PasswordHasher hasher) { this(hasher, Clock.systemDefaultZone()); } public CredentialStore(PasswordHasher hasher, Clock clock) { this.hasher = hasher; this.clock = clock; } /** * Creates the initial account for every employee in the roster that does not already have one. * Existing accounts are left alone so a restart never resets somebody's password or first-login flag. */ public int provision(List<String> employeeIds) { int created = 0; for (String employeeId : employeeIds) { if (accounts.containsKey(employeeId)) continue; accounts.put(employeeId, new Account(employeeId, hasher.hash(PasswordPolicy.INITIAL_PASSWORD), true)); created++; } return created; } public boolean has(String employeeId) { return employeeId != null && accounts.containsKey(employeeId); } public Optional<Account> account(String employeeId) { return Optional.ofNullable(accounts.get(employeeId)); } public int size() { return accounts.size(); } /** Outcome of a sign-in attempt. {@code reason} is for logs, never for the browser. */ public static final class Result { public final boolean ok; public final Account account; public final String reason; // "unknown" | "locked" | "password" | "" on success Result(boolean ok, Account account, String reason) { this.ok = ok; this.account = account; this.reason = reason; } } public Result signIn(String employeeId, String password) { Instant now = clock.instant(); Account account = employeeId == null ? null : accounts.get(employeeId.trim()); if (account == null) return new Result(false, null, "unknown"); if (account.locked(now)) return new Result(false, account, "locked"); if (!hasher.verify(password, account.passwordHash())) { account.recordFailure(MAX_ATTEMPTS, now, LOCK_FOR); return new Result(false, account, "password"); } account.recordSuccess(now); // Parameters may have been raised since this hash was written; upgrade it on the way through. if (hasher.needsRehash(account.passwordHash())) account.replaceHash(hasher.hash(password)); return new Result(true, account, ""); } /** * Changes a password after verifying the current one.     private FirestoreRestClient firestoreClientFor(HttpExchange exchange) {
        String authorization = exchange.getRequestHeaders().getFirst("Authorization");
        String uid = exchange.getRequestHeaders().getFirst("X-Firebase-UID");
        if (authorization == null || !authorization.startsWith("Bearer ") || uid == null || uid.trim().isEmpty()) {
            throw new FirestoreException("Sign in with your Firebase account to continue.", 401);
        }
        String token = authorization.substring("Bearer ".length()).trim();
        if (token.length() > 8192 || uid.length() > 128 || uid.contains("/")) {
            throw new FirestoreException("Invalid Firebase session information.", 401);
        }
        return firestoreApiRoot == null
            ? new FirestoreRestClient(firebaseProjectId, uid, token)
            : new FirestoreRestClient(firebaseProjectId, uid, token, firestoreApiRoot);

    /**
     * The signed-in demo account, from the X-Demo-User header the browser sends after choosing an account.
     * Firebase mode: the signed-in Firebase user acts as one fake person from their own private sandbox (same rules).
     * shortcut: a call without the header (scripts, older tests) is unrestricted with explicit=false; replace with
     * a real login before anything leaves the demo. In Firebase mode the data is the caller's own sandbox either way.
     */
    private AccessPolicy.Actor actorFor(HttpExchange exchange) {
        String id = exchange.getRequestHeaders().getFirst("X-Demo-User");
        if (id == null || id.trim().isEmpty()) return new AccessPolicy.Actor("", AccessPolicy.Role.ADMIN, false);
        String trimmed = id.trim();
        if (!firebaseProjectId.isEmpty()) {
            if (!servicesFor(exchange).employeeService.findEmployee(trimmed).isPresent()) throw new RequestException(401, "That person is not in your sandbox.");
            return new AccessPolicy.Actor(trimmed, AccessPolicy.roleOf(trimmed), true);
        }
        if (!localEmployeeService.findEmployee(trimmed).isPresent()) throw new RequestException(401, "Unknown demo account.");
        if (hrRecords.isSeparated(trimmed, clockService.now().toLocalDate())) throw new RequestException(401, "This account was closed after the employee's last day.");
        if (!twoFactor.sessionOwner(exchange.getRequestHeaders().getFirst("X-Demo-Session")).filter(trimmed::equals).isPresent()) {
            throw new RequestException(401, "Sign in again: enter the 2FA code for this account first.");
        }
        return new AccessPolicy.Actor(trimmed, AccessPolicy.roleOf(trimmed), true);
    }
