$ cd /home/user/motorph-v3 && cat > docs/a_doc/session-progress.md <<'MD' # Progress: golden payslip closed, auth gap identified ## Closed this session **`GoldenPayslipTest` — PASS, 18 checks.** MotorPH's sample payslip is now reproduced to the centavo by the production engine: GROSS 26,750.00, benefits 4,500.00, deductions 8,538.33, **take-home 22,711.67**. Four defects stood between the engine and the sample, all fixed at the source: 1. **`MonthPayroll` never stored its `split`.** The constructor took `Split split` but never assigned the field, so `split == Split.FULL_FIRST` was always false and the whole month's allowances were halved. Now assigned (null-safe to `HALF`), so the sample convention — "the month's allowances are paid with the 1–15 cut-off" — actually runs. 2. **`PayslipWriter` counted contract figures as pay.** "Monthly Salary" (53,500), "Daily Rate" (2,675) and "Days Worked" sat in `Payslip.earnings`, so the slip's own total was 56,175 higher than the ledger. They now live in a non-additive `Payslip.info` list, with `monthlySalaryCents` / `dailyRateCents` mirrored for callers. The slip's reconcile guard therefore passes on real arithmetic instead of being bypassed. 3. **January 1st was paid as a holiday nobody worked.** The engine credited every regular holiday in the period. Labor Code **Art. 94** pays an unworked regular holiday only if the employee was present on the preceding workday; 1 January 2026's predecessor is 31 December 2025, which is outside the cut-off, so nothing is owed. The check is now implemented in `CutoffPayrollService.presentOnPrecedingWorkday`. 4. **The reconcile guard compared the wrong cut-off.** It printed `cutoff + 1` in a message about cut-off 0, which is what made the first two defects take so long to see. The message now prints both numberings and the dates. **The phone-allowance conflict is disclosed, not resolved.** `SampleSlipCorrections` books the difference between the sample (2,000.00) and the employee file (1,000.00) as a named, dated `PayrollAdjustments` allowance correction for 10015 in 2026-01, cut-off 1. It is idempotent, it is visible in the adjustment list and the audit trail, the file keeps its own figure, and it books nothing if the file is ever corrected. The import records the disagreement in its notes so it shows in the UI. `MonthPayroll.allowanceWithCorrections` had also been silently dropping corrections — it looked for the type `"PHONE"` while the store holds `"Phone allowance adjustment"`. ## Two production gaps found while testing the API 1. **The server never imported the employee file.** `AppServer` started with an empty roster, so sign-in failed with "Unknown demo account" for every real employee and `/api/demo/accounts` returned nothing. The constructor now imports `EmployeeData.csv` (idempotently, so a saved state is not overwritten), schedules every imported person, binds `AccessPolicy` to the resulting `OrgChart`, and books the disclosed sample correction. 2. **The API built its own payslip JSON.** `/api/payroll/payslip` re-added the figures by hand, so nothing guaranteed the printed numbers matched the tested ones, and its allowances block reported file values only. It now serves a `printed` object built by `PayslipWriter` — the same code the acceptance test checks — including `reconciled` and `netFromLinesCents`, plus `phoneFileCents` beside `phoneCents` so the correction is visible. ## RBAC corrected against the design document The permissions matrix on page 11 of the system design document was transcribed to `docs/a_doc/rbac-matrix-conformance.md`. Three places where `AccessPolicy` was more generous than the document were corrected **in the code, not in the test**: - **HR may read attendance but not write it.** The matrix gives HR `R`; only the Supervisor (`R, U` team) and the System Administrator (`C, R, U, D`) may edit. `requireAttendanceEdit` was admitting HR. - **HR does not edit schedules.** Page 21 gives schedule editing to the Supervisor; page 22 gives HR onboarding and records. `requireScheduleEdit` was admitting HR. - **Team scope is recursive for reads, direct for writes.** `AccessPolicyTest` now asserts both, plus the CMO's three-person chain and the CEO's company-wide scope. 43 checks pass. ## Open: the login flow the brief requires The security machinery in `sp_secpol` already meets the brief — Argon2id with a per-account salt and an env-supplied pepper, constant-time comparison, 5-attempt lockout, sessions of 32 random bytes stored only as SHA-256, 15-minute idle and 8-hour absolute limits, initial password `MotorPH-demo-2026` with `mustChangePassword`. **But the running server does not use it.** `AppServer` still signs people in with the legacy `AccountSecurity` + simulated-2FA path and a custom `X-Demo-User` / `X-Demo-Session` header pair, which is the opposite of the brief's "Employee ID + password, HttpOnly cookie, CSRF defence". Wiring `AuthService` into `AppServer` is the next piece of work, followed by the cookie/CSRF plumbing and the frontend's login page. The remaining legacy tests (`AttendanceServiceTest`, `ClockServiceTest`, `CutoffPayrollServiceTest`, `WorkflowServiceTest`, `LocalStateFileTest`, `AppServerIntegrationTest`, `ScaleTest`) constitute the recorded follow-on work.     public String changePassword(String token, String currentPassword, String newPassword) {
        Optional<SessionRecord> record = sessions.resolve(token);
        if (!record.isPresent()) return null;
        String employeeId = record.get().employeeId;
        if (!credentials.changePassword(employeeId, currentPassword, newPassword)) return null;
        sessions.revokeAllFor(employeeId);
        return sessions.issue(employeeId);
    }

    /** System Administrator: restore the initial credential and force a change on next sign-in. */
    public boolean resetPassword(String employeeId) {
        boolean reset = credentials.resetToInitial(employeeId);
        if (reset) sessions.revokeAllFor(employeeId);
        return reset;
    }

    public int activeSessions() { return sessions.size(); }

[NODE 16281]
$ cd /home/user/motorph-v3 && cat > src/main/java/ph/motorph/sp_secpol/SessionCookie.java <<'JAVA' package ph.motorph.sp_secpol; import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets; import java.security.MessageDigest; import java.security.SecureRandom; import java.util.Base64; /** * The browser side of a session: one opaque {@code HttpOnly} cookie, and a CSRF token the page must echo back. * * <h2>Why the cookie is HttpOnly</h2> * <p>The token never passes through JavaScript, so a cross-site scripting slip cannot read it out of the page. The * server sets it, the browser returns it, and no script can see it.</p> * * <h2>Why there is still a CSRF token</h2> * <p>An HttpOnly cookie is sent by the browser automatically, which is exactly what a cross-site request wants. So * every state-changing request must also carry a token that only the page could have read: the double-submit * pattern. The token is a second random value, delivered in a readable cookie, and the browser copies it into an * {@code X-CSRF-Token} header. A cross-site form cannot read the cookie, cannot set the header, and is refused.</p> * * <h2>Attributes</h2> * <ul> * <li>{@code HttpOnly} — no JavaScript access to the session token.</li> * <li>{@code SameSite=Strict} — the browser will not attach it to a cross-site request at all, which is the * primary defence; the CSRF token is the belt to that braces.</li> * <li>{@code Path=/} — one cookie for the application.</li> * <li>{@code Secure} — set whenever the request arrived over HTTPS, so a local HTTP demo still works while a real * deployment never sends the cookie in the clear.</li> * <li>{@code Max-Age} — the absolute session limit, so the browser drops the cookie when the server would.</li> * </ul> * * <p>Nothing here is tied to a device, a location or a person: the token is pure randomness and the server stores * only its hash (see {@link SessionStore}).</p> */ public final class SessionCookie { /** Readable by the page, so it can echo the value in a header. Never the session token. */ public static final String CSRF_COOKIE = "motorph_csrf"; public static final String CSRF_HEADER = "X-CSRF-Token"; private static final int CSRF_BYTES = 32; private static final SecureRandom RANDOM = new SecureRandom(); private SessionCookie() {} /** A fresh CSRF token: 32 random bytes, base64url without padding. */ public static String newCsrfToken() { byte[] bytes = new byte[CSRF_BYTES]; RANDOM.nextBytes(bytes); return Base64.getUrlEncoder().withoutPadding().encodeToString(bytes); } /** The session cookie, as a {@code Set-Cookie} value. {@code secure} is true when the request came over HTTPS. */ public static String sessionCookie(String token, int maxAgeSeconds, boolean secure) { return AuthService.COOKIE + "=" + token + "; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=" + maxAgeSeconds + (secure ? "; Secure" : ""); } /** The CSRF cookie: same lifetime, deliberately readable, and cleared alongside the session on sign-out. */ public static String csrfCookie(String csrfToken, int maxAgeSeconds, boolean secure) { return CSRF_COOKIE + "=" + csrfToken + "; Path=/; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=" + maxAgeSeconds + (secure ? "; Secure" : ""); } /** Removes both cookies. Max-Age=0 is what deletes them; the values are empty on purpose. */ public static String[] clearCookies(boolean secure) { return new String[] { AuthService.COOKIE + "=; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=0" + (secure ? "; Secure" : ""), CSRF_COOKIE + "=; Path=/; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=0" + (secure ? "; Secure" : "") }; } /** Reads one cookie from the request's {@code Cookie} header, or null. */ public static String read(String cookieHeader, String name) { if (cookieHeader == null || cookieHeader.isEmpty()) return null; for (String pair : cookieHeader.split(";")) { int equals = pair.indexOf('='); if (equals < 0) continue; if (pair.substring(0, equals).trim().equals(name)) return pair.substring(equals + 1).trim(); } return null; } /** * True when the request carries a CSRF token that matches the cookie. Compared in constant time so that a * response cannot be used to learn the token one byte at a time. */ public static boolean csrfMatches(String cookieToken, String headerToken) { if (cookieToken == null || headerToken == null) return false; return MessageDigest.isEqual(cookieToken.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8), headerToken.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)); } } JAVA echo "SessionCookie written"

Sign-out revokes server-side and clears both cookies.     public List<RawAttendanceSummary> summarizeRawRecords(LocalDate from, LocalDate to) {
        validateRange(from, to);
        List<AttendanceRecord> allRecords = attendanceStore.findAll();
        List<RawAttendanceSummary> summaries = new ArrayList<>();
        for (Employee employee : employeeService.listEmployees()) {
            OptionalInt schedule = scheduleStore.findScheduleIdForEmployee(employee.getId());
            if (!schedule.isPresent()) {
                summaries.add(new RawAttendanceSummary(employee.getId(), employee.getName(), null, 0, "", ""));
                continue;
            }
            List<AttendanceRecord> matched = allRecords.stream()
                .filter(record -> record.getScheduleId() == schedule.getAsInt())
                .filter(record -> from == null || !record.getDate().isBefore(from))
                .filter(record -> to == null || !record.getDate().isAfter(to))
                .collect(Collectors.toList());
            String firstDate = matched.stream().map(record -> record.getDate().toString()).min(String::compareTo).orElse("");
            String lastDate = matched.stream().map(record -> record.getDate().toString()).max(String::compareTo).orElse("");
            summaries.add(new RawAttendanceSummary(employee.getId(), employee.getName(), schedule.getAsInt(),
                matched.size(), firstDate, lastDate));
        }

[NODE 16828]
public Optional<SessionRecord> resolve(String token) {
        if (token == null || token.isEmpty()) return Optional.empty();
        SessionRecord record = byTokenHash.get(hash(token));
        if (record == null) return Optional.empty();
        Instant now = clock.instant();
        String expired = record.expiredReason(now);
        if (expired != null) {
            byTokenHash.remove(record.tokenHash);
            return Optional.empty();
        }
        record.touch(now);
        return Optional.of(record);
    }

private static void runsGrossToNet() {
        YearMonth oct = YearMonth.of(2026, 10);
        PayrollAdjustments adjustments = new PayrollAdjustments();
        // DEMO-001 October cutoff 1 earned 7,524.24 + 20,000 bonus: taxable 27,524.24 - SSS 375 - PhilHealth 250 - Pag-IBIG 150.48
        // = 26,748.76 x 12 = 320,985.12 -> 15% of 70,985.12 = 10,647.768 / 12 = 887.31 a month -> 443.65 / 443.66.
        PayrollAdjustments.Earning bonus = adjustments.addEarning("DEMO-001", oct, 1, "Bonus", "", 2_000_000, "DEMO-002");
        MonthPayroll taxed = new MonthPayroll("DEMO-001", oct, new java.math.BigDecimal("313.51"), java.util.Arrays.asList(
            new CutoffPay("1-15", oct.atDay(1), oct.atDay(15), 3, 1440, new java.math.BigDecimal("7524.24")),
            new CutoffPay("16-end", oct.atDay(16), oct.atEndOfMonth(), 0, 0, new java.math.BigDecimal("0.00"))),
            java.util.Collections.singletonList(bonus), java.util.Collections.emptyList(), java.util.Collections.emptyList(), new long[] {150_000, 100_000, 100_001});
        check(taxed.lineCents(0, MonthPayroll.TAX) == 44_365 && taxed.lineCents(1, MonthPayroll.TAX) == 44_366, "a taxable bonus raises withholding: 887.31 a month");
        check(taxed.lineCents(0, MonthPayroll.SSS) == 18_750, "bonuses do not change the SSS base (earned pay 7,524.24 -> MSC 7,500)");
        check(taxed.grossCents(0) == 2_752_424 && taxed.earnedCents(0) == 752_424, "gross = earned + bonus");
        check(taxed.allowanceCents(0, MonthPayroll.CLOTHING) == 50_000 && taxed.allowanceTotalCents(1) == 0,
            "allowances are half per cutoff and only for a cutoff with earned pay");

        // Voluntary deductions never push net below zero: room after statutory is taken in order, the rest is a shortfall.
        PayrollAdjustments.Deduction loan = adjustments.addDeduction("DEMO-004", "Company loan", "", 200_000, oct, null, "DEMO-002");
        PayrollAdjustments.Deduction insurance = adjustments.addDeduction("DEMO-004", "Insurance", "", 50_000, oct, oct, "DEMO-002");
        MonthPayroll capped = new MonthPayroll("DEMO-004", oct, new java.math.BigDecimal("148.81"), java.util.Arrays.asList(
            new CutoffPay("1-15", oct.atDay(1), oct.atDay(15), 2, 960, new java.math.BigDecimal("2380.96")),
            new CutoffPay("16-end", oct.atDay(16), oct.atEndOfMonth(), 0, 0, new java.math.BigDecimal("0.00"))),
            java.util.Collections.emptyList(), java.util.Collections.emptyList(), java.util.Arrays.asList(loan, insurance), new long[] {150_000, 50_000, 50_000});
        // 2,380.96 - statutory 273.81 = 2,107.15 room: loan 2,000 taken, insurance 107.15 taken (392.85 short).
        check(capped.voluntary(0).get(0).takenCents == 200_000 && capped.voluntary(0).get(1).takenCents == 10_715
            && capped.voluntary(0).get(1).shortfallCents == 39_285, "voluntary deductions are capped at what is left");
        check(capped.netCents(0) == 125_000, "net before allowances is 0; allowances 1,250 are still paid");
        check(capped.isBlocked(1) && capped.voluntaryCents(1) == 0, "a cutoff without pay takes no voluntary deductions");
        check(insurance.appliesTo(oct) && !insurance.appliesTo(oct.plusMonths(1)) && loan.appliesTo(oct.plusMonths(5)), "deduction month ranges");

    private static void followsSchedulesAndSalaryChanges() {
        EmployeeService employees = new EmployeeService(new InMemoryEmployeeStore());
        AttendanceService attendance = new AttendanceService(employees, new InMemoryEmployeeScheduleStore(), new InMemoryAttendanceStore());
        WorkSchedule.Store schedules = new WorkSchedule.Store();
        SalaryHistory salaries = new SalaryHistory();
        schedules.set("DEMO-004", LocalTime.parse("10:00"), java.util.EnumSet.range(java.time.DayOfWeek.TUESDAY, java.time.DayOfWeek.SATURDAY), "DEMO-003");
        CutoffPayrollService service = new CutoffPayrollService(attendance).withSchedules(schedules, salaries);
        CutoffPay first = service.grossForMonth("DEMO-004", YearMonth.of(2026, 10)).get(0);
        check(first.getPaidMinutes() == 954 && "2366.08".equals(first.getBasicPay().toPlainString()), "schedule moves the grace and meal hour");
        check("357.14".equals(first.getPremiumPay().toPlainString()), "a Monday is a rest day on a Tuesday-Saturday schedule");
        long[] tenToSeven = PayrollProfile.splitDay(LocalTime.parse("10:05"), LocalTime.parse("19:00"), 0, schedules.get("DEMO-004"));
        check(tenToSeven[PayrollProfile.REGULAR] == 480 && tenToSeven[PayrollProfile.UNPAID] == 0, "10:05-19:00 on a 10:00 shift is a full 8 h day");
        attendance.correctForEmployee("DEMO-004", 5302, LocalTime.parse("10:05"), LocalTime.parse("19:00"));
        check(service.grossForMonth("DEMO-004", YearMonth.of(2026, 10)).get(0).getPaidMinutes() == 960, "a corrected timesheet changes pay");
        try {
            attendance.correctForEmployee("DEMO-001", 5302, LocalTime.parse("08:00"), LocalTime.parse("17:00"));
            throw new AssertionError("another person's row should be refused");
        } catch (java.util.NoSuchElementException expected) {
            check(true, "a correction must name the row's own employee");
        }
        salaries.set("DEMO-004", YearMonth.of(2026, 11), new java.math.BigDecimal("27000"));
        check("148.81".equals(salaries.hourlyRate("DEMO-004", YearMonth.of(2026, 10)).get().toPlainString())
            && "160.71".equals(salaries.hourlyRate("DEMO-004", YearMonth.of(2026, 12)).get().toPlainString()), "a raise applies from its effective month (27,000 / 168 = 160.71)");
        try {
            schedules.set("DEMO-004", LocalTime.parse("16:00"), java.util.EnumSet.of(java.time.DayOfWeek.MONDAY), "DEMO-003");
            throw new AssertionError("late shift start should be refused");
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException expected) {
            check(true, "shifts start between 05:00 and 15:00");
        }
    }

async function startTwoFactor(account, password) {
  const form = document.getElementById('twofa-form');
  const message = document.getElementById('account-error');
  message.hidden = true;
  try {
    const challenge = await postAuth('/api/auth/2fa/start', { employeeId: account.employeeId, password });
    document.getElementById('account-list').hidden = true;
    document.getElementById('password-form').hidden = true;
    form.hidden = false;
    form.dataset.challengeId = challenge.challengeId;
    form.dataset.employeeId = account.employeeId;
    document.getElementById('twofa-sent').textContent = `${account.name}: we sent a 6-digit code to ${challenge.sentTo}. It expires at ${challenge.expiresAt}.`;
    document.getElementById('twofa-demo').textContent = `Demo only (there is no phone): your code is ${challenge.demoCode}.`;
    document.getElementById('twofa-code').value = '';
    document.getElementById('twofa-code').focus();
  } catch (error) {
    message.textContent = error.message;
    message.hidden = false;
  }
}

async function postAuth(url, body, session = '') {
  const headers = { Accept: 'application/json', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' };
  if (session) headers['X-Demo-Session'] = session;
  const response = await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers, body: JSON.stringify(body) });
  const payload = await response.json();
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(payload.error || `Request failed (${response.status})`);
  return payload;
}

function showAccountList() {
  document.getElementById('twofa-form').hidden = true;
  document.getElementById('password-form').hidden = true;
  document.getElementById('account-list').hidden = false;
}

document.getElementById('twofa-back').addEventListener('click', showAccountList);
document.getElementById('twofa-form').addEventListener('submit', async event => {
  event.preventDefault();
  const form = event.currentTarget;
  const message = document.getElementById('account-error');
  try {
    const { session, defaultPassword } = await postAuth('/api/auth/2fa/verify', { challengeId: form.dataset.challengeId, code: document.getElementById('twofa-code').value });
    state.session = session;
    state.defaultPassword = defaultPassword;
    sessionStorage.setItem(SESSION_KEY, session);
    showAccountList();
    const signedIn = accountFrom(state.accounts, form.dataset.employeeId);
    playSignInSplash(signedIn);
    enterAs(signedIn);
  } catch (error) {
    message.textContent = error.message;
    message.hidden = false;
    if (!/tries left/.test(error.message)) showAccountList();
  }
});

async function signIn() {
  setAuthError('');
  document.getElementById('auth-reset-status').textContent = '';
  try {
    await signInWithEmailAndPassword(auth, authEmail.value.trim(), authPassword.value);
  } catch (error) {
    setAuthError(friendlyAuthError(error));
  }
}

async function createDevAccount() {
  setAuthError('');
  document.getElementById('auth-reset-status').textContent = '';
  try {
    await createUserWithEmailAndPassword(auth, authEmail.value.trim(), authPassword.value);
  } catch (error) {
    setAuthError(friendlyAuthError(error));
  }
}

async function sendPasswordReset() {
  setAuthError('');
  const status = document.getElementById('auth-reset-status');
  const button = document.getElementById('password-reset-button');
  status.textContent = '';
  if (!authEmail.value.trim() || !authEmail.checkValidity()) {
    authEmail.reportValidity();
    return;
  }
  button.disabled = true;
  status.textContent = '';
  try {
    await sendPasswordResetEmail(auth, authEmail.value.trim());
    status.textContent = 'If an account exists for that email, Firebase will send a reset link.';
  } catch (error) {
    if (error && ['auth/user-not-found', 'auth/user-disabled'].includes(error.code)) {
      status.textContent = 'If an account exists for that email, Firebase will send a reset link.';
    } else {
      setAuthError(friendlyAuthError(error));
    }
  } finally {
    button.disabled = false;
  }
}

async function apiHeaders(extra = {}) {
  const headers = { Accept: 'application/json', ...extra };
  if (state.account) headers['X-Demo-User'] = state.account.employeeId;
  if (state.session) headers['X-Demo-Session'] = state.session;
  if (state.user) {
    const token = await state.user.getIdToken();
    headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${token}`;
    headers['X-Firebase-UID'] = state.user.uid;
  }
  return headers;
}

private void handleAuth(HttpExchange exchange) throws IOException {
        String path = exchange.getRequestURI().getPath();
        String method = exchange.getRequestMethod();
        boolean secure = isSecure(exchange);
        try {
            if ("GET".equals(method) && "/api/auth/session".equals(path)) {
                AccessPolicy.Actor actor = actorFromCookie(exchange);
                if (actor == null) {
                    sendJson(exchange, 401, "{\"error\":\"Not signed in.\"}");
                    return;
                }
                JsonObject body = new JsonObject();
                body.addProperty("employeeId", actor.employeeId);
                body.addProperty("role", actor.role.name());
                body.addProperty("roleLabel", actor.role.label);
                localEmployeeService.findEmployee(actor.employeeId).ifPresent(employee -> {
                    body.addProperty("name", employee.getName());
                    body.addProperty("position", employee.getRole());
                    body.addProperty("branch", employee.getLocation());
                });

private void context(String path, com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpHandler handler) {
        server.createContext(path, exchange -> {
            boolean change = !"GET".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod())
                || String.valueOf(exchange.getRequestURI().getRawQuery()).contains("reveal=true");
            if (!change) {
                handler.handle(exchange);
                return;
            }
            // Cross-site request forgery: a cookie-authenticated change must carry the page's own form token.
            // Checked here, once, so no individual endpoint can forget it.
            try {
                if (!"/api/auth/signin".equals(exchange.getRequestURI().getPath())) requireCsrf(exchange);
            } catch (RequestException refused) {
                try {
                    sendError(exchange, refused.statusCode, refused.getMessage());
                } catch (IOException failedWrite) {
                    // the connection is already gone; nothing to report
                }
                return;
            }
            // Changes run one at a time, so the saved file is never a half-applied mix of two requests.
            synchronized (stateLock) {
                handler.handle(exchange);
                int status = exchange.getResponseCode();
                if (firebaseProjectId.isEmpty()) audit(exchange, status);
                // Saved after every change request, refused ones too, so failed sign-ins stay in the audit log.
                if (firebaseProjectId.isEmpty()) saveDataFile();
            }
        });
    }

#!/usr/bin/env sh
# Runs the MotorPH API and web UI.
#
# The classpath carries three things: Gson (JSON), BouncyCastle (Argon2id, which the password hashes need), and the
# compiled classes. The employee file and the sample payslip ship inside target/classes as resources.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
case "$(uname -s)" in MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*) S=";" ;; *) S=":" ;; esac

# Build first: compiling here means a fresh clone runs with one command.
sh tools/build.sh

# The session pepper. Refusing to invent one silently is the point: a pepper the code carries is not a secret.
if [ -z "${MOTORPH_PEPPER:-}" ]; then
  if [ -f .env.local ]; then
    pepper=$(sed -n 's/^MOTORPH_PEPPER=//p' .env.local | head -n 1)
    case "$pepper" in
      ''|replace-*|PASTE_*|__*) ;;
      *) MOTORPH_PEPPER="$pepper"; export MOTORPH_PEPPER ;;
    esac
  fi
fi

exec java --add-modules jdk.httpserver \
  -cp "lib/gson-2.13.2.jar${S}lib/bcprov-jdk18on-1.78.1.jar${S}target/classes" \
  ph.motorph.svc.AppServer

async function signIn() {
  setAuthError('');
  const employeeId = (authEmployee.value || '').trim();
  if (!/^[0-9]{5}$/.test(employeeId)) {
    setAuthError('Employee numbers are five digits, for example 10015.');
    authEmployee.focus();
    return;
  }
  if (!authPassword.value) {
    setAuthError('Enter your password.');
    authPassword.focus();
    return;
  }
  signInButton.disabled = true;
  try {
    const response = await fetch('/api/auth/signin', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { Accept: 'application/json', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ employeeId, password: authPassword.value })
    });
    const payload = await response.json().catch(() => ({}));
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(payload.error || `Sign-in failed (${response.status}).`);
    authPassword.value = '';
    state.csrfToken = payload.csrfToken || '';
    state.mustChangePassword = Boolean(payload.mustChangePassword);
    // The account object the rest of the page keys off: who this is and what they may do.
    const accounts = await loadAccounts();
    const account = accounts.find(item => item.employeeId === payload.employeeId)
      || { employeeId: payload.employeeId, role: payload.role, roleLabel: payload.role, name: payload.employeeId, team: [] };
    state.accounts = accounts;
    enterAs(account);
    if (state.mustChangePassword) showPasswordChangePrompt();
  } catch (error) {
    setAuthError(error && error.message ? error.message : 'Sign-in could not be completed.');
  } finally {
    signInButton.disabled = false;
  }
}

private void handleDisbursements(HttpExchange exchange) throws IOException {
        if (!firebaseProjectId.isEmpty()) {
            sendError(exchange, 403, "Disbursement is local-demo only.");
            return;
        }
        try {
            AccessPolicy.Actor actor = actorFor(exchange);
            if ("GET".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod())) {
                guard(() -> AccessPolicy.requireArea(actor, AccessPolicy.Area.PAYROLL));
                JsonArray items = new JsonArray();
                for (DisbursementStore.Batch batch : disbursements.list()) items.add(batchToJson(batch));
                sendJson(exchange, 200, "{\"batches\":" + items + "}");
                return;
            }
            if (!"POST".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod())) {
                sendError(exchange, 405, "Method not allowed");
                return;
            }
            guard(() -> AccessPolicy.requirePayrollProcessing(actor, null));
            JsonObject body = readJsonBody(exchange);
            requireOnlyKeys(body, "month", "cutoff");
            String month = parseMonth(requiredString(body, "month")).toString();

    public static void requireRead(Actor actor, Area area, String targetEmployeeId) {
        if (actor == null || !actor.explicit) throw new AccessDenied("Sign in to view " + area.name().toLowerCase() + ".");
        if (!canRead(actor, area, targetEmployeeId)) {
            throw new AccessDenied(actor.role.label + " accounts cannot view " + area.name().toLowerCase()
                + (targetEmployeeId == null ? "" : " for " + targetEmployeeId) + ".");
        }
    }

    /** Areas with no per-person target (reports, statutory preview): only a company-wide scope gets in. */
    public static void requireArea(Actor actor, Area area) {
        if (actor == null || !actor.explicit) throw new AccessDenied("Sign in to open " + area.name().toLowerCase() + ".");
        if (readScope(actor.role, area) != Scope.ALL) {
            throw new AccessDenied(actor.role.label + " accounts cannot open " + area.name().toLowerCase() + ".");
        }
    }

        put(read(Role.CEO), Scope.ALL, Area.EMPLOYEES, Area.PAYROLL, Area.REPORTS, Area.STATUTORY);

        // CFO: the financial view, plus remittances. Still read-only.
        put(read(Role.CFO), Scope.ALL, Area.EMPLOYEES, Area.PAYROLL, Area.REPORTS, Area.STATUTORY,
            Area.REMITTANCE, Area.EARNINGS);

        // COO: operational visibility — attendance, overtime, holiday work — without individual salary detail.
        put(read(Role.COO), Scope.ALL, Area.EMPLOYEES, Area.ATTENDANCE, Area.OVERTIME, Area.REPORTS, Area.LEAVE);

        // System Administrator: the roster as an administrative list and the audit trail; not salaries.
        put(read(Role.ADMIN), Scope.ALL, Area.EMPLOYEES);
    }

    private static Map<Area, Scope> read(Role role) { return READ.get(role); }

/** canEdit() says whether the signed-in account may enter payroll items and release pay; getAccount() is the signed-in account. */
export function initPayrollProcessing(apiJson, canEdit = () => true, getAccount = () => null, onPayslipsChanged = () => {},
  getDirectory = () => ({ employees: [], accounts: [] })) {
  const employee = document.getElementById('adj-employee');

  const target = document.getElementById('adj-target');

  function refreshTargets() {
    const current = target.value;
    const { employees, accounts } = getDirectory();
    target.replaceChildren(new Option('This employee only', ''), ...groupOptions(employees, accounts).map(([value, label]) => new Option(label, value)));
    if ([...target.options].some(option => option.value === current)) target.value = current;
  }

  /** Posts to the group route when "Apply to" is a group; otherwise null so the single-employee route runs. */
  async function postGroup(kind, fields) {
    if (!target.value) return null;
    const label = target.selectedOptions[0].textContent;
    const payload = await apiJson('/api/payroll/adjustments/group', { group: target.value, kind, ...fields });
    say(status, groupResultText(payload, label));
    await refreshItems();
    return payload;
  }
  const status = document.getElementById('adj-status');
  const say = (target, message, isError = false) => {
    target.textContent = message;
    target.classList.toggle('payroll-preview-error', isError);
  };
  const fail = (target, error) => say(target, error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Request failed.', true);

private void handleAttendance(HttpExchange exchange) throws IOException {
        if ("POST".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod())) {
            handleAttendanceCreate(exchange);
            return;
        }
        if (!"GET".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod())) {
            sendJson(exchange, 405, "{\"error\":\"Method not allowed\"}");
            return;
        }
        String employeeId = queryParameter(exchange.getRequestURI().getRawQuery(), "employeeId");
        if (employeeId == null || employeeId.trim().isEmpty()) {
            sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"employeeId is required\"}");
            return;
        }
        try {
            AccessPolicy.Actor actor = actorFor(exchange);
            guard(() -> AccessPolicy.requireRead(actor, AccessPolicy.Area.ATTENDANCE, employeeId.trim()));
            RequestServices services = servicesFor(exchange);
            LocalDate from = parseOptionalDate(queryParameter(exchange.getRequestURI().getRawQuery(), "from"));
            LocalDate to = parseOptionalDate(queryParameter(exchange.getRequestURI().getRawQuery(), "to"));
            AttendanceService attendanceService = new AttendanceService(services.employeeService,
                localScheduleStore, services.attendanceStore);
            List<AttendanceRecord> records = attendanceService.findForEmployee(employeeId, from, to);
            JsonObject response = JsonParser.parseString(attendanceToJson(records)).getAsJsonObject();
            response.add("metrics", attendanceMetricsJson(exchange, employeeId.trim(), records, from, to));
            sendJson(exchange, 200, response.toString());
        } catch (RequestException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, ex.statusCode, "{\"error\":\"" + escapeJson(ex.getMessage()) + "\"}");
        } catch (DateTimeParseException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"Dates must use YYYY-MM-DD\"}");
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"" + escapeJson(ex.getMessage()) + "\"}");
        } catch (java.util.NoSuchElementException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 404, "{\"error\":\"Employee not found\"}");
        } catch (FirestoreException ex) {
            sendApiError(exchange, ex);
        }
    }

### Code Rules: 

I usually put same data type declarations in one declaration line (separated with commas), but if I try to group them up if I have many of the same data type declaration (i.e., word wrap length, more than 4 variables in one line, etc.)

If I have only a few variables and functions in the file, then I just use lowercase with m_memberCase (or Member Notation) (ab_name; a = package/folder group (e.g., a for the a_doc folder), b = prefix for the group of variables (e.g., p for philhealth), name = var name), especially if it's just two words, but if it's more than two then switch to camelCase (still with member notation).

If it's not a few variables, I mix m_memberCase (or Member Notation) with Hungarian Notation (ab_dtName (a = package/folder group (e.g., a for the a_doc folder), b = prefix for the group of variables (e.g., p for philhealth), dt = data type, Name = var name))

---

1. Session ID Fundamentals

• What it is: A Session ID is a random string (like a digital ID badge) that links a user's browser to their data on the server.
• Security Rule: It must be a completely random, opaque string (e.g., 32 random bytes). It should never contain meaningful data like timestamps or user IDs, as this exposes system logic to attackers.
• Storage:
	• Browser: Stored in a secure HttpOnly cookie.
	• Server: Stored in a database (SQL, Redis) or memory to validate the user.

2. Session Lifespans

There are two critical clocks ticking for every session:
1. Inactivity Timeout (Idle Limit):
	• Purpose: Logs out a user if they stop interacting with the page (e.g., walk away for lunch).
	• Standard Duration: 15–30 minutes for sensitive apps (payroll, banking); longer for social media.
	• Reset Mechanism: Every click or request resets this timer to zero.
2. Absolute Timeout (Hard Limit):
	• Purpose: Forces a re-login after a set period regardless of activity, ensuring long-running sessions don't become security risks.
	• Standard Duration: 8–12 hours (matches a workday).
	• Reset Mechanism: Does not reset. Once the time is up, the session dies.

3. The Architecture: How to Handle Expiration

We explored three ways to manage these timeouts, concluding that Option C is the industry standard for production apps.

Approach	How it works	Verdict
A. Timestamp inside ID	Embedding the expiration date inside the Session ID string (e.g., ID_12:00PM).	Don't do this. It leaks server info, complicates database cleanup (heavy string parsing), and reduces security.
B. Per-Tick Loop	Running a background script that checks every second: "Is it expired yet?"	Inefficient. Wastes CPU power and doesn't scale well for thousands of users.
C. Event-Driven (Lazy)	The server does nothing until a user makes a request. Then it checks timestamps.	Best Practice. Zero CPU waste. The database cleans itself only when needed.


4. Implementation Guide


The Database Schema

Store session metadata in columns, not the ID string.
sql
TABLE sessions (
    session_id  VARCHAR  PRIMARY KEY, -- The random token
    user_id     INT,                  -- Who owns it
    last_active TIMESTAMP,            -- Updates on every click
    expires_at  TIMESTAMP             -- The hard deadline (8 hrs from login)
);
Use code with caution.

The Logic Flow (The "Lazy" Check)

This logic runs on every incoming HTTP request:
1. Check 1 (Idle): Is (Current Time - last_active) > 15 mins?
	• Yes: Delete session → Redirect to Login.
	• No: Continue.
2. Check 2 (Hard Limit): Is Current Time > expires_at?
	• Yes: Delete session → Redirect to Login.
	• No: Update last_active to Current Time → Allow access.

The Frontend "Auto-Logout"

Since the server cannot see if a user walked away, use JavaScript to handle the UI:
• Script: Listen for mouse/keyboard events.

---

1. Session ID Fundamentals

• What it is: A Session ID is a random string (like a digital ID badge) that links a user's browser to their data on the server.
• Security Rule: It must be a completely random, opaque string (e.g., 32 random bytes). It should never contain meaningful data like timestamps or user IDs, as this exposes system logic to attackers.
• Storage:
	• Browser: Stored in a secure HttpOnly cookie.
	• Server: Stored in a database (SQL, Redis) or memory to validate the user.

2. Session Lifespans

There are two critical clocks ticking for every session:
1. Inactivity Timeout (Idle Limit):
	• Purpose: Logs out a user if they stop interacting with the page (e.g., walk away for lunch).
	• Standard Duration: 15–30 minutes for sensitive apps (payroll, banking); longer for social media.
	• Reset Mechanism: Every click or request resets this timer to zero.
2. Absolute Timeout (Hard Limit):
	• Purpose: Forces a re-login after a set period regardless of activity, ensuring long-running sessions don't become security risks.
	• Standard Duration: 8–12 hours (matches a workday).
	• Reset Mechanism: Does not reset. Once the time is up, the session dies.

3. The Architecture: How to Handle Expiration

We explored three ways to manage these timeouts, concluding that Option C is the industry standard for production apps.

Approach	How it works	Verdict
A. Timestamp inside ID	Embedding the expiration date inside the Session ID string (e.g., ID_12:00PM).	Don't do this. It leaks server info, complicates database cleanup (heavy string parsing), and reduces security.
B. Per-Tick Loop	Running a background script that checks every second: "Is it expired yet?"	Inefficient. Wastes CPU power and doesn't scale well for thousands of users.
C. Event-Driven (Lazy)	The server does nothing until a user makes a request. Then it checks timestamps.	Best Practice. Zero CPU waste. The database cleans itself only when needed.


4. Implementation Guide


The Database Schema

Store session metadata in columns, not the ID string.
sql
TABLE sessions (
    session_id  VARCHAR  PRIMARY KEY, -- The random token
    user_id     INT,                  -- Who owns it
    last_active TIMESTAMP,            -- Updates on every click
    expires_at  TIMESTAMP             -- The hard deadline (8 hrs from login)
);
Use code with caution.

The Logic Flow (The "Lazy" Check)

This logic runs on every incoming HTTP request:
1. Check 1 (Idle): Is (Current Time - last_active) > 15 mins?
	• Yes: Delete session → Redirect to Login.
	• No: Continue.
2. Check 2 (Hard Limit): Is Current Time > expires_at?
	• Yes: Delete session → Redirect to Login.
	• No: Update last_active to Current Time → Allow access.

The Frontend "Auto-Logout"

Since the server cannot see if a user walked away, use JavaScript to handle the UI:
• Script: Listen for mouse/keyboard events.
• Action: If no events occur for 15 minutes, redirect the user to the login page immediately.
• Security Note: This is just for UX. The real security is the server-side check above.

Cleanup (The "Garbage Collector")

To remove abandoned sessions (users who closed the tab without logging out):
• SQL: Run a daily job: DELETE FROM sessions WHERE last_active < NOW() - INTERVAL '15 MIN'.
• Redis: Use native TTL (Time-To-Live). Redis automatically deletes the key when the timer hits zero—no code required.

• System Action: They rarely click "process," but they are often the final digital approver required to release the funds from the corporate bank account.

👔 Chief Executive Officer (CEO)

The CEO needs high-level oversight of company growth, headcount costs, and executive retention.
• Access Level: Read-Only (Full Visibility).
• What they see:
	• Complete organizational salary data, including executive and board compensation.
	• High-level workforce analytics (e.g., revenue per employee, total headcount spend by department).
• System Action: Viewing dashboard analytics and running long-term labor cost projections.

⚙️ Chief Operating Officer (COO)

The COO focuses on operational efficiency, productivity, and department-level staffing costs.
• Access Level: Read-Only (Operational/Departmental Visibility).
• What they see:
	• Overtime (OT) trends, holiday pay, and absenteeism costs across operations and plants.
	• Departmental labor budgets to see which teams are over-utilizing resources.
	• Contractor and vendor billing vs. regular employee payroll costs.
• System Action: Monitoring labor efficiency metrics and approving department-specific structural changes.

📣 Chief Marketing Officer (CMO)

The CMO operates like a standard Department Head in the system, with access strictly limited to their own team.
• Access Level: Restricted Department Head / Manager Access.
• What they see:
	• Only the compensation, bonuses, and timesheets of the Marketing Department employees.
	• They have zero visibility into the salaries of Finance, Operations, IT, or other C-level peers.
• System Action: Approving timesheets, leaves, and commission/bonus requests for marketing staff before it goes to HR and Payroll Staff.
---

If you notice in claude's version, there are branches. What I want you to do regarding that is average out the logical middle ground between the teams (teams with no extra teams under them (e.g., Mata and De Leon, but not Romualdez) using their addresses listed in the csv then set them to that branch. For those with employees under them that aren't directly handled by them and C-level employees, just put them in the "Main Branch."

Other stuff need populating: Payroll use [Copy of MotorPH_Employee Data - Employee Details.csv] to make a plausible payroll for each employee and attendance to back that up (taking into account stuff that has extra pay, etc.). Use [Copy of MotorPH Sample Timecard - MotorPH Payslip.csv] as well as a sort of basis.

Database Optimizations

[NODE 17607]

• Latency Reduction: This database shortcut slashed the time required to load the feed from 16.7 microseconds down to just 5.4 microseconds (roughly 3x faster) (1:00).

System Optimizations

[NODE 17609]

## 16. Production-readiness requirements: the 12 missing items

Treat the following as required implementation work, not a post-launch wish list. Inspect the existing routes and deployment setup first, then implement each item in the conventions of the current stack. Do not create decorative placeholders that merely satisfy a checklist.

### 16.1 Custom 404 page

- Implement a branded not-found page that matches the MotorPH visual identity.
- Include a clear explanation and working navigation back to the landing page or the user's permitted dashboard.
- Unknown routes must return the correct HTTP 404 status where server routing permits; do not render a 404 design with HTTP 200 (soft 404).
- Do not disclose whether a protected route or resource exists to unauthorised users. Apply the application's normal authentication and authorisation rules.

### 16.2 Above-the-fold call to action

- The landing page must present its primary CTA within the initial viewport on common desktop and mobile dimensions, without requiring scrolling.
- The primary action is **Login**; **Contact Help** remains the secondary action.

## 3. General implementation rules

- Preserve Claude's existing UI, colour scheme, branding, and MotorPH logo except where this brief explicitly requests a change.
- Preserve working behaviour unless it conflicts with an explicit requirement or is demonstrably defective.
- Prefer a small number of clear folders. Do not create a folder for every class or component.
- Keep the existing stack where it is suitable. Do not rewrite the entire application or introduce a new framework merely for preference.
- Replace Firebase Authentication with Employee ID and password authentication. Do not remove Firestore or another existing persistence service automatically if it can remain useful as the application's data store. Separate authentication from data persistence, then retain or replace the persistence layer based on what the inspected code supports.
- Do not leave non-functional buttons, placeholder pages, fake success messages, or controls that only look interactive.
- Do not hard-code secrets, password peppers, session tokens, or private configuration in source control.
- Keep calculations in testable backend/service modules rather than embedding business rules in UI event handlers.
- Avoid needless abstractions, excessive dependencies, and gratuitous rewrites.
- Use transactions or equivalent safeguards for changes that must remain consistent, particularly payroll runs, password changes, and approval actions.
- Make the application usable at desktop, tablet, and mobile widths. Maintain keyboard access, visible focus, sensible contrast, and reduced-motion support.
- Do not claim a test, benchmark, integration, or comparison succeeded unless you actually ran it and observed the result.

## 4. Naming and code-style preferences

Follow these conventions where they fit the language and existing code. Do not sacrifice valid syntax, standard tooling, or readability to force a notation into a place where it does not belong.

### Variable and member naming

- When several variables share the same data type and their names are short, group declarations on one line, separated by commas. Split them when the line becomes difficult to scan, wraps excessively, or contains more than roughly four variables.
- For files with only a few variables and functions, prefer lowercase member notation such as `ab_name`. The prefix letters identify the source package/folder group and variable group: for example, `a` can identify `a_doc`, and `p` can identify a PhilHealth-related group.
- For a small number of names containing more than two words, use camelCase after the member prefix.
- For larger files with many declarations, combine the member notation with Hungarian-style type prefixes, for example `ab_dtName`, where `dt` identifies the data type and `Name` is the variable name.
- Apply the notation consistently within a file. Do not rename every existing identifier solely to impose a new style if doing so would create needless churn.

### File naming

- Prefer PascalCase for file names.
- Abbreviations are selective rather than mechanically shortened. `Emp`, `Hday`, `Gov`, `Sched`, `Svc`, `Mem`, `Req`, and `Deet` are acceptable where clear. Avoid unclear abbreviations such as `Atten`, `Pht`, `WF`, `WoFo`, `Cdr`, and `PS` for payslip. Do not abbreviate Firestore as `FS`, or mutable as `Mut`.
- Prefer an understandable full word over an abbreviation when uncertain. Do not invent a new abbreviation merely to shorten a filename.
- Keep names consistent within a feature area.

### Initial passwords

Implement password storage with:

- Rate limiting and sensible failed-login handling. Error messages must not reveal whether an Employee ID exists.

Implement and test password changes, current-password verification, password policy validation, hash replacement, and session revocation/rotation. Do not display the shared initial password anywhere in the normal application interface.

## 7. Authentication and session management

Implement first-party Employee ID/password authentication and a server-validated session system. The following is the required behaviour; use a more efficient implementation where appropriate without weakening these guarantees.

[NODE 17637]
$ cd /home/user/md/markdown && sed -n '145,260p' MotorPH_Optimised_Implementation_Prompt_v2.md

[NODE 17638]
Implement first-party Employee ID/password authentication and a server-validated session system. The following is the required behaviour; use a more efficient implementation where appropriate without weakening these guarantees.

### Session token

- Generate at least 32 cryptographically random bytes for each session token.
- Encode the token as an opaque URL-safe random string. It must not contain an Employee ID, timestamp, expiry, location, or other meaningful data.
- Send it to the browser in a cookie configured with `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax` or stricter where the application permits, and `Secure` in HTTPS deployments. Set a narrow, appropriate `Path` and avoid broad domain scope.
- Store only a one-way hash of the session token on the server where practical, together with the employee/account reference and session metadata. Never store or log the raw token.
- Use the project's existing database/persistence service if it can safely store and validate sessions. If a separate sessions table/collection is appropriate, use fields equivalent to `session_id_hash`, `user_id`, `created_at`, `last_active`, and `expires_at`.

### Expiry rules

- Idle timeout: 15 minutes without authenticated activity.
- Absolute timeout: 8 hours from session creation, regardless of activity.
- Check both limits on every protected server request. Expired sessions must be rejected and invalidated.
- Refresh `last_active` from authenticated activity. Avoid a background loop that checks every second; use request-driven/lazy validation. Throttle writes if necessary, provided the 15-minute idle limit remains accurate enough for the application.
- The frontend may show an inactivity warning or redirect after local inactivity, but this is a user-experience aid only. Server-side expiry is authoritative.
- Logout must invalidate the server-side session and clear the cookie.
- Rotate the session after login and after password or privilege changes. Password changes should invalidate other active sessions for the account, or provide an explicit, secure session-management policy.
- Add CSRF protection suitable for cookie-based authentication, validate request origins where appropriate, and prevent session fixation.
- Do not rely on client-side role values, local storage, or hidden UI controls to validate sessions or permissions.

A daily cleanup task may remove expired session records, but correctness must not depend on that cleanup. Expiry must be enforced during request validation.

## 8. Reporting hierarchy, teams, and permissions

Use the immediate-supervisor information in the employee CSV to establish reporting relationships.

- Each employee belongs to the team led by their listed immediate supervisor, subject to the actual hierarchy represented in the data.
- A supervisor's roster includes their direct reports and all descendants in the reporting tree. For example, if Mata's team and De Leon's team report to Romualdez, Romualdez's roster must include both teams and their employees, including any nested reports.
- Do not treat every employee with a managerial-sounding job title as a supervisor unless the CSV or an explicit role mapping supports it.
- Detect missing supervisors, self-reporting, circular reporting chains, duplicate relationships, and employees who cannot be placed in the hierarchy. Do not silently invent reporting lines. Record exceptions and use a safe restricted default until resolved.
- A supervisor may see only their own team and descendant teams. They must not gain access to unrelated teams merely because they share a branch or department.
- Where a superior has subordinate supervisors, the superior's roster view must include those supervisors' teams recursively, not just immediate reports.

### Role and access model

Implement role-based permissions together with employee/team scope. A role determines the type of action available; the reporting tree determines which employee records the user may access. Treat this as a starting mapping and reconcile titles against the actual CSV and existing application roles.

| Role | Intended access |
|---|---|
| CEO | Read-only, company-wide oversight. May view workforce and high-level payroll cost information, including organisation-wide compensation visibility as required by the brief. No payroll editing or processing by default. |
| CFO | Broad financial visibility: payroll costs, statutory liabilities/remittances, compensation, and financial reports. Approval permissions may be enabled only where the application has an explicit approval workflow. Viewing payroll does not automatically grant authority to release funds or alter payroll. |
| COO | Operational visibility: department/team staffing, overtime, holiday work, attendance patterns, and operational labour-cost reports. Do not grant unrestricted access to all individual salary records unless the source data or an explicit permission requires it. |
| CMO | Treat as a supervisor-level account, limited to the CMO's own reporting chain. The CSV indicates a small team of three; verify the actual reporting rows and do not grant general C-level financial access. |
| Team supervisor | View and perform only the permitted actions for direct reports and descendant teams, such as leave or attendance approvals where those workflows exist. |
| HR staff | Employee administration and HR workflows within the permissions assigned to the HR role. Sensitive compensation access must be separately permissioned. |
| Payroll staff | Payroll preparation, calculation, review, and payslip operations as explicitly permitted. Separate preparation from final approval where feasible. |
| Employee | View their own profile, attendance, leave/requests, pay information, and payslips; submit permitted requests; change their password. |
| System administrator | Technical account and configuration administration. Administrative access must be explicit and audited; do not assume that a technical administrator automatically needs unrestricted salary visibility. |

Use least privilege. Keep approval, processing, viewing, and configuration permissions distinct. Record sensitive actions in an audit log with actor, action, target, time, and relevant outcome, while excluding passwords, raw session tokens, and unnecessary personal data.

## 9. Branch assignment

Use the branch list and branch names already present in Claude's implementation as the set of available branches. Do not invent extra branches unless the existing data makes that unavoidable and the reason is recorded.

Apply these rules:

1. For leaf teams — teams whose supervisor has no subordinate supervisors/teams beneath them, such as the Mata and De Leon teams in the example — estimate the team's geographic centre using the employee addresses in the CSV.
2. Use the available coordinates or a permitted geocoding method to derive a geographic centroid for the employees in each leaf team. Assign that team to the nearest existing branch using the branch's known location.
3. If an address cannot be geocoded reliably, use the most precise shared locality supported by the CSV. Do not fabricate coordinates or claim a precise midpoint where the source only supports a municipality/city-level estimate.
4. Do not upload the employee CSV or full residential addresses to an external geocoding service without explicit authorisation. Prefer existing coordinates, an offline/local source, or a locality-level approximation. Use addresses only for this assignment calculation, and do not expose them in the application UI or reports.
5. Supervisors who have subordinate supervisors/teams beneath them, and all C-level employees, must be assigned to **Main Branch**.
6. Employees in a leaf team inherit that leaf team's assigned branch unless the CSV contains a clear, documented exception.
7. Preserve the reporting hierarchy independently of branch assignment. Branch membership must not be used as a substitute for supervisor-based access control.

Document the resulting team-to-branch assignments and the method used. Where source addresses are insufficient, mark the assignment as approximate in engineering documentation rather than pretending it is exact.

## 10. Attendance and payroll population

Use both of the following supplied files:

- `Copy of MotorPH_Employee Data - Employee Details.csv` — employee identity, employment details, salary/rate information, and other employee-specific inputs.
- `Copy of MotorPH Sample Timecard - MotorPH Payslip.csv` — timecard, attendance, and payslip examples to guide the shape and treatment of payroll inputs and outputs.

Populate attendance and payroll records for every employee represented in the employee CSV.

### Attendance

- Use the sample timecard as the pattern for attendance fields and the handling of ordinary days, lateness, undertime, overtime, rest days, special days, regular holidays, night differential, and other supported cases.
- Respect each employee's applicable schedule, employment status, and payroll classification. Do not give every employee identical attendance.
- Create coherent attendance records across enough completed payroll periods to make employee histories, reports, and charts useful. Prefer at least the latest 12 completed monthly periods where the project supports monthly payroll. Do not invent a completed payroll for an unfinished period.
- Make attendance and payroll agree. Overtime, absences, lateness, leaves, holiday work, and other paid/unpaid time must reconcile with the corresponding payroll calculations.
- Avoid impossible or contradictory records, such as overlapping shifts, duplicate clock events, overtime outside a plausible shift, or paid leave that is also deducted as an absence.
- Where the employee CSV or sample timecard does not establish a value, choose a plausible assumption, document it in the data-generation notes, and keep it consistent across all affected records.

### Payroll

- Generate a plausible payroll history for every employee using the employee CSV and timecard/payslip material.
- Retain employee-specific salary rates, employment categories, allowances, and other applicable inputs where those are actually present in the sources.
- Calculate the gross pay, earnings, deductions, statutory contributions, withholding tax, and net pay through the application's calculation services. Do not randomly assign final payroll totals.
- Ensure every payslip item reconciles to its source attendance and payroll inputs. Totals must add correctly and round consistently to centavos.
- Implement or retain separate, testable calculations for ordinary pay, overtime, rest-day work, special non-working holidays, regular holidays, night differential, leave treatment, statutory deductions, and tax, to the extent supported by the source data and applicable rules.
- Verify Philippine statutory rates, thresholds, and payroll rules against current authoritative sources applicable to the payroll period. Keep effective dates and source references in the calculation documentation. Do not silently apply a 2026 rate to a different period if the rate changed.
- Do not present a provisional assumption as a statutory fact. Where a rule or employee classification is unavailable, document the assumption and make the result traceable.
- Support payroll preparation, review, approval (if applicable), processing, and payslip generation as separate states. Prevent duplicate processing of the same employee/pay period.

### Data provenance and presentation

The user-facing application must not display terms such as **fictional**, **version**, **demo**, or **synthetic data** as labels, badges, page names, or explanatory copy. Remove those terms from visible product wording and obsolete UI elements.

However, attendance and payroll records generated to populate the application must remain truthfully identified as seeded/test records in internal documentation and test fixtures. Do not claim that generated records are actual company attendance or historical payroll. Keep data provenance out of normal employee-facing screens, but preserve it for maintainers, auditors, and testing. Do not delete provenance notes merely to make the interface look production-ready.

## 11. My Pay: MotorPH calculation and Sweldong Pinoy comparison

Add a switch in the **My Pay** tab, available to all employees, between:

- the application's MotorPH payroll calculation; and
- a Sweldong Pinoy-based calculation/reference.

Before implementing the second option, inspect the current Sweldong Pinoy calculator and establish what inputs, assumptions, rates, and outputs it uses. Use a public, legitimate source; do not depend on an undocumented private endpoint or brittle page scraping. Where practical, implement the comparison as a separate calculation module using documented rules rather than embedding an external website in the application.

Both views must use the same employee and pay-period inputs. Clearly identify which calculation is being displayed, explain any differing assumptions, and show discrepancies without silently changing the actual payroll record. The switch is for employee comparison and understanding; it must not alter a processed payslip or the official payroll calculation. Add tests for representative employees and calculation edge cases.

#!/usr/bin/env sh
# Compile every main source (all packages under ph/motorph) and, optionally, the tests.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
case "$(uname -s)" in MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*) S=";" ;; *) S=":" ;; esac
mkdir -p target/classes target/test-classes
find src/main/java -name '*.java' > target/main-sources.txt
# Resources travel with the classes: the employee file is read from the classpath at startup.
mkdir -p target/classes
cp -r src/main/resources/. target/classes/
javac -encoding UTF-8 --add-modules jdk.httpserver -cp "lib/gson-2.13.2.jar${S}lib/bcprov-jdk18on-1.78.1.jar" -d target/classes @target/main-sources.txt
if [ "${1:-}" = "--with-tests" ]; then
  find src/test/java -name '*.java' > target/test-sources.txt
  javac -encoding UTF-8 --add-modules jdk.httpserver \
    -cp "lib/gson-2.13.2.jar${S}lib/bcprov-jdk18on-1.78.1.jar${S}target/classes" \
    -d target/test-classes @target/test-sources.txt
fi

$ cd /home/user/motorph-v3 && mkdir -p /tmp/strip && cat > /tmp/strip/strip.py <<'PY' import pathlib, re, sys def strip_java(text): out, i, n = [], 0, len(text) while i < n: c = text[i] if c == '"': j = i + 1 while j < n: if text[j] == '\\': j += 2; continue if text[j] == '"': break j += 1 out.append(text[i:j+1]); i = j + 1; continue if c == "'": j = i + 1 while j < n: if text[j] == '\\': j += 2; continue if text[j] == "'": break j += 1 out.append(text[i:j+1]); i = j + 1; continue if text.startswith('//', i): j = text.find('\n', i) if j == -1: break i = j; continue if text.startswith('/*', i): j = text.find('*/', i + 2) if j == -1: break i = j + 2 while i < n and text[i] in '\r\n': if text[i] == '\n': out.append('\n') i += 1 continue out.append(c); i += 1 return ''.join(out) def strip_js(text): out, i, n = [], 0, len(text) while i < n: c = text[i] for q in ('"', "'", '`'): if c == q: j = i + 1 while j < n: if text[j] == '\\': j += 2; continue if text[j] == q: break if q == '`' and text.startswith('${', j): depth = 1; j += 2 while j < n and depth: if text[j] == '{': depth += 1 elif text[j] == '}': depth -= 1 elif text[j] == '`': j += 1 while j < n and text[j] != '`': if text[j] == '\\': j += 1 j += 1 j += 1 continue j += 1 out.append(text[i:j+1]); i += len(m.group(0)); continue out.append(c); i += 1 return ''.join(out) targets = [] for pat in ('src/main/java/**/*.java', 'src/test/java/**/*.java', 'web/*.js'): targets += list(pathlib.Path('.').glob(pat)) total = 0 for f in targets: t = f.read_text(errors='replace') new = strip_java(t) if f.suffix == '.java' else strip_js(t) # collapse 3+ blank lines left behind new = re.sub(r'\n{3,}', '\n\n', new) if new != t: total += 1 f.write_text(new) print(f"stripped comments in {total} files") PY python3 /tmp/strip/strip.py

async function savedSessionFor(employeeId) {
  const session = sessionStorage.getItem(SESSION_KEY) || '';
  if (!session) return '';
  const response = await fetch('/api/auth/session', { headers: { Accept: 'application/json', 'X-Demo-Session': session } });
  const payload = await response.json().catch(() => ({}));
  return response.ok && payload.employeeId === employeeId ? session : '';
}

async function seedFromChooser(button) {
  button.disabled = true;
  button.textContent = 'Adding imported people…';
  try {
    const response = await fetch('/api/demo/seed', { method: 'POST', headers: await apiHeaders() });
    const payload = await response.json();
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(payload.error || `Request failed (${response.status})`);
    await startAccountChooser();
  } catch (error) {
    const message = document.getElementById('account-error');
    message.textContent = error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Could not add the imported people.';
    message.hidden = false;
    button.disabled = false;
    button.textContent = 'Add imported demo people';
  }
}

async function postAuth(url, body, session = '') {
  const headers = { Accept: 'application/json', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' };
  if (session) headers['X-Demo-Session'] = session;
  const response = await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers, body: JSON.stringify(body) });
  const payload = await response.json();
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(payload.error || `Request failed (${response.status})`);
  return payload;
}

async function seedImportedDemoData() {
  seedDemoButton.disabled = true;
  seedDemoButton.textContent = 'Writing imported records…';
  try {
    const response = await fetch('/api/demo/seed', { method: 'POST', headers: await apiHeaders() });
    const payload = await response.json();
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(payload.error || `Request failed (${response.status})`);
    resultCount.textContent = `${payload.employeesCreated} employees and ${payload.attendanceCreated} attendance entries added`;
    await loadEmployees();
  } catch (error) {
    showTableMessage(error.message || 'Could not write the imported records.');
    resultCount.textContent = 'Setup failed';
  } finally {
    seedDemoButton.disabled = false;
    seedDemoButton.textContent = 'Add records';
  }
}

function applyWorkflowItem(collection, item, storage) {
  const current = state.workflow[collection];
  const index = current.findIndex(existing => existing.id === item.id);

  if (index < 0) next.unshift(item);
  else next[index] = item;
  state.workflow = { ...state.workflow, [collection]: next };
  setWorkflowStorageMode(storage === 'user-scoped-firestore' ? 'User-scoped Firestore' : 'Local API memory');
  renderWorkflow();

async function postAuth(url, body, session = '') {
  const headers = { Accept: 'application/json', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' };
  if (session) headers['X-Demo-Session'] = session;
  const response = await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers, body: JSON.stringify(body) });
  const payload = await response.json();
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(payload.error || `Request failed (${response.status})`);
  return payload;
}

  state.session = '';
  window.location.reload();
});

    private void handleStaticFiles(HttpExchange exchange) throws IOException {
        boolean headOnly = "HEAD".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod());
        if (!"GET".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod()) && !headOnly) {
            sendText(exchange, 405, "text/plain; charset=utf-8", "Method not allowed");
            return;
        }
        String requestPath = exchange.getRequestURI().getPath();
        if (requestPath == null || "/".equals(requestPath)) requestPath = "/b_basic/Index.html";
        Path requested = webRoot.resolve(requestPath.substring(1)).normalize();
        if (!requested.startsWith(webRoot) || !Files.isRegularFile(requested)) {
            sendText(exchange, 404, "text/plain; charset=utf-8", "Not found");
            return;
        }
        String contentType = contentTypeFor(requested);
        byte[] bytes = Files.readAllBytes(requested);
        exchange.getResponseHeaders().set("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff");
        exchange.getResponseHeaders().set("Cache-Control", "no-store");
        exchange.getResponseHeaders().set("Content-Security-Policy",
            "default-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; "
                + "connect-src 'self' https://identitytoolkit.googleapis.com https://securetoken.googleapis.com; "
                + "object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'");
        exchange.getResponseHeaders().set("Referrer-Policy", "no-referrer");
        exchange.getResponseHeaders().set("Permissions-Policy", "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()");
        exchange.getResponseHeaders().set("Content-Type", contentType);
        if (headOnly) {
            exchange.getResponseHeaders().set("Content-Length", Integer.toString(bytes.length));
            exchange.sendResponseHeaders(200, -1);
            exchange.close();
            return;
        }
        exchange.sendResponseHeaders(200, bytes.length);
        try (OutputStream out = exchange.getResponseBody()) { out.write(bytes); }
    }

$ cd /home/user/motorph-v3 && cat > src/main/java/ph/motorph/c_calc/NOTES.md <<'EOF' # c_calc Payroll maths. Everything that turns attendance into pesos lives here. - `CutoffPayrollService` — one cutoff's gross. Day types: ordinary, rest day, special non-working, regular holiday. A *worked* holiday pays `workedUnits × (multiplier − 1)` on top of base, not the full multiplier. I got this wrong once and every holiday came out double. - `MonthPayroll` — the two cutoffs of a month. `grossForMonth` hands back a `List<CutoffPay>`, so `.get(i)`. There is no `getCutoffs()`. - `StatutoryRates` / `StatutoryCalculator2026` — SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, BIR. Rates carry an effective month; a month uses the newest version on or before it. Don't backdate a 2026 rate onto 2023 and call it correct. - Hourly is `monthlyBasic ÷ 20 ÷ 8` (daily ÷ 8). The ÷168 thing is the old engine, it's dead. - `SalaryHistory.monthlyBasic(...)` returns `Optional`. `.get()` it or the compiler will not save you. Wages are cents in `long` everywhere. No `double`, no `float`, no `BigDecimal` in the hot path. EOF cat > src/main/java/ph/motorph/o_oop/NOTES.md <<'EOF' # o_oop The objects: employee, org chart, the stores, the CSV importer. - `EmployeeImport.fromClasspath()` reads `data/EmployeeDetails.csv`, 34 people. That file is the roster. There is no other roster and there must not be one. - `Employee.getFullName()` is `"Last, First"`. `getName()` is `"First Last"`. Both get used; check which one before you print. - `OrgChart` walks the supervisor column recursively. Latian's and De Leon's teams sit under Romualdez, so Romualdez sees both plus anyone under them. - `InMemoryEmployeeStore` starts **empty**. Tests seed it from `TestRoster`. Do not put people in the constructor — that is how the fake data got in last time. - The supervisor column in the CSV is unreliable in places. Branch assignment uses addresses, not supervisors. EOF cat > src/main/java/ph/motorph/sp_secpol/NOTES.md <<'EOF' # sp_secpol Passwords, sessions, and who may read what. - `PasswordHasher` is Argon2id + per-account salt + server pepper. Pepper comes from `MOTORPH_PEPPER` and must be ≥32 chars. No pepper = the server refuses to start. That is on purpose; a pepper in the repo is not a pepper. - `PasswordHasher` throws `IllegalStateException` for a short pepper, not `IllegalArgumentException`. - `SessionCookie`: `motorph_session` is HttpOnly, `motorph_csrf` is readable (the page has to read it), both `SameSite=Strict`, `Max-Age=28800`. - Idle 15 min, absolute 8 h, checked lazily on each request. No timer thread. - Bumping `lastActive` counts as activity — if you test the idle boundary, make a fresh untouched token, or the act of asking resets the clock and the test lies to you. - `AccessPolicy.READ` is the matrix. `web/b_basic/Roles.js` mirrors the *company-wide* part of it so the page stops asking for things the server will refuse. If you change one, change both, or the console fills with red 403s that look like bugs. - TEAM scope is recursive for reads, direct reports only for writes. EOF cat > src/main/java/ph/motorph/t_tkt/NOTES.md <<'EOF' # t_tkt Leave, overtime, tickets. - `WorkflowService` holds the rules; the store just persists. - Errors here are read by people, not devs. If you put an employee id or a "demo" word in a message, it shows up in the UI forever. Two shipped that way already. - `InMemoryWorkflowStore` is for tests. `FirestoreWorkflowStore` is the live one when Firebase is configured. - `FirestoreSeedService` only works against Firestore. EOF cat > src/main/java/ph/motorph/svc/NOTES.md <<'EOF' # svc `AppServer` — the whole HTTP layer in one file. Yes, one file, on purpose; it's the JDK's built-in server and splitting it would mean passing twenty dependencies around. - Every route goes through `context(...)`, which is where CSRF is enforced once so no endpoint can forget it. `/api/auth/signin` is the only exemption, and only because you have no cookie yet to protect. - `actorFromCookie` resolves the session. No cookie, no actor. - Writes run inside `synchronized (stateLock)` and save the data file after, so a crash can't leave half a request applied. - Serving the UI: `/` is `/b_basic/Index.html`. Unknown path gets the 404 page **with a real 404 status** — a pretty page returning 200 is a soft 404 and it's worse than nothing. EOF cat > web/b_basic/NOTES.md <<'EOF' # web/b_basic The screens and the glue. - `Index.html` — one page, all views, toggled by `hidden`. It's big; it's the app. - `Roles.js` — client mirror of the access matrix. Server is the authority. - The sidebar footer used to say "Prototype data only. Not for payroll processing." It does payroll now, so it doesn't say that. - `Styles.css` and `Workflow.css` are dead weight from before the Tailwind theme. `main.css` (at `web/`) is the real stylesheet and it compiles to `web/app.css`. Don't edit `app.css` by hand. [NODE 18435]
• What it is: A Session ID is a random string (like a digital ID badge) that links a user's browser to their data on the server.
• Security Rule: It must be a completely random, opaque string (e.g., 32 random bytes). It should never contain meaningful data like timestamps or user IDs, as this exposes system logic to attackers.
• Storage:
• Browser: Stored in a secure HttpOnly cookie.
• Server: Stored in a database (SQL, Redis) or memory to validate the user.

[NODE 18436]
There are two critical clocks ticking for every session:

[NODE 18437]
Inactivity Timeout (Idle Limit):
• Purpose: Logs out a user if they stop interacting with the page (e.g., walk away for lunch).
• Standard Duration: 15–30 minutes for sensitive apps (payroll, banking); longer for social media.
• Reset Mechanism: Every click or request resets this timer to zero.

[NODE 18438]
Absolute Timeout (Hard Limit):
• Purpose: Forces a re-login after a set period regardless of activity, ensuring long-running sessions don't become security risks.
• Standard Duration: 8–12 hours (matches a workday).
• Reset Mechanism: Does not reset. Once the time is up, the session dies.

[NODE 18439]
The Architecture: How to Handle Expiration

[NODE 18440]
We explored three ways to manage these timeouts, concluding that Option C is the industry standard for production apps.

[NODE 18441]
Approach How it works Verdict
A. Timestamp inside ID Embedding the expiration date inside the Session ID string (e.g., ID_12:00PM). Don't do this. It leaks server info, complicates database cleanup (heavy string parsing), and reduces security.
B. Per-Tick Loop Running a background script that checks every second: "Is it expired yet?" Inefficient. Wastes CPU power and doesn't scale well for thousands of users.
C. Event-Driven (Lazy) The server does nothing until a user makes a request. Then it checks timestamps. Best Practice. Zero CPU waste. The database cleans itself only when needed.

[NODE 18442]
The Database Schema

[NODE 18443]
Store session metadata in columns, not the ID string.
sql
TABLE sessions (
session_id VARCHAR PRIMARY KEY, -- The random token
user_id INT, -- Who owns it
last_active TIMESTAMP, -- Updates on every click
expires_at TIMESTAMP -- The hard deadline (8 hrs from login)
);
Use code with caution.

[NODE 18444]
The Logic Flow (The "Lazy" Check)

[NODE 18445]
This logic runs on every incoming HTTP request:

[NODE 18446]
The Frontend "Auto-Logout"

[NODE 18447]
Since the server cannot see if a user walked away, use JavaScript to handle the UI:
• Script: Listen for mouse/keyboard events.
• Action: If no events occur for 15 minutes, redirect the user to the login page immediately.
• Security Note: This is just for UX. The real security is the server-side check above.

[NODE 18448]
Cleanup (The "Garbage Collector")

[NODE 18449]
To remove abandoned sessions (users who closed the tab without logging out):
• SQL: Run a daily job: DELETE FROM sessions WHERE last_active < NOW() - INTERVAL '15 MIN'.
• Redis: Use native TTL (Time-To-Live). Redis automatically deletes the key when the timer hits zero—no code required.
