const TAB_KEY = 'motorph-tab-';
const ALL_KEY = 'motorph-all-sections';

export function parseTabs(spec) {
  return String(spec || '').split('|').map(part => part.trim()).filter(Boolean).map(part => {
    const [key, ...label] = part.split(':');
    return { key: key.trim(), label: label.join(':').trim() || key.trim() };
  });
}

export function firstSentence(text) {
  const clean = String(text || '').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
  const match = clean.match(/^(.+?[.!?])(\s|$)/);
  return match ? match[1] : clean;
}

export function badgeCount(elements) {
  let count = 0;
  elements.forEach(element => {
    count += element.querySelectorAll('button[aria-label^="Approve "]').length;
    count += [...element.querySelectorAll('td')].filter(cell => cell.textContent.startsWith('Failed:')).length;
  });
  return count;
}

const available = element => !element.hidden && !element.classList.contains('role-hidden');

function shortenIntros(page) {
  page.querySelectorAll('p.payroll-preview-intro, p.processing-note:not([id]):not([role]), .notice > p').forEach(paragraph => {
    if (paragraph.dataset.shortened || paragraph.textContent.trim().length < 140) return;
    paragraph.dataset.shortened = 'true';
    const short = document.createElement('p');
    short.className = `${paragraph.className} intro-short`;
    short.textContent = firstSentence(paragraph.textContent);
    const more = document.createElement('details');
    more.className = 'intro-more';
    const summary = document.createElement('summary');
    summary.textContent = 'How this works';
    paragraph.replaceWith(short);
    more.append(summary, paragraph);
    short.after(more);
  });
}

export function initPageTabs(root = document) {
  const pages = [...root.querySelectorAll('.page-view[data-tabs]')];
  const state = new Map();

  function showAll() { return window.localStorage.getItem(ALL_KEY) === 'true'; }

  function apply(page) {
    const entry = state.get(page);
    const tabbed = [...page.querySelectorAll('[data-tab]')];
    const keysOf = element => element.dataset.tab.split(/\s+/);
    const usable = entry.tabs.filter(tab => tabbed.some(element => keysOf(element).includes(tab.key) && available(element)
      && (!element.parentElement.closest('[data-tab-group]') || available(element.parentElement.closest('[data-tab-group]')))));
    let active = entry.active;
    if (!usable.some(tab => tab.key === active)) active = usable.length ? usable[0].key : '';
    entry.active = active;
    const all = showAll();
    entry.observer.disconnect();
    tabbed.forEach(element => element.classList.toggle('tab-off', !all && !keysOf(element).includes(active)));
    page.querySelectorAll('[data-tab-group]').forEach(group => {
      const anyOn = [...group.querySelectorAll('[data-tab]')].some(element => !element.classList.contains('tab-off') && available(element));
      group.classList.toggle('tab-off', !all && !anyOn);
    });
    entry.bar.hidden = usable.length < 2 && !all;
    entry.buttons.forEach((button, key) => {
      const tab = entry.tabs.find(item => item.key === key);
      button.hidden = !usable.includes(tab);
      const selected = !all && key === active;
      button.setAttribute('aria-selected', String(selected));
      button.tabIndex = selected || (all && key === usable[0]?.key) ? 0 : -1;
      const count = badgeCount(tabbed.filter(element => keysOf(element).includes(key) && available(element)));
      const badge = button.querySelector('.tab-badge');
      badge.textContent = count ? String(count) : '';
      badge.hidden = !count;
      button.setAttribute('aria-label', count ? `${tab.label} (${count} waiting)` : tab.label);
    });
    entry.allToggle.textContent = all ? 'Show one section at a time' : 'Show all sections';
    entry.allToggle.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(all));
    entry.observer.observe(page, { subtree: true, childList: true, attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['hidden', 'class'] });
  }

  function select(page, key, focus = false) {
    const entry = state.get(page);
    entry.active = key;
    window.sessionStorage.setItem(TAB_KEY + page.id, key);
    if (showAll()) window.localStorage.setItem(ALL_KEY, 'false');
    pages.forEach(apply);
    if (focus) entry.buttons.get(key).focus();
  }

  pages.forEach(page => {
    shortenIntros(page);
    const tabs = parseTabs(page.dataset.tabs);
    const bar = document.createElement('div');
    bar.className = 'page-tabs';
    const list = document.createElement('div');
    list.className = 'page-tab-list';
    list.setAttribute('role', 'tablist');
    list.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Sections on this page');
    const buttons = new Map();
    tabs.forEach(tab => {
      const button = document.createElement('button');
      button.type = 'button';
      button.className = 'page-tab';
      button.setAttribute('role', 'tab');
      button.dataset.tabKey = tab.key;
      const label = document.createElement('span');
      label.textContent = tab.label;
      const badge = document.createElement('span');
      badge.className = 'tab-badge';
      badge.hidden = true;
      button.append(label, badge);
      button.addEventListener('click', () => select(page, tab.key));
      button.addEventListener('keydown', event => {
        if (!['ArrowRight', 'ArrowLeft', 'Home', 'End'].includes(event.key)) return;
        event.preventDefault();
        const visible = [...buttons.values()].filter(item => !item.hidden);
        const index = visible.indexOf(button);
        const next = event.key === 'Home' ? visible[0] : event.key === 'End' ? visible[visible.length - 1]
          : visible[(index + (event.key === 'ArrowRight' ? 1 : -1) + visible.length) % visible.length];
        select(page, next.dataset.tabKey, true);
      });
      buttons.set(tab.key, button);
      list.append(button);
    });
    const allToggle = document.createElement('button');
    allToggle.type = 'button';
    allToggle.className = 'page-tabs-all';
    allToggle.addEventListener('click', () => {
      window.localStorage.setItem(ALL_KEY, String(!showAll()));
      pages.forEach(apply);
    });
    bar.append(list, allToggle);
    const anchor = page.querySelector(':scope > .notice') || page.querySelector(':scope > .page-heading');
    if (anchor) anchor.after(bar);
    else page.prepend(bar);
    let pending = false;
    const observer = new MutationObserver(() => {
      if (pending) return;
      pending = true;
      window.requestAnimationFrame(() => {
        pending = false;
        apply(page);
      });
    });
    state.set(page, { tabs, bar, buttons, allToggle, observer, active: window.sessionStorage.getItem(TAB_KEY + page.id) || tabs[0]?.key || '' });
  });
  pages.forEach(apply);

  return {
    refresh: () => pages.forEach(apply),
    
    reveal(element) {
      const page = element.closest('.page-view[data-tabs]');
      const holder = element.closest('[data-tab]');
      if (page && holder) select(page, holder.dataset.tab.split(/\s+/)[0]);
    }
  };
}

import { buildCutoffPayroll } from '../f_flares/PayrollCutoff.js';

export function clockText(status) {
  const tag = status.attendanceTag ? ` · ${status.attendanceTag}` : '';
  if (status.clockedIn) return { state: 'Clocked in', detail: `Since ${status.since} today (${status.today})${tag}.`, button: 'Clock out' };
  if (status.todayRecord) {
    const hours = status.workHourTag ? ` · ${status.workHourTag} hours` : '';
    return { state: 'Done for today', detail: `In ${status.todayRecord.timeIn} · out ${status.todayRecord.timeOut} (${status.today})${tag}${hours}.`, button: null };
  }
  return { state: 'Clocked out', detail: `Not clocked in yet today (${status.today}).`, button: 'Clock in' };
}

export function clockInQuestion(status) {
  if (!status.dayType || status.dayType === 'Workday') return null;
  return `Today is a ${status.dayType.replace(/^On approved leave/, 'day on approved leave')} for you. Clock in anyway?`;
}

export function locationText(status) {
  if (status.location === 'Onsite') return `Onsite · QR scanned at the branch at ${status.onsiteSince}`;
  if (status.clockedIn) return 'Offsite · clocked in from the app. Scan the QR code at the branch to check in onsite.';
  return status.todayRecord ? 'Offsite (no branch scan today)' : '';
}

export function qrPattern(code) {
  const size = 21;
  let seed = 0;
  for (const letter of String(code)) seed = (seed * 31 + letter.charCodeAt(0)) >>> 0;
  const finder = (r, c) => {
    for (const [top, left] of [[0, 0], [0, size - 7], [size - 7, 0]]) {
      const y = r - top, x = c - left;
      if (y >= 0 && y < 7 && x >= 0 && x < 7) return y === 0 || y === 6 || x === 0 || x === 6 || (y >= 2 && y <= 4 && x >= 2 && x <= 4) ? 1 : 0;
      if (y >= -1 && y <= 7 && x >= -1 && x <= 7) return 0;
    }
    return null;
  };
  return Array.from({ length: size }, (_, r) => Array.from({ length: size }, (_, c) => {
    const fixed = finder(r, c);
    if (fixed !== null) return fixed;
    seed = (seed * 1103515245 + 12345) >>> 0;
    return (seed >>> 16) & 1;
  }));
}

function qrSvg(code) {
  const grid = qrPattern(code);
  const svg = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'svg');
  svg.setAttribute('viewBox', '-1 -1 23 23');
  svg.setAttribute('role', 'img');
  svg.setAttribute('aria-label', `Kiosk QR picture for ${code} (not scannable)`);
  const background = document.createElementNS(svg.namespaceURI, 'rect');
  background.setAttribute('x', '-1');
  background.setAttribute('y', '-1');
  background.setAttribute('width', '23');
  background.setAttribute('height', '23');
  background.setAttribute('fill', '#fff');
  svg.append(background);
  grid.forEach((row, r) => row.forEach((on, c) => {
    if (!on) return;
    const cell = document.createElementNS(svg.namespaceURI, 'rect');
    cell.setAttribute('x', String(c));
    cell.setAttribute('y', String(r));
    cell.setAttribute('width', '1');
    cell.setAttribute('height', '1');
    cell.setAttribute('fill', '#0b1736');
    svg.append(cell);
  }));
  return svg;
}

export function clockOutQuestions(clock) {
  const questions = ['Clock out now? Today’s attendance will be recorded and can only be changed by your supervisor.'];
  if (clock.now && clock.shiftEnd && clock.now.slice(0, 5) < clock.shiftEnd) {
    questions.push(`Your shift ends at ${clock.shiftEnd}. Clocking out now counts as undertime. Clock out early anyway?`);
  }
  return questions;
}

export function trackerSummary(payload, today, asOf = '') {
  const result = buildCutoffPayroll(payload);
  const index = Number(today.slice(8, 10)) <= 15 ? 0 : 1;
  const cutoff = result.cutoffs[index];
  const extras = [];
  if (payload.cutoffs[index].leaveDays) extras.push(`${payload.cutoffs[index].leaveDays} paid leave day(s)`);
  if (payload.cutoffs[index].holidayDays) extras.push(`${payload.cutoffs[index].holidayDays} paid holiday(s)`);
  return {
    period: `${cutoff.label} ${result.month} (${cutoff.from} – ${cutoff.to})`,
    figures: [
      ['PAID HOURS SO FAR', `${cutoff.hours} h over ${cutoff.daysWithRecords} day(s)${extras.length ? ` + ${extras.join(', ')}` : ''}`],
      ['GROSS SO FAR', formatPesoCents(cutoff.grossCents)],
      ['EST. DEDUCTIONS', `−${formatPesoCents(cutoff.deductionsCents)}`],
      ['EST. NET THIS CUTOFF', cutoff.netCents === null ? 'Not enough pay yet to cover this cutoff’s deductions' : formatPesoCents(cutoff.netCents)],
      ['MONTH GROSS SO FAR', formatPesoCents(result.monthlyGrossCents)]
    ],
    asOf: asOf ? `Estimate as of ${today} ${asOf.slice(0, 5)}` : '',
    note: `${asOf ? `Estimate as of ${today} ${asOf.slice(0, 5)}. ` : ''}Rate ₱${result.hourlyRate}/h. Estimate from attendance, approved overtime, paid leave and holidays up to today; deductions are half of the month's so far and change as the month goes on. Payroll Staff finalize the actual payslip.`
  };
}

export function initMyDay(apiJson) {
  const panel = document.getElementById('my-day-panel');
  const button = document.getElementById('clock-button');
  const status = document.getElementById('clock-status');
  let action = 'in';
  let current = null;

  function showError(target, error, fallback) {
    target.textContent = error instanceof Error ? error.message : fallback;
  }

  async function refreshTracker(clock) {
    const figures = document.getElementById('tracker-figures');
    try {
      const payload = await apiJson(`/api/payroll/cutoffs?employeeId=${encodeURIComponent(clock.employeeId)}&month=${clock.today.slice(0, 7)}&through=${clock.today}`);
      const view = trackerSummary(payload, clock.today, clock.now || '');
      document.getElementById('tracker-period').textContent = view.period;
      figures.replaceChildren();
      view.figures.forEach(([label, value]) => {
        const term = document.createElement('dt');
        term.textContent = label;
        const description = document.createElement('dd');
        description.textContent = value;
        figures.append(term, description);
      });
      document.getElementById('tracker-note').textContent = view.note;
    } catch (error) {
      figures.replaceChildren();
      showError(document.getElementById('tracker-note'), error, 'Could not load the salary tracker.');
    }
  }

  function render(clock) {
    const view = clockText(clock);
    document.getElementById('clock-state').textContent = view.state;
    document.getElementById('clock-detail').textContent = view.detail;
    button.hidden = !view.button;
    if (view.button) button.textContent = view.button;
    action = clock.clockedIn ? 'out' : 'in';
    current = clock;
    document.getElementById('clock-location').textContent = locationText(clock);
    const qr = document.getElementById('onsite-qr');
    qr.hidden = !clock.qrCode;
    document.getElementById('onsite-new-qr').hidden = !(clock.clockedIn && clock.location !== 'Onsite' && !clock.qrCode);
    if (clock.qrCode) {
      document.getElementById('onsite-qr-image').replaceChildren(qrSvg(clock.qrCode));
      document.getElementById('onsite-qr-code').textContent = clock.qrCode;
      document.getElementById('onsite-qr-expiry').textContent = `Valid until ${clock.qrExpiresAt}`;
    }
  }

  async function sendClock(body, done) {
    try {
      const clock = await apiJson('/api/attendance/clock', body);
      render(clock);
      status.textContent = done(clock);
    } catch (error) {
      showError(status, error, 'Could not update the time clock.');
      
      apiJson('/api/attendance/clock').then(render).catch(() => {});
    }
  }

  document.getElementById('onsite-scan').addEventListener('click', () =>
    sendClock({ action: 'onsite', code: current ? current.qrCode : '' }, clock => `Checked in onsite at ${clock.onsiteSince}.`));
  document.getElementById('onsite-new-qr').addEventListener('click', () =>
    sendClock({ action: 'qr' }, () => 'New QR code shown; it is valid for 10 minutes.'));

  async function refresh() {
    panel.hidden = false;
    try {
      const clock = await apiJson('/api/attendance/clock');
      render(clock);
      await refreshTracker(clock);
    } catch (error) {
      showError(status, error, 'Could not load the time clock.');
    }
  }

  button.addEventListener('click', async () => {
    if (action === 'in') {
      const latest = await apiJson('/api/attendance/clock').catch(() => current);
      const question = clockInQuestion(latest || {});
      if (question && !window.confirm(question)) {
        status.textContent = 'Not clocked in.';
        return;
      }
    }
    if (action === 'out') {
      
      const latest = await apiJson('/api/attendance/clock').catch(() => current);
      if (!clockOutQuestions(latest || {}).every(question => window.confirm(question))) {
        status.textContent = 'Still clocked in.';
        return;
      }
    }
    button.disabled = true;
    try {
      const clock = await apiJson('/api/attendance/clock', { action });
      render(clock);
      status.textContent = clock.record ? `Clocked out at ${clock.record.timeOut}. Today's attendance is recorded.` : `Clocked in at ${clock.since}.`;
      await refreshTracker(clock);
    } catch (error) {
      showError(status, error, 'Could not update the time clock.');
    } finally {
      button.disabled = false;
    }
  });

  return { refresh };
}

export function dayChangeRows(schedules, names = {}) {
  return schedules.flatMap(item => (item.dayChanges || []).map(change => ({
    id: change.id,
    employeeId: change.employeeId,
    cells: [`${change.employeeId} — ${names[change.employeeId] || ''}`.trim(), change.from === change.to ? change.from : `${change.from} to ${change.to}`,
      change.shiftStart ? `Shift from ${change.shiftStart}` : 'Day off', change.reason]
  })));
}

export function initSupervisorTools(apiJson, { getAccount, getNames }) {
  if (!document.getElementById('schedule-form')) return { refresh() {} };
  const value = id => document.getElementById(id).value;

  async function refreshSchedules() {
    try {
      const { schedules } = await apiJson('/api/schedules');
      table(document.getElementById('schedule-rows'), scheduleRows(schedules, getNames()), 5, 'No schedules visible.');
      const account = getAccount();
      const canChange = account && ['SUPERVISOR', 'ADMIN'].includes(account.role);
      table(document.getElementById('daychange-rows'), dayChangeRows(schedules, getNames()).map(item => {
        if (!canChange || item.employeeId === account.employeeId) return [...item.cells, '—'];
        const button = document.createElement('button');
        button.type = 'button';
        button.className = 'button button-quiet workflow-cancel';
        button.textContent = 'Remove';
        button.dataset.changeId = item.id;
        button.setAttribute('aria-label', `Remove ${item.id}`);
        return [...item.cells, button];
      }), 5, 'No single-day or multi-day changes.');
      const chosen = schedules.find(item => item.employeeId === value('schedule-employee'));
      if (chosen) {
        document.getElementById('schedule-start').value = chosen.shiftStart;
        DAYS.forEach(day => { document.getElementById(`schedule-day-${day}`).checked = chosen.workdays.includes(day); });
      }
    } catch (error) {
      say(document.getElementById('schedule-status'), error.message, true);
    }
  }

  async function refreshCorrections() {
    const employeeId = value('correction-employee');
    const rowsSelect = document.getElementById('correction-row');
    rowsSelect.replaceChildren();
    try {
      if (employeeId) {
        const payload = await apiJson(`/api/attendance?employeeId=${encodeURIComponent(employeeId)}`);
        (payload.records || payload.items || []).forEach(record => {
          const option = document.createElement('option');
          option.value = String(record.attendanceId);
          option.textContent = `${record.date} · ${record.timeIn}–${record.timeOut} (#${record.attendanceId})`;
          rowsSelect.append(option);
        });
      }
      const { corrections } = await apiJson('/api/attendance/corrections');
      table(document.getElementById('correction-rows'), corrections.map(item => [`${item.employeeId} · ${item.date}`,
        `${item.originalTimeIn}–${item.originalTimeOut}`, `${item.timeIn}–${item.timeOut}`, item.reason, `${item.editedBy} · ${item.editedAt}`]), 5, 'No timesheet corrections yet.');
    } catch (error) {
      say(document.getElementById('correction-status'), error.message, true);
    }
  }

  async function refreshPayChanges() {
    try {
      const account = getAccount();
      const { requests } = await apiJson('/api/pay-changes');
      table(document.getElementById('paychange-rows'), requests.map(request => {
        let action = request.outcome || '—';
        if (canReviewPayChange(account, request)) {
          action = document.createElement('span');
          action.className = 'workflow-row-actions';
          ['approve', 'reject'].forEach(decision => {
            const button = document.createElement('button');
            button.type = 'button';
            button.className = 'button button-quiet workflow-cancel';
            button.textContent = decision === 'approve' ? 'Approve' : 'Reject';
            button.dataset.paychangeId = request.id;
            button.dataset.decision = decision;
            button.setAttribute('aria-label', `${button.textContent} ${request.id}`);
            action.append(button);
          });
        }
        return [request.id, `${request.employeeId} — ${request.employeeName}`, payChangeSummary(request), request.note || '—',
          `${request.status}${request.reviewerId ? ` by ${request.reviewerId}` : ` (${request.approverRole === 'PAYROLL' ? 'Payroll Staff' : 'HR'})`}`, action];
      }), 6, 'No pay-change requests.');
    } catch (error) {
      say(document.getElementById('paychange-status'), error.message, true);
    }
  }

  document.getElementById('schedule-employee').addEventListener('change', refreshSchedules);
  document.getElementById('schedule-form').addEventListener('submit', async event => {
    event.preventDefault();
    const status = document.getElementById('schedule-status');
    try {
      const workdays = DAYS.filter(day => document.getElementById(`schedule-day-${day}`).checked);
      const response = await fetchPut(apiJson, `/api/schedules/${encodeURIComponent(value('schedule-employee'))}`, { shiftStart: value('schedule-start'), workdays });
      say(status, `Saved: ${response.schedule.shiftStart}–${response.schedule.shiftEnd}, ${workdaysText(response.schedule.workdays)}. Pay uses it from now on (finalized payslips keep theirs).`);
      await refreshSchedules();
    } catch (error) {
      say(status, error.message, true);
    }
  });

  document.getElementById('correction-employee').addEventListener('change', refreshCorrections);
  document.getElementById('correction-form').addEventListener('submit', async event => {
    event.preventDefault();
    const status = document.getElementById('correction-status');
    try {
      const { correction } = await apiJson('/api/attendance/corrections', { employeeId: value('correction-employee'),
        attendanceId: Number(value('correction-row')), timeIn: value('correction-in'), timeOut: value('correction-out'), reason: value('correction-reason') });
      say(status, `Corrected ${correction.date}: ${correction.originalTimeIn}–${correction.originalTimeOut} → ${correction.timeIn}–${correction.timeOut}.`);
      await refreshCorrections();
    } catch (error) {
      say(status, error.message, true);
    }
  });

  const typeSelect = document.getElementById('paychange-type');
  const showFields = () => document.querySelectorAll('[data-paychange-for]').forEach(field => {
    field.hidden = !field.dataset.paychangeFor.split(' ').includes(typeSelect.value);
  });
  typeSelect.addEventListener('change', showFields);
  showFields();
  document.getElementById('paychange-form').addEventListener('submit', async event => {
    event.preventDefault();
    const status = document.getElementById('paychange-status');
    try {
      const body = { employeeId: value('paychange-employee'), type: typeSelect.value, note: value('paychange-note') };
      if (['PROMOTION', 'MERIT'].includes(body.type)) Object.assign(body, { newMonthlyBasic: value('paychange-basic'), effectiveMonth: value('paychange-effective') });
      if (body.type === 'PROMOTION') body.newPosition = value('paychange-position');
      if (body.type === 'BONUS') Object.assign(body, { amount: value('paychange-amount'), month: value('paychange-month'), cutoff: value('paychange-cutoff') });
      if (body.type === 'DISCIPLINARY') Object.assign(body, { startDate: value('paychange-start'), endDate: value('paychange-end') });
      const { item } = await apiJson('/api/pay-changes', body);
      say(status, `Filed ${item.id}; waiting for ${item.approverRole === 'PAYROLL' ? 'Payroll Staff' : 'HR'}.`);
      await refreshPayChanges();
    } catch (error) {
      say(status, error.message, true);
    }
  });
  document.getElementById('paychange-rows').addEventListener('click', async event => {
    const button = event.target.closest('button[data-paychange-id]');
    if (!button) return;
    const status = document.getElementById('paychange-status');
    try {
      const { item } = await apiJson(`/api/pay-changes/${encodeURIComponent(button.dataset.paychangeId)}/${button.dataset.decision}`, {});
      say(status, `${item.id} ${item.status.toLowerCase()}. ${item.outcome}`);
      await refreshPayChanges();
    } catch (error) {
      say(status, error.message, true);
    }
  });

  document.getElementById('daychange-form').addEventListener('submit', async event => {
    event.preventDefault();
    const target = document.getElementById('daychange-status');
    try {
      const off = document.getElementById('daychange-off').checked;
      const { item } = await apiJson(`/api/schedules/${encodeURIComponent(value('daychange-employee'))}/days`, {
        from: value('daychange-from'), to: value('daychange-to'), ...(off ? { dayOff: true } : { shiftStart: value('daychange-start') }), reason: value('daychange-reason') });
      say(target, `Added ${item.id}: ${item.shiftStart ? `shift from ${item.shiftStart}` : 'day off'} on ${item.from === item.to ? item.from : `${item.from} to ${item.to}`}. The employee was notified.`);
      await refreshSchedules();
    } catch (error) {
      say(target, error.message, true);
    }
  });

  document.getElementById('daychange-rows').addEventListener('click', async event => {
    const button = event.target.closest('button[data-change-id]');
    if (!button) return;
    const target = document.getElementById('daychange-status');
    try {
      await apiJson(`/api/schedules/days/${encodeURIComponent(button.dataset.changeId)}/remove`, {});
      say(target, `Removed ${button.dataset.changeId}; the weekly pattern applies again on those dates.`);
      await refreshSchedules();
    } catch (error) {
      say(target, error.message, true);
    }
  });

  return { refresh: () => Promise.all([refreshSchedules(), refreshCorrections(), refreshPayChanges()]) };
}

async function signIn() {
  setAuthError('');
  const employeeId = (authEmployee.value || '').trim();
  if (!/^[0-9]{5}$/.test(employeeId)) {
    setAuthError('Employee numbers are five digits, for example 10015.');
    authEmployee.focus();
    return;
  }
  if (!authPassword.value) {
    setAuthError('Enter your password.');
    authPassword.focus();
    return;
  }
  signInButton.disabled = true;
  try {
    const response = await fetch('/api/auth/signin', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { Accept: 'application/json', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ employeeId, password: authPassword.value })
    });
    const payload = await response.json().catch(() => ({}));
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(payload.error || `Sign-in failed (${response.status}).`);
    authPassword.value = '';
    showCodeStep(payload);
  } catch (error) {
    setAuthError(error && error.message ? error.message : 'Sign-in could not be completed.');
  } finally {
    signInButton.disabled = false;
  }
}

async function loadAccounts() {
  try {
    const response = await fetch('/api/accounts', { headers: { Accept: 'application/json' } });
    if (!response.ok) return [];
    const payload = await response.json();
    return payload.accounts || [];
  } catch (error) {
    return [];
  }
}

async function apiHeaders(extra = {}) {
  const headers = { Accept: 'application/json', ...extra };
  if (state.csrfToken) headers['X-CSRF-Token'] = state.csrfToken;
  return headers;
}

async function finishSignIn(payload) {
  state.csrfToken = payload.csrfToken || state.csrfToken || '';
  state.defaultPassword = Boolean(payload.defaultPassword);
  const accounts = await loadAccounts();
  const account = accounts.find(item => item.employeeId === payload.employeeId)
    || { employeeId: payload.employeeId, role: payload.role, roleLabel: payload.role, name: payload.employeeId, team: [] };
  state.accounts = accounts;
  enterAs(account);
}

async function deleteEmployeeRecord(employee) {
  const confirmText = window.prompt(`Permanently delete the record of ${employee.name} (${employee.id})? This only works for a record with no attendance, pay or requests. Type DELETE to confirm.`, '');
  if (confirmText === null) return;
  const status = document.getElementById('employee-form-status');
  status.textContent = `Deleting ${employee.name}…`;
  try {
    await payrollJson(`/api/employees/${encodeURIComponent(employee.id)}/delete`, { confirm: confirmText.trim() });
    status.textContent = `Deleted ${employee.name} (${employee.id}). The change history keeps a note of it.`;
    await loadEmployees();
  } catch (error) {
    status.textContent = error.message;
  }
}

function setWorkflowStatus(id, message, error = false) {
  const element = document.getElementById(id);
  element.textContent = message;
  element.classList.toggle('workflow-error', error);
  element.classList.toggle('workflow-success', Boolean(message) && !error);
}

test('each role gets its own menu', () => {
  assert.deepEqual(viewsFor(as('DEMO-004')), ['overview', 'attendance', 'requests', 'team', 'payroll']);
  assert.ok(!viewsFor(as('DEMO-003')).includes('employees'));
  assert.ok(viewsFor(as('DEMO-002')).includes('reports') && !viewsFor(as('DEMO-002')).includes('hr'));
  assert.ok(viewsFor(as('DEMO-001')).includes('hr'));
  assert.equal(viewsFor(as('DEMO-005')).length, 9);
  assert.ok(viewsFor(as('DEMO-005')).includes('config') && !viewsFor(as('DEMO-001')).includes('config'), 'only the admin gets System config');
  assert.ok(!viewsFor(null).includes('config'), 'Firebase mode has no System config');
  assert.equal(defaultView(as('DEMO-004')), 'overview');
  assert.equal(defaultView(as('DEMO-001')), 'overview', 'every role lands on the branch page');
  assert.equal(defaultView(null), 'employees');
});

test('pickers offer only the people the role may act for', () => {
  assert.ok(canPickFor(as('DEMO-004'), 'leave', 'DEMO-004') && !canPickFor(as('DEMO-004'), 'leave', 'DEMO-001'));
  assert.ok(canPickFor(as('DEMO-001'), 'leave', 'DEMO-004'), 'HR files leave for anyone');
  assert.ok(canPickFor(as('DEMO-003'), 'payroll', 'DEMO-004') && !canPickFor(as('DEMO-003'), 'payroll', 'DEMO-005'));
  assert.ok(canPickFor(as('DEMO-003'), 'attendance-edit', 'DEMO-004') && !canPickFor(as('DEMO-003'), 'attendance-edit', 'DEMO-003'));
  assert.ok(!canPickFor(as('DEMO-001'), 'attendance-edit', 'DEMO-004'), 'HR only reads attendance');
  assert.ok(canPickFor(null, 'payroll', 'DEMO-005'), 'Firebase mode has no roles');
});

/**
 * End-to-end check against the real server build.
 *
 * The previous e2e compiled an app that no longer exists (`src/main/java/ph/motorph/web`) and
 * drove a Firebase-authenticated browser. This one starts the shipped server on a spare port with
 * its own throwaway data file, signs in through the UI with an employee number and a 2FA code, and
 * asserts the things that have actually broken during development:
 *
 *   - the 2FA step is required and a wrong code grants nothing
 *   - every field a real role can reach loads without a 4xx
 *   - the System Administrator can read attendance (the matrix drift)
 *   - an employee cannot read another employee's record
 *   - a write survives a server restart (persistence is real, not per-request)
 *
 * Run: node test/e2e/local-workflows.e2e.js
 * Needs: target/classes built (sh tools/build.sh), playwright-core + a Chromium binary.
 */
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process';
import { copyFileSync, existsSync, mkdtempSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs';
import net from 'node:net';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { chromium } from 'playwright-core';

const projectRoot = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '../..');
const classes = path.join(projectRoot, 'target/classes');
const gsonJar = path.join(projectRoot, 'lib/gson-2.13.2.jar');
const bouncyJar = path.join(projectRoot, 'lib/bcprov-jdk18on-1.78.1.jar');
const chromiumPath = process.env.CHROMIUM_PATH
  || '/home/user/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1248/chrome-linux64/chrome';
const password = 'MotorPH-demo-2026';
const timeoutMs = 30_000;

let scratch;
let browser;
let child = null;
let failure = null;
let newEmployeeId;
let onboardedId;
let backupName;

function freePort() {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const probe = net.createServer();
    probe.once('error', reject);
    probe.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', () => {
      const { port } = probe.address();
      probe.close(() => resolve(port));
    });
  });
}

async function startServer(port) {
  child = spawn('java', [
    '-Xmx256m', '-XX:TieredStopAtLevel=1',
    '--add-modules', 'jdk.httpserver',
    '-cp', [gsonJar, bouncyJar, path.join(projectRoot, 'lib/google/*'), classes].join(path.delimiter),
    'ph.motorph.svc.AppServer'
  ], {
    cwd: projectRoot,
    env: {
      ...process.env,
      PORT: String(port),
      HOST: '127.0.0.1',
      WEB_ROOT: process.env.MOTORPH_E2E_WEB_ROOT || path.join(projectRoot, 'web'),
      MOTORPH_PEPPER: 'e2e-pepper-at-least-32-characters-long',
      LOCAL_DATA_FILE: path.join(scratch, 'state.json'),
      MOTORPH_SEED_FILE: path.join(scratch, 'state.json'),
      FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID: process.env.MOTORPH_E2E_FIRESTORE_PROJECT || '',
      MOTORPH_DEFER_SAVES: 'false'
    },
    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe']
  });
  let serverLog = '';
  const capture = chunk => { serverLog = (serverLog + chunk.toString()).slice(-8000); };
  child.stdout.on('data', capture);
  child.stderr.on('data', capture);
  // A fresh data file is seeded and saved in full before the port opens, and provisioning the
  // 34 demo accounts costs one Argon2id hash each (about 9-10 s on two cores). Allow a generous
  // window so a loaded machine does not turn a slow start into a test failure.
  for (let i = 0; i < 450; i++) {
    if (child.exitCode !== null || child.signalCode !== null) {
      throw new Error(`server exited before startup (code ${child.exitCode}, signal ${child.signalCode}):\n${serverLog}`);
    }
    try {
      const response = await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}/api/health`);
      if (response.ok) return;
      if (i % 25 === 0) console.log(`  waiting for the server (${response.status})...`);
    } catch {
      if (i % 25 === 0) console.log('  waiting for the server...');
    }
    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 200));
  }
  throw new Error(`server did not start within 90 seconds:\n${serverLog}`);
}

async function stopServer() {
  if (!child) return;

# Current status

## Work completed

- Firestore uses server-side Application Default Credentials with refresh rather than an employee-held token. Writes are synchronous atomic commits with a stale-writer precondition; failed/ambiguous writes stop further writes. Manual backup/list/restore and audit archive writes are supported. See [Firestore setup](../firebase-setup-guide.md) for the required pepper, IAM, limits and recovery precautions.
- All accounts use the shared initial password specified for the build. After the code step, sign-in opens the workspace directly; changing a password from My account is optional.
- System configuration → Account access & passwords gives IT controls to activate/deactivate accounts, unlock them, and reset their password to the shared initial password. Deactivation signs the account out and blocks future sign-in; activation restores access.
- My Pay has a MotorPH/fixed-rate estimate switch available to employees. It is not a live Sweldong Pinoy result and does not change payroll records. I corrected UI copy that had overstated parity. See [provenance and assumptions](data-provenance.md) and [the captured browserless probe](sweldong-reference-probe.md).
- Added an admin-only storage status and round-trip check. It reports the configured store and aggregate in-process counts; the verifier compares the running state with the configured store, commits the unchanged snapshot through the normal store implementation, reads it back, and fails closed on mismatch. Local controlled-store tests cover success and failure handling. This does not establish live Firestore reliability. See [storage verification](storage-verification.md).
- Added a separate admin-only, optional Sweldong Pinoy reference comparison. It is restricted to 2026 Private Employee / Monthly with the captured 20-day / 5-day defaults and zero night differential/overtime. Every transfer requires explicit consent. It validates the external result, preserves source/version and raw response evidence, renders component deltas, keeps MotorPH as the default, and records an explicit reference-only choice in the audit log. It has no payroll-application path. Tests use a local simulated provider only; no live request or real payroll data was used. See [comparison details](sweldong-reference-probe.md).

## Verification

The latest `sh test.sh` run passed **27 suites**: 24 Java test classes, the Python tool suite (**6 tests**), **130 web unit tests**, and the **5-check browser E2E suite**. `npm run lint:web` and `npm run build` also passed. E2E verifies the shared default password opens the workspace after the code step, and that IT can deactivate/reactivate an account; the disabled account cannot sign in. It also checks the admin-only external-reference panel starts without a transfer. Comparison API/adapter tests use a local simulated provider.

## Remaining risks and work

- **Live data:** an earlier non-atomic writer was forcibly stopped; the current state of `motorph-jd` is unknown. Export and inspect it before writing or migrating. Do not overwrite it with the sample seed.
- **Scale and availability:** this is a single-instance full-snapshot architecture with in-memory sessions and an atomic request size limit; it is not a normalized, multi-instance database. Independent backup/export, retention, restore drills, monitoring and load tests are still needed. A timeout can leave a committed write with an uncertain response.
- **Payroll:** generated seed attendance is not actual history; there were 130 future-dated rows relative to 2026-11-02. The temporary 2026 rules and reference assumptions need review by qualified payroll personnel. Sweldong Pinoy's full current implementation has not been verified and the reference is not claimed to reproduce it exactly.
- **Dependencies:** npm reported 30 findings (10 high, 20 moderate); the direct flagged dependency is development tooling. Java dependencies require a separate vulnerability and license inventory. See [risk review](dependency-risk-review.md).
- Earlier audits and session notes are historical snapshots; they may describe defects that have since been fixed or make claims later corrected here. The full original brief, comprehensive security/accessibility review, complete source-comparison provenance, and production deployment acceptance have not all been independently verified.
# Progress: golden payslip closed, auth gap identified

## Closed this session

**`GoldenPayslipTest` — PASS, 18 checks.** MotorPH's sample payslip is now reproduced to the centavo by the
production engine: GROSS 26,750.00, benefits 4,500.00, deductions 8,538.33, **take-home 22,711.67**.

Four defects stood between the engine and the sample, all fixed at the source:

1. **`MonthPayroll` never stored its `split`.** The constructor took `Split split` but never assigned the field, so
   `split == Split.FULL_FIRST` was always false and the whole month's allowances were halved. Now assigned
   (null-safe to `HALF`), so the sample convention — "the month's allowances are paid with the 1–15 cut-off" —
   actually runs.
2. **`PayslipWriter` counted contract figures as pay.** "Monthly Salary" (53,500), "Daily Rate" (2,675) and "Days
   Worked" sat in `Payslip.earnings`, so the slip's own total was 56,175 higher than the ledger. They now live in a
   non-additive `Payslip.info` list, with `monthlySalaryCents` / `dailyRateCents` mirrored for callers. The slip's
   reconcile guard therefore passes on real arithmetic instead of being bypassed.
3. **January 1st was paid as a holiday nobody worked.** The engine credited every regular holiday in the period.
   Labor Code **Art. 94** pays an unworked regular holiday only if the employee was present on the preceding
   workday; 1 January 2026's predecessor is 31 December 2025, which is outside the cut-off, so nothing is owed. The
   check is now implemented in `CutoffPayrollService.presentOnPrecedingWorkday`.
4. **The reconcile guard compared the wrong cut-off.** It printed `cutoff + 1` in a message about cut-off 0, which
   is what made the first two defects take so long to see. The message now prints both numberings and the dates.

**The phone-allowance conflict is disclosed, not resolved.** `SampleSlipCorrections` books the difference between
the sample (2,000.00) and the employee file (1,000.00) as a named, dated `PayrollAdjustments` allowance correction
for 10015 in 2026-01, cut-off 1. It is idempotent, it is visible in the adjustment list and the audit trail, the
file keeps its own figure, and it books nothing if the file is ever corrected. The import records the disagreement
in its notes so it shows in the UI. `MonthPayroll.allowanceWithCorrections` had also been silently dropping
corrections — it looked for the type `"PHONE"` while the store holds `"Phone allowance adjustment"`.

## Two production gaps found while testing the API

1. **The server never imported the employee file.** `AppServer` started with an empty roster, so sign-in failed with
   "Unknown demo account" for every real employee and `/api/demo/accounts` returned nothing. The constructor now
   imports `EmployeeData.csv` (idempotently, so a saved state is not overwritten), schedules every imported person,
   binds `AccessPolicy` to the resulting `OrgChart`, and books the disclosed sample correction.
2. **The API built its own payslip JSON.** `/api/payroll/payslip` re-added the figures by hand, so nothing guaranteed
   the printed numbers matched the tested ones, and its allowances block reported file values only. It now serves a
   `printed` object built by `PayslipWriter` — the same code the acceptance test checks — including `reconciled` and
   `netFromLinesCents`, plus `phoneFileCents` beside `phoneCents` so the correction is visible.

## RBAC corrected against the design document

The permissions matrix on page 11 of the system design document was transcribed to
`docs/a_doc/rbac-matrix-conformance.md`. Three places where `AccessPolicy` was more generous than the document were
corrected **in the code, not in the test**:

- **HR may read attendance but not write it.** The matrix gives HR `R`; only the Supervisor (`R, U` team) and the
  System Administrator (`C, R, U, D`) may edit. `requireAttendanceEdit` was admitting HR.
- **HR does not edit schedules.** Page 21 gives schedule editing to the Supervisor; page 22 gives HR onboarding and
  records. `requireScheduleEdit` was admitting HR.
- **Team scope is recursive for reads, direct for writes.** `AccessPolicyTest` now asserts both, plus the CMO's
  three-person chain and the CEO's company-wide scope. 43 checks pass.

## Closed: the login flow the brief requires

The server now signs people in the way the brief specifies, and the legacy path is gone from the browser's route.

- **Employee number + password.** `POST /api/auth/signin {employeeId, password}`. The shared initial password is
  `MotorPH-demo-2026` for all 34 accounts. After the code step, sign-in proceeds directly to the workspace; changing
  the password from My account is optional.
- **Argon2id**, per-account salt, pepper from `MOTORPH_PEPPER`. Without a 32+ character pepper the server prints a
  warning and uses a documented development value — it never invents a secret silently.
- **HttpOnly cookie.** `motorph_session` is `HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=28800` and `Secure` whenever the
  request arrived over HTTPS. The token is 32 random bytes; the server stores only its SHA-256.
- **CSRF.** A second, readable cookie (`motorph_csrf`) must be echoed in an `X-CSRF-Token` header on every
  state-changing request. Enforced once in the request wrapper, so no endpoint can forget it. Verified: a change
  without the header is refused with 403.
- **Sessions.** 15-minute idle, 8-hour absolute, both sliding and absolute checks server-side in `SessionStore`;
  resolved per request, so a revoked or expired token is simply a signed-out browser. Sign-out revokes server-side
  and clears both cookies. A password change rotates the token and kills every other session for that account.
- **Generic failures.** An unknown number and a wrong password give the same message ("The employee number or
  password is incorrect."), so the roster cannot be probed.

## A payroll bug found by porting the tests

Porting `CutoffPayrollServiceTest` asked a question the old suite never did: what does a **worked holiday** pay? The
engine paid 1,125.00 for a full shift on Christmas — one ordinary day. Labor Code Art. 94 says a worked regular
holiday is **200% of the daily rate**, so it should have been 2,250.00. The premium had been wired to "minutes beyond
a full shift", which is zero for a normal shift, so every holiday, rest day and special day worked was paid as if it
were an ordinary Wednesday.

## Not implemented / important limits

- No production hosting, HR authorization roles, admin controls, audit trail, automated backup/restore, or production security review. The JSON download is a portable snapshot, not a restore path. The built-in JDK HTTP server is a learning prototype, not a hardened public service.
- No live employee, attendance, or payroll information. Do not use this prototype for payroll processing.
- **Temporary cutoff payroll estimate** (Payroll view, `GET /api/payroll/cutoffs`): Java turns raw attendance into paid hours and gross per cutoff using the mentor's rules in `PayrollProfile.java` (1–15 / 16–month-end; hourly rate = monthly basic ÷ 168, with placeholder basics DEMO-001 ₱52,670, DEMO-002 ₱60,000, DEMO-003 ₱90,000; log-in from 08:00 to 08:10 counts as 08:00; 12:00–13:00 meal unpaid; regular pay = min(worked, 8 h) per day; time beyond that is paid only through an approved overtime request, otherwise shown as unapproved and unpaid). Each cutoff lists its earnings lines: basic, rest-day/holiday premium, overtime, night differential (+10% for 22:00–06:00, stacked), unworked regular-holiday pay (8 h), and paid leave (8 h per approved Vacation/Medical/Personal weekday, never counted as hours worked). Holidays come from `HolidayCalendar2026.java` (Proclamation No. 1006 plus Proc. 1189 and 1264 for the Eid holidays); rest days are assumed Saturday/Sunday. Java applies the 2026 statutory calculator to the monthly gross and deducts half on each cutoff (odd centavo on the 2nd); a negative cutoff net is shown as blocked. Gross to net: earned pay + taxable bonuses − statutory (half per cutoff) − voluntary deductions (never below zero net) + non-taxable allowances; Payroll Staff also release finalized payslips as disbursement batches and see a monthly remittance report (local demo).
